title: Espionage: Codename Tian Du Chao Feng
author: Zhuan Sheng
synopsis:
Shen Zhizhen went to a tomb with her professor,
only to be killed by a group of grave robbers who suddenly broke into the chamber.
When she opened her eyes again, not only had she become the descendant of a grave robber,
but she had also been branded as a little traitor...

chapters.title: Dialogue Between Father and Daughter
chapters.content:
In the first lunar month of 1940, the festive atmosphere of the Spring Festival had not yet fully dissipated when Shenyang City was once again shrouded in a cold wave of midwinter.

The north wind was biting and snow was falling heavily. Outside the city, the snow was nearly a foot deep; inside, nine out of ten shops on the streets were closed, and pedestrians were few and far between.

On Wanquan Street, a horse-drawn carriage moved slowly, the wheels making a faint friction sound against the snow-covered ground. The carriage finally stopped in front of the Shen family pawnshop.

Shen Tingshan shook the snow off his body, took two large leather suitcases from the carriage, and entered the pawnshop. As he closed the door, he glanced casually in the direction he had come from and saw a carriage appearing at the street corner.

Shen Tingshan’s eyes narrowed slightly. He closed the door, slid the bolt, and carried the suitcases behind the counter. He placed the two cases down and sat on a small stool near the stove, removing his mittens to warm his hands.

Shen Tingshan called out softly to his daughter, who was wiping down porcelain: "Jiu'er, come over and talk to Dad for a while."

The kettle on the stove made a "gurgling" sound, and white steam swirled in the cold air.

Shen Tingshan raised his hand to take off his hat and placed it on the table; the brim was stained with a few melting snow beads.

Shen Zhizhen replied softly, placed a Ming Dynasty official kiln blue-and-white vase into its box, opened the cabinet door to store it properly, and only then walked over to sit by the stove.

She took two roasted potatoes out of the stove pit, placed one on the small table, and began to peel the other. Her demeanor was a stark contrast to the quiet, bright girl who had been wiping the porcelain just moments before.

"Why did you come over at this time?" Shen Zhizhen asked casually.

It was windy and snowing outside, and she had already sent the shop assistants home. What could her father want by coming here now? She took a bite of the potato—mm, Northeast potatoes were just delicious; she hadn't gotten tired of them even after a year here.

Shen Tingshan looked up at his daughter gnawing on a potato, a sense of helplessness welling up in his heart. Ever since the child had nearly lost her life in a tomb a year ago, she had been carefree and indifferent after being saved. She either spent her days in the pawnshop fiddling with antiques and paintings or stayed holed up in her room repairing broken porcelain and pottery.

"You see the situation now. Your second uncle is working for the Japanese, and our Shen family has been branded as traitors. If you don't leave now, you won't be able to later." Shen Tingshan repeated his old warning; the situation here was becoming increasingly urgent, and Little Jiu had to leave Shenyang City.

The second brother’s actions were undoubtedly putting the Shen family on the fire. How badly they would be scorched depended entirely on whether the second brother still had a conscience and cared about their kinship.

Shen Zhizhen curled her lips upon hearing this and asked with a raised eyebrow: "Leave? Where to?"

She had arrived here inexplicably a year ago. Based on the original owner's memories, she discovered she had transmigrated into a Republic of China-era novel. She was the "white moonlight" (first love) of the male lead, Wan Donglai, who died young. The novel's historical background was written with reference to Chinese history; apart from some different country names and unfamiliar dynasties, the historical trends were largely the same.

The book was roughly about the male lead, Wan Donglai, returning from studying abroad to find his family destroyed and seeking revenge. She didn't remember the specific details, but because she shared the same name as the original owner, she remembered there was such a background character who appeared in the male lead's memories. The original owner's ending in the book was to die while grave robbing a year ago—which was exactly when she had arrived.

Ever since she understood her new identity, she had been pondering where she could be safe, only to find that in such chaotic times, there was no place that was absolutely safe.

The Shen family was a pawnshop on the surface, but in secret, they controlled the "fresh pit" (newly excavated) business in the Guandong region. In layman's terms, the Shen family was one of the leaders of the Guandong grave-robbing gangs. The current head was her second uncle, Shen Jingshan, who now worked for the Japanese, which was why the Shen family was branded as traitors.

A little traitor wouldn't be safer anywhere else than at home, which was why she didn't want to leave. With her identity, if she went to fight the Japanese, people would suspect she was a Japanese spy. Most importantly, even if she cleared the "traitor" label, the original owner was still a genuine grave robber. Now that she had taken over this body, she had to bear the karma.

Moreover, according to the historical trajectory, there would be a reckoning after the victory. It would be difficult for her to fully clear her name, so the ideal state was to keep a low profile and go to Hong Kong after the Japanese surrendered.

Unfortunately, ever since Shen Jingshan became a traitor, the Shen family's situation had become awkward. Her cheap second uncle seemed ready to explode at any moment, and the epicenter was the Shen family!

The Shen family possessed a treasure map. Only the heads of the family knew about it, but for some reason, Shen Jingshan had found out.

Her cheap father was the current head of the family and was worried that his second brother would be heartless enough to target the Shen family, which was why he wanted to send her away. As for why he told her these things, it was because she was the candidate for the next head of the family. Her father told her the secret as a sort of final testament.

A sudden sourness pricked her nose. She bit down hard on the potato, trying to suppress the sudden urge to cry.

When she first arrived, her heart was full of resistance toward the Shen family. She had originally been a senior archaeology student, accompanying her professor into an ancient tomb for archaeological work.

When they entered the main chamber inside the mountain, they encountered a group of grave robbers. During the standoff, a clumsy grave robber accidentally triggered the hidden mechanism of the main chamber. Countless giant stones fell from the ceiling, and the grave robbers who had been confronting them were instantly crushed into meat paste.

She had been standing by the coffin in the main chamber, terrified, pressing herself tightly against the coffin in an attempt to avoid the falling rocks. Unfortunately, she couldn't escape the fate of being crushed.

When she opened her eyes again, she found she had transmigrated into a female grave robber. Not only did she transmigrate into a book, but she also possessed a storage space.

Not everyone gets a second chance at life. Even though she had been given this identity, she wanted to live well, especially since she had a "cheat" (golden finger).

She had been well cared for by her cheap father over the past year, and the resentment she felt across time and space had long faded. She had begun to accept this new identity, though the complex situation always gave her a headache.

Seeing his daughter asking, Shen Tingshan immediately gave his well-thought-out suggestion: "Go to Shanghai and find your third sister. She has been transferred to work in Shanghai. She holds a decent position and can protect you."

Over the years, he had intentionally downplayed the third daughter's presence. No one in the Shen family except him knew where she was, all to keep a backup plan for his two daughters.

Shen Zhizhen rummaged through her memories for information on Shen Zhimei. This third sister had left home five years ago to study and had never returned. So, she had been keeping in touch with their father all along? It seemed her not returning was intentional.

The characteristic of a large family was its sprawling branches. Her father's generation had seven brothers; now, only he and Shen Jingshan remained, as the other five had died in tombs.

There were nine cousins in Shen Zhizhen's generation. She was the ninth, named Shen Zhizhen, and her nickname was...

chapters.title: Storage Space
chapters.content:
This body and the third sister were sisters by the same father but different mothers. The third sister's mother was Shen Tingshan's first wife, who died in childbirth. After she passed, Shen Tingshan married the original owner's mother. Six years ago, the original owner's mother died of illness. Last year, her cheap father married a young girl, and now that woman was pregnant with a "little tenth."

Shen Zhizhen glanced at her cheap father at this thought. As the eldest son of the family, he had struggled for many years and only had two daughters, which touched on some things that could only be understood implicitly.

Tsk tsk, fortunately, he had self-awareness. He knew that because he had done too many wicked things, his difficulty in having heirs was retribution. Therefore, he had put his heart into cultivating both daughters. Not to mention the original owner, Shen Zhimei had been admitted to the National Central University.

Among the younger generation of the Shen family, only the original owner had the talent for the ancestral craft. She had practiced martial arts, studied grave-robbing knowledge, and geomancy since she was a child. At five, she followed her father to the pawnshop to practice appraising antiques and paintings. At ten, she learned how to make high-quality forgeries; in just three years, her creations were indistinguishable from the real thing, showing her talent. At fifteen, she began following her uncles into tombs—she was truly a grave-robbing prodigy.

Why did such a person die? It could only be said that if you walk by the river often, you're bound to get your shoes wet. She triggered a trap while grave robbing a year ago, and after she was saved, the soul inside had been replaced by her.

Shen Tingshan strictly forbade his daughter from entering any more tombs for three years, which suited her perfectly. Over the past year, she had eaten and lived in the pawnshop, mastering most of the original owner's skills. No one noticed the soul had changed; even if her personality had shifted slightly, everyone just assumed she was traumatized from her brush with death.

Shen Zhizhen pulled back her wandering thoughts. "Where does the third sister work in Shanghai?" A government official? Shanghai was an occupied territory; who was the third sister working for?

Shen Tingshan frowned and thought for a while. "It seems to be a newly established department! She is a secretary-general there. Your third sister didn't say the specifics, but I know her address. You can just go find her when you get there."

Shen Tingshan added some firewood to the stove and continued: "I'm asking you to find your third sister partly out of selfishness. In these chaotic times, it's hard to stand alone. If you two sisters are together, you can look out for each other." With that, he took a waterproof leather case from his chest and handed it to Little Jiu.

"This is the treasure map your second uncle is obsessed with! Legend has it that it hides countless rare treasures, as well as the legendary 'Feng Dynasty's Supreme Treasure: The Nine Domains Hanging Coffin'! It is said that this coffin was refined from the bones, blood, and feathers of the divine beast, the Phoenix. It contains endless mysteries of heaven and earth. If one can comprehend these mysteries, they can feel the spiritual energy between heaven and earth and thus embark on the path to immortality."

Shen Zhizhen was successfully amused. Immortality! What era was this, and people still had such thoughts!

The Feng Dynasty was not recorded in official history, and there were only a few brief descriptions in unofficial records. It was said to have been a very prosperous dynasty that perished due to disaster and plague. Strangely, such a prosperous dynasty left behind no cultural relics. Therefore, some historians concluded from myths and legends that this dynasty existed, but most believed it was a fabrication, and that the Feng Dynasty never existed in the long river of history.

After laughing, she took the item under her father's glare. She opened the slightly worn leather case and took out a sheepskin scroll.

The sheepskin had clearly been through the baptism of time; its color had yellowed, yet it still exuded an ancient and mysterious aura.

Shen Zhizhen looked closely, and her brows furrowed slightly: "A partial map?" And only one-third of it at that.

Shen Tingshan rolled his eyes at his daughter. "Nonsense. If it were complete, would it have lasted until now? Our ancestors would have cracked it long ago."

This treasure map was known only to each successive head of the Shen family because its origins were illicit. Every head of the family dared not leak even the slightest detail, and he had no idea how the second brother had found out about it.

Shen Zhizhen chuckled after hearing this, revealing two dimples that instantly softened her cold demeanor. She blinked playfully and said, "How about we use a delaying tactic? If Second Uncle wants it, just give it to him. He won't be able to find the treasure anytime soon anyway. We can just find an opportunity to take it back later."

It wasn't worth risking everything for something so intangible. It would be better to indulge Shen Jingshan and play the role of the oriole behind the mantis stalking the cicada. If by some chance the Second Uncle found other clues, they could just sweep everything up at once—how wonderful that would be.

"Talk nonsense. If this thing could be exposed, would our Shen family have been so cautious for hundreds of years, even only daring to secretly search for other fragments?" If things were that simple, he wouldn't be in such a difficult position. The moment this thing surfaced, the Shen family would surely face disaster.

This left Shen Zhizhen confused. What did he mean? Was there a hidden story? "Dad, you’d better explain in detail. Otherwise, if my third sister and I disappear one day without a trace, we won't even know who to seek revenge from as ghosts." She put the fragment back and tucked it away, though in reality, she slipped it into her spatial dimension.

Heh, she was the right person to hide things. She wasn't sure if the spatial dimension was a gift for her transmigration or something the original owner possessed, as part of the original owner's memory was missing.

A golden phoenix coffin rotated in her sea of consciousness. Yes, the space she possessed was shaped like a coffin. She had been speechless when she first saw it; others got bracelets, rings, or jade pendants, but she got a coffin. Fortunately, it was completely empty. If there had been a corpse inside, she might have fainted on the spot.

Inside the phoenix coffin was a "mustard seed" space, though it wasn't quite the vast world described in Buddhist texts.

However, it contained a static space of over a hundred square meters. Because time stood still within the storage space, items placed inside remained exactly as they were when taken out, without the slightest change. Placing and retrieving items was done entirely through her thoughts.

Living things couldn't be placed inside. She had experimented, and living creatures came out dead. Since that experiment, she had abandoned any thought of entering it herself; she didn't want to die inexplicably inside a coffin.

Over the past year, she hadn't been idle! She had stockpiled a large amount of necessities for chaotic times—food, clothing, housing, and transport. Even if she had to hide in the deep mountains, she could live comfortably for several years.

The phoenix coffin in her sea of consciousness looked the same size as an imperial coffin from an ancient tomb, but the interior space was nearly a hundred square meters.

She had lined the four walls with antique shelves. A feature of the static space was that items would remain in place even if left in mid-air, so she stacked the shelves. At a glance, it looked like a small museum.

The antiques, calligraphy, and paintings that the original owner had accumulated over the years had all been placed on these shelves.

Shen Tingshan frowned, realizing that some things really couldn't be kept from her. If they were targeted by enemies, she wouldn't even know how she died. So, he began to tell Xiao Jiu about the grievances.

chapters.title: Old Stories
chapters.content:
This story had to start with the Mao Mountain and Lao Mountain sects. The two sects had been at odds for thousands of years, and the root of their conflict was buried deep in the dust of history, impossible to trace.

Lao Mountain Taoists were skilled in exorcising ghosts, capturing demons, suppressing zombies, casting and breaking curses, and geomancy. They were daring and known for following only the mandate of heaven while ignoring human sentiment. Many of their disciples used their skills to rob tombs for profit.

When Shen Zhizhen heard "Lao Mountain," she remembered a strange fortune she had drawn while visiting Lao Mountain during her junior year of college. Two lines of the fortune read: "The beacon fires burn through the dense years; the dust of a past life continues today." She hadn't taken it seriously at the time and didn't bother to interpret it, but now she wondered if it had been a foreshadowing!

Could it be that she had some connection to the Shen Zhizhen here, or was this place her past life? Terrified by the thought, she quickly reined in her wandering mind. Things were complicated enough; she wouldn't go looking for more trouble.

After regaining her composure, she guessed aloud: "Our Shen family ancestors came from the Lao Mountain sect."

Shen Tingshan nodded and continued: "And the Mao Mountain sect has unique expertise in locating tombs, geomantic sacrifices, mechanical formations, and changing destiny against the heavens. They are well-versed in the ways of heaven and earth and can use the secrets of tomb sites to alter a person's fate..."

Shen Zhizhen understood instantly why the two sides were at odds. Mao Mountain Taoists must have despised the Lao Mountain Taoists' behavior of destroying tombs for profit, viewing it as a desecration of the deceased and a trampling of the natural order.

In short, one side destroyed tombs to get treasures, while the other spent all their effort studying how to protect tombs and prevent them from being looted.

As a result, the conflict between the two sects intensified, leading to countless deaths. The hatred accumulated over thousands of years could likely not be washed away even by the waters of Heaven Lake.

When she heard that the fragment was obtained by a Shen ancestor from a Mao Mountain Taoist named Bai, she finally understood why they didn't dare to expose it. Heh, it was murder for gain! They were worried about the descendants coming for them.

Shen Zhizhen raised her eyelids, a flash of wisdom in her eyes, and spoke her guess without hesitation: "That Mao Mountain Taoist had descendants, and they are powerful. They have been searching for this thing, which is why the Shen family has been hiding outside the Great Wall."

Time flows like a mighty river; even the deepest blood feuds are gradually submerged by the passage of time.

How could grievances from hundreds of years ago persist until today? The reason the other side never gave up on their "revenge" was merely a pretext; the real goal was this fragment.

Although his daughter's words were harsh, she had hit the nail on the head. Shen Tingshan nodded, confirming she was right. "The reason our Shen family moved outside the Great Wall was indeed to avoid the Bai family of Xiangxi. Just remember, if you ever meet anyone named Bai, you must be extremely careful."

Thinking about the karma of her ancestors killing for treasure—a burden she, an outsider, now had to bear—Shen Zhizhen felt nauseated. She took another fierce bite of her potato, chewing it indignantly.

Shen Tingshan didn't know what had gotten into his daughter; she had been acting strange ever since she was rescued from a tomb last year. He took a rectangular sandalwood box from his pocket and handed it to her.

Shen Zhizhen looked at her "cheap" father speechlessly, muttering to herself about his habit of pulling things out one by one.

When her eyes fell on the sandalwood box, she recognized its value. She placed the potato on the table, wiped her hands carefully, and took it. Inside were a token engraved with a phoenix pattern and an abacus the size of a palm. Both items exuded an ancient aura.

Shen Zhizhen immediately saw that these were no ordinary objects. She asked what they were while instinctively holding them in her palms to examine them closely.

The front of the token was carved with a phoenix spreading its wings, and the back with a phoenix feather. The feather was delicate and vivid, shimmering with a faint luster, and the edges were engraved with ancient runes.

The abacus was made of mysterious iron. The beads, the size of corn kernels, were embossed with Bagua symbols, and the sides were inscribed with the four characters "Tiandu Chaofeng" in small seal script.

Seeing these four characters, Shen Zhizhen had an epiphany. This mysterious iron abacus was the token of the Shen family head. Upon closer inspection, she realized it was also a weapon; the abacus had a built-in magnetic mechanism, with the arrangement of the Bagua symbols corresponding to the firing angles of hidden weapons!

The design was quite ingenious. She put down the abacus and picked up the phoenix token, her fingers gently stroking the surface. The delicate texture and unique patterns seemed to tell an ancient story.

She had grown up with her grandparents, who were both archaeology professors with deep knowledge of ancient culture and history. Influenced by them, she had developed a strong interest in antiques.

In her eyes, every antique was a carrier of a mysterious and ancient story, silently bearing the memories of history and the traces of time.

They could transport people back to the past, allowing them to feel the culture, customs, and human affairs of that era.

These antiques were witnesses of time; through them, one could glimpse the wisdom and creativity of the ancients. They were guardians of history, carrying the bloodline and foundation of human civilization.

Because of this, when it came time to choose a major, she had chosen archaeology without hesitation.

Shen Tingshan looked grave and said in a deep voice: "This is our Shen family heirloom and the symbol of the clan leader's status. Take them with you; I'm worried I won't be able to protect them."

Shen Zhizhen's heart sank, and she felt the weight on her shoulders increase. "Let's go together."

Shen Tingshan replied: "Talk nonsense. There are so many people in the Shen family; how can we all leave? I have things to handle here. After you leave, I will close the shop and return to Shen Family Village. Even if your Second Uncle is a scoundrel, he won't drag the whole clan down with him. He wouldn't dare."

The entire Shen Family Village was populated by the Shen clan. If they armed themselves properly, they wouldn't be helpless even if the Japanese army arrived. They could retreat into the mountains, and survival wouldn't be a problem.

Shen Tingshan checked his pocket watch and saw that fifteen minutes had passed. Worried that those following them might grow suspicious, he whispered the purpose of the two items to Xiao Jiu: "The abacus is the token of the family head, and the phoenix token is the key to opening the Shen family treasury..."

The fact that the Shen family had a treasury was truly unexpected. Honestly, even though she wasn't a materialistic person, she was dazed by the information her father had revealed.

It was like the shock of suddenly inheriting tens of billions in assets.

Shen Tingshan stood up after finishing his instructions, putting on his hat and gloves. "The train ticket, address, and money are all in the trunk. Leave the shop in the middle of the night. Decide where to go yourself; not letting anyone know is the safest way."

He gave these instructions because he trusted Xiao Jiu's ability to protect herself. He believed that if his daughter wanted to leave, no one could stop her.

chapters.title: Dizziness
chapters.content:
Shen Zhizhen nodded to show she understood, telling her father not to worry, that she could take care of herself, and urged him to take care as well.

Shen Tingshan patted his daughter comfortingly and turned to leave. When he opened the pawnshop door, snow blew in. He glanced at the street corner, then walked out as if nothing was wrong, casually brushing the snow off the carriage before driving away.

As Shen Zhizhen closed the door, she noticed a carriage following from a distance. She bolted the door and frowned. No wonder he was in such a hurry for her to leave; they were being watched.

She walked slowly back to the stove, opened the trunk, and looked at the train ticket. A ticket for ten days later! He wanted her to leave tonight? Was this a premonition that something was going to happen? She took out the gold bars and silver dollars, put them in her spatial dimension separately from the trunk, and then sat down to study the phoenix token.

I never imagined the Shen family actually had a treasure vault! My "cheap" father said it contained the entire family fortune accumulated over hundreds of years.

The Shen family had their roots in grave robbing, keeping all the precious artifacts they unearthed for themselves. For centuries, they had also operated a pawnshop, likely acquiring many fine items along the way. One can only imagine how many astonishing treasures were hidden in that vault!

I suspect my "cheap" second uncle wasn't just eyeing the treasure map, but the Shen family vault itself. I truly cannot fathom why he would work for the Japanese and spill his own family's secrets. Wasn't he afraid of bringing total ruin upon the Shen family?

Thinking about it, something seemed off. Logically, if Shen Jingshan really wanted these things, he could have simply competed for the position of family head! After all, once he became the head, both items would be within his grasp.

Yet, throughout this past year—and based on the original owner's memories—I have never seen any sign of Shen Jingshan vying for the headship. Instead, he has been entirely focused on the underworld, serving as their "big boss."

I rubbed my fingers over the Phoenix Token, my eyes gradually deepening. If it wasn't Shen Jingshan, then did the Japanese want it? What exactly is my "cheap" second uncle planning, and why is he letting the Japanese reach into the Shen family?

Shen Zhizhen sat there, brow furrowed in deep thought for a long while, but she couldn't make sense of it. She decided not to dwell on these matters for now; packing up was more urgent.

My "cheap" father's meaning was clear: the pawnshop was to be closed for the time being. Even though I didn't know what would happen next, it was always better to be prepared. I would strike first! I’d clear out my own pawnshop! Hehe, I wouldn't leave a single hair for the Japanese!

At this thought, a sly smile appeared on Shen Zhizhen's face. She tossed the sandalwood box containing the black iron abacus and the Phoenix Token into her space. Just as she stood up, a sudden, intense wave of dizziness washed over her.

The dizziness caught her off guard. Her vision went black, and her body tilted backward uncontrollably, hitting the ground with a loud "thud."

Lying on the cold, hard floor, her mind remained clear, but her body felt as if it had lost all strength; no matter how hard she tried, she couldn't move an inch.

Shen Zhizhen felt as if her soul had left her body, drifting in a void. Here, she could clearly see the image of her soul; it emitted a faint light, like a lonely star.

Suddenly, a dazzling light shot from afar, catching her attention. The moment she thought of going to look, she instantly transported to where the light was. She focused her gaze—it was the Phoenix Token!

It was circling around a phoenix coffin. The coffin was a deep, reddish-gold, carved with lifelike, exquisite patterns and runes that seemed to tell of the vicissitudes of time and the weight of history.

The phoenix coffin floated silently in mid-air, emitting a soft glow. On the side of the coffin, a phoenix with wings spread, ready to take flight, was carved with stunning detail.

The moment Shen Zhizhen saw the phoenix coffin, she knew this void was her sea of consciousness. Who would believe that her soul had not only entered her own consciousness but was witnessing such a miraculous scene?

The Phoenix Token emitted an intense, blinding golden light that was almost impossible to look at. Yet, as if it had found its target, the token suddenly flew toward the phoenix coffin, embedding itself perfectly into a groove on the lid. The token and the coffin fit together seamlessly.

When the dazzling golden light finally dissipated, Shen Zhizhen saw the scene on the lid clearly. It was carved with a phoenix rising from the ashes, its body covered in dense runes. There were nine grooves the size of the Phoenix Token on the lid; one was already occupied by the Shen family's token, while the other eight remained empty.

She wanted to walk over and study it, though her consciousness could only see the space inside the phoenix coffin clearly, while the rest of her sea of consciousness remained a hazy blur.

Her soul's ability to enter her sea of consciousness this time must be related to this phoenix coffin and the token! So, she intended to get closer for a better look.

However, just as she approached, a brilliant golden light flashed, stinging her eyes so she couldn't keep them open. Immediately after, her soul vanished from the sea of consciousness.

Shen Zhizhen slowly opened her eyes. Everything she saw was familiar; she knew her soul had returned to her body. She stood up, rubbed the back of her head, and a mocking smile curled her lips. "Thanks a lot for making me fall backward."

If she had fallen forward, her face would have hit the stove. Disfigurement would have been the least of her worries; if it had started a fire, she would have lost her life. No matter how many "cheat codes" she had, they were meaningless if she didn't have the life to use them.

After her mocking thought, she realized something was wrong. She looked down at her body and felt a sticky sensation. Her hands were covered in a layer of black sludge, and a pungent, foul odor filled her nostrils. She was shocked—what was going on?

Shen Zhizhen quickly sensed the changes in her body and was pleasantly surprised to find it felt exceptionally light, as if it had lost all weight, yet it was filled with strength. She tried a light leap and easily jumped onto the high counter.

The original owner had practiced martial arts since childhood, and her physical fitness was already excellent. After she transmigrated, she had kept up a daily exercise routine, so she knew this body better than anyone.

Yet, at this moment, she clearly felt that her physical strength and five senses had surpassed their previous levels by several times over.

Thinking of the golden light in her sea of consciousness, could it have performed a "marrow-cleansing" ritual on her? Otherwise, how else could she explain this situation?

Shen Zhizhen's wandering thoughts were interrupted by the foul odor emanating from her body. She decided to stop overthinking; she couldn't figure it out anyway. She had clearly transmigrated into a Republic-era novel, yet everything happening to her was turning into a fantasy story.

chapters.title: Changes
chapters.content:
Shen Zhizhen hurried to the backyard to boil water for a bath. It took three changes of water to wash away the black sludge and the foul stench.

After changing into clean clothes, she belatedly remembered that the Phoenix Token was the key to opening the Shen family vault!

Shen Zhizhen quickly checked her space and discovered it had grown! And it wasn't just a little bit—it was a world of difference. It had grown a full ten times larger!

She noticed a few lines of golden text at the top of the space and focused her mind to read them: "Nine Phoenix Tokens unite to break the nine heavens; time and space shift as one soars through the clouds. Dancing gracefully, transcending the sun and moon; the phoenix dances in the firmament, startling the world."

She could understand the literal meaning. The first line meant the Phoenix Token, named "Nine-Union," possessed the power to break the limitations of the nine heavens!

Could the second line be hinting at the ability to travel through time and space? "Time and space shift" certainly sounded like that. Perhaps her arrival here was related to the mysterious phoenix coffin in her sea of consciousness.

And since the Phoenix Token was a Shen family heirloom, could it be that she had some connection to the Shen family all along? Was that why the phoenix coffin brought her soul here to be reborn?

In that case, the phoenix coffin in her sea of consciousness wasn't just a simple storage space; it seemed to contain things she didn't yet understand. The physical changes she just experienced confirmed this.

The third line painted a vivid picture, as if one could see a phoenix soaring between the sun, moon, and stars, passing through layers of clouds, sometimes shining with the sun and moon, sometimes vanishing into the galaxy—mysterious and unrestrained.

The final line was full of dominance, acting as both a conclusion and a hint.

Hmm... interpreted literally, this seemed like a fantasy story filled with magical elements.

Using her rational judgment, Shen Zhizhen concluded that this fantasy story had nothing to do with her.

The appearance of these words and the change in the space were clearly linked. The position of the text corresponded exactly to the Phoenix Token; perhaps the fusion of the token and the coffin had triggered a special mechanism.

Regrettably, a mere human like her would likely find it difficult to interpret or decipher the secrets hidden within this phoenix coffin.

Honestly, when faced with such profound and unimaginable things, the feeling that welled up in her heart wasn't just a sense of her own insignificance, but a deep awe for this mysterious world full of unknowns.

She had never imagined that behind her ordinary life, the vast world held countless things that defied logic and were difficult to comprehend. Perhaps one day, fate would lead her to explore them, but for now, reality was what mattered most.

That Phoenix Token was linked to whether the Shen family vault could be opened; she had to remove it from the coffin. Shen Zhizhen focused her mind on the token. *Whoosh*—the token appeared in her hand, and the space returned to its original size.

Shen Zhizhen breathed a sigh of relief. It was good that she could remove it. She tested it a few more times, confirming that the token could be inserted and removed at will, and that the space would change accordingly.

Having understood the function of the Phoenix Token, Shen Zhizhen began to ransack her own pawnshop. She used her mind to place the antiques and paintings scattered on the floor onto the shelves, and moved the display racks and empty crates from the warehouse into the space. Since the space could expand, she planned to visit the Shen family vault before heading to Shanghai, performing a "Great Shift" on the fortune the Shen family had accumulated over hundreds of years.

The Japanese had excavated many ancient tombs in the Three Eastern Provinces over the years. Since the Shen family moved in the underworld circles of the Northeast, they couldn't be kept in the dark about which tombs were being disturbed. The Japanese were cunning; for any major military operation, they acted personally and maintained excellent secrecy, which led to everyone else's information being delayed.

Her main reason for wanting to put the contents of the Shen family vault into her space was to guard against the Japanese. If the items were in her hands, even if she donated them to atone for the Shen family's sins in the future, it would be better than them falling into the hands of the invaders.

Although she didn't know where the Japanese had heard rumors about the Shen family treasure map, she felt it wasn't Shen Jingshan who told them. But one thing was certain: the Shen family was being targeted.

Now that the entire Three Eastern Provinces were under Japanese control, it was only a matter of time before they got what they wanted. So, she intended to strike first, ensuring those thieves' schemes would come to nothing.

At this thought, her eyes narrowed. Perhaps she could use the space to do more. She couldn't just stand by and watch the Japanese transport China's cultural relics back to Japan.

Though she thought this, she still had to ponder how to implement it. She used to be a student buried in archaeology, having never even experienced the harsh realities of the workplace, and she had always been the type to mind her own business.

In contrast, the original owner had more spirit and a "rivers and lakes" temperament, even having blood on her hands from the Japanese. As for her, she had never even killed a chicken, let alone a person.

Therefore, after arriving here, she chose to keep a low profile at first. Once she had familiarized herself with everything regarding the original owner, she used the information she had gathered from the streets to do some of the things a Chinese person ought to do.

Bang! Bang! Bang! The sudden sound of gunfire shattered the surrounding silence, startling Shen Zhizhen, who had been lost in thought. A wave of unease welled up in her heart. With no time to overthink, she hurriedly ran to the door and carefully peered out through a crack.

She saw a squad of Japanese soldiers surrounding the Wan family jewelry store next door, packing the street so tightly that not even water could pass through. Sounds of smashing and crying drifted over from time to time.

It was obvious what the Wan family next door was suffering, and the occasional gunshot was like a funeral knell, signaling the passing of yet another vibrant life.

Shen Zhizhen clenched her fists tightly, her heart filled with anger and helplessness. She watched helplessly as the Japanese soldiers ransacked the Wan family jewelry store, arrested many people, and then marched off in triumph.

She gripped the gun in her hand tighter and tighter, as if she were about to crush it.

As time ticked by, Shen Zhizhen tried hard to calm her emotions, but the anger burning in her heart refused to dissipate. She took a deep breath, slowly loosened her clenched fists, and tossed the gun into her space.

She swore to herself: No matter what, I must do something for this era! I must not choose to escape just because I come from another world, and I certainly cannot sit by and watch the invaders slaughter my compatriots because of my own inner fear!

The things she had experienced since arriving made it impossible for her to continue living a cowardly life under the excuse that this was just a world from a book. After all, this life was a gift; the worst that could happen was that she would return it. With this thought, the fog that had shrouded her heart for a year instantly dissipated.

Shen Tingshan did not know that after he left, the Shen family pawnshop had first been ransacked by his own young heir, and then a sudden fire from next door had spread, burning the pawnshop and the residence and warehouse in the backyard into ruins.

At this very moment, Shen Tingshan was lying on a warm heated brick bed with his young wife, chatting about moving back to Shen Family Village.

chapters.title: My Little Nine! How Could You Be Burned to Death?
chapters.content:
An Hui did not understand why he had suddenly decided to return to Shen Family Village. With confusion in her eyes, she asked softly, "Master, why did you suddenly have such an idea? Did something happen?"

Shen Tingshan had originally intended to tell her the real reason, but changed his mind when the words reached his lips; this was a major matter, and the fewer people who knew, the better.

He sighed and made up an excuse: "Sigh, it’s all because of that business with the second brother! Now everyone in Shenyang City knows that our Shen family has produced a traitor. Who would still want to come to the Shen family pawnshop? Business is getting colder and colder, and there’s no point in keeping it open. So, I thought we might as well close the pawnshop for now and go back to Shen Family Village to avoid the limelight, and we can make other plans after you give birth."

Hearing this, An Hui lowered her eyes slightly, appearing thoughtful. Just as she was about to speak, she was interrupted by a chaotic sound of footsteps.

The butler ran in, looking panicked and hurried. He said urgently, "It’s bad! Master, our pawnshop is on fire!" His tone was anxious and worried; after all, the Ninth Miss was living in the pawnshop.

When Shen Tingshan heard this, his heart felt as if it had been struck by lightning. He, who had been lying leisurely on the brick bed, suddenly bolted upright. Without time to think, he scrambled to put on his shoes, grabbed his fur coat, and hurried out with the butler.

At this moment, he had only one thought in his mind: he must get to the pawnshop as quickly as possible to confirm whether his Little Nine was safe. As for other matters, they had long been cast to the back of his mind, so he did not notice the obscure, meaningful look from his young wife behind him...

Along the way, Shen Tingshan’s face was terrifyingly gloomy, as if covered by a thick layer of dark clouds.

He sat quietly in the carriage, but his heart was churning like a stormy sea, filled with wild speculations about various conspiracies.

He had just arranged for Little Nine to leave, and in the blink of an eye, the pawnshop was burned down. What did this fire mean? Could the Japanese have sensed something? Was the fire meant as a deterrent, or were they using Little Nine’s capture to blackmail the entire Shen family?

The more Shen Tingshan thought about it, the more he felt there was something behind it. No, he had to talk to his second brother as soon as possible. Hmph, if the second brother dared to stand by and watch his own niece die, he would definitely skin him alive.

The carriage stopped abruptly, the wheels screeching against the ground. The curtain was lifted, and Shen Tingshan hurriedly stepped down, his eyes scanning the scene before him like torches.

What met his eyes was a ruin ravaged by fire, scarred and devastated. The original building was now nothing but charred black remains, with precarious rafters that seemed ready to collapse at any moment.

Even though he knew in his heart that with Little Nine’s skills, she would never be buried in a sea of fire, he was still shocked by the scene. Burning with anxiety, he rushed in, shouting at the top of his lungs: "Daughter! My daughter!"

Shen Tingshan searched inside and out while calling for her, but he did not see any human remains or other suspicious items. The heart that had been hanging in his throat finally settled back into his chest at this moment.

If the Ninth girl hadn't been captured, she must have left here in advance and avoided this fire. It seemed the latter was more likely.

He thought this because there weren't even many remains of porcelain vases or jars at the scene; it was clear it had been ransacked before the fire started. It must be said that this was a fortunate misunderstanding.

Although the butler was worried, he was a clear-headed bystander. He knew that with the young lady's abilities, it was impossible for her to perish in a fire. Therefore, after arriving, he didn't rush in with the master to look for people, but instead asked the neighbors what had happened.

The butler, having learned the cause of the fire, came over: "Master, the Japanese soldiers came today and raided the Wan gold shop next door. They killed quite a few people and took many away. The head of the Wan family was arrested on charges of colluding with the Red Party. This fire spread from next door."

After the butler finished speaking, he felt a sense of sorrow. Eighty percent of the gold shops in Shenyang City belonged to the Wan family, and they even had shops all over the Three Eastern Provinces. Just like that, with a single accusation of colluding with the Red Party, the Wan family was wiped out. Where could one go to reason with such people? Sigh, no wonder the Master wanted to return to Shen Family Village. In this world, how can making money be more important than one's life?

Over these years, he had finally understood what the Japanese were doing in the Three Eastern Provinces: it was blatant robbery.

Shen Tingshan frowned upon hearing this. It was the Wan family that had been hit, so this fire was indeed collateral damage, not the conspiracy he had imagined on the way. He walked next door to take a look. There were over a dozen charred, shriveled, and twisted corpses scattered about!

Seeing this, a plan emerged in his mind. Taking advantage of the fact that no one was paying attention, he quietly moved the skeleton of a female corpse that was curled up in a corner near the Shen family residence into his own courtyard.

After Shen Tingshan finished all this, he immediately burst into loud wails: "My Nine! How could you be burned to death..."

The butler had witnessed his master's miraculous operation from beginning to end. His heart became as clear as a mirror; he knew that his master was planning to pull a "deceiving the heavens to cross the sea" and "cicada shedding its skin" trick for the Ninth Miss!

Therefore, he immediately understood and began to cooperate with his master in the performance. He let out a "waah" and began to wail loudly on the spot. The crying was truly earth-shattering, drawing the surrounding neighbors over from the Wan family's place. Upon learning that the young heir had passed, they all stepped forward to comfort and console him.

This scene was captured in its entirety by Shen Zhizhen, who was hiding nearby. A layer of amusement rose in her eyes: "My cheap father is really something!"

She raised her hand to pull her scarf up, covering most of her face, and then carefully moved her feet, quietly leaving the scene. She couldn't let anyone discover she was faking her death, or she would be letting down her cheap father's painstaking efforts.

Since her father had pulled such a stunt, it seemed the name Shen Zhizhen could no longer be used. From now on, she would use her childhood nickname, Shen Jiu, when walking outside. The original owner's nickname was only used by the Shen family for internal ranking; outside, everyone called her "Miss Shen" or "Young Heir."

However, Shen Zhizhen quickly dismissed this thought. Since she had a traitorous second uncle, it was best not to use the nickname Shen Jiu either. She scanned the Phoenix Coffin rotating in her consciousness with her mind, and a name surfaced in her heart—Jiu Zhao.

Shen Zhizhen blinked. Was it her imagination just now? Why did she seem to be able to perceive the emotions of that Phoenix Coffin?

Jiu Zhao! This name had an inexplicable sense of familiarity, as if she had a fateful connection with it. It was a very mystical feeling. Shen Zhizhen felt she was being a bit superstitious, so she quickly pulled back her wandering thoughts to focus on serious matters.

She thought of the original owner's superb, masterful forgery skills and immediately decided to make good use of them to make herself a few more IDs and various passes. The tools and materials needed for forging documents were all in her space; she only needed to find a quiet place to work. Hehe, this craft finally had a place to be used in her hands.

chapters.title: A Full Performance
chapters.content:
In the bitter winter, it was a snowy day and there were no customers in the shop. The elderly barber was sitting by the stove to keep warm. Seeing someone walk in, he hurriedly stood up to ask about the customer's needs.

Shen Zhizhen shook the snow off her body, glanced around casually, and pointed to an old photo hanging next to the mirror: "Give me a clean and neat haircut, just like the short hair in the photo."

Her body was tall and slender, at 1.72 meters. Cutting her hair short and disguising herself as a man to walk outside would not only be much safer but would also create confusion.

In this war-torn era filled with crises, beauty was not important to her at this stage. Being able to save her life, act conveniently, and ensure that her actions would not implicate others was what she needed most right now.

The barber felt a bit regretful, but he understood the difficulties a beautiful woman faced in these troubled times. He picked up his scissors and began to work. His movements were skillful, and every snip was precise. Ten minutes later, the long, dark, and shiny hair that had originally fallen over her shoulders had turned into a handsome short haircut.

Seeing that there was hot water on the stove, Shen Zhizhen asked the master for some hot water to wash her hair. While waiting for her hair to dry, she sat by the stove and chatted idly with the old master.

"It's too cold lately. It's a good thing the Japanese army caught the homeless people on the street; at least they won't freeze to death on the streets if they go to dig coal!" the old master said with emotion.

Shen Zhizhen frowned upon hearing this. No wonder there wasn't a single homeless person on the street; it turned out they had been captured by the Japanese army. But where would they go to dig coal at this time of year? Thinking this, she asked the question.

The old master: "They say they are being sent to the Heilongjiang province. They've captured quite a few people. I heard that prisoners in jail are also being sent there."

Shen Zhizhen had a bad premonition in her heart. Could it be that they were sending these people to Heilongjiang for live bacterial experiments? She immediately decided to go and find out.

After her hair dried, she stood up, put on her hat, bought a few wigs from the old master, and left after paying.

At this very moment, Shen Tingshan and the butler finished their self-directed performance. With faces full of sorrow, they bid farewell to their neighbors, then carefully placed the corpse into a coffin purchased for the occasion and departed silently, the carriage moving slowly toward the old family estate in the east of the city.

Shen Tingshan sat in the carriage with a grave expression. He turned his head and whispered to the butler, who was driving: "Remember, no matter who asks, you must firmly insist that the Ninth Miss has passed away. Do you understand?" His voice carried an unquestionable authority.

The butler nodded respectfully and replied, "Rest assured, Master, I understand."

Back at the Shen residence, the master and servant performed once more, staging another scene of grief. The entire Shen household seemed to be shrouded in a heavy haze, with an air of solemnity and sorrow permeating the atmosphere.

Above the main gate, white silk hung high, swaying gently in the wind as if seeing the Ninth Miss off on her final journey.

The news that the young master of the Shen family had burned to death spread across most of Shenyang City in less than half a day. The reactions from various parties associated with the Shen family were mixed, with most finding it unbelievable. Those on the Guandong circuit who had dealt with the young master and knew his skills already suspected the cause of death was suspicious. Especially after learning the details of the incident, they speculated one after another that he had been murdered by the Japanese; otherwise, how could a mere fire claim the life of the Shen young master?

An Hui looked through the swirling snowflakes at the white silk hanging on the door, a mocking curve appearing at the corner of her mouth. So, the "pride of the Shen family" that the old master spoke of had died in a fire just like that. It seemed the rumors on the circuit could not be fully trusted; the Shen young master, who was rumored to be god-like, was nothing more than this...

The next day, Master Shen left Shenyang City with the coffin and the Shen clansmen. After holding a grand funeral at the Shen family estate, he buried the body in haste. The butler was left speechless; his master truly knew how to put on a full act.

Shen Zhizhen did not know that her "cheap" father had handled things so beautifully. At this moment, she was in the Yamato Hotel, located in the Japanese residential area of the South Manchuria Railway (Mantetsu) zone. Wearing a dark kimono, she sat cross-legged on the tatami, fully focused on the task at hand: forging various identification documents.

Under the dim light, her eyes were focused. With every stroke and line, she meticulously replicated the documents. The tatami beneath her radiated warmth. This high-end hotel, operated by the South Manchuria Railway Company, was not only pleasant in environment but also provided meticulous service.

From the enthusiastic welcome at the entrance to the facilities in the room, everything made one feel its high quality and luxury. Tsk tsk, the Japanese lived such extravagant lives using the wealth plundered from China—where was the justice in that?

The Mantetsu zone was a special area occupied by Japan in the Northeast, mainly distributed along the South Manchuria Railway and its branch lines. By 1937, the area of the zone had expanded to over five hundred square kilometers.

The zone could be understood as a colony. Japan had established its own administrative and judicial institutions, residential areas, schools, and hospitals there, with an independent legal system.

Mantetsu not only operated the railway but also used the zone to monopolize important industrial sectors in the Northeast, such as coal, steel, transportation, and electricity. Through these economic activities, they plundered a massive amount of resources and wealth from the Northeast.

The Japanese residential area of the Mantetsu zone where she was staying was the main settlement for Japanese people in Shenyang. One could hear a lot of news here, provided, of course, that one knew the Japanese language. As it happened, she did.

She had chosen this room after scouting the location beforehand. A newly arrived archaeology professor from Japan lived upstairs. What would a Japanese archaeology professor be doing here? Naturally, he was after the ancient tombs of the Northeast.

A few years ago, the Goguryeo ancient tomb complex in Ji'an was looted, and the ringleaders were renowned archaeologists from Japan. They used the name of archaeology to carry out tomb raiding.

She had found out that there would be major activity at the East Station the day after tomorrow. The Japanese army was dispatching two special trains—one heading to Heilongjiang Province and the other to Dalian. She planned to hitch a ride on the train to Heilongjiang to reach the Shen family's treasure cache, and incidentally, see if she had a chance to save anyone.

In this day and age, most of those captured by the Japanese were good people. She had no moral burden about letting prisoners go; who knew, there might be a few Communist Party cadres among them, and she would even be accumulating merit for herself.

With this plan in mind, Shen Zhizhen prepared to purchase some hot food. The magical thing about her storage space was that whatever she put in remained exactly the same when she took it out. She would buy plenty to eat while in the mountains.

After buying food, she entered a teahouse to purchase some hot drinks. In the freezing, desolate deep mountains, being able to drink a hot beverage was a luxury.

Just as she was sitting by the window drinking tea and waiting for the waiter to fill her thermos, she suddenly heard two Japanese men talking in Japanese in a tea room on the second floor of the Japanese teahouse across the street. Driven by curiosity, she pricked up her ears to listen to what they were saying.

chapters.title: Eavesdropping
chapters.content:
Ever since undergoing that baptism of golden light, Shen Zhizhen had discovered that not only had her five senses become exceptionally sharp, but her physical fitness had also increased several times over.

Today, she deliberately tried to focus her mental energy and was pleasantly surprised to find that she could hear faint sounds from over ten meters away!

Consequently, the conversation between the two Japanese men fell into her ears without reservation. Tonight, a high-ranking Japanese officer would come to Room 331 of the Yamato Hotel to meet with an archaeology professor who had just arrived from Japan. This professor was named Tanaka Fumiya, and his background seemed to be quite significant.

Thus, she had disguised herself as a young Japanese man and checked into the Yamato Hotel. Her fluent Japanese allowed her to check in successfully.

She was currently forging various passes and documents, preparing for her long journey after retrieving the treasure.

Shen Zhizhen’s ears twitched slightly. She immediately put down the work she was busy with, closed her eyes, and listened with full concentration to the conversation coming from the room upstairs.

Night fell, and the Yamato Hotel was brightly lit. Several military vehicles stopped in front of the hotel. A Japanese officer stepped out of a black sedan; the rank on his crisp military uniform revealed a sense of authority and confidence. It was Colonel Nakajima, a high-ranking officer of the Japanese army in Shenyang.

Two rows of Japanese men standing at the entrance immediately bowed to welcome the Colonel. Colonel Nakajima nodded slightly and strode inside, his eyes flashing with a sharp light.

Upon entering the target room, he saw a man in a kimono with a refined temperament sitting quietly on the tatami, his gaze fixed on the falling snow outside the window.

On the table sat a set of antique teacups and an open book. The man turned his head upon hearing the sound, a gentle smile tracing his lips.

A flash of surprise crossed Nakajima’s eyes. He had never expected that the famous Japanese archaeologist Professor Tanaka Fumiya who had come here would be him! "Bai-san?"

The name carried a certain special magic, causing a complex emotion to well up in Nakajima’s heart.

The man had a refined and steady temperament, giving one a sense of composure and hidden depth. But Nakajima knew this was only a facade; he had been fortunate enough to witness the madness and cruelty beneath this elegant skin, and it was something he still remembered vividly to this day.

Tanaka Fumiya smiled slightly and stood up to greet Nakajima: "Long time no see, Colonel Nakajima. You are still as imposing as ever. Please call me Tanaka; it is more intimate that way."

Upon hearing this, Nakajima smiled and nodded in response: "Very well, Tanaka-kun. You are most welcome. On this mission, I will do everything in my power to assist you in completing your task."

The archaeology professor was merely a cover identity for this man. In reality, he had come with a secret order from the Emperor, and Nakajima had no choice but to cooperate.

Tanaka Fumiya replied modestly: "You are too kind, Colonel. It is my supreme honor to serve His Majesty the Emperor. I will certainly do my utmost and not fail His Majesty’s expectations."

After a brief exchange of pleasantries, the two sat facing each other on the tatami. Tanaka Fumiya poured a cup of hot tea for Colonel Nakajima and then turned to switch on the record player.

As the record spun, a light Japanese tune began to play. Amidst the wonderful musical atmosphere, Tanaka Fumiya and Colonel Nakajima began to enter the main topic of today’s meeting.

The two spoke in Japanese throughout, keeping their volume low enough that only they could hear, and occasionally using encrypted methods to communicate. This cautious attitude fully demonstrated the high importance they placed on the confidentiality and significance of this conversation.

Shen Zhizhen cursed inwardly: "Cunning Japanese!"

The sound interference tactic was useless against her. Now that her hearing was extraordinary, such slight interference could not affect her at all.

Regrettably, what frustrated her was that when the two stopped talking, they used their fingers to tap on the table to communicate, as if using some kind of code similar to Morse code, which caused the content she heard to be fragmented and impossible to piece together.

It had to be said that this method of preventing eavesdropping was indeed extremely effective.

No matter what advanced equipment was used to eavesdrop, it would be affected by the strong interference signal emitted by that record.

Even if one could record the code used during the conversation, it would be quite difficult to extract truly useful information from these intercepted fragments alone.

Likewise, for someone like her who could hear the content of the speech but could not piece it together due to incomplete information, it was almost impossible to decipher the entire conversation.

That Tanaka Fumiya could have a high-ranking Japanese officer come to see him in person, and without the slightest hint of arrogance in his tone, meant his identity was very special. Moreover, acting with such caution meant he was plotting something significant.

When she heard the words "treasure map," a look of surprise flashed in her eyes. Could the treasure map they were talking about be the remnant map of the Shen family? Thinking of this, a flash of inspiration struck her mind. Wait—the surname Bai—could that Tanaka Fumiya be a member of the Bai family from Western Hunan?

My god! If that were true, wouldn't the Shen family be in "danger"?

At this very moment, Shen Zhizhen keenly sensed a slight movement from above outside the window. Her brows arched involuntarily. It seemed she was not the only one eavesdropping in the dark. If it weren't for the fact that the words "treasure map" were too shocking, perhaps that person would not have lost their composure and caused a disturbance.

At the same time, the conversation that had been taking place in the next room came to an abrupt halt, and then there was movement.

Shen Zhizhen felt a tightening in her chest. She immediately realized that the eavesdropper outside had been discovered. Decisively, she swept all the items on the table into her spatial storage, then quickly stood up, nimbly putting on her shoes and coat. Just as she finished adjusting her hat and scarf, a sharp, piercing warning whistle rang out, and chaos erupted outside.

Accompanied by bursts of intense gunfire, the sound of "bang, bang, bang" echoed continuously in the air. Shen Zhizhen quietly walked to the window and peered out cautiously.

She saw a blurred afterimage flash by. A nimble figure with remarkable agility leaped lightly from the upper floor in a few swift motions, landed steadily on the ground, and vanished into the vast night before the Japanese soldiers could surround them.

Shen Zhizhen’s gaze remained locked on the figure as it disappeared. That person’s movements looked somewhat familiar... Chapter 9: If the Roots Are Not Cleared When Cutting the Grass

The sound of voices from above interrupted Shen Zhizhen’s thoughts. Realizing that Tanaka Fumiya and Nakajima were standing directly above her, she quickly held her breath, not daring to move.

Tanaka Fumiya looked into the distance with deep eyes: "That person has excellent skills. There shouldn't be many in the Guandong region with such ability."

Colonel Nakajima’s eyes darkened at these words. Such skills were indeed rare. He already had a few candidates in mind and decided to send men to investigate as soon as he returned.

"How is the investigation into the list the General gave you?" Tanaka Fumiya asked, withdrawing his gaze.

"The person lurking within the Wan family has been exposed. I ordered the arrest of the Wan family members and searched their residence several times, but found no treasure map. During interrogation this afternoon, the head of the Wan family bit his tongue and committed suicide. Before he died, he insisted that the Wan family had never possessed a treasure map, and the others we tortured all claimed to know nothing." Nakajima’s tone was heavy; he was extremely dissatisfied with this result.

"If they are useless, there is no need to keep them." Tanaka Fumiya’s voice remained gentle, yet it lightly tolled the death knell for the Wan family.

Upon hearing this, Colonel Nakajima said, "The Wan family has deep roots in Shenyang. Wouldn't it be better to replace them with a Wan family member who works for me?"

Tanaka Fumiya replied: "If the grass is not cleared by the roots, the spring breeze will bring it back to life."

Shen Zhizhen felt a chill run down her spine. Is this Tanaka Fumiya a devil? He decided the fate of the Wan family so casually. So, this is how the family of the male lead, Wan Donglai, was wiped out.

How could she remember that the male lead’s enemies in the book did not include anyone named Tanaka Fumiya? Did she remember wrong, or did the male lead actually not know that the mastermind behind the destruction of his family was this Tanaka Fumiya?

Honestly, she had originally treated the story in the book as a work of fiction and had not truly immersed herself in it emotionally. Therefore, even when she saw the incident at the Wan family shop with her own eyes, she hadn't made much of a connection to the male lead.

But now, hearing such a cruel conversation with her own ears made her feel the cruelty and ruthlessness of the world within the book. These seemingly distant, virtual plot points actually contained the dark side of real human nature.

Shen Zhizhen’s mood at this moment was both heavy and deeply powerless.

She knew clearly that she could not save the Wan family on her own. No matter how good her skills were, she couldn't stop the enemy's real bullets. Go find the male lead? She didn't even know where he was; where would she look?

Who could she turn to for outside help? The entire Northeast was now occupied territory. Wouldn't looking for acquaintances just be sending them to their deaths?

Judging from the Wan family affair, it was clear that the Japanese army had already compiled a list of people suspected of having the treasure map. Not only that, but they had also placed people in these homes to quietly conduct investigations.

Judging by Tanaka Fumiya’s ruthless nature, the families on this list would likely follow in the Wan family’s footsteps sooner or later. She just didn't know if the Shen family was on this list.

Thinking of this, Shen Zhizhen could no longer care about the "cicada shedding its skin" ruse her cheap father had set up for her. Even if it meant exposure, she had to see her cheap second uncle to figure out how he knew about the Shen family’s treasure map. If he had learned it from the Japanese, wouldn't the Shen family be in great danger?

A rhythmic, orderly sound of footsteps came from the hallway, sounding like a large group moving in unison. Shen Zhizhen looked out and her heart sank—the outside had been surrounded by the Japanese army.

Cursing inwardly, she quickly went back into the room, took off the clothes and hat she had just put on, hung them up neatly, and then messed up the bed to make it look like someone had just been sleeping in it.

*Knock, knock, knock.* A series of urgent knocks sounded at the door. Shen Zhizhen tried to calm herself, took a deep breath, and went to open the door.

As soon as the door opened, a group of Japanese soldiers rushed in to search everywhere, not missing a single corner.

Shen Zhizhen pretended to be at a loss, babbling in Japanese, explaining that she had just been awakened by the gunfire and, seeing the martial law outside from the window, was asking what had happened.

The Japanese squad leader, hearing the young, handsome man speak fluent Japanese, immediately judged him to be one of their own. His vigilance dropped significantly, but he still routinely asked to check his identification.

Shen Zhizhen took the Japanese identification she had just made out of her pocket and handed it to him with a calm face, though her palms were sweating and her body was ready to bolt at any moment.

The squad leader took it, flipped it open, and glanced at it. The searching soldiers returned to report that there were no suspicious items in the room, so he closed the document and handed it back.

"You, stay in the room honestly. Do not step out of the door until the alert is lifted! Anyone who violates this will be severely punished!"

Shen Zhizhen did not dare to show the slightest hesitation. She immediately reached out with both hands to take the document, nodding and bowing while smiling, indicating that she would certainly comply.

Only after all the Japanese soldiers had left the room did she let out a long sigh of relief. She opened the document she had just made and looked at the seal that hadn't fully dried yet, a flash of luck crossing her eyes.

If that Japanese squad leader had taken one more look, she might have been finished today. She locked the door and listened intently to the movements outside, waiting until the soldiers went to search other floors before returning to sit on the tatami in the living room.

Shen Zhizhen listened and realized there was no one upstairs. Clearly, Tanaka Fumiya and Colonel Nakajima had left that room—she didn't know if they had left or changed rooms. While her mind wandered, she took out her tools to quickly make another document, just in case there was another inspection.

Shen Zhizhen had originally thought the Japanese would withdraw after the search, but unexpectedly, the area remained under martial law! Even worse, the number of Japanese soldiers outside had actually increased. It was clear that the Yamato Hotel had been blockaded. "Why?"

At this very moment, in the dimly lit and oppressive basement of the Yamato Hotel, an inhumane interrogation was unfolding like a nightmare.

Tanaka Fumiya sat in a chair with his legs crossed, looking relaxed. His gaze was cold and ruthless as he stared at the man tied to the torture rack, covered in blood.

The man’s body trembled continuously from the intense pain, and every wound on his body was oozing blood, staining his originally white shirt a shocking red.

Tanaka Fumiya, however, ignored all of this, as if the scene before him were nothing more than an ordinary performance.

He had shed his usual mask here; his gentle and humble appearance had vanished, and his eyes had become like ice, revealing a chilling, bloodthirsty glow.

"You have a stiff backbone, but that’s fine. I have plenty of time and patience to torture you slowly until you speak." Chapter 10: Why Did He Come to Her?

"If you don't want a life worse than death, tell me: who ordered you to come here? How many accomplices are with you in this Yamato Hotel? Is the person who just escaped one of you?" With every word he uttered, his tone grew colder, making one’s blood run cold.

This man had been captured in the room adjacent to his. It was obvious that the person who fled the scene had intentionally created the noise to buy time for this man to escape, but unfortunately, he had seen through it.

In fact, he had long since detected the bug in the room and had set up surveillance in advance. It could be said that no matter what information this man had heard today, there was no way he would leave the Yamato Hotel unscathed.

However, there had been an unexpected twist: the tape in the listening device was gone, and the content discussed today must never be leaked.

Tanaka Fumiya’s patience was running thin. With a flick of his finger, a thin, sharp silver needle appeared at his fingertip. With a casual wave, the needle shot out at an astonishing speed.

In the blink of an eye, it struck the center of the man’s forehead on the torture rack with perfect accuracy, leaving only a tiny red dot that would be hard to notice without close inspection.

"Ah..." A shrill scream echoed through the room. The man’s body began to twitch uncontrollably, his facial muscles twisting into a hideous expression of agony, as if the tiny silver needle had completely destroyed his nervous system.

The Japanese soldiers nearby had only seen a flash of silver light and hadn't had time to react before the entire interrogation room was filled with the miserable screams, a sound that seemed to come from the depths of hell, causing one’s skin to crawl.

The man, who had been putting up a desperate resistance, was now gasping for breath, as if he were about to die at any moment. Finally, unable to bear it any longer, he said in an extremely weak voice: "I... I will talk..." His eyes were filled with fear and despair.

A cold smile hung on Tanaka Fumiya’s face. "If you had spoken sooner, why suffer such torture? I only want to hear the truth." As soon as he finished speaking, another silver needle shot out like lightning.

This needle entered the man’s head at a different angle, instantly intensifying his pain while simultaneously bringing a moment of relief. With two silver needles deeply embedded in his brain, how could he possibly be okay?

Tanaka Fumiya watched the man coldly; he had no intention of sparing his life. What he had just done was merely to force the truth out of him.

The man struggled to lift his head, looking at the terrifying devil. Deep within his desperate eyes, a fierce hatred and regret flickered. He muttered to himself: "The mountains and rivers are broken, and my heart still aches; I swear to slay the enemy chieftain to sacrifice to my homeland."

As he finished speaking, he revealed a bitter smile and used the last of his strength to bite down hard on his tongue. In an instant, blood gushed from the corners of his mouth, like enchanting red flowers blooming on his pale face.

As his head slumped, the man’s eyes remained wide open, shining like two bright stars. The spark in his eyes did not fade, as if the final flame of hope deep within his heart was still burning.

The accident happened far too suddenly! The Japanese soldiers in the interrogation room didn't even have time to react. By the time they stepped forward to check the man’s breathing, he had already expired! One of the soldiers quickly turned around to report the situation to Officer Tanaka.

Tanaka Fumio heard those two muttered sentences, and a look of contempt curled his lips. "Heh? So that’s how it is... A Red Party member, no wonder his mouth was so stubborn!"

Tanaka Fumio turned to the soldiers behind him and issued an order: "Continue the thorough search! Drag this man's accomplices out for me! You must find that cassette tape! Do you understand?" As his voice faded, the Yamato Hotel was subjected to an even more meticulous search.

In her room, Shen Zhizhen racked her brains to devise several escape methods, only to find that escaping silently was almost impossible. By now, the entire Yamato Hotel had been surrounded by Japanese soldiers, and it wasn't just the outside; the inside was also under tight surveillance.

Not long ago, two Japanese soldiers had been stationed outside every room on the second floor. Forget about a person; not even a fly could have flown out.

Given the current situation, it would never have reached this point if not for some unexpected event. Unfortunately, the Japanese soldiers had come to inspect the rooms at a critical moment; otherwise, she definitely could have discovered some clues from Tanaka and Nakajima.

A loud explosion rang out, giving Shen Zhizhen a start, followed immediately by the chaotic sound of gunfire. After a moment of thought, she cautiously opened her door and, through the crack, asked the Japanese soldier at the door in Japanese what was happening.

The soldier, currently on high alert with his rifle raised, barked a harsh reprimand, ordering her to return to her room and not to take a single step out.

Shen Zhizhen knew she wouldn't get anything out of him, so she feigned fear, indicated she would cooperate, retreated into the room, and locked the door with a click.

The two soldiers outside assumed she was just scared and thought nothing more of it, immediately returning their focus to their guard duty. Their orders were to not let anyone step out of their rooms; as long as she didn't come out, they didn't care if she locked the door or not.

Once Shen Zhizhen was sure the two soldiers outside were not suspicious of her, she took a pistol from her space and gripped it tightly. With light, cautious steps, she moved toward the bathroom. Just a moment ago, while talking to the soldier, she had heard a faint sound coming from the bathroom, which was why she had changed her mind and locked the door.

When Shen Zhizhen slowly pushed open the bathroom door, the sight before her made her gasp. A man covered in blood was lying on the floor, and the ventilation duct near the ceiling was open; clearly, this man had entered through there.

Shen Zhizhen realized immediately that the lockdown of the Yamato Hotel had everything to do with him. A wry smile touched her lips—how did this huge mess end up in her room? Did it have to be such a coincidence?

Despite her internal grumbling, she resigned herself to checking if he was still breathing. She reached out to test his breath, and upon feeling a weak but steady pulse, she felt a slight sense of relief. At least he was still alive.

She immediately took hemostatic medicine and bandages from her space—items she had prepared as essentials for wartime—and skillfully applied the medicine and bandaged his wounds. Once finished, she gently patted the man's cheek, trying to wake him.

Seeing no reaction, she pinched his philtrum and pressed firmly on several key acupoints. After some effort, she finally saw the man's eyelids flicker, and he gradually opened his eyes.

chapters.title: Wang Shun
chapters.content:
Seeing this, Shen Zhizhen whispered, "Comrade? Since you're awake, you should leave quickly!" She stated her request bluntly; there was no other way—if they were discovered, they would both be finished.

Wang Shun recalled jumping in here and passing out from exhaustion. Looking at the person speaking Chinese in front of him, he asked, "You... are you Chinese?"

The man's voice was very weak, as if it might drift away on the wind at any moment.

"Yes, otherwise why would I save you?" Shen Zhizhen helped the man up, letting him lean against the wall to rest for a moment, hoping he would regain his strength and leave soon.
