"Thank you..." Wang Shun squeezed out the two words with difficulty, his eyes shining with gratitude.

"No need to thank me. Once you regain some strength, you should leave through the ventilation duct. I'm worried the Japanese army will come to inspect soon."

As she spoke, Shen Zhizhen picked up a rag to wipe the bloodstains off the floor and opened the window a crack, hoping to dissipate the smell of blood in the room quickly.

Wang Shun knew very well that under the current circumstances, he definitely couldn't escape, and his companion, who had been captured while covering his retreat, had likely already been killed. The items he carried were obtained at the cost of their lives, and he had to find a way to get them out.

Thinking of this, Wang Shun looked at the handsome young man. He was a good person. Although he didn't know why this person was at the Yamato Hotel wearing Japanese clothes, the fact that he had not only saved him but hadn't handed him over to the Japanese soldiers showed that he was a person of integrity.

Rather than letting what he carried fall into the hands of the Japanese army, it was better to take a risk and trust this young man once. Perhaps the other party could successfully take these two items out of here! Even if he couldn't, it wouldn't be a loss for him, as he couldn't get them out anyway. As for whether this would implicate the young man, he didn't have time to think about it.

With that thought, Wang Shun took a deep breath and carefully pulled a palm-sized notebook with a black cover and a brand-new cassette tape from his chest.

"My name is Wang Shun, a member of the Red Party underground organization in Shenyang," Wang Shun said in a low, firm voice.

He stared at the young man before him, his eyes filled with expectation. "These two items are important intelligence we obtained. I implore you, little brother, to take them to the Heji Noodle Shop near the East Station and hand them personally to the owner, Uncle Mancang."

Shen Zhizhen was speechless. Hearing movement in the hallway, she realized the Japanese soldiers might be coming to search, so she reached out and took them to encourage him to leave quickly. "Hurry, the Japanese soldiers are coming."

Seeing that the other party had agreed, Wang Shun didn't linger. He stood up, used his remaining strength to leap into the ventilation duct, and thoughtfully replaced the vent cover.

Seeing that he was sensible, Shen Zhizhen frowned and asked, "What if I can't find this Uncle Mancang?"

Don't blame her for being pessimistic; with Tanaka Fumio's temperament, who knew what madness he might commit? If Uncle Mancang was caught or had already retreated upon hearing the news, who would she look for?

"Then find a way to get them to my organization." After saying this, the man endured the pain throughout his body and crawled away, trying to lead the enemy away so as not to implicate the young man.

Shen Zhizhen gripped the cassette tape and the notebook tightly, knowing that these items must contain vital intelligence. Wang Shun had handed them to a stranger like her only because he knew he was a dead man walking.

The noisy sounds outside grew louder, and it seemed they had discovered something; the Japanese soldiers had stopped searching the rooms. Shen Zhizhen quickly tucked the cassette and notebook into her space.

She worried whether Wang Shun had been exposed. Thinking of this, her mind became a mess—that guy wouldn't sell her out, would he?

A bright searchlight swept past the window, catching Shen Zhizhen's attention. She leaned toward the window to look out, her gaze involuntarily falling on the manhole cover directly below.

Thinking of how Wang Shun had entered through the ventilation duct, if the duct was a viable path, then the sewer should also lead outside. With this thought, she felt a surge of joy and immediately decided to give it a try.

If that man named Wang Shun was unfortunately captured and happened to be unable to withstand the torture and sold her out, wouldn't staying here be waiting for death?

With that, she took several grenades from her space, went out, and tied them one by one to the door handle. This way, as soon as the Japanese soldiers pushed the door open, the grenades would detonate, buying her time to escape.

She then quickly took the overcoat hanging on the rack, put it on, and donned a hat and scarf, wrapping herself up tightly.

She then went to the bathroom window, patiently waiting for the searchlight to sweep over the area again.

When the searchlight beam passed the window, she took a deep breath and leaped out without hesitation, landing lightly on the ground. The entire process was clean and neat, without making a sound.

Upon landing, she immediately reached out to lift the manhole cover and quickly climbed inside. She held her breath, carefully replaced the cover, and pulled a pig-snout-style gas mask from her space to wear.

Before leaving, Shen Zhizhen hung two grenades on the manhole cover—a little trap for anyone following. It would be great if it could blow Tanaka Fumio to bits.

Honestly, in an environment where she could be gunned down at any moment, Shen Zhizhen found her psychological resilience improving rapidly. She, who had once been somewhat timid and cowardly, was now gradually approaching the realm of decisiveness and ruthlessness of the original owner.

She even began to think that if she had the chance to try shooting and killing a few enemies, it might further temper her courage.

Two muffled explosions reached her ears; the sound came from the direction of her room! Shen Zhizhen immediately realized she had been exposed and began to run wildly, wondering what had happened as she went.

Was it a coincidence? Did they accidentally trigger the grenades on the door while searching the room? Or did that guy named Wang Shun betray her? Countless questions flooded her mind, leaving her unable to determine which was the case.

Shen Zhizhen used the wind to determine her direction at intersections. When she encountered iron gates, she chose to dismantle them with brute force—let's just say, her current strength was enough to scare even herself.

Wang Shun had been captured by Tanaka Fumio himself. When Tanaka returned to his room and found his codebook missing, his rage was ignited. He personally took charge of the capture, and upon searching him and finding neither the cassette nor the codebook, he immediately employed his unique interrogation techniques.

He held several silver needles, and with a light flick, the sharp tips sank into Wang Shun's body like a viper striking.

In an instant, Wang Shun felt a wave of excruciating pain, as if thousands of ants were gnawing at his bone marrow. His consciousness began to blur, the scene before him became distorted and fuzzy, and his mind fell into chaos.

Under this bizarre and cruel torture, Wang Shun's psychological defenses completely collapsed, and he lost all self-control.

chapters.title: Escape
chapters.content:
By now, Wang Shun had become a puppet in Tanaka Fumio's hands, at his mercy. Finally, under Tanaka's inducement, he spilled everything he knew without reservation.

After receiving the information, Tanaka Fumio stood up and ordered Kuwata Onoro: "Kuwata-kun, take men to the second floor immediately! You must not let that person escape!"

Kuwata Onoro nodded without hesitation and quickly turned to lead his men toward the stairwell, descending rapidly to the second floor.

Tanaka Fumiya returned to his room to call Colonel Nakajima, informing him of the information he had just obtained and ordering Nakajima to arrest the Red Party members within Shenyang.

Tanaka Fumiya hung up the phone, and two booming explosions followed, shaking the floorboards. A sense of foreboding rose in his heart. He walked quickly out of the room and headed toward the second floor.

Upon arriving at the scene of the explosion, what met his eyes was a scene of utter chaos and carnage. The bodies of Tanaka Koyaro and several Japanese soldiers were scattered about, and the air was thick with the pungent smell of gunpowder and blood.

Frowning deeply, he walked into the room to investigate and discovered a faint footprint on the bathroom windowsill. Tanaka Fumiya immediately leaned out, looked down along the windowsill, and saw a manhole cover lying quietly where his gaze landed.

A thought struck Tanaka Fumiya; he seemed to understand something. He waved at the patrol soldiers outside, ordering them to go and check it.

However, the moment they opened the manhole cover, two more explosions suddenly rang out. A massive shockwave knocked the surrounding Japanese soldiers to the ground, and thick smoke and flames billowed from the manhole.

Tanaka Fumiya was so angry he laughed. Such underhanded tactics—could that person be from the Guandong underworld, part of the same group as the person eavesdropping outside the window?

With that thought, he leaped, landing lightly and steadily. He then jumped into the sewer without hesitation, leading a group of Japanese soldiers in pursuit.

However, they had already missed the best opportunity. By then, Shen Zhizhen had long since slipped away through one of the manholes, disappearing into the vast city of Shenyang.

Shen Zhizhen had originally intended to quickly get rid of the hot potato in her hands; as long as she could hand it over, she would have fulfilled her obligation to Wang Shun.

Unfortunately, this plan was disrupted by the sudden increase in Japanese soldiers on the streets. It was clear these soldiers were out to catch her, which made her wary and afraid to act rashly. She found an empty house owned by a pawnshop and decided to spend the night there.

Shen Zhizhen chose a room that was draft-proof, took a thick fur bedding set from her space, and stretched out comfortably. She marveled once again at how good it was to be tempered by golden light; even without a fire, she didn't feel the slightest bit of cold while lying in the fur bedding.

After ensuring she wouldn't freeze to death in her sleep, Shen Zhizhen began to carefully recall the fragments of information she had heard.

These scattered clues seemed to hide some important operation of the Japanese army. By the time her eyes grew heavy and her consciousness began to blur, she still hadn't figured it out.

The next morning, the weather was uncharacteristically good. People walked out of their homes, and the streets gradually became lively.

Shen Zhizhen changed back into women's clothing, put on a wig, and went out, blending into the crowd as she walked unhurriedly toward the East Station. As she neared the station, a strange feeling suddenly welled up in her heart. She stopped immediately and carefully observed her surroundings, noticing that things seemed different from usual.

The original owner of the body had followed her father in and out of Shenyang since childhood and was very familiar with the city. After taking over, Shen Zhizhen hadn't been idle, having already thoroughly mapped the place out by cross-referencing the original owner's memories.

In broad daylight, with no wind or snow, how could there be no vendors near the train station? Yet, the street before her was unusually deserted. Forget about street vendors; there wasn't even anyone selling cigarettes or newspapers! When things are abnormal, there must be something sinister afoot!

Thinking of this, she changed her mind. She decided not to go to the He Family Noodle Shop from the front. Instead, she turned on her heel and circled to the back, pretending to be a passerby while actually pricking up her ears to listen for movement inside. Sure enough, she found something was wrong and immediately left with a calm expression.

In a private room at a teahouse, after finishing a cup of hot tea, Shen Zhizhen figured out what was going on. Wang Shun must have been captured and had betrayed her and the He Family Noodle Shop. They had likely set an ambush last night, just waiting for her to take the bait. Fortunately, she hadn't been foolish enough to walk right into it last night.

At this moment, a million "grass mud horses" were galloping through her mind. Being dragged into this was one thing, but to be set up like this? If her body and senses hadn't been strengthened by the golden light, she would have been walking to her death.

While complaining internally, Shen Zhizhen took a notebook and a cassette tape out of her space. Information was time-sensitive; this stuff had to be delivered. She opened the notebook and glanced at it—oh, it was a codebook.

In this era, the military used special methods to encrypt important information to ensure that even if intercepted, the content could not be easily deciphered. The codes recorded in this book were the keys to reading the information.

Needless to say, this belonged to Tanaka Fumiya. Thinking of the encryption method they used yesterday, she realized this codebook could decipher that conversation. Her gaze fell on the cassette tape; it seemed the answer was on that tape.

Unfortunately, she hadn't made a point to memorize it, nor had she received any agent training. Even with the codebook in hand, she didn't know how to use it!

Moreover, in the 1940s, tape recorders were rare items; being foreign goods, you couldn't necessarily buy one even with money. The only one in the entire Shen family was at the old residence. If she knew how to decipher the code, a trip to the Shen family estate wouldn't be impossible, but the key was that she didn't know how, and her cheap father likely didn't either.

Forget it! She would just have to find a way to get rid of this hot potato first and not delay the anti-Japanese cause. Although she might have been sold out by Wang Shun, this was something he and his comrades had risked their lives to obtain. Compared to the greater good, her little bit of resentment was nothing. Sighing, she wondered what that guy had been through.

With that, she threw the tape and notebook into her space, then got up, paid the bill, and left.

Over the past year, Shen Zhizhen had paid close attention to Red Party news and knew of a few secret contact stations. Unfortunately, she visited three places in a row, and all were empty! Had they received the news and relocated? Or had they been captured like the noodle shop owner?

She got the answer after spending ten silver dollars for information: the Japanese army had been conducting precise arrests of the Red Party since last night. Half of the Red Party members in Shenyang had been captured, and those who hadn't were already on the run.

Shen Zhizhen felt a headache coming on. What was she supposed to do? She couldn't find the Red Party to deliver the hot potato, and these two items were useless in her hands.

chapters.title: I Just Attended Your Funeral Yesterday
chapters.content:
Shen Zhizhen thought of the familiar figure from last night and immediately decided to find Shen Jingshan. Someone who could eavesdrop on Tanaka Fumiya and Colonel Nakajima meant that Second Uncle Shen was not on the side of the Japanese.

She searched around but couldn't find him, though she discovered that Shen Jingshan had stayed at the small Western-style building near the East Station.

This building had been seized by a pawnshop and later claimed by Shen Jingshan. Over the past year, Shen Jingshan had taken no fewer than five properties from the Shen family pawnshop; her second uncle clearly had more than just three hiding spots.

Shen Zhizhen put down the ashtray, her gaze lingering for a moment on the tape recorder on the desk. She decided to finish her investigation before coming back to deal with it. She climbed to the third-floor attic and raised an eyebrow to see a telescope set up by the window.

She walked over, bent down, and looked through the telescope. It was aimed directly at the East Station's largest warehouse—a warehouse reserved for the Japanese military, guarded by Japanese soldiers year-round.

Seeing twice as many Japanese soldiers as usual, she understood it was because of the two trains departing tomorrow.

Shen Zhizhen came down from the attic to the desk, sat in the chair, took the tape from her space, put it into the recorder, and pressed play...

In the evening, a rickshaw stopped in front of the small building. Shen Jingshan got off, gave the puller a silver dollar, glanced behind him, took out his key, entered, and locked the door behind him.

Shen Jingshan climbed the stairs with a deep frown, intending to take down the telescope in the attic. The Japanese were already suspicious of him, and they might come to search at any time.

As he reached the second-floor landing, he sensed something wrong. He turned sharply to find someone lying on the sofa. He pulled out his pistol, walked over, and was so angry he laughed.

"I just attended your funeral yesterday, and today you appear alive and well in front of me. Are you trying to scare me to death, girl?"

As he spoke, Shen Jingshan put his gun away, turned to check that the curtains were drawn, and then sat down on the single sofa nearby, relieved.

Shen Zhizhen was amused by her uncle's words. "It was an emergency! Otherwise, why would I come here and expose myself?"

She sat up from the sofa. It was good she had waited for him; she had been bored and taken a nap, and she had woken up the moment Shen Jingshan opened the door, also sensing that someone was watching outside.

Shen Jingshan: "Hmph, I thought your father was acting strange. I insisted on opening the coffin to see you one last time, but he refused no matter what, saying that little Jiu had already been burned to a pile of bones and there was nothing to see, and that I shouldn't disturb you and let you go on your way in peace!"

He amused himself as he spoke. His big brother was really something—to think he could pull off having his own daughter fake her death.

Shen Zhizhen couldn't stop the corners of her mouth from curling up at the thought. Her cheap father was actually quite cute.

"Tell me, why are you here looking for a traitor like me instead of leaving?" Shen Jingshan crossed his legs, waiting for the ninth girl to explain her purpose.

Shen Zhizhen didn't beat around the bush. "Last night, I was staying in Room 231 of the Yamato Hotel. While standing by the window admiring the moon, I saw a black shadow come down from upstairs. The footwork that person used was exactly the same as our Shen family's ancestral footwork."

At these words, a flash of surprise crossed Shen Jingshan's eyes. Little Jiu was at the Yamato Hotel yesterday. He immediately realized the danger and pointed a finger at her. "Your father staged this whole thing just to give you a chance to escape, and you—you actually dared to run to the Yamato Hotel! Are you tired of living?"

Since last night, the entire city of Shenyang had been on high alert, and the culprit behind this tension was exactly what had happened at the Yamato Hotel.

The more Shen Jingshan thought about it, the more he felt something was off. He paused, suddenly realizing something. "Wait, the Yamato Hotel is still under martial law. How did you get out, girl? Could it be that the youth mentioned in the Japanese army's wanted notice is you?"

Shen Jingshan's reaction undoubtedly confirmed that the person from last night was him. It seemed her cheap second uncle did have a purpose for working for the Japanese, though she didn't know what it was that could make him willing to bear the stigma of being a traitor. With that, she nodded frankly. "It's me."

Shen Jingshan...

Things had reached this point; there was no point in holding a grudge. "Fine, I'll arrange for someone to send you to Fushun. Once you're there, do whatever you want, just don't come back."

Shen Jingshan knew in his heart that his brother must have already arranged a place for the ninth girl, which was why he said this.

Shen Zhizhen frowned. "We'll talk about my affairs later. Now, tell me, what exactly did you hear last night?"

Shen Jingshan was so furious at this that he couldn't even find the words. "Outside that window, besides hearing those wretched Japanese ditties, what else could I possibly hear?"

"Then why did you run?" Shen Zhizhen asked, looking speechless. It was true; without her keen hearing, one would likely only hear the Japanese music.

Shen Jingshan replied, "It’s because those two guys eavesdropping next door accidentally made a noise and were spotted by Tanaka Fumiya! I figured since I wasn't hearing any useful intel anyway, I might as well play the good guy and create a distraction to draw the Japanese away so they’d have a chance to escape." He felt he’d gotten a raw deal—he hadn't gathered any information and had only ended up in a mess.

Shen Zhizhen immediately sensed her "cheap" uncle was being dishonest and called his bluff. "If you didn't hear anything, how do you know one of them is named Tanaka Fumiya? And why were you eavesdropping in the first place?"

Shen Zhizhen raised an eyebrow. "At this point, there's no need to hide anything, is there? Tell me about it."

Shen Jingshan was so annoyed he laughed. "Fine! So that’s where you were waiting for me!"

How could he have forgotten that this niece of his was always craftily clever, with a mind full of endless ideas? She had probably come here specifically to test him.

Shen Jingshan said, "Your father wouldn't want you getting mixed up in this. Be a good girl; I’ll draw them away in a moment, and you leave immediately."

Shen Zhizhen replied with an innocent look, "I don't want to be mixed up in this either, but it’s like one thing after another just happened to fall into place, and I ended up here in a daze."

"My father had everything arranged, but who would have thought the Wan family next door would catch fire and burn down our pawnshop? After my father rushed over to make sure I was safe, he staged this whole act. With the heavy snow blocking the roads, I got stranded here. You tell me, where in Shenyang could I go without being recognized? It had to be the Japanese-occupied territory. And then I ran into last night’s mess. Tell me, am I not the victim here?"

Shen Zhizhen spun a tale of truth and lies, her words dripping with feigned innocence.

Shen Jingshan knew the girl wasn't telling the whole truth, but he didn't expose her. Since she wanted to know, he might as well tell her. If he died one day, he needed someone to confirm his identity so he wouldn't be barred from the ancestral grave.

Shen Jingshan took out a cigarette and lit it. "Isn't your second uncle a traitor? I deal with the Japanese all day; how could I not know when Tanaka Fumiya arrived?"

A colonel meeting an archaeology professor—there was definitely something fishy going on. Naturally, he had to listen in, and that was how he’d ended up in this mess.

Shen Jingshan knew his niece's personality; if he didn't explain it clearly, she would never let it go. Rather than letting her stir up trouble, it was better to tell her so she would know where she stood.

Seeing that Shen Jingshan was willing to talk, Shen Zhizhen kept asking questions, and the doubts in her heart were gradually unraveled... Chapter 14: Uncle and Niece Talk

Shen Zhizhen hadn't expected that Shen Jingshan became a traitor for the sake of the Shen family! She had considered countless possibilities, but never that one.

A year ago, Shen Jingshan accidentally learned that the Japanese were looking for the treasure map of the Ancient Feng Kingdom and had listed the Shen family as suspects, planting a Japanese agent within the household. To find that agent and gain more information, he had gone along with it when the Japanese tried to recruit him.

Shen Zhizhen asked, "Does the fact that they haven't found it mean they've confirmed the map isn't in the Shen family and have withdrawn?" No wonder they were testing her father; it was all to see if the map was in the Shen family.

Did this mean the secret of the Shen family's treasure map hadn't been leaked? If so, the family was safe for the time being.

She knew it—this secret was only known to the heads of the family through the generations. If her father didn't say anything, who could possibly know the map was in the Shen family?

Now that the map was in her hands, even if those Japanese dug three feet into the ground in Shenyang, they would never find it.

Shen Jingshan shook his head and flicked the ash into the tray. "As far as I know, Colonel Nakajima has planted Japanese agents in every major power in Shenyang. Judging by what happened to the Wan family, they haven't withdrawn."

The fact that they hadn't found it only meant it was well-hidden. This was why he dared not tell his older brother. His brother was different from him; he was always at home, and any slight change would be easily noticed. Once that agent realized they had been exposed, the outcome would be another Wan family tragedy.

Shen Zhizhen rubbed her temples. It was so complicated! She realized her second uncle had to continue being a traitor to stabilize the Japanese high command. Thinking about how Nakajima already suspected him and had sent people to monitor him, it seemed she needed to find a way to clear Shen Jingshan's name. That way, the agent would realize the treasure map wasn't there and would quietly withdraw from the Shen family, preventing another disaster like the Wan family.

Shen Zhizhen asked, "Who exactly is the agent Nakajima planted in the Wan family?" How did they manage to wipe out the Wan family just by being discovered?

Shen Jingshan replied, "Bai Moli, the seventh concubine taken by Master Wan. Her Japanese name is Hyakushima Kaori, and she is a high-level Japanese agent."

Shen Zhizhen's mouth fell open. That "pure white jasmine" Master Wan spoke of was a Japanese agent! Thinking of the scene where Master Wan had boasted to her father, it was so ironic—truly, lust is a blade hanging over one's head.

She then thought of the young stepmother her "cheap" father had married and asked with wide eyes, "Uncle, do you think An Hui has any problems?"

An Hui had appeared around the same time as that "jasmine." Could she be a problem too?

Shen Jingshan laughed. "Who knows? Why don't you go ask your father?" Of course, he was joking. He had checked An Hui's background, and it was clean. But then he remembered that the "jasmine" had also had a clean background before she was exposed, and the smile on his lips faded.

Shen Zhizhen also found it amusing and said casually, "Whether there's a problem or not, we have to act as if there isn't, otherwise we'll be the next Wan family."

She had listened to the tape on the recorder that afternoon. It contained the complete conversation between Tanaka Fumiya and Colonel Nakajima. The parts involving code-breaking were clear, and the sound of tapping on the table was distinct. Based on the clarity of the vibration frequency, the bug was likely hidden under the table.

Judging by yesterday's developments, it was impossible for Tanaka Fumiya not to have known about the bug. He probably hadn't removed it because he was using it as bait.

When she reached this conclusion, she briefly wondered if the code-breaking part of the tape was fabricated information. After all, knowing someone was recording, who would talk about classified matters? And the fact that Wang Shun had found the codebook—wasn't that too much of a coincidence?

Could this be a fishing operation? If it was, then sending this stuff out might turn into a death warrant. Of course, she couldn't rule out the possibility that Tanaka Fumiya was just arrogant and had overplayed his hand.

Thinking of this, Shen Zhizhen asked, "Uncle, do you know how to send telegrams or decode ciphers?"

Shen Jingshan didn't know why Little Nine was asking this. "No. That requires specialized training. We're tomb robbers; who learns that stuff? Why are you asking?"

Shen Zhizhen thought that made sense. It seemed she would have to find the Red Party; let the professionals handle professional matters. She would just give them a heads-up and trust that they had their own judgment.

"The pawnshop received a radio. I've been studying it for days and haven't figured out how to use it. I thought if you knew, you could teach me, and then we could communicate by telegram in the future."

That radio had been brought in by Damao, a local thief. She heard he’d gotten it from the Japanese, so she’d taken it. As for whether she’d get caught, well, let them try to find it. If they dared to report her, she’d bite back. Mostly, she’d taken it because she had saved Damao once and knew the kid wouldn't harm her.

Shen Jingshan was speechless at his niece. Why did she collect everything? Wasn't she afraid of being investigated? He glanced out the window, saw that it was already dark, picked up his coat, and stood up. "I'm going to draw them away. Help me take down the telescope in the attic later, then leave. Follow your father's arrangements. The Shen family has your second uncle; don't worry." He put on his coat and walked out. Since they had been talking in the dark, there was no need to turn off the lights.

Shen Zhizhen looked at her uncle and asked, "So you're not coming back?"

"Not coming back. It's not safe here. I'm going to find another place." He needed to find a lively spot to maintain his cover.

Shen Zhizhen watched her uncle leave with a smile in her eyes. Once she heard the lock click, she flopped onto the sofa. If he wasn't coming back, she wasn't leaving either. She would wait until midnight to visit the warehouse, cause some trouble for the Japanese army, and incidentally clear her "cheap" uncle of suspicion. As for the telescope, it was hers now. Oh, and she’d take the tape recorder too.

Shen Jingshan didn't know his niece was about to ransack the Japanese warehouse. After stepping out, he hailed a rickshaw and headed toward the Daxian Nightclub, with the tails behind him following as expected.

Shen Zhizhen slept for a while and didn't open her eyes until the early hours. She got up, stretched her body, put on her coat, and walked to the desk to put the tape recorder into her space. Then she went up to the attic. Looking through the telescope, she saw that there were clearly fewer guards on duty.

Well, it was thirty degrees below zero; standing outside all night would freeze anyone to death. After observing for half an hour and confirming the shift change times, she put away the telescope and left the house.

A black figure merged into the night, gradually approaching the East Station warehouse during the shift change. The figure dodged the searchlights and patrols to reach the warehouse's back door.

Shen Zhizhen took two lock-picking needles from her pocket, inserted them into the keyhole, and twisted them back and forth. With a click, the lock opened. She pushed the door open gently and closed it behind her.

She took a flashlight from her space and shone it around. Oh my, more than half the warehouse was packed.

Taking everything was impossible. This was the largest warehouse in all of Shenyang, and its area was several times larger than her space. Also, she didn't want to cause any "supernatural" events.

Possessing a treasure is a sin; the existence of her space must never be exposed. So she had to be cautious. She planned to set a fire after taking some things. She had a few barrels of gasoline in her space; she would use them later. Chapter 15: Encounter

Although there were many goods in the warehouse, the packaging for each type was different, so she only needed to open one of each to confirm what it was.

Shen Zhizhen took a crowbar from her space and pried open the box nearest to her. Seeing it contained weapons, her eyes lit up. She held the flashlight in her mouth, picked up the crowbar, and opened several more boxes with different patterns nearby.

She took two crates each of pistols, submachine guns, rifles, sniper rifles, and mortars, and cleared out all the ammunition, including grenades, landmines, and explosives.

Shen Zhizhen's heart raced. She felt she had already stepped onto a different path and could never go back. The old her would never have done such a thing.

When Shen Zhizhen opened a batch of cultural relics, her anger flared up. Over a hundred crates of relics—how many tombs must they have dug? If she hadn't come today, wouldn't all these relics have been shipped to Japan? She reminded herself that when facing robbers, she must learn from the original owner of this body. She wouldn't set that fire; she would use the original owner's methods instead.

Well, mainly, she thought that if she set the fire now, it might affect the train heading to Heilongjiang in the morning. If the train didn't leave, how would she hitch a ride? And if she didn't hitch a ride, how would she save people?

She was gambling on the time difference between the departures of two trains: the one to Heilongjiang departed at 7:00 AM, while the one to Dalian departed at 2:00 PM. The Japanese were meticulous; they would certainly ensure the train transporting the prisoners had departed before they began loading the afternoon train. Therefore, to erase her tracks, she had to act in the style of the original owner of this body.

Shen Zhizhen secured the crates containing the artifacts and subsequently discovered another batch containing traditional Chinese medicinal herbs and imported Western medicine.

Medicinal herbs and Western medicine were valuable commodities, so she naturally took them all. She took half of the grain, cotton, and other supplies—mainly because the space in her dimension was limited and couldn't hold everything—and for items like tea, she picked only the best.

After finishing her work, her forehead was beaded with sweat. She raised her arm to wipe it away and began the next task.

Shen Zhizhen buried a dozen explosive packs among the remaining cargo in the warehouse. She then rigged long wires to the front and back doors, tying one end to the door and the other through the cargo crate's latch, connecting it to the pull-ring of a hand grenade.

This way, as soon as the doors were opened, the force would pull the grenade pins, detonating them. The fire would then ignite the explosive packs. With over a dozen packs exploding in succession, the entire warehouse would be razed to the ground. It would be even better if it took a few more Japanese soldiers with it.

To be absolutely certain, she poured gasoline over the cargo near the grenades and explosive packs, ensuring a fire would break out. The thought that she was about to start killing made her heart pound with tension.

Shen Zhizhen took a grappling hook out of her dimension, threw it with force, and it successfully caught on the angle iron near the warehouse skylight. She then climbed up the rope, exited through the skylight, and specifically circled back to the rear door to lock it. Only after doing all this did she quickly leave the scene and hide in the train car bound for Heilongjiang.

As the sky began to brighten, a convoy of military trucks drove into the East Station and stopped near the Heilongjiang-bound train. With a loud clang, the iron doors of the train were opened by the Japanese guards stationed there. The prisoners were herded off the trucks and into the cars. Once the headcount was finished, the doors were closed and locked.

The floor of the car was covered in straw, but it was still unbearably cold; everyone could only huddle together for warmth.

*Woo...* The whistle blew, and the train started moving. *Clang-clang, clang-clang,* accompanied by the vibration of the carriage against the tracks, cold wind whistled into the car as the train picked up speed.

Shen Zhizhen lay in a pile of straw in the corner of the car, covering herself with a layer of straw to hide. Fortunately, it was dark enough in the car that she wouldn't be exposed as long as no one came near.

She had originally wanted to hide in the passenger cars at the front, which were warmer, but after arriving, she discovered that this train only had nine cars. The first four were a passenger car, a sleeper car, a dining car, and a supply car. The rear five cars were boxcars, and they were empty, filled with straw by the Japanese soldiers.

She understood immediately: the Japanese intended to put the prisoners in the boxcars and, worried they would freeze to death, had provided plenty of straw.

Shen Zhizhen immediately had an idea. Taking advantage of the Japanese soldiers' distraction, she quietly climbed onto the roof of the train and slipped inside by opening the lock on the roof vent.

Her heart, which had been in her throat, finally settled once the train started moving. *Heh heh*, as long as the train was moving, it wouldn't matter even if it exploded now.

Of course, she now understood why the Japanese were comfortable putting the prisoners in the last five cars. Everyone was in handcuffs and shackles, locked inside a sealed carriage; it would be a miracle if they didn't freeze to death on the way. With no one to rescue them, they were effectively trapped.

The train rattled along at a steady speed. Shen Zhizhen boredly calculated the time; she planned to make her move after midnight, when people were most drowsy. She would only need to climb out of the roof vent, pull the coupling pin connecting the last five cars, and by the time the Japanese realized something was wrong, they would be long gone.

Suddenly, a familiar name reached her ears. Shen Zhizhen immediately pricked up her ears to listen.

"Uncle Mancang, will my eldest brother really betray the organization?" Wang Li asked the middle-aged man beside him in a low voice.

The events of the past few days had nearly shattered his faith. Now, everyone was suspecting that his eldest brother had betrayed the organization.

He Mancang looked at Wang Li, wanting to say something but hesitating, and finally shook his head to signal him not to overthink it.

The liaison station in Shenyang had been precisely wiped out; someone must have betrayed the organization. As for whether that person was Wang Shun, Zhang Zhitong, or someone else, there was no way to know.

Moreover, the Japanese were acting very strangely this time. Logically, with so many Red Party members captured, they should be used as bait to lure out others. But for some reason, after two interrogations, they stopped, and today they were thrown onto this train.

Some said they were being sent to Heilongjiang to mine coal. He felt something was wrong with that—didn't Heilongjiang have its own people to mine coal? Why transport people across provinces?

This doubt was not unique to He Mancang; others had it too, and some were already whispering about it with those nearby.

Wu De watched these Red Party members guessing back and forth without hitting the mark and let out a scoff. "Stop guessing. We are being sent to Heilongjiang for human experimentation."

Silence fell over the carriage at these words. He Mancang frowned and looked at the young man who had spoken. "Comrade, how do you know this?"

It was the first time Wu De had been called "comrade." He chuckled, looked at his legs which were already festering with pus, and thought, *I'm going to die anyway; might as well say something kind and hope for a better life in the next one.*

"My name is Wu De, and I'm a grave robber. I’ve spent years traveling throughout the Three Eastern Provinces, naturally looking for tombs. Last year, while searching for tombs in the deep mountains of Heilongjiang, I accidentally discovered a cave guarded by Japanese soldiers. I thought there must be something good inside—why else would the Japanese come to such a remote wilderness? So, I laid low nearby, waiting for an opportunity."

*Heh heh*, grave robbing was for money, and with wealth right there, he naturally had to scheme a little. He didn't expect that after waiting for three days, three trucks would arrive.

"The people who got off the trucks were all wearing prison uniforms. They were taken into the cave, and later, the Japanese soldiers would occasionally carry out things wrapped in sealed bags..."

chapters.title: Treating the Wound
chapters.content:
"I followed them out of curiosity and saw the Japanese soldiers throw the sealed bags into a deep pit. When they left, I went over to take a look." Thinking of that scene, Wu De still felt nauseous. Only then did he understand why the Japanese soldiers there were all bundled up so tightly.

"What was it?" Wang Li, listening intently, asked hurriedly when the man paused.

"I opened it and saw they were corpses. The way they died was extremely cruel—some had their limbs severed, some had their extremities rotting, some had burn marks all over their bodies, and others were oozing pus and emitting a foul stench."

He had been so scared he ran away immediately. After returning to Bincheng and asking around among his brothers who were puppet soldiers, he learned that every dozen days or so, the Japanese would take away a group of people from the prison there. He didn't know where they went, but they never came back.

A bitter smile appeared on the corner of Wu De's mouth. He had finally managed to escape, only to be schemed into prison, and now that he was on a train to Heilongjiang, how could he not understand what was going on?

Wu De's words were like a funeral bell ringing in everyone's hearts. Everyone fell silent after hearing them. The Red Party members felt even more conflicted; they had obtained such important intelligence, but there was no way to get it out.

When Shen Zhizhen heard the name "Wu De," she found it familiar. She rummaged through the original owner's memories and finally remembered who this person was: "Flying Leg" Wu De, the original owner's young cousin!

The original owner's uncle—Wu De's father—had been one of Shen Tingshan's tomb-raiding crew, skilled in geomancy and very adept at finding tombs.

Three years ago, this uncle and Fifth Uncle Shen had perished in a large tomb. Wu De, who was only 16 at the time, relied on the skills he learned from his father to start making a living on the Guandong road. Over three years, he had made a name for himself, and because he knew a divine footwork technique, people nicknamed him "Flying Leg Wu De."

Shen Zhizhen had already noticed that Wu De's leg was injured, and it looked quite serious. She had to save him. With that in mind, she took a medical kit out of her dimension, filled it with plenty of gauze and medicine until it was full, and then stopped. After a moment's thought, she also took out a travel bag and packed some essentials inside. Everything was done under the straw, so she didn't worry about being discovered.

Worried that if she waited too long, Wu De might lose his life, she didn't care about being exposed and stood up, brushing the straw off her body.

*Heh*, so what if she was exposed? In this sealed carriage, she was the one in charge.

The movement in the corner immediately drew the attention of everyone in the carriage. Through the light filtering in from the gaps, they saw a person standing there and were all taken aback—how had they not noticed someone there?

When they saw that the person was not only wearing a thick fur coat but also had free movement of their hands and feet, they immediately realized this person was not a prisoner.

Shen Zhizhen picked up the backpack and medical kit and smiled at the people present. "I was just hiding there to catch a free ride. I didn't expect to run into all of you, heh."

After saying this, she walked toward Wu De, not caring whether they believed her far-fetched story. She would let them go in the middle of the night anyway, and for now, she didn't want to cause unnecessary trouble.

The crowd was stunned, then exchanged bitter smiles. They didn't really doubt her words—why else would someone hide there if not to catch a ride? They thought this, but their eyes remained fixed on her.

Shen Zhizhen walked up to Wu De. Although she could see his condition, she didn't want to invite speculation, so she took a flashlight out of her pocket and shone it on his face. *Tsk tsk*, his little face was quite handsome, much more mature than the naive boy in the original owner's memories.

Wu De squinted, trying to see who the person was through the flashlight's beam, but the person was bundled up tightly. He only felt that those eyes had a sense of familiarity.

He immediately felt that this person must know him. When he saw her kneel down to clean his wound, he was even more certain of this. He understood the rules of the road; since the other party didn't speak, she naturally didn't want to reveal too much information, so he chose to remain silent as well.

But the joy that welled up in his heart was enough to mask even the pain in his leg. He was saved.

Shen Zhizhen used a dagger to cut open Wu De's pants, first cleaned the wound, then disinfected it and used the dagger to trim away the necrotic flesh. *Tsk tsk*, this kid was lucky to have lived long enough to meet her.

Her hands were swift and skillful as she cleaned the wound, applied medicine, and bandaged it in one go. She even fed him two aspirin tablets. Finally, fearing the kid would freeze to death, she dragged him to the corner where she had just been—it was clean there—and took off her overcoat to cover him.

She was wearing a lambskin vest underneath, which was much warmer than what these prisoners were wearing, so she wasn't cold at all.

Wu De looked at the fur coat covering him, his confusion deepening. From the way she had dragged him over by his collar just now, she definitely wasn't some gentle, soft-hearted person, yet she had taken off her fur coat to cover him. Why would she take such care of him?

Wu De frowned, struggling to think of who had those familiar eyes. He ended up thinking of his uncle-in-law and almost laughed at himself—his uncle-in-law wasn't this young. Suddenly, a flash of inspiration hit him, and his eyes widened. *No way, it couldn't be her. How could the young mistress of the Shen family be here?*

Wu De's thoughts were written all over his face. Shen Zhizhen understood that her young cousin had guessed it; now, he was likely just waiting for confirmation.

Shen Zhizhen ignored him and turned to look at the silent group. There were many Red Party members among them, so she smiled and said, "I have medicine here, and I can give it to you. But you must promise that if we encounter Japanese troops stopping the train for inspection, you won't sell me out. Can you do that?"

The Japanese troops were using a special train to transport this group; they wouldn't let them starve to death, so they would certainly provide food when the train stopped. That was why she said this—courtesy first, then force. Of course, her main intention was to provide medicine to the Red Party side.

Seeing that no one objected, Shen Zhizhen distributed the medicine to those in need and even helped treat the wounds of several severely injured Red Party members. Only after finishing this did she go back and sit down.

Wu De said, "Human hearts are unpredictable. When people know they are facing a dead end, they will certainly struggle for a chance to live."

He had already pointed out the path ahead for everyone. There were surely people among them with ulterior motives; after all, it is human nature to look out for oneself. He could understand this, which was why he offered the warning.

Since his father died, he hadn't seen Shen Jiu, but based on his previous impression of Shen Jiu, this style of acting didn't match. Could he have guessed wrong?

"In the face of absolute strength, petty tricks are useless," Shen Zhizhen replied indifferently.

Upon hearing this, Wu De was overjoyed. This was Shen Jiu's style. He wanted to speak up to confirm it, but the words died on his lips. He couldn't expose Shen Jiu's identity. A smile curled at the corners of his mouth; he would wait for a suitable time to ask.

Wu De didn't know if it was because he had confirmed that this person was his little cousin, but knowing she wouldn't leave him behind, the tension he had been holding onto finally snapped, and drowsiness washed over him until he fell asleep without realizing it.

Shen Zhizhen glanced at him. This kid was also a tough character; he hadn't made a sound while she was removing the necrotic tissue. She raised her wrist to check the time on her watch... Chapter 17: Which Wicked Bastard Did This?

Inside Shenyang City, at nine in the morning, a series of explosions boomed, shocking the entire downtown area. People thought a war had broken out and scrambled toward air-raid shelters.

Shen Jingshan was currently undergoing a test by Colonel Nakajima and Tanaka Fumiya. Tanaka Fumiya had proposed a sparring match in the spirit of "making friends through martial arts." Shen Jingshan knew the other party wanted to probe his bottom line and force him to use the footwork he had employed while escaping the previous night.

Unfortunately, Tanaka Fumiya was destined to be disappointed. The footwork he used on the streets was a different set. The Shen family's ancestral footwork was known only to the Shen family; others wouldn't know it was unique to them.

Thus, he used a different set of footwork combined with his moves to engage Tanaka Fumiya. He didn't know if he had fooled Tanaka, but he was certain that the other party had no evidence to prove that the person from that night was him. Without evidence, they could only remain suspicious.

Shen Jingshan also wanted to probe Tanaka Fumiya's strength. And so, the two began a fierce exchange. The moves they unleashed gradually contained hidden killing intent and became increasingly sharp. Neither side used their full strength, intending only to test the other's capabilities.

Colonel Nakajima watched with great interest; such exchanges between experts were rare. He had already had someone investigate Shen Jingshan's itinerary the previous night. Shen Jingshan had stayed at the Red Mansion, and the commotion that night had been loud enough for the guests next door to hear clearly. Therefore, in his mind, Shen Jingshan was no longer a suspect.

Tanaka-kun was suspicious by nature and insisted on testing him. He believed that after today's match, he should be able to let go of his doubts.

Suddenly, a series of explosions rang out. Shen Jingshan and Tanaka Fumiya tacitly stopped at the same time. The three stood by the window and looked toward the direction of the explosions, seeing that it was the East Station.

Colonel Nakajima's face darkened. "Baka!" he shouted, rushing out.

Tanaka Fumiya and Shen Jingshan followed. After the three got into a car, they headed straight for the East Station warehouse.

The East Station was already in chaos. The fire was soaring and uncontrollable, and the thick smoke was enough to make people's throats ache.

Shen Jingshan looked at the tragic state of the East Station and couldn't help but sigh. The main warehouse had been razed to the ground, and the surrounding warehouses were all affected by the spreading fire. By the time the fire was extinguished, the contents would likely be burned to nothing. Not far away, Japanese wounded and corpses were being carried out from time to time.

He felt puzzled as to why the casualties were so heavy. He pricked up his ears to listen to the East Station master reporting the situation to Colonel Nakajima, and only then did his confusion clear.

He didn't know which wicked bastard had done this, but they had actually used the tension of opening the door to detonate hand grenades, and used the fire from the grenades to detonate explosive packs!

Because they were preparing for loading at the time, two squads of Japanese troops had arrived. The explosion caused by the grenades didn't cause casualties because it was near the cargo. The casualties occurred because, seeing the fire, the Japanese soldiers rushed in to put it out. At that moment, over a dozen explosive packs detonated almost simultaneously. The two squads of Japanese soldiers inside the warehouse were wiped out, and those who were injured were hit by the sheer force of the blast, which affected everyone outside the warehouse as well.

He had been counting on the supplies in the warehouse, but now they had all been sent to the King of Hell. He thought about finding a chance to send a message later to tell them to retreat; the train bound for Dalian today was definitely not going to depart!

After hearing the station master's report, Colonel Nakajima raised his hand and slapped the station master across the face.

Outrageous! To cause such serious losses and then tell him he didn't know which side had done it.

Shen Zhizhen didn't know that her "cheap" second uncle was also eyeing the warehouse supplies and cursing her as a wicked bastard. She also didn't know that by using the original body's methods to destroy the entire East Station warehouse, she had wiped out two squads of Japanese troops and caused incalculable losses to the Japanese.

The train rattled along and stopped at a station in the afternoon.

Shen Zhizhen took out two hand grenades and smiled at the people in the carriage: "Everyone, allow me to remind you again. If anyone dares to sell me out later, I will send everyone on their way. So, please keep an eye on each other. If you notice any suspicious movement from those around you, please stop it in time."

After saying this, Shen Zhizhen covered herself and Wu De with straw. *Sigh*, she had done her best. She hoped no one would be ungrateful and ruin her efforts; otherwise, she would have to run away with her little cousin.

Although she thought this, she was still prepared. She took a handful of steel balls from her space and put them in her pocket, ready to hit anyone who acted suspiciously.

Whether the people in the carriage were intimidated by her two grenades or everyone was a person of their word, when the Japanese soldiers opened the door and threw two bags of steamed buns into the carriage, no one made any move.

The Japanese soldier glanced casually, locked the door, and went to the next carriage.

Shen Zhizhen put away the steel balls in her hand, a smile curling at the corners of her mouth. She was inexplicably happy; the people she saved were worth it. Very good.

In the early morning, Shen Zhizhen checked her watch. Seeing that the time was right, she got up and walked over to unlock the handcuffs and leg shackles of Uncle Mancang.

He Mancang looked at this mysterious young person in surprise. "This is?"

As she unlocked the shackles, Shen Zhizhen said, "I'm going out in a moment to uncouple the last five carriages of the train. Once the carriages stop, I'll open the doors, and everyone can run for their lives."

This statement left the people in the carriage incredibly excited. Those who had harbored ulterior motives secretly rejoiced that they hadn't acted impulsively—though they were mainly threatened by the grenades. Regardless, any chance to escape was a good one.

After Shen Zhizhen unlocked everyone's handcuffs and shackles, she asked Uncle Mancang to help look after Wu De. Once he agreed, she jumped up to the top of the carriage, pushed open the ventilation hatch, and climbed out. The howling north wind almost blew her hat off; she quickly held onto it with one hand and braved the wind to reach the supply carriage.

Yes, she had changed her mind. She decided to uncouple the supply carriage. When she was unlocking everyone earlier, she saw that these prisoners were wearing thin clothes. In such cold weather, she worried they wouldn't get far in the wilderness before freezing to death. Even if they didn't freeze, if they didn't encounter a village in a day or two, they would easily starve.

Shen Zhizhen peeked and saw no one on guard, realizing they were probably slacking off and sleeping in the cold. She jumped down and uncoupled the carriage. With a *clack*, the carriage quickly separated from the front of the train.

Shen Zhizhen waved at the front of the train. "Bye-bye." By the time the Japanese troops discovered it and came back, they would be long gone.

The people in the carriage clearly felt the speed of the carriage slowing down. Those who knew the truth were overjoyed—it had succeeded. Those who didn't just thought the train was stopping again.

When the carriage came to a halt, Shen Zhizhen opened the door of the carriage she had been in and said to everyone inside, "The carriage at the very front is the supply carriage. Comrade Mancang, please organize the distribution of items to everyone."

He Mancang excitedly agreed. Most of the people in this carriage were their comrades, so it was easy to organize. Everyone orderly went to the front carriage, each taking a Japanese cotton-padded coat to wear. Once they were warm, they began distributing canned food, biscuits, and other supplies. Those who weren't their people left as soon as they got their items, fearing that if they stayed too long, they would be captured and taken back for human experimentation—the thought alone was terrifying.

Just like that, the people from one carriage finished and left, and the people from another carriage came. By the time everyone had left, the supply carriage was also... Chapter 18: Fulfilling the Promise

After Shen Zhizhen unlocked everyone and let them go, she also took a cotton-padded coat. She returned to the carriage she had been staying in, put the fur coat on her little cousin, and wrapped his legs and feet with cotton coats.

She pulled down her mask and smiled: "You kid are lucky to be alive." After saying that, she pulled the mask back up, put him on her back, and walked out.

Wu De's eyes were full of smiles. He had said it, hadn't he? That Wang the Blind's claim that he wouldn't live past twenty was just bullshit. How could he be a short-lived ghost?

He Mancang and the other Red Party members came over to thank her before leaving. The gratitude in everyone's hearts was beyond words; they hadn't expected to be saved. Many of them were old comrades who had been captured, and this time they had truly turned a misfortune into a blessing.

Shen Zhizhen confirmed that the other party was indeed Uncle Mancang from He's Noodle Shop, then took the codebook and cassette tape from her pocket and handed them to He Mancang.

"This was given to me at the Yamato Hotel by one of your comrades named Wang Shun. He asked me to take it to He's Noodle Shop at the East Station and give it to Uncle Mancang. I didn't expect that after several twists and turns, we would meet here. I'm handing these two things to you now, so I can consider my promise fulfilled."

After handing over these two things, she felt much lighter. She finally didn't have to carry this responsibility anymore.

Wang Li's tears fell instantly upon hearing this. His big brother hadn't betrayed the organization.

He Mancang took the cassette and codebook with trembling hands. Their comrades were all good comrades; even if organization information had been leaked, it must have been due to the enemy using underhanded tactics.

Shen Zhizhen recounted the situation and her guesses from that day. "I don't know if what I said is correct, but I just wanted to remind you all to be cautious. Alright, let's part ways here."

After saying this, she turned and left with her little cousin on her back. *Sigh*, she really didn't want to see a collective scene of mourning and sadness; it was inexplicably heartbreaking.

Everyone watched their benefactor leave. Those who had once suspected Wang Shun and Zhang Zhitong of betraying the organization felt guilty. Their comrade had already... in order to get the intelligence out.

"Why were you in the carriage?" Wu De asked, unable to contain his curiosity once they were away from the crowd. As for why Shen Jiu went to the Yamato Hotel, he didn't dare to ask. Since it concerned the Red Party, he pretended he hadn't heard anything.

Shen Zhizhen, carrying a person on her back and a travel bag hanging in front, still walked with a light gait. Hearing this, she casually spouted nonsense: "The pawnshop burned down, so I’m unemployed, aren't I? I figured I’d come out to find some work, and then I told your uncle that a daughter’s ambitions lie in the four corners of the world, so I just ran off."

Wu De let out a snort of laughter, amused. His little cousin was quite the storyteller. The two continued to chatter as they walked, finally spotting a village at daybreak.

Shen Zhizhen carried Wu De into the village and stopped at a house at the entrance for an hour, mainly to change the little cousin's dressings and have some hot water to warm up. After inquiring about their location and the surrounding geography, Shen Zhizhen carried Wu De and continued on her way.

Three days later, Shen Zhizhen drove a horse-drawn carriage into the Siping market. Passing by the morning market, she was drawn by the hawking and got off to buy two portions of breakfast. She handed one to her little cousin lying in the carriage, and after dropping the curtain, she took a bite of a hot steamed bun. Her breath mingled with the steam from the bun, making it hard to tell what was hot and what was cold.

After finishing the bun, Shen Zhizhen finally had a moment to speak: "I need to leave for a few days to take care of some business. Are you going to stay at an inn or a hospital?"

Wu De knew that Shen Jiu must have something important to do, otherwise, she wouldn't have come out alone. Since his little cousin didn't say, he didn't feel right asking, and in his condition, he wouldn't be able to help anyway.

Wu De: "Let's go to the hospital." There were people at the hospital to change his dressings, and he could call a nurse if he needed anything. Staying at an inn made it inconvenient even to relieve himself; he had been holding it in for the past few days, terrified that if he accidentally annoyed Shen Jiu, she would stop looking after him.

Shen Zhizhen had no idea that Wu De was holding it in just to avoid embarrassing himself in front of her. "Do you have any acquaintances in Siping? If you do, I'll go notify them." The boy seemed quite familiar with Siping in his speech, so she figured he might know someone.

If her trip went smoothly, she could return in about seven or eight days; if something delayed her, it was hard to say. Having a local around to look after her little cousin would give her some peace of mind.

Wu De only knew "Blind Wang" in Siping, but he didn't want to ask him for help, so he explained the situation to his little cousin.

Shen Zhizhen agreed; a blind man certainly couldn't look after a patient. She drove the carriage to the hospital, used the forged documents she had made to register Wu De, got him into a ward, left him fifty silver dollars, and hired a caregiver before leaving.

After leaving the hospital, Shen Zhizhen found an inn that could store the carriage, washed up, changed her clothes, took a map out of her space to study for a while, and then put it back after memorizing the general route.

Shen Zhizhen paid for ten days of lodging, left the inn, and bought plenty of food before heading out of the city.

Every entrance and exit of the Siping market had checkpoints where puppet troops checked the travel permits of those passing through. She had passed many such checkpoints with her little cousin over the past two days, all using forged documents.

When Shen Zhizhen reached the eastern checkpoint, there was a rare long line. She had no choice but to stand at the back. After waiting for a while without seeing anyone being let through, she curiously pricked up her ears to listen, only to realize that they were waiting for a Japanese military unit to pass before letting anyone else through.

Ten minutes later, the sound of vehicles approached, accompanied by the rhythmic sound of marching boots. The people in line quickly moved to the side of the road. Everyone waited for the Japanese unit to pass before returning to their original positions to continue waiting.

After clearing the checkpoint, Shen Zhizhen took a pair of skis out of her backpack, walked to a slope by the side of the road, put them on, pushed off with her legs, and zoomed away.

Accompanied by the howling, biting north wind, she galloped across the vast, snow-covered expanse, completely blanketed in pristine white.

Shen Zhizhen traveled using her skis whenever there was a slope and ran on her own two legs when there wasn't. Whether by coincidence or not, she managed to maintain a distance, neither too far nor too close, from the Japanese unit she had encountered at the checkpoint.

They maintained this subtle distance all the way until they entered the territory of the Changbai Mountains.

This piqued Shen Zhizhen's curiosity. What kind of mission could this group of Japanese soldiers have in the Changbai Mountains? Surely they weren't planning to target a neighboring country.

Taking advantage of a break, she took out her binoculars to observe the Japanese soldiers camping at the foot of the mountain. She even took the time to pour herself a cup of hot tea, sitting in a tree with a teacup in one hand and binoculars in the other to observe the enemy situation.

There were many scholars in the Japanese camp; they didn't wear military uniforms and some wore glasses, making them easy to identify. She watched for a while but couldn't make sense of it.

Shen Zhizhen decided to focus on her own mission first. Mainly, she knew she couldn't take on a force of several hundred soldiers by herself. She drank her now-lukewarm tea, packed up, climbed down from the tree, and used the Shen family's ancestral movement technique to head into the mountains.

The Shen family treasury was in the Changbai Mountains. It had once been a large tomb, later converted by the Shen ancestors into a place to hide their treasures.

One would think that since the Shen family were tomb robbers themselves, why would they choose a tomb chamber as a treasury? Wouldn't that just be a gift to other tomb robbers?

The Shen ancestors would naturally never do such a foolish thing. They had altered the feng shui layout of the tomb.

chapters.title: Practice
chapters.content:
The Shen ancestors sealed off the original auspicious burial spot, preserved an escape route leading to the cliff, and changed the way the stone door opened. If it wasn't opened correctly, it would trigger a mechanism that dropped ten massive gates to seal it shut.

Shen Zhizhen recited the mantra under her breath: "Qian Heaven seeks the dragon's head, atop the mountain peak lies a strange summit; Li Fire reflects the sunset glow, red clouds by the cliff illuminate the treasure land." She didn't know which ancestor had come up with this mantra, but it was easy to understand.

"Qian Heaven" refers to the Qian trigram in the Bagua, which represents the northwest direction; "Heaven" represents height; the "dragon's head" symbolizes the start or key position of the dragon vein; and the "strange summit" is the coordinate.

Shen Zhizhen looked up. Well, the weather was clear today. She hoped that before she found the coordinate of the strange summit, there wouldn't be any overcast or snowy weather; otherwise, without the sunset glow to locate the entrance, she would have to wait indefinitely.

Shen Zhizhen traveled rapidly, identifying the direction along the way. Her body was covered in a thick layer of frost, but she enjoyed the thrill of extreme skiing.

Two days later, at dusk, Shen Zhizhen finally found the place. Standing on the cliff, she understood why they used the sunset glow to find the entrance: the glow shone through a gap between two mountains diagonally opposite, forming a beam of light that hit the cliff face.

She took a rope out of her space, tied one end to a tree and the other around her waist, then went to the cliff face where the light was shining. She descended slowly along the beam of light, carefully watching for any cave openings.

Shen Zhizhen glanced down and her heart pounded with fear. Oh my, she had really grown up; she was actually daring enough to climb a cliff.

The wind had kept the cliff face relatively clean, without large areas of snow, which was friendly for finding the entrance.

Shen Zhizhen found the entrance in the middle of the cliff face. The opening wasn't large and was blocked by withered vines, with a layer of snow hanging above it. Without the guidance of the light, this place would have been truly hard to find. She pushed aside the vines and crawled in.

Shen Zhizhen brushed the frost and snow off her body while taking out a flashlight to look around. She walked deeper into the cave; there were clear signs of manual excavation on the cave walls. After walking about ten meters, she encountered a three-way fork.

Shen Zhizhen followed the path on the far right, as her father had instructed. Only this path was safe; the other two were said to be filled with traps and were extremely dangerous—if one entered them by mistake, it would be a narrow escape from death!

The traps were naturally not left by the Shen family, but were anti-theft measures built by the tomb's original owner. The Shen ancestors hadn't dismantled or destroyed them, out of a selfish desire to protect their own treasury.

Shen Zhizhen stopped. Directly in front of her was a stone door, carved with a stone dragon, with half of the dragon's body protruding.

Shen Zhizhen took off her gloves and put them in her pocket. She walked over and ran her hand over the dragon scales from top to bottom. Her finger stopped at the forty-ninth scale. She twisted it slightly and removed the scale, revealing a slot.

After confirming this was the right spot, Shen Zhizhen took all the supplies out of her space and placed them on the surrounding open ground. She took the Phoenix Token off the Phoenix Coffin and placed it into the slot. With a firm press, a clicking sound rang out, and the dragon's head extended outward.

The Shen ancestors were truly talented; who would have thought that the key to the mechanism was hidden among these dense dragon scales?

She waited for the dragon's head to stop, then reached out to grasp the two horns, rotating the head to align with the exposed Bagua compass: Dui (7), Zhen (3), Li (9), Xun (4), Gen (8). After rotating the head in this sequence, she heard a click, and the stone door loosened.

Shen Zhizhen pushed the stone door open and walked in. The passage extended downward, and she occasionally used her flashlight to illuminate the surroundings; it was dry inside, not damp at all.

The Shen family's belongings were placed in a spacious area at the end of the passage. On the wall was a sealed tomb door, and on the ground were many boxes of various kinds, none of them large.

She guessed this was for the convenience of entering and transporting them. She squatted down and opened a few boxes, and sure enough, she saw many good things. Besides antiques, there was plenty of gold, jewelry, and jade. Because the storage environment was dry, these antiques were well-preserved.

Shen Zhizhen collected all the Shen family's items into her space. She didn't linger after taking the things; the thought of the ten gates above the passage made it impossible for her to stay there with peace of mind. If they were triggered and fell, wouldn't she be buried alive?

A figure flashed out of the stone door. She reached back to press the dragon head back into place, the stone door closed, and the Phoenix Token popped out of the slot.

Shen Zhizhen put the Phoenix Token back on the Phoenix Coffin, the space instantly expanded, and after collecting the supplies on the ground into her space, she put the scale back in place. She then turned and walked out. When she reached the entrance, she saw that it was already dark and it had started snowing at some point, so she decided to wait until daybreak to leave.

She took bedding out of her space, spread it on a flat spot, took out two hot buns, and poured a cup of hot tea. After eating, the exhaustion from days of travel washed over her, and she crawled into the bedding to sleep.

The next day, as dawn broke, it was still snowing. Shen Zhizhen crawled out of the cave entrance and climbed up, pulling on the rope. This place was too dangerous; if the rope were cut, would she have to free-climb? She secretly decided never to come back again.

A loud boom shook the entire mountain. Shen Zhizhen was so startled she almost let go of the rope. Who the hell was setting off cannons in the mountains? She quickly climbed up, pulled up the rope, and another loud boom followed.

Shen Zhizhen frowned and cautiously walked down the mountain. The sound must be very close to her, otherwise, the tremor wouldn't be so strong. The image of the Japanese unit she had been traveling with flashed through her mind. Was it such a coincidence?

However, besides the Japanese soldiers, who would be bored enough to set off cannons in the deep mountains in the middle of winter? This piqued her curiosity. What exactly was this Japanese unit trying to do?

After descending the mountain, Shen Zhizhen circled to the front, peeked out, and sure enough, it was that Japanese unit. She hid behind a large tree and used her binoculars to observe.

The Japanese soldiers had already set up camp there. The loud noise just now was caused by the Japanese soldiers shelling the mountainside with small mortars. A huge crater had been blasted into the mountain in front, and dozens of Japanese soldiers were digging with entrenching tools while several scholars and officers nearby discussed something.

Seeing this, how could Shen Zhizhen not know what these people were up to? Heh, so they were here to rob a tomb. And I'll be damned, they found it quite accurately. There was indeed a large tomb here, but unfortunately, it had long since been looted, and even the tomb door had been sealed shut by the Shen ancestors.

Shen Zhizhen knew this group of Japanese soldiers was destined to return empty-handed. She put away her binoculars, pulled a few landmines from her space, and decided to teach this team of Japanese grave robbers a lesson before leaving.

She buried the landmines on the only path the Japanese soldiers could take to return, then quickly departed, the falling snow soon erasing her tracks.

Shen Zhizhen did not leave the area but hid in a large tree seven hundred meters away. She figured that sooner or later she would have to kill the Japanese invaders, so she wanted to use this group of soldiers to practice her courage and marksmanship.

She retrieved a sniper rifle from her space—a U.S.-made M40 sniper rifle with an effective range of 800 meters. After loading it, she raised the rifle and took aim.

At this moment, Shen Zhizhen possessed an absolute calmness she didn't usually have. This surprised her slightly; she had expected to feel somewhat nervous or uneasy about killing an enemy with a gun for the first time, but she was terrifyingly calm, as if she were born to hold this rifle and kill enemies!

Shen Zhizhen cleared her mind, locked onto her target, and pulled the trigger. With a "bang," the bullet fired and struck the cliff wall next to the target.

Shen Zhizhen blinked and continued to aim at the same target. Although the Japanese soldiers were in disarray due to the gunshot, they couldn't spot her yet because of the distance.

This time, she summarized her previous experience and slightly adjusted the angle of the scope.

Her finger pulled the trigger, and with another "bang," the bullet flew toward the target. Instantly, the Japanese soldier fell to the ground.

Bang, bang, bang... A series of gunshots echoed in the air.

Shen Zhizhen hit her targets with precision every time, hardly missing a shot. Once the enemy determined her position, she quickly put away the rifle and fled.

chapters.title: The Person is Gone?
chapters.content:
Two days later, Shen Zhizhen returned to the entrance of the mountain. A few military trucks remained where the Japanese soldiers had originally camped.

Shen Zhizhen picked a relatively new truck, used a steel needle to pick the lock, and hot-wired it based on the original owner's memories. After starting the engine, she checked the cargo beds of the other trucks, moved all the fuel drums and food supplies to the truck she had started, tied the curtain at the back of the truck bed with a rope, and after finishing, drained the fuel from the tanks of the other vehicles.

She couldn't help but chuckle after finishing; she was truly going further and further down the path of sabotaging others.

Shen Zhizhen sat in the driver's seat, closed the door with a click, studied the gears on the shift lever, pressed the clutch, shifted into gear, and drove the truck away.

This was a mountainous area with no nearby villages. In the freezing cold, the hunters were all staying home for the winter; let alone in the mountains, even in the villages, you rarely saw anyone during the day unless they were the type who liked to visit neighbors.

As for those Japanese soldiers who escaped the landmine explosions and were trying to leave the mountains, well, that would depend on their luck.

Large snowflakes fell in abundance, turning the world into a vast expanse of white. The road had long been covered by accumulated snow, becoming exceptionally slippery and difficult to traverse.

Shen Zhizhen sat in the driver's seat, gripping the steering wheel tightly, her eyes focused on the road ahead. While driving cautiously, she pondered the fate of the supplies in her space.

The quantity of these supplies was significant, but due to their special origin, they could not be brought out openly.

A large-scale appearance of items from her space would certainly attract the attention of the Japanese military, and once her identity was exposed, it would inevitably implicate the Shen family.

When her gaze inadvertently fell upon a village by the roadside, she subconsciously stepped on the brake...

Shen Zhizhen drove the truck toward the direction of Siping Street. Whenever she encountered a village, she would stop the car and quietly enter, placing a bag of grain in each courtyard. For the impoverished families living in particularly dilapidated houses, she would leave some cotton or cloth.

This was the method she devised to clear out her space. Those supplies were originally looted from the people by the Japanese, so there was nothing wrong with her returning them to the people.

The farmers who received the grain saw the extra bag in their courtyards, but no one dared to speak of it. Everyone in their hearts felt it was sent by the Anti-Japanese United Army comrades, and each felt deeply grateful.

Shen Zhizhen discovered that the checkpoints were even stricter than when she had arrived. When passing the first checkpoint, she used the Japanese military pass she had found in the truck and fished for information, only to realize that everything was related to her.

Due to the explosion at the Shenyang East Station and the hijacking of the prisoner train in Heilongjiang, the Japanese military stationed in the Northeast was furious and ordered a strict investigation. Now, not only were all checkpoints conducting rigorous inspections, but even the villages outside the city were being searched by the Japanese military at irregular intervals.

Once Shen Zhizhen heard it was related to her, she became much more cautious.
