Before reaching each checkpoint, she would store the truck in her space in advance, and after slipping past the checkpoint to an uninhabited area, she would take it out and continue driving. She was also much more careful when delivering grain and supplies to villages, focusing on ensuring no one noticed she had been there.

Late at night, Wu De lay in his hospital bed, feeling increasingly uneasy. During the day, when he had the caregiver push him to the restroom, he saw two newly admitted patients near the stairwell. He recognized them at a glance as former cellmates; they had lived in the same cell and even taken the same train to Heilongjiang.

Worried about being recognized, Wu De immediately covered his face. It was a joke—everyone was a fugitive now; there was no room for reunions. He waited until the two men followed the nurse into their ward before having the caregiver push him back to his own room.

He had thought that since he was in a private room, he wouldn't run into them if he stayed inside. Who would have thought that trouble would strike in the afternoon? A team of Japanese soldiers suddenly arrived at the hospital to conduct a search, and those two men were taken away by the soldiers that afternoon.

Later, he learned from the caregiver that the Japanese military had recently intensified their search efforts, conducting a carpet search of the entire city. Only then did Wu De understand why those two men had hidden in the hospital.

Although he had used the forged documents provided by his little cousin to pass the afternoon inspection, a fake was a fake, and he felt quite insecure.

After much deliberation, Wu De felt this hospital was no place to stay. He put on his clothes, leaned against the bed to sit in his wheelchair, turned the wheels to the window, and left a mark for his little cousin in an inconspicuous spot. Then, he picked up his belongings, went to the door, and quietly opened a crack...

On the ninth day, Shen Zhizhen returned to Siping Street. She first went back to the inn to wash up, checked out, and then drove a horse-drawn carriage to the hospital.

"What? He left on his own?" Shen Zhizhen asked the nurse in surprise.

Wu De's legs were injured and he couldn't walk. How did he leave the hospital, and why would he leave?

The nurse nodded and said, "Yes, five days ago when we did our rounds, Mr. Wu was no longer in his room. He didn't return by the afternoon, and all his things were gone. Since you're here, please pay the hospital fees and the cost for the wheelchair."

There were too many people who snuck out to avoid medical expenses in their hospital. That Mr. Wu even took the hospital's wheelchair; it was simply outrageous. Since a family member had come, the medical bills and the wheelchair fee had to be paid.

Shen Zhizhen...

"No, the person disappeared in your hospital. Aside from asking me for money, don't you have an explanation?" Shen Zhizhen was almost amused by anger. This wasn't right.

The nurse, hearing that she wanted to blame the hospital, said, "This kind of thing happens every day in the hospital. What can we do? This is a hospital, not a prison. Can we watch the patients every second? If you want to make a scene, then call the police." Once the police came, everyone would behave.

Shen Zhizhen narrowed her eyes upon hearing this. Threatening her?

Fine, her fake documents really couldn't withstand a thorough investigation. After thinking it over, she followed the nurse to pay the medical bills and the wheelchair fee.

Shen Zhizhen left the hospital and walked to the carriage. Sitting on the carriage seat, she looked at the hospital gate and thought about the nurse's words: patients sneaking out every day to avoid medical fees?

It was possible in such chaotic times, but Wu De wouldn't have left for that reason. Before she left, she had given her little cousin fifty silver dollars; the few days of medical expenses wouldn't have used that up. Furthermore, knowing she would return to pay the bills, how could he leave because of that while injured and having limited mobility?

So, what exactly happened to Wu De that caused him to leave? Thinking of this, her gaze toward the hospital became profound. Should she investigate even if she had left? If there was nothing wrong with the hospital, then he must have encountered some emergency.

Thinking of this, Shen Zhizhen climbed into the carriage, took out two large leather suitcases containing clothes from her space, opened the one with clothes, and took out a black wool coat and a suit. She then opened the shoe box, took out a pair of black leather boots, took off the large fur coat she was wearing, changed into the new outfit, took out a pair of black round sunglasses, put them on, and walked toward the hospital.

She encountered a Japanese military patrol at the entrance and walked into the hospital with a calm expression.

Shen Zhizhen entered the hospital, looked back, and seeing that the patrol had passed, she frowned slightly, wondering if her little cousin's departure from the hospital had anything to do with the sudden search.

Shen Zhizhen slowly stepped onto the stairs to the second floor and arrived at the door of the ward her little cousin had stayed in. She turned her head to check that no one was paying attention and quickly slipped into the room, coming face-to-face with the patient lying on the bed.

"Who are you?" Ueda Yoshinobu asked with a serious expression, his hand reaching under the pillow to draw a gun.

Shen Zhizhen smiled at the patient. A Japanese soldier? Then she wouldn't be polite. She pulled out her pistol and signaled for him not to move.

Ueda Yoshinobu held his gun under the pillow, not daring to move, and watched coldly as the young man in glasses approached. Before he could see the movement clearly, he felt a pain in his neck and fainted.

Shen Zhizhen retracted her hand and began to inspect the room to see if there was any information left by Wu De. Because she wasn't short on money and wanted Wu De to rest well, she had booked a private room for him.

If her little cousin had left on his own, he should have left a signal for her. She searched the room and found a pair of glasses drawn in the corner of the windowsill.

A look of confusion flashed in Shen Zhizhen's eyes. What did it mean? She frowned, thinking about what Wu De had said, and a flash of inspiration hit her: Wang the Blind—

chapters.title: Borrowing His Luck to Change Your Fate
chapters.content:
In a residential house in the south of Siping Street, Wu De lay on the kang, chatting idly with Wang the Blind.

He wondered if his little cousin had returned and if she had seen the mark he left. Thinking about how he had spent two silver dollars to have Xi Ya guard outside the hospital every day, he couldn't help but sigh.

After he snuck out of the hospital that day, he came here. It cost him thirty silver dollars to get Wang the Blind to agree to let him hide here temporarily. When the Japanese soldiers came to search, he and the Blind Man's daughter, Wang Xiya, would hide in the vegetable cellar and come out only after the soldiers had left.

It was just that Wang the Blind inevitably lost some money dealing with the Japanese, but fortunately, he wasn't beaten or anything.

Wang the Blind wasn't actually blind; to be precise, only one eye was blind. His eyeballs, one black and one white, looked creepy. To avoid scaring people, he wore black glasses every time he went out. Over time, everyone forgot his real name and just called him Wang the Blind.

"Uncle Wang, calculate for me again. See if I've passed the hurdle in my life," Wu De asked anxiously. He wouldn't turn twenty until the day after tomorrow, and his heart had been hanging in the balance, always worried about whether he would really not live past twenty.

Those in their line of work all believed in fate, especially since he had almost died this time, which made him believe even more that Wang the Blind's calculations were truly accurate.

Blind Wang was rolling tobacco leaves. Hearing this, he looked up at Wu De and held up two fingers.

Wu De curled his lip, pulled two silver dollars from his pocket, and with a slight flick of his finger, the coins landed in the blind man’s hand with a hum.

Blind Wang had nearly squeezed him dry of every silver dollar he had over the past few days. If his "little cousin" didn't show up soon, Wu De figured he’d be in debt to the old blind man by the time he left.

Although Wu De complained in his heart, he knew that aside from being a bit greedy, the blind man was a decent person; otherwise, he wouldn't have come here to seek refuge.

After pocketing the silver dollars, Blind Wang took out three copper coins, placed them in his palm, and pressed his hands together, muttering, "First look for emptiness, second for clashes, third for punishments, combinations, and the strength of the elements, fourth for the progression or regression of the hexagram, fifth for the presence of malevolent spirits..."

Wu De knew a little about the I Ching. Seeing the blind man begin the divination, he sat up, leaned in, and felt his heart sink as he watched the hexagram take shape.

Blind Wang frowned at the hexagram and said, "The six lines reveal a great calamity, a death sentence looms. The world is in decline, the subject is trapped, and the path is hard to find. Emptiness, clashes, punishments, and combinations all signal a reversal of fortune. The White Tiger’s malevolent light shrouds the sun in darkness. Yet, a single thread of hope remains; the light of the 'useful god' pierces the dark clouds. Reversals and repetitions hide a turning point; guard against disaster and wait for the time to change."

Upon hearing the reading, Wu De felt as if he had fallen into an ice cellar. He was well-versed in geomancy himself; he didn't need Blind Wang to explain the meaning. It was precisely because he understood it that he knew the danger.

A death sentence had arrived, and he was trapped. All the unfavorable omens—emptiness, clashes, punishments—had appeared. The White Tiger, a symbol of disaster, cast its baleful light like dark clouds blocking the sun, leaving no room to escape.

After finishing the reading, Blind Wang looked up to see Wu De’s grim expression and offered some comfort: "Though a death sentence looms, there is, after all, a single thread of hope."

The last time he had divined for this kid, it was a guaranteed death trap. He hadn't expected the hexagram to change this time. Although it was still a hexagram of great calamity, the appearance of that single thread of hope meant it was still possible for Wu De to escape his fate.

Wu De nodded, slightly panicked. "Right, a turning point. It indicates that despite the great calamity, there is still a glimmer of hope. Uncle Wang, calculate it for me—what exactly is this glimmer of hope?"

"Calculate what? Didn't the hexagram say it? Guard against disaster and wait for the right moment to welcome a new turning point." From the hexagram, the turning point would appear when the time was right.

Wu De slumped backward with a thud and replied, unwilling to accept it, "What if it never comes?" Just waiting around doing nothing felt like waiting for death.

Blind Wang ignored him, put away the copper coins, and went back to rolling tobacco, his black and white eyes flickering as he pondered the matter of Xi Ya.

Wu De asked, "Uncle Wang, help me analyze what this turning point might be." As he spoke, he pulled a silver dollar from his pocket and tossed it into the tobacco basket.

Blind Wang reached out, picked up the silver dollar, and tossed it back without a word, continuing to roll his tobacco and think.

This place was becoming increasingly unstable. The Japanese army was arresting people from time to time, and he worried about when it would be his and his daughter's turn. Because their profession had a taboo—that one could divine for others but not for oneself, or else disaster would follow—he had divined for his daughter a few days ago. It showed that they shouldn't stay here long, but to leave, they would need the help of a noble person to get out safely.

After getting that result, he had gone to his senior brother, worried, and asked him to divine for both himself and Xi Ya, but they had received opposite results.

Xi Ya had to leave, or disaster would strike, and to leave safely, she needed the help of a noble person. But his own hexagram was the exact opposite: if he left this place, he would meet with a violent death.

When Wu De had first shown up, he thought this kid might be Xi Ya's noble person. Later, he divined again and realized it wasn't him, but the clues to the noble person were related to him. Now, combined with the recent hexagram, it was highly likely that Wu De’s "glimmer of hope" was the same noble person who would help Xi Ya leave safely.

Wu De fiddled with the silver dollar in his hand, squinting at Blind Wang. What was the meaning of this? Was he not taking money anymore, or did he think it was too little?

"Uncle Wang, let's be direct. There's no need for us to play guessing games."

Blind Wang looked up and said, "Dezi, I have a favor to ask of you."

"Uncle Wang, just say it. As long as it's within my power, I will definitely do it for you." Even though Blind Wang had charged him thirty silver dollars, he appreciated that the man had helped him during his time of need.

If Blind Wang hadn't taken him in, he could only imagine what would have happened if the Japanese had caught him.

Blind Wang told him about the hexagrams his senior brother had cast for him and Xi Ya. "I want you to take Xi Ya away from here."

Hearing this, Wu De agreed immediately. "Don't worry, Uncle Wang. From now on, Xi Ya is my sister. As long as I'm alive, I won't let anything happen to her."

Wu De was happy. Since Blind Wang was willing to entrust Xi Ya to him, it meant he had already glimpsed what that "glimmer of hope" was.

Blind Wang felt much more at ease after receiving the promise. Seeing the kid waiting eagerly for an explanation, he couldn't help but smile. "Whoever broke your death trap is that glimmer of hope."

Wu De was stunned for a moment, then burst into laughter. He had been blinded by his own situation. It was his "little cousin" who had saved his life—wasn't Shen Jiu that glimmer of hope?

Seeing that Wu De understood, Blind Wang warned, "Your fate is full of hardships. If you want to change it, you must stay by that noble person's side and use their fortune to alter your own."

Wu De nodded, indicating he understood. He decided he would cling to his little cousin for the rest of his life—no, wait, he would work like a horse or an ox to repay her for saving his life.

chapters.title: Are people in the 1940s all this open-minded?
chapters.content:
Shen Zhizhen sneezed twice as she walked out of the hospital. She rubbed her nose, a hint of confusion in her eyes. It stood to reason that her constitution shouldn't be catching a cold, so why was she sneezing for no reason? She glanced back, walked to the carriage, and sat on the carriage step, smiling at the chubby girl approaching.

That chubby girl had appeared while she was talking to the nurse, and she had seen her again when she went to the ward. Now, following her out, it was obvious she was looking for her.

Shen Zhizhen sized up the girl walking toward her. She was about the same height, with a sturdy, rounded build and delicate features—a pleasant-looking chubby girl.

"Is there something you need, miss?" Shen Zhizhen asked as the girl approached.

Wang Xiya thought this sister was truly beautiful. After changing her clothes, her entire temperament had changed. Oh my, being stared at by her made her little heart thump.

"Sister, do you know Dezi-ge's little cousin?" Wang Xiya asked, blinking her large eyes.

In fact, she was already almost certain, because she had overheard the sister's conversation with the nurse, and later saw her go to the ward Dezi-ge had mentioned. She felt it was nine out of ten that this person was indeed Dezi-ge's little cousin.

Shen Zhizhen realized this was someone Wu De had sent to wait for her. She smiled and said, "I do. What is your name, miss? Could you take me to see my little cousin?"

Seeing that the code matched, Wang Xiya hurriedly said, "My name is Wang Xiya. Dezi-ge is staying at my house now. I'll take you to him."

Shen Zhizhen didn't know she had accidentally matched her little cousin's secret code. She had only said that to go along with what Xiya said; she truly hadn't expected Wu De to use "little cousin" as a code for recognition!

Shen Zhizhen let Xiya get into the carriage. She drove as Xiya directed, and the girl’s constant chatter along the way let her learn quite a bit about the connection between Wu De and the Wang family.

The further south they went, the fewer pedestrians were on the street. The desolation stirred Wang Xiya's desire to confide.

"This street used to be very lively. Ever since the little Japanese devils came, it's been getting quieter and quieter." The Japanese army burned, killed, and looted, committing every evil, so people stopped coming out for the sake of safety.

Shen Zhizhen turned to look at the disappointed little girl. "This street will be lively again. One day, the invaders will be driven out."

"Will there really be such a day?" A hint of confusion flickered in Wang Xiya's eyes.

Shen Zhizhen said with absolute certainty, "As long as we endure the darkness before the dawn, the light of victory will surely come."

Wang Xiya didn't know why, but she just felt that what the sister said would definitely come true. The confusion in her eyes was replaced by starlight; she would definitely be able to wait for it.

The carriage stopped in front of the Wang house. Wang Xiya hopped down nimbly and opened the gate so the sister could drive the carriage into the courtyard.

Although the Wang family's courtyard wasn't large, it had the advantage of high walls. Once the gate was closed, it could completely block the view from the outside.

The two people inside had noticed when there was movement in the courtyard. Wu De was lying by the window, and seeing it was indeed his little cousin, he couldn't help but give Blind Wang a thumbs-up. Blind Wang’s calculation was too accurate—it really was just a matter of waiting for the turning point to appear. He knew that whether he could grasp this glimmer of hope depended on today.

Wu De knew that once Shen Jiu finished her business, she would leave the Northeast. He looked at his injured leg; if he couldn't get his little cousin to agree to take him with her today, Shen Jiu would surely dump him on his uncle.

Wu De’s eyes rolled, and a plan formed. As soon as his little cousin entered the room, he began to wail and carry on.

Shen Zhizhen had just entered the room when Wu De started howling on the kang. What was this for? She ignored her little cousin and greeted the old man sitting on the kang politely.

Wang Xiya followed behind her sister, looking confused. What was wrong with Dezi-ge? Wasn't he fine when she left just now?

Seeing her sister looking calm, she quickly brought over a chair. After her sister sat down, she went to her father and asked with her eyes what was going on.

Blind Wang ignored his daughter, his gaze fixed on the young woman who had just entered. His fingers were constantly calculating, but he found he couldn't deduce anything at all.

His skills couldn't calculate anything about her, which could only mean her fate was not something an ordinary person could divine. This conclusion only strengthened his inner conviction: this person was undoubtedly a noble person.

Shen Zhizhen leaned back in the chair, crossed her legs, and took off her glasses, playing with them while watching her little cousin's performance.

Heh, very good. This was the rascal from the original body's memories. She had thought he had changed after growing up; indeed, a leopard cannot change its spots.

"Little cousin, you must save your brother this time. Wuwu, I'm the only one left in the Wu family; you can't just stand by and watch me die..." Wu De knew Shen Jiu's temperament; if he wanted to stay by her side, he had to start with his aunt.

After listening for a while, Shen Zhizhen finally understood what Wu De wanted: he wanted to stay by her side to change his fate, otherwise he wouldn't live past twenty!

She was almost amused to the point of laughter. Where did all this come from? She wanted to give her little cousin a lecture on how feudal superstition was bad, but thinking that there were no tomb robbers who weren't superstitious, she swallowed the words.

"I'll send you back to Shenyang City. You can stay with my father; he should be able to protect you, right?" Shen Zhizhen said with an amused expression.

She was going to Shanghai to find Shen San and really couldn't bring someone with an injured leg. She felt she had done her duty by sending Wu De to the Shen family.

After all, she wasn't the original body. What Wu De said couldn't touch her heart at all. Of course, the main thing was that she didn't believe in fortune-telling.

Hearing this, Wu De let out a howl of genuine despair. Wuwuwu, he knew Shen Jiu was cold-hearted.

Wu De: "Are you just finding me troublesome?"

Shen Zhizhen: "That's right. It's good that you know."

Wu De: "You don't care about my life or death at all?"

Shen Zhizhen: "Nonsense. If I didn't care about your life or death, I would have just left. You think I'd actually send you back to Shenyang City? Are you dreaming?"

Wu De: "Then let me follow you."

"No way. Why should this young lady take care of a cripple?" Wu De’s injuries would take at least a month to fully heal, and the thought of having to look after a man for a month left her without a shred of pity.

Hearing this, Wu De perked up. "I don't need you to take care of me. Xi Ya will take care of me."

Wang Xiya was enjoying the show, not expecting Brother Dezi to drag her into it. She pointed at herself, speechless, and just as she was about to deny it, her father stopped her.

Blind Man Wang: "That’s right. Xi Ya was born with great strength; she can take care of Dezi."

Shen Zhizhen scanned the three people opposite her. She seemed to understand a little! "How old is Xiya this year?"

When Wang Xiya heard her age being asked, she smiled quickly: "Sister, I'm eighteen this year."

Shen Zhizhen had a good impression of the girl, so she smiled at her and then turned her gaze to Wu De. "Although your parents are gone, marriage is still a serious matter. When we return to Shenyang City, I’ll have my father arrange it for you."

Although she saw them as still young, it was common for people to marry at eighteen or nineteen here. Since the two were willing, there was no need to wrong the chubby girl. She would have her "cheap" father host a wedding for them and provide them with some household assets.

As soon as these words were spoken, all three were stunned. They looked at each other, not knowing what to say.

In the end, it was Wu De who stammered an explanation that he and Xiya didn't have that kind of relationship.

"You don't? And you'd let a maiden take care of you?" Shen Zhizhen looked at the three of them, puzzled. *People in the 1940s are this open-minded?*

chapters.title: Pestered
chapters.content:
Wang Xiya felt that since this concerned her, she had the right to express her opinion. "Brother Dezi, it’s no problem for me to take care of you, but you have to marry me later. Otherwise, what will I do if my reputation is ruined and I can't get married?"

A girl has to marry eventually. Rather than marrying a stranger, she would rather marry Brother Dezi; that way, she could also be related to the pretty sister.

Shen Zhizhen’s lips curled up slightly as she watched her frustrated little cousin. *Haha, now it’s my turn to watch the show.*

As long as his daughter married Wu De, she could stay by the side of a noble person. For this reason alone, Blind Man Wang was happy with the marriage.

Blind Man Wang: "Dezi, look, don't you think you should give an answer?"

Wu De glanced at Xiya’s sturdy frame, which could easily hold him, and felt like crying. *Wuwu, this isn't my type.*

Wu De struggled internally, but finally decided that nothing was more important than his own life. If he didn't live past twenty, he wouldn't even be able to get a wife like Xiya.

Having thought it through, he turned to Shen Jiu and asked: "If I marry Xiya, will you let us stay by your side?"

Shen Zhizhen shook her head and chuckled: "No. My uncle has already arranged a place for me. I must leave as soon as possible. Once I send you back to Shenyang City, I have to go. I won't even be able to attend your wedding."

Her "cheap" father had faked her death, so she couldn't show her face in Shenyang City. Plus, she had caused quite a bit of trouble over the last ten days or so; although they hadn't traced it back to her yet, leaving as soon as possible was the best strategy.

The train ticket Shen Tingshan had prepared for her had already expired. Because of the explosion at the Shenyang East Station, the Japanese military had tightened control over train lines leaving the pass, and she was still thinking about how to get out.

Blind Man Wang and Wu De were anxious upon hearing this. They looked at each other, reached a consensus, and indicated that the wedding could be held today.

Shen Zhizhen...

Things had reached this point; it seemed a bit heartless if she refused again. However, their persistence made Shen Zhizhen believe a little in the fortune-telling.

Although the Master did not speak of strange phenomena, she had a space in her consciousness and was a transmigrator herself—she really couldn't ignore the words of fate.

Thinking of this, Shen Zhizhen simply nodded in agreement. *If they want to follow, let them follow.* For her, it was at most a bit inconvenient, but for Wu De and Xiya, it was a life-altering event.

And so, Shen Zhizhen witnessed the simplest of weddings. There were no guests, no banquet, and not even a hint of joy in the house. Blind Man Wang and she represented the families on both sides, occasionally having to act as emcees to cue the process.

Shen Zhizhen gave Blind Man Wang two large gold bars as a dowry. She didn't know when Xiya would be able to return, and with these two gold bars, Blind Man Wang could live very well in these chaotic times.

Wu De was deeply moved when he saw this. His little cousin really did care about him. She gave two large gold bars right off the bat. One large gold bar weighed ten taels, and at the current exchange rate, one tael of gold could be exchanged for a thousand silver dollars. That meant these two gold bars were worth twenty thousand silver dollars. Thinking of this, he looked at his new wife—this chubby girl was truly valuable.

Blind Man Wang looked at his chubby girl with relief. He had thought she would be left on his hands, but he never expected to meet a noble person. She was so generous with her first gift; she was truly worthy of being the young mistress of the Shen family.

Wang Xiya looked at Shen Jiu with stars in her eyes. She had decided that from now on, this woman was her own sister. Following her would surely mean never going hungry.

The wedding was just a formality; it ended after bowing to heaven, earth, and their elders.

Wang Xiya went to cook, while Shen Zhizhen, Wu De, and Blind Man Wang discussed how to enter the pass.

Shen Zhizhen: "Uncle Wang, can you buy high-priced train tickets here?"

Blind Man Wang shook his head and said: "Ticket scalpers can't get tickets at all. I heard someone blew up the Fengtian East Station and hijacked a train heading to Heilongjiang. The Japanese military is now enforcing total control." It was almost impossible to leave by train.

Fengtian was Shenyang. When the puppet Manchukuo was established in '32, the Japanese renamed Shenyang to Fengtian. The locals didn't want to call it that because the name was changed by the Japanese, so they still used the old name, but other regions mostly used the new city name.

Wu De glanced at his cousin, knowing that some things had to be kept secret, even from close relatives, or the whole family would suffer if it leaked.

His leg made taking a carriage unrealistic. It was the middle of winter, the weather was cold, and the roads were slippery—not to mention that the roads could be blocked by heavy snow at any moment.

Wu De: "Uncle Wang, are there any freight trains heading into the pass?" Blind Man Wang knew many people in the Siping market and was very well-informed; he knew exactly when trains passed through.

Blind Man Wang thought for a moment and said: "There actually is one. Tonight at midnight, there's a coal train passing through from Heilongjiang that’s heading into the pass."

Shen Zhizhen was pondering the feasibility of driving a car into the pass. She had a ready-made military truck in her space anyway. If she made a fake license plate and forged some identification documents, passing through the checkpoints shouldn't be a big problem.

Hearing what Blind Man Wang said, she raised an eyebrow. She glanced at her cousin's leg; it wouldn't be impossible to bury him in a pile of coal with some thick bedding.

After some discussion, everyone decided to try it tonight. If they could successfully board the coal train, they would leave; if something went wrong, they would take a car.

Wang Xiya brought the cooked food over and placed it on the kang table. She served rice to everyone, climbed onto the kang, sat cross-legged, and invited everyone to eat.

The Wang family's vegetables and rice were served in basins. There was a huge basin of stewed cabbage, pork, and vermicelli. Shen Zhizhen had thought it was too much when Xiya served her rice in a large bowl, but when she saw Xiya eating from a sea bowl, she realized that was the smallest bowl the Wang family had.

The meal gave Shen Zhizhen a glimpse of Wang Xiya's appetite. No wonder she was so sturdy and round; this girl ate three sea bowls of rice and half a basin of vegetables.

Shen Zhizhen looked at her little cousin with pity. *Kid, once your injury heals, you better figure out how to make money, otherwise, you won't even be able to feed your wife.*

At midnight, the three said goodbye to Blind Man Wang, left the house, and followed Xiya to the section of the tracks where the train passed, hiding nearby.

Wu De was carried on Wang Xiya's back the whole way. Shen Zhizhen was astonished to see that she wasn't even flushed or out of breath after carrying him for so long, and she couldn't help but praise her.

Wang Xiya chuckled, "Sister, I can lift a 500-jin millstone. I've been practicing with my dad since I was little. Taking down eight or ten men like Brother Dezi is no problem at all."

A flash of pleasant surprise crossed Shen Zhizhen's eyes. *This girl is great, much more useful than Wu De. No wonder she eats so much.*

Wu De rolled his eyes at this. *Hmph, if she wants to take me down, she has to be fast enough to catch me. My nickname 'Flying Legs' isn't just for show.*

Shen Zhizhen sat on her travel bag, chatting idly with Wang Xiya. She had left the carriage for Blind Man Wang. The sheepskin coat she had exchanged at the hospital was now being worn by Wu De.

Wu De was shorter than her and Wang Xiya, and his build was better than a bamboo pole, so winter clothes like the sheepskin coat generally fit him.

When the three heard the sound of the train, they stood up and prepared to climb aboard. When the train arrived, Wang Xiya carried Wu De and climbed up in a few agile steps. Shen Zhizhen followed with her luggage.

***

chapters.title: Shen San's a Secret Agent? And a Mistress Too?
chapters.content:
Shanghai, 76 Jessfield Road. A black sedan drove out. The guards at the gate saw the license plate, quickly opened the gate to let it pass, and saluted the woman driving.

One of the new soldiers asked, puzzled: "Captain, aren't we going to inspect it?" Wasn't there an order that every car entering or leaving had to be inspected?

"Inspect my foot. Orders are dead, but people are alive. There are always some people you can't afford to offend," the squad leader said with a sigh, watching the rear of the car.

"Who was that woman driving?" She was really beautiful.

The squad leader sneered: "Shen Zhimei, Secretary-General of the Secretariat. There are several big shots inside who have their eyes on her. Be smart when you see her in the future." It wasn't that he didn't want to do his duty, but people had already come to give him a heads-up.

"Rumor has it that she is the mistress of a high-ranking official in Nanjing, and she only came here to be Secretary-General after being dealt with by the original wife. Heh, even when she's 'exiled,' she still gets to be a Secretary-General. She's not someone small fry like us can mess with."

The soldier nodded, indicating he understood. He understood that a fair lady is a gentleman's desire. Even if they didn't say anything when they searched the beauty, there might be some men looking to show off who would jump at the chance to stir up trouble.

*Tsk tsk*, anyone who was doing well in this place was a ruthless person. The captain was right; he needed to learn from him.

Shen Zhizhen walked out from the street corner, watching the black sedan drive away. A grave look appeared in her eyes. *Shen San became a secret agent? And someone's mistress?*

The conversation between the two soldiers had reached her ears; she couldn't deny that the person driving was Shen Zhimei.

Shen Zhimei's address had been kept with the train ticket. She hadn't looked at it at the time, and later, when the ticket wasn't used, she had forgotten about it.

Yesterday, the three of them had finally arrived in Shanghai after a month of traveling.

She took out the address her "cheap" father had given her and looked at it: 76 Jessfield Road. The notorious secret agent headquarters.

Shen Zhizhen never imagined that when Shen Tingshan said Shen Zhimei was a secretary-general in a newly established department, he was referring to the No. 76 Secret Service Headquarters! This place had already earned quite a notorious reputation in both books and history.

Today, she had come here alone and ended up overhearing that conversation.

Shen Zhizhen raised her hand to hail a rickshaw. Once seated, she said, "Driver, follow this road ahead. I'll tell you where to turn."

No matter what, she had to meet with Shen San and confirm things in person to see if there were any extenuating circumstances. *Sigh.*

Although automobiles were fast, the roads in Shanghai were crowded with people and vehicles, so the speed wasn't much to brag about. Plus, Shen Zhimei would get out of the car every two blocks, making it hard for her to lose her.

Whenever Shen San’s car stopped by the roadside, Shen Zhizhen would also get out to take a look. She wanted to observe what exactly was going on with Shen Zhimei. Once Shen Zhimei got back into the car, she would hail a new rickshaw to follow.

Along the way, Shen San visited six shops, emerging from each with bags in hand, taking "shopping" to the extreme. The black car finally stopped on Fengyuan Road, and by then, the sky had already darkened.

Seeing the black sedan parked by the side of the road, Shen Zhizhen signaled the rickshaw puller to stop. After paying and waiting for the rickshaw to leave, she surveyed the surroundings, finally fixing her gaze on No. 36 Fengyuan Road.

No. 36 Fengyuan Road was a three-story enclosed Western-style house. In the center was a courtyard, and the four sides were buildings connected on each floor by circular corridors. Shen Zhizhen observed while pricking up her ears, trying to locate Shen San.

There were two households on each side of the first floor, totaling eight, while the second and third floors had four households each, one per side. After discerning the layout, Shen Zhizhen stopped at the door of the unit on the south side of the second floor.

Shen Zhimei carried her bags home, kicked off her shoes, placed the items by the door, turned on the phonograph, changed into loungewear, and reclined on the sofa to think.

Father said Shen Jiu would come to find her at the end of February. It was almost the end of March; how was it that there wasn't even a shadow of her? She knew what that girl was capable of, so she wasn't worried about her safety; perhaps she had been delayed by something.

*Click.* The sound of the door opening. Someone had entered. Shen Zhimei pulled a gun from under the cushion, sat up, and aimed it at the door. When she saw who it was, she put the gun away.

"What kind of habit is that? Can't you knock? Change your shoes." The brat really couldn't be talked about; she appeared just as she was being thought of.

Shen Zhizhen shrugged and retorted, "I was worried you’d be assassinated and wanted to test your vigilance." She changed into slippers, walked over, and plopped down into an armchair.

"You didn't even know you were being followed the whole way, and you call yourself a secret agent? Who gave you the courage!" Shen Zhizhen was in a foul mood. With a second uncle who was a traitor at home and an older sister who was a secret agent here in Shanghai, she figured she’d never be able to wash the labels off her back in this lifetime.

Shen Zhimei...

This girl’s tongue was still as sharp as ever. She hadn't become any cuter in five years. *Hmph.* With the entire Shen clan’s resources poured into training her as the successor, it would be a miracle if she *could* be discovered.

"When did you arrive?" Shen Zhimei put the gun back in its place and asked lazily, reclining again.

The little girl had cut her hair; she looked quite dashing. She hadn't seen her in five years, and she had grown taller than her.

Shen Zhizhen: "Arrived yesterday."

Shen Qi’s beauty was of the alluring type, the kind that carried charm in every glance and smile. Coupled with her graceful figure, she was certainly someone who would attract attention, but Shen Zhizhen didn't believe for a second that she was someone's mistress.

Women became mistresses either for money or love. The Shen family was wealthy, and their father was the head of the family; how could he possibly let Shen San go without money? As for love, that was even more impossible. A high-ranking official in Nanjing would have to be at least fifty; why would someone as beautiful as her go find herself a "daddy"? That would be insane.

Shen Zhimei looked at Little Jiu and asked, "Where did you go to play?" She was a month late.

Shen Zhizhen chuckled at this. That month had been quite spectacular—a veritable "Great Escape." Well, it was a process of constantly causing trouble for the Japanese army and being chased by them. Of course, the main culprits were her and Xi Ya, while their little cousin could only be an accomplice due to his injured leg.

They didn't have a plan; they just struck whenever they had the chance, which led to them being wanted and hunted. Since they were on the run, they certainly wouldn't follow a set route, so they took a huge detour, wandering around for a month before finally reaching Shanghai.

Of course, she couldn't tell Shen San all of this. "I brought Wu De and his wife this time. The kid hurt his leg and needs his dressing changed every two days, so that’s why we were delayed."

Shen Zhimei’s eyes dimmed at the mention of this, and she chuckled softly: "That kid Wu De is married? Tell me, what does his wife look like? Is she pretty?"

Shen Zhizhen: "She’s delicate and pleasant to look at, just a bit on the heavy side—could fit two Wu Des inside her."

Shen Zhimei confirmed her suspicions and couldn't help but sigh inwardly. Her little Jiu was indeed a handful.

"No. 76 recently received a report. Over the past month, three criminal gangs have been committing crimes repeatedly from north to south. Among them, one person with a bad leg was being carried by a very fat woman. That was you guys, right?"

A flash of surprise crossed Shen Zhizhen's eyes. Just two sentences and she’d been exposed! As expected of someone from No. 76; they were truly formidable.

Fortunately, because they had caused so much trouble along the way, they had made a plan before entering Shanghai: to split up. The three of them were too conspicuous together. Now that Wu De's leg was mostly healed, they were scattered across three different inns.

chapters.title: You Don't Look Like a Good Person at All
chapters.content:
Shen Zhimei looked at Little Jiu playfully. She wanted to see how the Ninth Miss would handle this—would she trust her sister and confess, or find another excuse?

When she had seen that report, noting that the crimes were committed all the way south from their hometown, she had made a mental note of it. It turned out it really was related to her.

Shen Zhizhen rolled her eyes at the playful look. Facing someone who could expose her in two or three sentences, she chose to be direct and nodded in admission. Well, mostly because she couldn't outsmart her anyway!

"You trust me, a secret agent, that much?" Shen Zhimei said with a smile in her eyes. This girl had been mocking her just after walking through the door.

"I do. You're my own sister; you wouldn't harm me." She trusted Old Man Shen and the memories of the original body.

If Shen San couldn't be trusted, Shen Tingshan wouldn't have sent her to seek refuge with her. Moreover, Shen Tingshan had made it very clear: he wanted the two sisters to support and look after each other in these chaotic times.

In fact, the brief exchange of questions and answers was a mutual probing between the two sisters, testing the weight of their kinship and blood ties.

As the next head of the Shen family, Shen Zhizhen had a responsibility to look after her kin, especially someone who was her own sister by blood.

On the other hand, Shen Zhimei was testing whether Little Jiu, after five years apart, still trusted her as a sister.

Shen Zhimei was very happy to hear Little Jiu say that. She teased, "I wouldn't dare. I will protect the young mistress with my life." This girl carried the weight of the entire Shen clan; she wouldn't dare let anything happen to her.

"But this is Shanghai. You can't be so reckless. If something happens, I'll have to sell myself to bail you out." She didn't know if it was right or wrong for Father to let this daring girl out.

Although said in a teasing tone, it touched Shen Zhizhen deeply, reminding her of Old Man Shen and her second uncle, Shen Jingshan. They had different styles, but both were united in their commitment to protecting the Shen family.

"Shen San, remember this: no matter what happens to your sister in the Shanghai Bund, you don't need to bail me out. I'll run away on my own." With the "cheat" of her space, it wouldn't be hard for her to escape. How could she let Shen San sell herself to save her?

Shen Zhimei nodded perfunctorily at this. "Got it." The little girl was so impudent.

"Now, can you tell me why you became a secret agent at No. 76?" Shen Zhizhen hoped that Shen San, like Shen Jingshan, had an unavoidable reason.

"What else could it be? Assigned by superiors. Don't worry, your sister hasn't done anything evil at No. 76." Although she was in an administrative role, she couldn't deny the "secret agent" part. After all, No. 76 was the secret service headquarters; what else would someone working there be if not a secret agent?

Seeing Shen Zhimei’s candor, Shen Zhizhen felt a strange sense of relief. Otherwise, what could she do? Living in these chaotic times was not easy. As long as she wasn't a heinous villain, she could turn a blind eye.

The two chatted casually, mostly with Shen Zhizhen sharing news about home and the reasons for her arrival.

When Shen Zhimei heard that her father had faked Little Jiu's death, she laughed heartily. Father was still as interesting as ever. But when she heard about the second uncle being a traitor and the Japanese agent hidden within the Shen family, her smile faded, and her expression turned grave.

Shen Zhimei frowned and thought for a moment. "If the second uncle says there is a high-level Japanese agent, then this matter cannot be kept from Father."

"Why?" Shen Zhizhen felt that Shen Jingshan’s caution made sense; not knowing was the only way to avoid revealing flaws.

The treasure map was already with her, and only the successive heads of the family knew about it. If Shen Tingshan didn't say anything, no one would know the Shen family possessed that map.

"If the second uncle hasn't found them, it means the agent is hidden very deep. It's very likely someone close to Father," Shen Zhimei analyzed.

When she was in university, she began receiving training in intelligence work. She had seen many methods; an excellent high-level agent was often the person least suspected.

Shen Zhizhen thought of the Wan family—this was also her second uncle's concern—so she told her about the Wan family incident. "If we tell Father, will we follow in the footsteps of the Wan family?"

Shen Zhimei was almost infuriated by this. She sneered, "Womanly kindness! With the Wan family as a warning, we should find them as soon as possible, kill them, and then find a perfect excuse to cover it up."

The Shen family had significant influence in the Guandong region, which the Wan family’s type of merchants couldn't compare to. The Japanese army wouldn't dare move against the Shen family easily; otherwise, many people like Little Jiu would constantly cause trouble for them.

Shen Zhizhen...

What did Shen San just say? She said to rest assured, she hadn't done anything evil. Looking at this "femme fatale" with her decisive and ruthless demeanor, why did it feel like she had quite a bit of blood on her hands?

Shen Zhimei sat up, reached for the phone, and made several calls before finding Shen Jingshan.

Shen Jingshan was drinking with people at the Daxian Nightclub. The bartender came over to say there was a call for him. Dizzily, he stood up, walked to the front desk, and picked up the phone: "Hello, this is Shen Jingshan."

Shen Zhimei: "Second Uncle, it's Zhimei. I had a little to drink today and got a bit homesick, so I wanted to chat with you for a while."

Hearing it was Shen San, Shen Jingshan’s eyes grew deep. "Zhimei, Second Uncle misses you too. I heard your father mentioning you the day before yesterday."

Shen Zhimei: "Is Father in good health? Next time you see him, Second Uncle, please give him my regards. Tell him I miss him. My mother’s death anniversary is coming up; tell him to burn more paper for her. Don't let him forget his old love just because he has a new one."

Shen Jingshan was stunned. "Don't worry, niece, leave it to me. I'll buy the yellow paper tomorrow and go back to Shen Family Village to burn it for your mother." The two exchanged a few more pleasantries and hung up.

After making the call, Shen Zhimei lay back down and closed her eyes to think.

Shen Zhizhen had sharp hearing and naturally caught the entire conversation. Being well-versed in the Shen family’s secret code, she understood perfectly: with a casual phone call, Shen Zhimei had issued an assassination order to Second Uncle Shen, and the target was their stepmother!

Shen Zhizhen: "Aren't you afraid of killing the wrong person? She’s still carrying little Tenth in her belly, isn't she?" This woman was truly ruthless.

In fact, when she first heard that the jasmine flower was the cause of the Wan family's massacre, she had suspected An Hui. She had even mentioned it to Shen Jingshan as if by chance, wanting him to be careful. Back then, she was still a kind, naive girl who hadn't touched blood, and with An Hui pregnant with little Tenth, she had let the matter go once she was sure the Shen family was temporarily safe.

Shen Zhimei opened her eyes and sneered: "Don't be naive. It’s not even certain whose child that little Tenth in An Hui’s belly is." There is nothing high-level Japanese agents won't do to complete a mission; you can only imagine what they are capable of.

"Third Sister, you don't seem like a good person at all," Shen Zhizhen remarked with deep feeling.

Shen Zhimei was almost amused to the point of anger. In the past month, the number of Japanese soldiers who had died at this girl's hands was at least eighty, not to mention the lost supplies and the important Red and White party prisoners she had set free. This girl and her partner Wu De were already on the Japanese military's death list; once it was confirmed that the three of them had entered Shanghai, a kill order would inevitably be issued at No. 76.

She retorted sharply: "There are no good people in the Shen family." What kind of good people could a bunch of grave robbers and their descendants be?

Shen Zhizhen... Chapter 26: Third Sister, I'm a Little Worried About You

Shen Zhizhen had to nod in agreement. The Shen family really weren't good people, including herself now.

She discovered that ever since her soul had been cleansed by the golden light, her personality and way of handling things had become increasingly similar to the original owner's. Things like the sniping of Japanese soldiers in the Changbai Mountains and the events that occurred on the way to Shanghai would have been impossible for the "old" her.

The first time she killed a Japanese soldier with her own hands, she felt no fear, but rather a faint sense of satisfaction. Once you start something like this, there is no turning back; she was becoming more and more adept at killing Japanese soldiers.

*Gurgle...* Shen Zhizhen looked at her stomach. "I'm hungry."

She had only eaten breakfast today, spent the day staking out No. 76, and then followed Shen Zhimei all the way here.

"The kitchen is over there, go make something yourself," Shen Zhimei said, gesturing toward the kitchen.

Shen Zhizhen sighed softly and got up to head to the kitchen. Her own sister was certainly not standing on ceremony.

The kitchen was clean and tidy, clearly not used for cooking often. She opened the cabinet, took out two eggs and a package of dried noodles, then turned on the gas to boil water.

Shen Zhizhen turned to ask Shen Third: "I'm cooking noodles, do you want some?" She had been shopping non-stop since leaving No. 76 and hadn't eaten a thing.

"Yes, bring me a bowl," Shen Zhimei said with her eyes closed. She needed to think about how to arrange things for little Ninth and Wu De's couple.

Shen Zhizhen went back to the kitchen to cook. Two bowls of egg noodles were ready quickly. She placed them on the dining table and called Shen Third over to eat.

The first meal the two sisters had eaten together in five years was noodles. Shen Zhimei looked at the clear, watery soup with a hint of disdain, but after one bite, she found it surprisingly good.

Shen Zhizhen finished her bowl of soup noodles while the person opposite her hadn't even finished half. She put down her chopsticks and leaned back in her chair. "I want to rent a place with gas pipes like this. Do you know where I can find one?"

She liked to cook for herself, and after using the gas just now, she really didn't want to use a coal stove. Gas was so much better—clean and convenient. It was a bit more expensive, but she wasn't short on money, so why should she settle for less?

Hearing this, Shen Zhimei looked up at little Ninth. "You're living with me from now on." Keeping her close meant she could keep an eye on her; otherwise, who knew when she might stir up trouble.

"No, what if I expose you if I'm found out?" Shen Zhizhen shook her head and refused. You shouldn't put all your eggs in one basket, and besides, she preferred the freedom of living alone.

Shen Zhimei: "If you cause trouble out there, you'll implicate me anyway."

Shen Zhizhen: "I won't cause trouble."

Shen Zhimei: "Heh, do you believe that?" There’s a saying that a leopard can't change its spots.

Shen Zhizhen was left speechless. Well, she really couldn't guarantee that. Shanghai was occupied territory; she might just feel the urge to intervene if she ran into something.

Shen Zhimei finished her noodles in a leisurely manner, wiped her mouth, and looked at the silent little Ninth. She smiled lightly: "Go wash the dishes. Once you're done, we'll discuss how to arrange for you and the others." With that, she got up and went to sit on the sofa.

Shen Zhizhen rolled her eyes at Shen Third. She realized that if she lived here, she would be enslaved by this woman forever.

Shen Zhimei leaned back on the sofa, a curve forming on her lips. It felt quite nice to have another living person in the house.

Shen Zhizhen finished washing the dishes, wiped the kitchen counter clean, came out, and sat in her previous spot. "How do you want to arrange us?"

Shen Zhimei: "If the three of you want to stay in Shanghai for the long term, you need legal identities. If you're living with me, you also need a proper job."

"As for Wu De and his wife, you can ask them what they want to do. I can arrange jobs for them, but as for their livelihood, you'll have to figure that out yourselves."

Shen Zhizhen: "What identity will I have while staying with you?" The family had already faked her death; she couldn't stay here as the younger sister.

"To stay by my side, you must be able to withstand scrutiny. Only the truth can withstand investigation," Shen Zhimei said nonchalantly.

She worked at No. 76; whoever appeared around her would be investigated. Even if little Ninth didn't live here, as long as they were in frequent contact, she would be investigated anyway. She was worried that Shen Ninth didn't understand this, so she explained it.

"The fake death story is easy to patch up. Just say you had a fight with Father and ran away to find me. It just so happens that the Wan family next door was raided by the Japanese and the fire burned down our pawnshop, so Father mistakenly thought you were burned to death."

Shen Zhizhen nodded to show she understood. As long as the Shen family and Shen Third were safe, none of this was a problem.

"Do you want to work in a government department, or perhaps the police station? Of course, it's not impossible to get you into No. 76," Shen Zhimei said lazily, looking up at Shen Ninth to see how she would choose.

Shen Zhizhen was surprised. Her "cheap" sister seemed to have a lot of power—she could choose between the police, government, or special services! "Does the Secretary-General have that much authority?"

"Of course. I am the eyes placed at No. 76 by the Nanjing faction. Everyone has to give me some face when I speak." The establishment of No. 76 was a move planned in advance by the Nanjing faction.

"You're part of the Nanjing faction?" Shen Zhizhen frowned. Wasn't Nanjing the Wang Jingwei regime? And behind the Wang regime was the Japanese military!

Shen Zhimei: "What else?" There would be big movements in Nanjing in a couple of days, and the situation would change.

However, for her, it was a good thing. Although her power wouldn't change, her deterrent force would be greater than before, so no one would say anything if she arranged a position for her own sister.

Shen Zhizhen knew that it wasn't easy to build a future in these troubled times, but for her, knowing the historical trajectory, she couldn't watch Shen Third walk down this path of no return.

Shen Zhizhen: "Third Sister, I'm a little worried about you."

Shen Zhimei: "Worried about what?"

Shen Zhizhen: "Worried that you've gone down the wrong path and can't turn back."

"The people at No. 76 have committed countless evils. I'm worried you won't have a good end."

"Why don't I take you back to our hometown?"

Shen Zhimei: "To go grave robbing with you?"

Shen Zhizhen...

"Don't worry, I know what I'm doing. Back to the point, where do you want to go?" Shen Zhimei smiled lightly. Well, being cared for by the little girl felt warm.

Seeing this, Shen Zhizhen didn't say much more. *Sigh*, take it one step at a time. At worst, she would just pack up Shen Third and take her away when the time came.

"Let's go to the police station." Being a policeman didn't require sitting in an office; she could patrol every day, wandering around, which was quite nice.

"Hmm, I'll buy you a car so you can drive to work every day." The police station wasn't in the concession, so it was a bit far; having a car would make commuting convenient.

"How much is a car?" Buying a car would indeed be convenient.

"I'll buy it for you, you don't need to pay." Consider it a gift for little Ninth. Having been away from home for five years, she owed this little girl five birthday gifts.

Shen Zhizhen raised an eyebrow. "Is the salary at No. 76 very high?" If the salary was high, it wasn't impossible to consider working at No. 76. That way, she could keep an eye on Shen Third and prevent her from making any major mistakes.

"It's alright. I'm going to take a bath. You sleep here tonight. Tomorrow, go ask Wu De and his wife what they want to do. If they want a job, tell me. If not, you figure it out, but be careful. You have to be cautious when meeting up in the future, otherwise, people will investigate them." After giving her instructions, Shen Zhimei got up and went to the bedroom to get her clothes.

Shen Zhizhen said "oh," then got up to explore the house. Since she would be staying here often, she definitely needed to get to know the place.

The layout was two bedrooms, two living rooms, one kitchen, and one bathroom. The south-facing window looked out onto Fengyuan Road. Opening the window and leaning out, she could see Shen Zhimei's car. Across the street were single-story storefronts, so there was no risk of being monitored from a building opposite. The living room and dining room were connected, making the space feel extra large. The remaining two rooms were a bedroom and a study.

After looking around, Shen Zhizhen said to Shen Third, who was heading to the bathroom: "Wait, you only have one bed here?"

"What, is it beneath you to sleep with me? If you don't want to sleep in the bed, there's a sofa in the living room." Shen Zhimei rolled her eyes coquettishly and ignored the little girl as she walked toward the bathroom.

Shen Zhizhen... Chapter 27: The White Silk Hangs Again

The next day, by the Huangpu River.

Shen Zhizhen, Wu De, and Wang Xiya sat on the embankment, eating steamed buns while watching the boats pass by on the river and chatting.

Shen Zhizhen conveyed Shen Third's meaning. "The three of us are on the Japanese military's kill list, so we need to lay low for a while. Tell me what you two want to do." Fortunately, the Japanese intelligence was flawed; Wu De's leg had healed, which could actually serve as a distraction.

Wang Xiya swallowed the bun in her mouth and was the first to speak: "Sister, I'm pretty good at cooking, I want to open a small restaurant." She was worried that the money she earned from a job wouldn't be enough to feed herself.

Yesterday, she and Brother De had walked around all day and learned a lot. The cost of living in Shanghai was much higher than back home, so she wanted to open a small restaurant—at the very least, she could ensure she had enough to eat.

Shen Zhizhen thought of the meal she had at the Wang house and her mouth twitched involuntarily. "That works. Why don't you open a small restaurant near the docks? There are a lot of laborers there who just want to be full. You can make a few pots of stewed dishes, put a little of each on a plate with a bowl of rice—that should sell well." Selling boxed lunches to dock workers was a solid idea.

Wang Xiya was happy to agree. Her sister's idea was great; she might not be good at other things, but she was an expert at making stews.

Shen Zhizhen turned her gaze to Wu De. "What about you?" Did he want to open the restaurant with Xiya or do something else?

Wu De chuckled. He had already thought about it. "I'll go pull a rickshaw first. Pulling that thing every day will not only earn money but also help me get familiar with Shanghai as quickly as possible. Plus, it'll be convenient to come find you."

He had noticed that all the rickshaw pullers wore black felt hats, so he would get one too. If he pulled it down low, who would recognize him?

Since the little cousin is going to be a police officer, once he gets familiar with the traffic conditions in Shanghai, he will work in the area under Shen Jiu’s jurisdiction. This way, they can look out for each other, and he won’t have to be too far from his little cousin.

He had never considered getting a regular job. Unless he could be in the same police station as his little cousin, he wouldn't even think about it. He was used to freedom and wasn't accustomed to being restrained. Heh, once he got to know this great city of Shanghai, there would naturally be no shortage of ways to make money.

Both of them were people with their own ideas and plans, so Shen Zhizhen naturally wouldn't say anything. In fact, she thought this was quite good; by not involving Shen San’s connections, they wouldn't attract attention. It was much safer for Wu De and his wife to hide among the crowd, and it would be more convenient for them to do things in the future.

Shen Zhizhen took out two money bags and handed them to Wu De and Wang Xiya respectively. "Inside, besides the silver dollars, I’ve also put in some small gold bars. You two decide how to manage them. If you have any trouble or run out of money, come find me. In any case, what we’ve done along the way must be buried in our stomachs; otherwise, everyone will be in danger."

Wu De and Wang Xiya nodded to show they understood. With their lives at stake, how could they not be cautious? However, both of them whispered that they must be called upon if there were any future operations.

As the elder cousin said, everyone has a responsibility to drive out the invaders. Even if no one knows, so what? Their consciences are clear; unsung heroes are heroes nonetheless.

Wu De had changed a lot since being by the little cousin's side. In the past, his choice would have been to protect himself and watch from the sidelines; he had never thought about living such a passionate life.

Heh, it didn't feel half bad. So what if they were grave robbers? They could still contribute to this broken country. Hmph, kill more little Japanese invaders and vent some anger for their fallen compatriots.

After Wu De and his wife left, Shen Zhizhen sat alone by the river for a long time. The river breeze tousled her short hair, which actually helped her clear her thoughts a little...

At Shen Family Village, Shen Jingshan returned early in the morning with yellow paper, using the excuse of burning paper for Little Jiu to drag his eldest brother up the mountain.

Shen Tingshan stood before the tombstone and frowned, asking, "Second brother, what kind of act is this?" It wasn't a holiday or an anniversary; what kind of paper was he burning?

Shen Jingshan turned his head to look behind him. Confirming no one was following, he took out a cigarette, lit it, and tossed the match onto the yellow paper. He took a puff and recounted the contents of Shen San’s phone call and the fact that a high-ranking Japanese agent was lurking in the Shen family.

When Shen Tingshan heard that Little Jiu had arrived in Shanghai, he was very happy. But after hearing what followed, his heart skipped a beat: An Hui was a high-ranking Japanese agent.

Shen Tingshan squatted down and used a small stick to poke at the yellow paper, letting the flames rise. Watching the fire, his eyes flickered with uncertainty.

Seeing this, Shen Jingshan squatted beside his eldest brother and asked softly, "What, can't bear to do it? Or do you not believe in Zhimei’s judgment?" That girl Zhimei was the smartest child in the Shen family. If she had made such a judgment, it was almost certainly correct.

Furthermore, ever since he began suspecting An Hui based on Little Jiu’s warning, he had been investigating in secret. This person definitely had problems, but he just couldn't find concrete evidence. After all, that woman was carrying Little Ten in her womb; without proof, he truly couldn't make a move.

In this regard, he was not as decisive as that girl Zhimei.

Shen Tingshan shook his head. He was just feeling a bit of melancholy and a lingering fear. The person sleeping beside him had been after the treasure map all along. Fortunately, he had always been cautious and never revealed any flaws, otherwise, the consequences would have been unimaginable.

The yellow paper burned to ash and was scattered by a gust of wind into the mountain forest. Shen Tingshan stood up and signaled for his second brother to head down the mountain.

That afternoon, his wife An Hui was kicked in the stomach by a startled horse, leading to a miscarriage and massive hemorrhaging. On the way to the hospital, the carriage wheel broke, delaying medical treatment, and she bled to death.

A month later, white mourning silk was hung on the Shen family gates once again.

Inside the Shen family study, the two brothers were having a conversation about how to handle what came next.

Shen Jingshan looked at the radio set they had unearthed and couldn't help but feel a sense of relief. At the very least, they hadn't killed an innocent; An Hui was indeed a Japanese agent.

"Zhimei’s wisdom is nearly demonic, and she has a heart as intricate as a seven-holed jade. She is calm and decisive when facing trouble. Big brother was right to send Little Jiu to her," Shen Jingshan said with emotion.

Hearing his two daughters mentioned, Shen Tingshan’s mood improved quite a bit. "If you had told me earlier that you were acting as a traitor for the sake of the Shen family, I certainly wouldn't have let Little Jiu go."

Although that girl’s temperament seemed to have changed a lot, as the saying goes, "Mountains and rivers are easy to change, but a person’s nature is hard to alter." He was truly worried that once the little girl reached Shanghai, her original nature would return and she would cause trouble that Third Girl couldn't handle.

Colonel Nakajima hung up the phone, frowned, and relayed the content. "Tanaka-kun, do you think the Shen family sensed something and killed Keiko?"

He did not believe their Great Japanese Empire’s high-ranking agent would die from a miscarriage and hemorrhage. Although pregnancy and childbirth were indeed dangerous for women, this would absolutely not happen to an excellent agent.

"And if they did? The Shen family provided a perfect reason," Tanaka Fumiya said with a light laugh. He was leaving tomorrow and no longer cared much about these matters.

After a month of secret searching, he could confirm the treasure map was not here. Since that was the case, he wouldn't waste too much thought on it.

Colonel Nakajima’s brows were tightly knit. The Shen family had a great reputation in the Guandong region. They used Shen Jingshan to suppress the local gangs, and it would be very troublesome to move against the Shen family, so for now, they could only swallow this bitter pill.

chapters.title: Shen Jiu Starts Work
chapters.content:
Extra! Extra! The traitor Wang established a puppet National Government in Nanjing on March 30, 1940, openly surrendering to Japan.

Shen Zhizhen parked her car next to the newspaper boy, took out money to buy a paper, scanned it briefly, and continued driving toward the Western Shanghai Branch.

Shen Zhimei’s efficiency was incredibly high. Yesterday, not only did she buy the car, but she also bought her a pile of clothes and shoes, and arranged her job properly, telling her to report to the Western Shanghai Branch today to work as a patrol sergeant.

A patrol sergeant in the police station was similar to a squad leader. She had a few people under her and was responsible for leading her patrol team to maintain public order and handle problems encountered during patrols.

The salary was fifty silver dollars a month. It looked like a lot, but it wasn't even enough for gas money. A gallon of gasoline in Shanghai sold for two silver dollars; she had spent twenty silver dollars on gas yesterday.

At the Western Shanghai Branch, a black sedan pulled into a parking space. Shen Zhizhen opened the door and stepped out. Her attire today was a neutral, British-style look—a trench coat paired with sunglasses. In Shen San’s words, it could charm a whole crowd of men and women.

Her black leather boots clicked on the police station floor. She walked toward the station chief’s office while looking around, a demeanor that attracted quite a bit of attention.

Shen Zhizhen received a warm welcome in the chief’s office. After dealing with that, she followed the internal affairs officer to complete her onboarding, received two sets of police uniforms, a service pistol, a police baton, and other gear, and then followed the patrol officer—her superior—to the office.

Huang Dashan had been notified by the chief and knew this young woman had backing. But what he couldn't figure out was, if she had backing, why come to the police station to be a patrol sergeant? The officers in the station were all old hands; he was truly worried she would be bullied to tears.

Huang Dashan pushed open the door to the Third Patrol Group. The smoky environment made him frown. "Everyone, come over. Let me introduce your new sergeant."

There were six people in the room. Seeing the patrol officer, they quickly stood up, their eyes falling on the short-haired woman in sunglasses next to him. They looked at each other—no way, a woman coming to be their boss?

Huang Dashan: "This is your new sergeant. From now on, you six must obey the sergeant’s orders." After giving a few instructions, he left.

The people in the room dispersed as soon as the patrol officer left, each returning to their desks. No one took the new sergeant seriously.

Shen Zhizhen raised an eyebrow, a curve appearing at the corner of her mouth. She issued the first order of her new tenure: "You have ten minutes to clean this office. From now on, smoking is prohibited inside the office."

The words triggered a burst of laughter. Wang Jiangsheng had some prestige among them. He had thought he would be the one promoted to sergeant, but he hadn't expected to be cut off by some little girl who appeared out of nowhere. He was feeling annoyed.

He decided to give the new sergeant a warning to let her know that in the Third Patrol Group, she had no say in giving orders. Provocatively, he picked up a cigarette, lit it, stood up, and walked over to the new sergeant. He took a puff and blew the smoke into the sergeant’s pretty face, his eyes turning lecherous. Tsk tsk, this skin was really good. Just as he was about to reach out and touch her, he took a kick to the stomach and went flying.

With a bang, he hit the wall and landed, kicking up a layer of dust. For a moment, the air seemed to freeze. At this moment, everyone knew this new sergeant didn't seem so easy to bully, and her temper wasn't very good.

Shen Zhizhen raised her hand to take off her glasses and glanced at her wristwatch. She said nonchalantly, "Two minutes have passed; you have eight minutes left. If it’s not cleaned up when the time is up, he will be your fate." She pointed at the man sprawled on the ground, then turned and walked out.

The people in the room quickly walked over to help "Brother Sheng" up. "How is it? Do you need to go to the hospital?" He Ergou asked with a frown.

The others asked with similar concern. Everyone turned to look from time to time; the distance from the door to here was at least three meters. If Brother Sheng hadn't hit the wall, who knew how much further he would have been kicked.

Wang Jiangsheng bared his teeth as he sat in his chair, shaking his head to indicate he was fine. "This woman is a bit ruthless. Everyone, hurry up and clean; don't let her find an excuse to deal with us."

Things had reached this point; they had to yield. That kick just now told him that even if they all went at her together, they might not be her match. A wise man doesn't fight when the odds are against him. Hmph, there’s plenty of time for revenge.

Hearing this, everyone looked at each other and then all started cleaning the office.

Huang Dazhi finished wiping his desk and said to his brothers, "Guys, I’ll go find out what the sergeant’s background is." Hearing this, everyone urged Huang Dazhi to go quickly.

In the patrol officer’s office, Huang Dazhi opened the door and, seeing only his uncle inside, slipped in to inquire about the situation.

Huang Dashan was wiping a blue and white porcelain vase in his hand. Hearing this, he raised an eyebrow and asked, "What, did you get the short end of the stick?" If he hadn't suffered, this kid wouldn't have come to him so quickly to ask.

Huang Dazhi gave a silly laugh and recounted what had just happened. "Uncle, what’s her background?" He had come from his hometown last year to rely on his uncle and was arranged to be a patrolman at the beginning of the year. Relying on his uncle’s connection, he was doing quite well in the group. This time, he had thought Wang Jiangsheng would become sergeant, but he hadn't expected a surprise arrival.

"What does her background matter? Just remember that she isn't someone you lot can afford to offend. Go back and tell them all to tone it down," Huang Dashan said with a frown.

The chief hadn't said exactly what her background was, but the warm way the chief had acted in his office just now said everything. If the chief had to give her face, then they certainly had to as well.

Huang Dazhi nodded to show he understood. After saying goodbye to his uncle, he went back and conveyed the message. Although no one said anything, their hands were clearly moving much faster.

Shen Zhizhen took her police uniform to the changing room to put it on. After changing, seeing she still had time, she simply put the other uniform and her changed clothes into the car.

When she returned to the office, the desk and floor were already clean, and the window was open for ventilation. She walked to the patrol leader’s desk, sat in the chair, leaned back, and looked at the nervous group with a smile: "Come over here, let’s get to know each other."

"My name is Shen Jiu. I’m new here and there’s a lot I don’t know, so I’ll need your help in the future. Please introduce yourselves by name, age, years of service, and specialties."

The name Shen Zhizhen would immediately make some people think of Shen Zhimei. She didn't want to make their relationship public so soon, so she would use the name Shen Jiu from now on.

Although the heads of the No. 76 branch and the high-ranking Japanese military officials already knew about her relationship with Shen Zhimei, others were unaware due to the confidentiality measures surrounding Shen Zhimei.

"Wang Jiangsheng, 25 years old, 6 years of police service, specializing in combat!" This was the reason he had backed down so quickly; his specialty couldn't withstand a single kick from her.

"He Ergou, 23 years old, 3 years of police service, specializing in gathering information." He wasn't sure if this counted as a specialty, but he had nothing else.

"Mu Daqiang, 25 years old, 4 years of police service, specializing in marksmanship." His shooting was quite good.

"Ma San, 23 years old, 3 years of police service, sensitive sense of smell." His nickname was "Ma the Dog" precisely because of his keen nose.

"Lin Wu, 22 years old, 2 years of police service, specializing in gambling." This statement drew a burst of suppressed laughter. Lin Wu immediately put on a mournful face and told the new patrol leader that he really had no other specialties.

"Huang Dazhi, 21 years old, 3 months of police service, specializing in eating."

This time, it wasn't suppressed laughter; after Huang Dazhi finished speaking, the room erupted into an uproar.

chapters.title: Going on Patrol
chapters.content:
Shen Zhizhen’s lips curled slightly as she laughed along with them for a moment before pointing to Wang Jiangsheng, whom she had just beaten, and asking: "Tell me about our squad's patrol area and schedule." It was clear that the others implicitly looked to him as their leader.

Wang Jiangsheng was taken aback by the question, then said: "Our squad is responsible for the Cross-Border Road area. There hasn't been a set patrol schedule recently."

"Oh, why isn't there a schedule? Is it because there was no patrol leader?" She had seen them all chatting and smoking when she walked in earlier.

They looked at each other. How were they supposed to answer? If they didn't tell the truth, they were worried about getting themselves into trouble; if they did, they were also worried about the consequences.

Seeing this, Shen Zhizhen narrowed her eyes. There was something going on here. She stood up and said: "Let's go. We're going on patrol."

The six men immediately tried to stop her. He Ergou felt it was better to be clear, otherwise, if the new patrol leader didn't understand the complexities, it would be bad for them too.

"Patrol Leader, it’s like this: the area we are responsible for has been a bit chaotic lately."

This confused Shen Zhizhen. If it was chaotic, didn't that mean they needed the police even more? She signaled for He Ergou to continue.

He Ergou explained the situation. Originally, the Cross-Border Road area didn't belong to the Third Patrol Squad; it was the patrol zone of the First Patrol Squad. Since last year, the area had become increasingly chaotic, with frequent incidents of public disorder and escalating conflicts.

Several patrol leaders and officers from the First Patrol Squad had been killed, and they had demanded a change of patrol zone. The Cross-Border Road was then kicked to the Third Patrol Squad like a hot potato. The previous patrol leader had taken them out on patrol and was shot in the head immediately.

The others added a few details from time to time, determined to make the new patrol leader understand the dangers of the Cross-Border Road.

Shen Zhizhen understood now. The Cross-Border Road area bordered the International Settlement, attracting various factions to set up strongholds for illegal activities, including casinos, opium dens, brothels, kidnappings, extortion, and assassinations.

After Shanghai became an occupied zone, the conflict between the Japanese and the International Settlement authorities added to the mix. In short, multiple forces were intertwined and fighting for control here. The police department's authority was severely challenged and eroded, but they couldn't withdraw and were just barely hanging on.

Shen Zhizhen became interested after hearing this. This place was perfect; there was so much room to maneuver. "Let's go, we're going on patrol." With that, she picked up her police cap from the table, put it on, and walked out first.

The others were stunned. Had they said all that for nothing? They looked at each other with deep suspicion in their eyes: was this new patrol leader a fool?

Shen Zhizhen waited at the police station entrance for a while before the Third Patrol Squad members dragged themselves over. She put on her glasses to hide her disdain and asked: "Does our squad have a vehicle?"

They couldn't walk to patrol. The Cross-Border Road was in the International Settlement, at least seven or eight miles away. Who knew when they would get there on foot?

Ma San pointed to the corner of the courtyard: "There are two sidecars, but since we have to pay for the fuel ourselves, basically no one drives them."
