When the previous patrol leader was around, they had some extra money, so they would drive occasionally. Now, they walked everywhere. With their meager monthly salary, it was hard enough to support their families; there was no spare money for gas.

Shen Zhizhen raised an eyebrow. She led everyone to the sidecars and saw they were still quite new. "Clean them up. From now on, we drive whenever we go out."

The others exchanged knowing glances. They understood now: their new patrol leader was a rich girl who didn't lack money. Tsk, no wonder she was so confident. They just hoped she wouldn't be scared off by the cruel reality soon.

Regardless of what they thought, everyone smiled. They quickly cleaned the vehicles; who would want to walk if they could drive?

Ma San, Lin Wu, and He Ergou—the thinner ones—rode with the patrol leader. Ma San stood on the footboard behind the sidecar, holding onto the backrest, while He Ergou shifted gears and accelerated, zooming out.

Wang Jiangsheng, Mu Daqiang, and Huang Dazhi took the other vehicle. Wang Jiangsheng sat in the sidecar, looking at the sidecar in front, chatting aimlessly with Mu Daqiang and Huang Dazhi, who were driving.

Huang Dazhi, worried that "Brother Sheng" would do something rash, advised: "Brother Sheng, don't take it out on the new patrol leader. She won't last long in our squad, so why look for trouble?"

Even if they didn't know if the new patrol leader was a "dragon crossing the river" or a "worm," she would eventually leave, so why bother?

Mu Daqiang added while driving: "Brother Sheng, Dazhi is right. Instead of opposing her, why not butter her up? If the patrol leader is happy, she might give us some perks."

"Have some ambition, buttering her up," Wang Jiangsheng laughed and scolded.

Even if he was unconvinced, what could he do? He couldn't beat her, and the higher-ups had told them to behave. Now, he just hoped this new patrol leader would keep a low profile and not get them killed.

Mu Daqiang: "Our new patrol leader is definitely loaded. Did you see the watch she’s wearing? An Omega costs at least three hundred silver dollars. We couldn't afford that in a year even if we didn't eat or drink." He didn't even have a Shanghai-brand watch yet.

Wang Jiangsheng and Huang Dazhi smacked their lips in envy. They both had watches, but one was an old one passed down from an uncle, and the other was a second-hand item.

Shen Zhizhen, with her keen hearing, listened to her squad members talking about her and a smile appeared on her lips. It was just a watch; in a few days, she would make sure they all had one.

Shen Zhizhen had thought it through clearly by the river that day. She wanted to stir up trouble in Shanghai. She had already decided on her persona: she would be a reckless, unpredictable fool who meddled in everything and fought anyone who provoked her.

After the two sidecars left the police station, they stopped for gas. Seeing the new patrol leader pay twenty silver dollars without blinking, everyone became even more certain that she was a rich girl who had come to the police station just for fun and would leave once she was bored.

As soon as the two sidecars entered the Third Patrol Squad's patrol area, they ran into an assassination. With a bang, a gunshot rang out, and a man not far away was hit and fell to the ground.

He Ergou, who was driving, was startled and quickly stopped the car to find cover. The others nimbly sought shelter behind obstacles.

Shen Zhizhen’s mouth twitched at the sight. She ran straight to the man who had been hit, dragged him to cover, and said: "Hold on, I'll take you to the hospital."

Old Hong’s vision was already blurring. While he still had a shred of consciousness, he stuffed a roll of film into her hand: "Don't let the secret agents get it." Then, he breathed his last.

Shen Zhizhen realized she had been handed something. She raised an eyebrow and tucked the item into her space. Hearing his words, she understood that the people who killed him were secret agents. The gunfire was still continuing.

Shen Zhizhen knew the assassins hadn't left because she had dragged the man into a blind spot. She peeked out, and a bullet hit the corner of the wall.

Shen Zhizhen had already pinpointed that the shooter was on the roof diagonally across from them. She signaled to Ma San, who was hiding nearby, to throw her his Arisaka rifle.

She had roughly calculated that the shooter's position was beyond the range of a pistol; she needed the Arisaka to hit that assassin.

Although Ma San didn't know what the patrol leader was doing, he obediently threw the rifle and the ammunition clip over.

Shen Zhizhen caught the gun, took a few bullets from the clip, and flew out. She aimed and pulled the trigger. With a bang, a person fell from the roof across the street.

Shen Zhizhen continued to lock onto other targets, pulling the bolt and pulling the trigger. With another bang, another person fell from the roof.

The members of the Third Patrol Squad were stunned. Their patrol leader wasn't a fool; she was a sharpshooter! No wonder she dared to come on patrol.

Mu Daqiang nudged Brother Sheng: "Good heavens, one shot, one kill, without even blinking. Let's behave ourselves."

Wang Jiangsheng nodded in agreement. He wouldn't dare provoke her. How many people must she have killed to be this smooth?

They no longer saw their patrol leader as a rich girl; she was a killing machine.

After six shots, the surroundings became quiet. Shen Zhizhen confirmed there were no more lurking assassins and gestured for her squad members to come out.

chapters.title: To Protect or Not
chapters.content:
The members of the Third Patrol Squad didn't dare to delay, their usual laziness completely gone.

He Ergou and Ma San ran over. The bloody scene made their scalps tingle. The men had been shot in the center of their foreheads and had fallen from the roof, their bodies a bloody mess. One shot to the center of the forehead—this marksmanship was both precise and ruthless.

The others were in similar states. Huang Dazhi was even vomited from the sight of the brains on the ground.

Wang Jiangsheng broke out in a cold sweat, swearing to himself that from now on, if the patrol leader told him to go east, he would never go west. This was just too ruthless.

Mu Daqiang and Lin Wu bit the bullet and moved the bodies. They had different thoughts, feeling that if they stuck with the patrol leader, they might actually make a name for themselves.

When everyone had laid out the bodies on the street, the shock they felt upon seeing the six corpses killed by the patrol leader was indescribable. They had been cleaning up the scene separately, thinking that one shot to the forehead was already impressive, but they never imagined it was a shot to the forehead every single time!

There were nine bodies in the open space on the street. Six of them were the assassins killed by Shen Zhizhen, and the other three were either part of the group or innocent bystanders caught in the crossfire; that would have to wait for the investigation results.

Shen Zhizhen was very satisfied with her marksmanship. It was worth the month of practice on the way to Shanghai. Back then, to practice accuracy and to confuse the enemy, she had decided where to aim before every shot—the arm, the heart, the leg, etc. Every hit was a target, but to others, it looked like poor marksmanship.

She had just established a persona for herself as a sharpshooter, and she did it on purpose. The goal was to prevent anyone from linking her to the trio. As long as the events of that month didn't come to light, she, Shen Zhimei, and Wu Dexi would remain safe.

He Ergou walked up to the patrol chief and said quietly, "Chief, we've got a big problem." He held out his hand to show the chief the small wooden plaque.

He had searched the bodies while lifting them just moments ago and found this token. "These people are Japanese puppet agents." The plaque bore the character "Mei," identifying them as agents of the Mei Kikan.

Shen Zhizhen picked up the wooden plaque and examined it. Japanese puppet agents were nothing more than traitors—people bought off by the Japanese to sell their souls and oppress their own countrymen. These people deserved to die, and she hadn't killed the wrong ones; it was just that this "Mei Kikan" was a bit troublesome.

Hmm, it seemed she had caused quite a bit of trouble for Shen San on her very first day of work. She’d likely get a lecture when she got home.

"Forget who they are. We just need to insist on one thing: these people were lawless, killing people in the street. The police patrol arrived at the scene of the shootout, and these killers attempted to shoot the police, so they were shot dead on the spot by the officers." A cold glint flashed in Shen Zhizhen’s eyes behind her sunglasses as she spoke nonchalantly.

At this moment, the members of the Third Patrol Squad walked over and heard this clearly. Everyone nodded to show they understood. This was the sequence of events, after all; if they pulled in any witness, this was the truth. The only question was whether the Bureau Chief could withstand the pressure.

He Ergou frowned and warned, "I'm just afraid that while open spears are easy to dodge, hidden arrows are hard to guard against." That was the Mei Kikan, after all. No one who killed their people ever walked away unscathed; otherwise, they wouldn't be so feared.

"It's fine. As long as they dare to come, I dare to kill." She was just worried she didn't have a legitimate excuse. Whoever attempts to kill a police officer must be prepared to be killed in return. Regardless of which side the dead belonged to, they wouldn't dare admit it openly and could only resort to assassination attempts against her.

When the others heard this, they realized she was planning to go head-to-head. They couldn't help but feel a sense of excitement; they really wanted to see how this would turn out.

"Chief, you wouldn't happen to be getting fired on your first day, would you?" Ma San asked cheekily.

If the Bureau Chief couldn't withstand the pressure, he would have no choice but to fire the patrol chief. As for handing her over, that wouldn't happen—after all, it was a case of legitimate self-defense, and those people had indeed attempted to kill police officers.

Shen Zhizhen blinked upon hearing this. "It wouldn't be that bad, would it? Is our Bureau Chief really that useless?" Seeing everyone nod in unison, she was left speechless.

Shen Zhizhen held up the small wooden plaque and said to everyone, "Go and collect all these little plaques. Don't miss any. We don't know anything about any 'Japanese puppet agents'; what this patrol chief shot dead were criminals who were shooting people in the street with guns."

Everyone understood her intent immediately. She wanted the Mei Kikan to swallow this bitter pill. Several of them set to work and collected all the plaques; including the one in the chief's hand, there were exactly six.

Shen Zhizhen put the wooden plaques into her pocket and casually tossed them into her space. Thinking of that roll of film, her eyes narrowed. This wouldn't be like the cassette tape and codebook Wang Shun had given her last time, would it? That man had died without saying a word, leaving her with no one to ask.

The group waited for a while. They didn't wait for the people from the Huxi Branch, but they did wait for the International Settlement police. After a friendly exchange between the two sides, the matter was eventually taken over by the Settlement Police Department.

Dong Li quite admired Shen Jiu. He smiled and said to her, "If you can't make it at the Huxi Branch, come find me, Dong Li, at the International Settlement Police Department. I'll recommend you for a position as a police inspector."

Shen Zhizhen thanked him with a smile, indicating that they could cooperate more in the future. Both understood the implication.

Currently, both the Settlement and the police stations were on the side that was being suppressed and bullied. With the Japanese momentum at its peak, the Settlement authorities didn't dare to confront them head-on and often had to swallow their pride and concede on many issues.

The police station was in the same boat, perhaps even worse off than the Settlement. If she continued to be responsible for patrolling this area in the future, the two of them could perfectly well join forces to deal with other factions.

Having the Settlement Police Department finalize the case was Dong Li's gesture of sincerity for their cooperation. Regardless of who the mastermind behind this assassination was, as long as the charge of shooting at police officers in the street held up, they wouldn't dare to step forward publicly.

In the office of the Huxi Branch Bureau Chief, Chief Wang hung up the phone and wiped the cold sweat from his forehead. He said to Huang Dashan, "In just this short time, I've had four phone calls. Some were trying to protect them, others were telling me how to handle it."

He truly hadn't expected that such a beautiful girl would shoot dead six Japanese puppet agents on her very first day. Although the Japanese wouldn't admit the identities of those six, everyone knew it in their hearts. Otherwise, why would people be calling him to exert pressure? It was all just to curry favor with the Japanese.

If he didn't handle today's matter, he would offend people; if he did handle it, where would the dignity of the police station be?

Their officers were on a routine patrol when they encountered people shooting and killing others. As a police officer, one had to intervene, right? Especially since those puppet agents had opened fire on the police, attempting to kill them. The new patrol chief shooting the criminals dead to protect the citizens was justifiable anywhere.

How many of their officers had been killed on Yuejie Road? This incident truly made him feel a sense of vindication.

Huang Dashan asked, "So, Chief, are we protecting her, or not?"

Chief Wang already had an idea, but he wanted to hear what his old subordinate had to say. He chuckled, "I can't afford to offend either side. Give me some advice."

Huang Dashan smiled and shared his thoughts, "Subordinate thinks that keeping Shen Jiu on Yuejie Road might just be able to reverse the disadvantageous position of our Huxi Branch."

Huang Dashan admitted he had underestimated her. He thought she was just a pampered girl, but she turned out to be a female demon—her methods were so ruthless.

chapters.title: Reactions from All Sides
chapters.content:
In the afternoon, the Third Patrol Squad's patrol car pulled into the Huxi Branch. After getting out, Shen Zhizhen said to the others, "You guys go back to the office first; I'm going to see the Bureau Chief."

Ma San watched the chief's retreating back. "What do you think the result will be?" After spending a day with her, he found he was actually a bit reluctant to see the new chief go.

Huang Dazhi thought about the Western meal they had at the International Settlement at noon and swallowed hard. "Sigh, I wish the chief could stay. Where else are we going to find such a generous chief?"

Hanging out with Shen Jiu meant having a car to ride in and big meals to eat, and she even took the blame for things herself. Where could you find such a great boss? Plus, she was beautiful and easy on the eyes, even if she was a bit of a cold-blooded killer.

The others nodded in agreement. Although Wang Jiangsheng was still a bit unconvinced, he had to admit that he certainly couldn't afford to treat everyone to a thirty-fabi meal. And after patrolling all afternoon, he had a feeling that if Shen Jiu didn't leave, she would definitely stir up trouble.

At the mention of that Western meal, Lin Wu quickly clutched his stomach. "Oh, I need to go to the latrine." With that, he ran off, clutching his belly.

He Ergou laughed and scolded, "A dog's stomach can't hold two taels of sesame oil." He insisted on eating the steak half-raw like a foreigner, and he had been having diarrhea since they were at the restaurant, forcing everyone to wait for him to finish in the latrine before they could leave.

Huang Dazhi: "Brother Gou, don't talk about yourself." He ran off immediately after saying that.

"You brat, looking for a beating!" He Ergou laughed and chased after him.

The others shook their heads with a chuckle and followed behind toward the Third Patrol Squad office. Along the way, they encountered many curious people asking questions, and the group boasted for a while before returning to the office, feeling quite satisfied.

In the No. 76 conference room, Director Ding Mocun delivered an important speech: "Fellow colleagues, today we gather here to participate in a grand event. The establishment of the Nanjing National Government marks our cause entering a new stage."

"The times are turbulent and precarious; however, it is precisely in these chaotic times that we have found our path and chosen to join hands with Mr. Wang to plan a great undertaking..."

After the Director finished his speech, everyone stood up and applauded. Shen Zhimei thought about how Xiao Jiu had provoked the Mei Kikan on her first day of work, and her hands itched with frustration; she clapped with extra force.

After the meeting, Ding Mocun called Secretary-General Shen into his office. "Xiao Shen, don't blame your sister for what happened today. After all, who could have guessed that the Mei Kikan was carrying out an assassination mission?" Shooting at police in the street and getting killed in return—no matter how you looked at it, the Mei Kikan was in the wrong.

Shen Zhimei replied sternly, "Thank you for your concern, Director. To be honest, I am very worried about my ninth sister's safety, and I hope the Director can help mediate."

Ding Mocun: "That's easy to say. You also need to help me handle things on the Nanjing side."

Shen Zhimei: "Rest assured, Director, I won't speak out of turn."

The two foxes, one old and one young, reached a consensus on the surface. After Shen Zhimei returned from the Director's office and sat down, before she could even take a sip of water, Deputy Director Li Shiqun arrived.

Shen Zhimei invited Director Li to sit down, only to hear that his intention was to get Xiao Jiu into No. 76.

"Director Li, my sister is a troublemaker. She’s been spoiled at home, and I worry that if she comes to No. 76, there will be no peace." Shen Zhimei leaned back in her chair and politely declined.

Li Shiqun was unhappy at being refused. "Secretary-General Shen, you're joking. Your sister is a sharpshooter; wouldn't it be a pity if she didn't come to No. 76?" Hitting the center of the brow with every shot—that kind of marksmanship was perfect for assassinations.

"Director Li, wait a while. If you still insist on my ninth sister joining No. 76, I won't stop you." Shen Zhimei knew that Li Shiqun was greedy and narrow-minded, so she used a stalling tactic.

Of course, she wasn't entirely lying to Li Shiqun. Shen Jiu had managed to provoke the Mei Kikan on her first day; who knew who she would provoke in the coming days? If Li Shiqun was still willing to protect Xiao Jiu then, joining No. 76 for refuge wouldn't be out of the question.

Li Shiqun...

At the Huxi Branch, Shen Zhizhen walked out of the Bureau Chief's office, looking thoughtfully at the end of the corridor, pondering the deeper meaning of the Chief's words as she walked back.

If she hadn't misunderstood, he was telling her to stir up trouble in the Yuejie Road area! Of course, that wasn't how he put it; the Chief said he wanted her to safeguard the public security of the Yuejie Road area, crack down on illegal crimes, and uphold fairness and justice.

In an area filled with all kinds of vices and intersecting dark forces, wasn't doing that exactly what she interpreted as stirring up trouble—muddying the waters to gain an advantage?

Shen Zhizhen returned to the Third Patrol Squad and gave instructions to her team members, then decided to leave work early. Today's events must have annoyed Shen San, so she decided to cook a few hometown dishes to coax her cheap third sister.

After the patrol chief left, the members of the Third Patrol Squad also finished their day. They were quite happy, joking all the way about how the Bureau Chief hadn't been a coward this time.

At the Mei Kikan, in the Chief's office, Kage-sa Zen-sho was wiping his katana while listening to his subordinate, Jing-shen Hao-yi, report.

Jing-shen Hao-yi: "Colonel, that roll of film was not found. Could it have been hidden by that reporter and not carried on his person?"

"Are you sure that police officer named Shen Jiu didn't take it?" Kage-sa Zen-sho's brows were locked, his gaze deep. Six secret agents were dead, and they hadn't even found the item. Baka.

"Baozi said he was watching the whole time. That police officer pulled the reporter, who had been shot and fallen to the ground, to the side, and the reporter died shortly after. During that time, until Shen Jiu opened fire and killed our men, her hands were open the entire time, and she didn't touch her pockets."

He had taken men to the International Settlement police morgue to search, but the film was not found on the three dead men. He had also interrogated several eyewitnesses at the scene, and their accounts matched Baozi's.

Kageza Masateru paused while wiping his katana. "Continue the investigation. Also, you are responsible for killing that meddlesome police officer. Regardless of how justified the reason may be, anyone who kills a member of the Mumei Kikan must pay the price."

"Yes, I will certainly complete the mission." Ibukai Koichi knew that someone from the Nanjing government had interceded, so this matter could not be handled openly; it had to be arranged as an assassination.

That person named Shen Jiu was an incredibly accurate shot. The assassination had to be a one-hit kill, otherwise, the consequence might be another counter-kill.

Kageza Masateru: "Issue a bounty for the assassination in the underworld. Let the gangs get involved as well. Your primary task is to find that roll of film."

Ibukai Koichi: "Yes."

Shen Zhizhen was unaware that an assassination was brewing. At that moment, she had just finished buying groceries at the market and was driving toward Fengyuan Road when she encountered a student protest opposing the establishment of the puppet Nationalist government.

The car was forced to stop at the side of the road. Shen Zhizhen sat in the car waiting for the crowd to pass, her gaze falling on a girl in the parade holding a camera. She blinked—wasn't that the neighbor who lived across from Shen San's house at 36 Fengyuan Road?

Is she a reporter?

They had met while heading to work that morning, so she couldn't be mistaken. Being able to live in a house with gas pipes, this reporter’s family must be quite wealthy.

A shrill whistle blew, and after a gunshot... Chapter 32: Wen Jiao, the Heroine of the Book!

The protesting crowd was dispersed by the police who had rushed to the scene.

Shen Zhizhen started the car and got back on the road. Not long after driving off, she saw the female neighbor walking alone. She slowed down and rolled down the window. "Do you need a ride back to Fengyuan Road?"

Wen Jiao turned her head and recognized her as Shen Zhimei's relative. She glanced at the police uniform she was wearing and smiled charmingly. "Thank you." With that, she opened the door and got in.

"Hello, let's get to know each other. My name is Wen Jiao, and I'm a reporter for *Ta Kung Pao*," Wen Jiao introduced herself with a smile.

Shen Zhizhen replied while driving: "Hello, my name is Shen Jiu, a police officer at the Shanghai West Branch." For some reason, the name "Wen Jiao" felt familiar; she felt like she had heard it somewhere before.

Wen Jiao: "I see you living at Sister Shen's place. What relation are you to her?"

Shen Zhizhen: "I'm her younger sister, here to stay with her for a while."

The two chatted idly like this until they returned to Fengyuan Road, where they got out and went to their respective homes.

Shen Zhizhen put the groceries in the kitchen and poured herself a glass of water. As she gulped it down, a flash of inspiration struck her. Her eyes widened, and she spat the water out with a *pfft*. Wen Jiao, the heroine of the book!

Shen Zhizhen set down the glass and wiped the water from her mouth, struggling to recall the plot of the book. Although she had forgotten most of it, she still remembered the key points. The heroine, Wen Jiao, was the youngest daughter of the wealthy Hangzhou merchant Wen Tingzhou and was indeed a female reporter for the Shanghai *Ta Kung Pao*.

The main setting of the book was always Shanghai. After the male lead, Wan Donglai, returned to the country, he joined the Red Party to avenge his blood feud, using his job at a bank to hide his identity. The book began with the heroine being injured and saved by the male lead, after which the two embarked on a path of red redemption.

That seemed to be the gist of it. Although she couldn't remember the plot and details clearly, she was certain that in the grand finale, the male and female leads waited for the dawn of victory.

Shen Zhizhen took the film out of her spatial storage. In the book, the heroine was introduced to the Red Party by the male lead. She didn't know if they had met yet, but even if she didn't know if the heroine had joined the Red Party, she could at least be sure that the heroine was a good person with a "red heart." Besides, a reporter should know how to develop photos, right?

She didn't know what secrets were on the film, but for something that could make Mumei Kikan agents hunt and kill for it, the secrets inside were likely significant.

The risk of finding a photo studio was too high; it was truly better to ask the heroine to develop them. Thinking this, she put on her shoes, went out, walked across the street, and knocked on the door.

Wen Jiao was in the darkroom developing photos. Hearing the knock, she set aside her work and opened the door to see Shen Jiu. "Oh, it's you. Is there something you need?"

"I have something I'd like to ask for your help with. Can I come in and talk?" Shen Zhizhen said with a smile.

"Ah, please come in." Wen Jiao stepped aside to invite her in and took a pair of slippers from the shoe cabinet for her.

Shen Zhizhen changed into the slippers and followed Wen Jiao to the sofa. She scanned the room casually; the layout was likely the same as Shen San's, with a cozy decor style.

Wen Jiao poured Shen Jiu a glass of water before asking what she needed.

Shen Zhizhen: "Reporter Wen, do you know how to develop film?"

Wen Jiao understood immediately. "I do. I have a darkroom at home, and I develop all the photos I take myself. Are you looking for me to develop a roll of film for you?"

Shen Zhizhen nodded. "Yes, is it convenient? I can pay you."

Wen Jiao: "Sure. I sometimes take on photo developing jobs. Five *fabi* per roll."

Shen Zhizhen took the film from her pocket and placed it on the coffee table along with five *fabi*. "Then I'll leave it to you. I'll head back now."

Wen Jiao saw her out, closed the door, and went to the darkroom. She placed the film on the counter and continued developing the photos she had been working on.

With one worry off her mind, Shen Zhizhen felt exceptionally relaxed and even cooked two extra dishes, totaling six dishes and one soup.

When Shen Zhimei returned home and saw the table filled with her favorite hometown dishes, she glared at Shen Jiu, who was acting quite obediently.

The meal was very much to Shen Zhimei's taste. Her mood improved significantly, and she didn't want to give Shen Jiu a hard time. Of course, the main reason was that, all things considered, Xiao Jiu wasn't in the wrong today.

If it were her, she would have done the same. Those puppet agents had already opened fire to kill you; if you didn't kill them back, were you supposed to just wait to be shot?

Shen Zhimei set down her chopsticks, leaned back in her chair, and looked at Xiao Jiu seriously. "Someone has issued a bounty in the underworld. Thirty thousand silver dollars for your life."

She had heard this news from Director Li before getting off work. His goal, naturally, was to force Xiao Jiu into the 76th Branch to work for him.

Hearing this, Shen Zhizhen replied while cleaning up: "Only that much?" Thirty thousand silver dollars was just three large gold bars. Was her life really that cheap?

Shen Zhimei was amused. She looked at Xiao Jiu's back and teased: "In Shanghai, your life as Young Master Shen is only worth that much."

If she were Xiao Jiu's enemy, she wouldn't choose to kill her. Instead, she would capture her and force her to grave-rob. The value of a major tomb could not be measured in money.

The sisters teased each other for a while, and the atmosphere became much lighter. "You should go back to your hometown."

If Xiao Jiu left Shanghai, she could find people to mediate, offer some concessions, and the matter could be smoothed over. Staying here meant facing endless assassinations. If something really happened, she would never be able to forgive herself.

Shen Zhizhen finished cleaning up and sat in a chair near Shen San, placing a plate of sliced fruit on the table. "I'll leave if you come back with me."

"Why?" Shen Zhimei picked up a piece of watermelon, took a bite, and asked nonchalantly.

Shen Zhizhen: "I'm worried about you being here alone." The 76th Branch—is there anyone there who ends up well?

Shen Zhimei: "Are you going to keep staying here and wait for me to collect your corpse?" Right now, this girl was in much more danger than she was.

Shen Zhizhen...

Wen Jiao looked at the developed photos. They showed a banknote printing factory, but the currency in the photos was not a style she was familiar with. Where did Shen Jiu get these photos?

Wen Jiao couldn't figure it out. She put the developed photos and the negatives into an envelope, thinking that since they were done, she might as well deliver them to Shen Jiu. She put on her shoes, went out, and knocked on the door across the hall.

The knocking interrupted the sisters' conversation. Shen Zhizhen got up to open the door and saw Wen Jiao. Seeing the envelope in her hand, she realized the photos were ready. "So fast?"

Wen Jiao nodded with a smile and said softly, "Yes, developing photos is quite quick. Can I come in?" She wanted to know where the photos came from and what was going on with the currency.

"Oh, it's Wen Jiao. Come in, come in." Shen Zhimei walked over, pulled Wen Jiao inside, and took the envelope of photos.

Wen Jiao looked at her empty hands, feeling a bit flustered as she looked at Shen Jiu. No, she hadn't intended to hand the photos to Shen Zhimei.

Shen Zhizhen was also curious about the contents. Seeing Shen Zhimei open the envelope, she quickly leaned over to look. "Is this a photo of a banknote printing factory?"

"Where did these photos come from?" Shen Zhimei frowned after looking at them.

Shen Zhizhen recounted what happened that day. "The person shoved them into my hand before dying. I didn't know what was in them, so I asked Wen Jiao to help develop them."

After hearing this, Shen Zhimei immediately understood that the Mumei Kikan agents were killing people to find the film. Who would have thought the film would accidentally fall into Xiao Jiu's hands and then be developed by their neighbor, a reporter?

Wen Jiao listened from the side, her heart trembling. This was too exciting. She really hadn't realized Shen Jiu was a sharpshooter.

Wen Jiao looked at Shen Zhimei and asked the question in her heart: "Sister Shen, why would this printing factory be printing such currency?" Chapter 33: Third Sister, I Want to Die Knowing the Truth

Shen Zhizhen was also curious. "Third Sister, I want to die knowing the truth." As soon as she finished speaking, her forehead was flicked.

Shen Zhimei pulled back her hand and scolded with a laugh, "With your prickly personality, even the King of Hell wouldn't take you." She never had a filter on her mouth, saying whatever came to mind.

Although Wen Jiao didn't quite understand, she was amused by the sisters' interesting interaction. It was clear they were very close.

Seeing the two looking at her expectantly for an explanation, Shen Zhimei picked up the newspaper on the table and pointed to the large headline.

"With the new government established, their primary task is to issue currency that benefits them. The currency in the photos is the Central Reserve Bank note that the Nanjing side is preparing to announce and issue next year."

Shen Zhizhen hadn't expected that what was being printed was the Central Reserve Bank note. She had an impression of them; they were a tool for the Japanese to plunder the economy of the occupied areas. Once issued, it would exacerbate inflation in the occupied zones and bring a heavy economic burden to the people.

Shen Zhizhen thought for a moment and said casually: "It's being issued next year, but they're printing it now?"

A cold sneer appeared on Shen Zhimei's lips: "As far as I know, the Nanjing side hasn't even received the templates for the Central Reserve Bank notes yet." And yet the Japanese were already printing them. It was truly laughable.

"I'm taking the negatives. You two had best act like you know nothing about this." She had to go to Nanjing on a business trip tomorrow.

Shen Zhimei took the negatives. Such an important matter had to be reported to her superiors regardless. As for how to negotiate or respond, that was a matter for those above her. For now, she was just "ringing the bell as long as she was a monk." When she didn't want to be a monk anymore, she would leave with Xiao Jiu.

Wen Jiao's family was in business, so she had some knowledge of currency and finance. This Central Reserve Bank note could not be allowed to be issued. If it were, the consequences would be unimaginable. Just imagine, if the Japanese army used their own printed currency to buy supplies in the future, wouldn't it be equivalent to paying only the cost of paper and ink?

Wen Jiao: "I want to report this." This matter couldn't be hidden from the public; it had to be exposed. Hopefully, it could prevent the issuance.

Shen Zhimei looked up and smiled lightly: "Aren't you afraid of being assassinated?"

Wen Jiao’s face turned deathly pale upon hearing this; how could she have forgotten that Shen Zhimei was a member of No. 76.

Shen Zhizhen: "Third Sister, I think a person should have a bottom line." As she finished speaking, her forehead was flicked again.

Shen Zhimei withdrew her hand and looked at Wen Jiao: "You are a journalist, so you should know what a reporter faces once something like this is exposed. If you want to report it, I have no intention of stopping you; you may take the photos." She would only hand the negatives over to the Nanjing side, and naturally, she would ensure Xiao Jiu and Wen Jiao were kept out of it.

Upon hearing this, Wen Jiao realized she had misunderstood Shen Zhimei, but she still insisted on taking the photos. This matter was of great importance, and she had to report it.

Shen Zhizhen was not worried; after all, as the heroine of a book, her fate was set—no matter how dangerous the situation, she would always turn bad luck into good.

Wen Jiao stood up, bowed to the two Shen sisters, and then took her leave.

Shen Zhizhen watched Wen Jiao return to the house across the street before closing the door. She walked back, sat on the sofa, and asked: "Third Sister, what do you think of the new government?" As she finished speaking, she picked up the water glass on the table to drink. She wanted to know what Shen San really thought and whether she was in too deep.

Shen Zhimei lay down lazily and replied bluntly: "A puppet regime, short-lived, and destined to be reviled for eternity." What else could she think? It was obvious.

Shen Zhizhen spat out the water she had just taken a sip of. Because she was looking directly at Shen San, she sprayed it all over her face. She jumped up and ran away before a cushion could be thrown at her.

Shen Zhimei, with her face covered in water, angrily threw the cushion at Shen Jiu. After missing, she stood up, aimed, and threw another one. Only after hitting her target did she go to the bathroom to wash her face.

Shen Zhizhen picked up the cushion, placed it back on the sofa, and walked cheekily to the bathroom door. Leaning against the frame, she defended herself: "I was just shocked by what you said." This woman truly never failed to shock with her words; she was far too bold.

Shen Zhimei snorted and ignored Shen Jiu. After washing her face and drying it, she began applying moisturizer.

"Since you see things so clearly, why are you still working for the Nanjing side?" She was genuinely curious.

"Where did you get the idea that I'm working for Nanjing?" Shen Zhimei put the moisturizer back in its place and said casually.

Shen Zhizhen felt an itch of curiosity and continued to pester Shen San about why she worked for the Nanjing side. When Shen San didn't answer, she kept following her around, nagging.

Unable to bear the pestering, Shen Zhimei finally cleared the young girl's doubts: "The Japanese are invading China. As a university student with thoughts and ambitions, don't you think I should stand up and resist the Japanese?"

At the time, in her school, some actively participated in the anti-Japanese salvation movement, some gave up their pens for the sword to join the fight directly, and of course, some remained calm and continued their studies to plan for the future.

Back then, she was swept up by the anti-Japanese atmosphere at school and acted on impulse. She felt that instead of going home to be a grave robber after graduation, she might as well take this opportunity to change her path. Thus, she joined the White Party and received agent training. Later, she went to Nanjing. How could she have known that her passionate choice back then would lead to this—the faction she followed defected to the Japanese and started an independence movement.

Sometimes, in the middle of the night, when she couldn't sleep, she felt nauseous thinking about it. She, who had always prided herself on being clever, had stumbled badly on such a major decision. Not only was there no hope of changing her path, but she might also be reviled in the family genealogy for eternity.

"I am currently stuck in a quagmire; it takes time to get out." If it were just her, it would be easy, but the massive Shen family was at stake; she couldn't disregard them.

After hearing this, Shen Zhizhen was no longer worried that Shen San would go down the wrong path; instead, she felt a sense of sorrow. No matter how clever, she was still played by reality.

Shen Zhizhen said whimsically: "Third Sister, why don't we join the Red Party? It seems they are the only ones truly resisting the Japanese now." The internal politics of the White Party were too chaotic, with factional strife, corruption, and some even defecting to the Japanese. Of course, the main reason was that she knew the direction of history—the Red Party would eventually win.

"Sure, when you join one day, take me with you." Shen Zhimei didn't want to deal with her sister's flighty ideas, so she gave a perfunctory reply and picked up her pajamas to take a shower.

Shen Zhizhen shrugged. She was just saying it casually; one was a grave robber and the other was a mid-to-high-level official at No. 76—how could the Red Party trust them?

At night, Shen Zhizhen turned off the lights and walked to the window. She lifted a corner of the curtain and peeked out. Seeing some things on the street that weren't usually there, she pursed her lips, let the curtain fall, and went back to bed.

As Shen Zhizhen was about to fall asleep, Shen San’s voice came to her ears: "I’m going to Nanjing on a business trip tomorrow. You take me to the train station."

Shen Zhizhen woke up instantly. Shen San was going to Nanjing? A flash of inspiration struck her: "You deliberately talked about the Central Reserve Bank notes in front of Wen Jiao so that she would report it!"

She knew it! With Shen San's shrewdness and intelligence, how could she tell a reporter about the Japanese printing of Central Reserve Bank notes on the photos? That was clearly not Shen San's style.

Shen Zhimei ignored Shen Jiu, turned over, lay on her side, and closed her eyes to sleep.

Shen Zhizhen's curiosity was piqued again. How could she let her sleep so easily? She poked Shen San's back with her finger: "Aren't you afraid Wen Jiao will sell you out?"

She trusted Wen Jiao because she had read the book, but why did Shen San...

chapters.title: Realization
chapters.content:
In the early morning, Shen Zhizhen opened her eyes, glanced at her watch, rubbed her sleepy eyes, and sat up. She turned to look at Shen San, who was still fast asleep, and resignedly got up to wash and make breakfast.

While cooking, she thought about what Shen San had said last night. Before falling asleep, she had asked why Shen San trusted Wen Jiao, and under her constant pestering, she had finally explained.

It turned out that Shen San had investigated everyone living at 36 Fengyuan Road. She knew exactly who Wen Jiao was, and besides, as long as she took the earliest train to Nanjing today, it wouldn't matter if Wen Jiao betrayed her or not.

At the time, she had silently lit a candle in her heart for the heroine—to be schemed against by Shen Zhimei and then used by her as well.

Shen Zhimei got up, washed, changed her clothes, and took out a small handbag. She packed a few essentials and two changes of clothes, left the bag by the door, and sat at the dining table to eat breakfast with Xiao Jiu.

"My return date for this trip is uncertain. Don't worry if I'm late coming back." Shen Zhimei informed her of the potential situation to keep the young girl from fretting.

Shen Zhizhen: "Ah, isn't it just to deliver some negatives? Why would you be late?"

Shen Zhimei: "Who knows if there will be other tasks."

Seeing that Shen San didn't want to say more, Shen Zhizhen didn't ask further and urged her to be careful.

After breakfast, Shen Zhizhen finished cleaning up, put on her police uniform, and carried the handbag Shen San needed downstairs. The two went down, looked at each other, and got into the car.

These people had been watching all night, which showed the appeal of thirty thousand silver dollars. It made sense; if they risked it for this job and succeeded, they wouldn't have to worry about food or clothing for the rest of their lives.

Shen Zhizhen made sure there was nothing unusual in the car before starting it and driving away from Fengyuan Road.

Five rickshaws followed closely behind. They had been watching all night. As for why they didn't dare to sneak in and assassinate her in the middle of the night, it was naturally because Shen Zhimei, the Secretary-General of No. 76, lived there.

Although they had accepted the job to assassinate her sister, no one dared to touch Shen Zhimei. First, her status was special; second, there were too many powerful figures behind her. If they touched her, their whole families would be finished.

But killing her sister was different; they would only face the retaliation of Shen Zhimei alone. How could a woman's retaliation compare to thirty thousand silver dollars?

Shen Zhimei did not know that because of her high-EQ style of handling things, she had been labeled a "vase" by the upper-class and underworld figures of Shanghai. Especially the gossip about her being the mistress of a high-ranking official in Nanjing made everyone agree that she was a vase that shouldn't be touched.

Shen Zhimei glanced at the rearview mirror and said nonchalantly, "Shake them."

Shen Zhizhen turned the steering wheel, changed roads, and accelerated. After ten minutes of maneuvering, she shook off the rickshaws behind them.

"The rickshaw pullers following us just now have good footwork." With few pedestrians on the road in the morning, it took ten minutes of speeding to shake them off.

"They should all be underworld people, but I don't know which gang they belong to. Be careful yourself and don't be careless," Shen Zhimei said, her lips parting slightly.

The people from the Mō Kikan wouldn't be so blatant. They would only lurk in one place to carry out an assassination, such as setting up an ambush at a high point on Xiao Jiu's usual route to work for a sniper attack.

Shen Zhimei roughly explained the operating styles of the gangs, the Mō Kikan, and the puppet agents: "It's easy to dodge an open spear, but hard to guard against a hidden arrow. Change your route to work at any time so that those people can't figure out your patterns; only then will the risk of being sniped be reduced."

Shen Zhizhen nodded to show she understood and told Shen San not to worry, she would be careful. She dropped her off at the train station and drove away. It wasn't that she didn't want to see Shen San onto the train, but she was worried that those following them would catch up. Shen San was going to Nanjing secretly this time and couldn't let anyone know in advance.

Shen Zhimei withdrew her gaze, put on sunglasses, and walked to the ticket office with her bag. She showed her credentials, bought a sleeper ticket for the train about to depart, then borrowed a phone to call No. 76 to ask for leave. After hanging up, she boarded the train and left Shanghai.

By the Huangpu River, Shen Zhizhen stood on the embankment, looking at the surging river. At her feet lay five men covered in injuries, unable to resist, their eyes filled with fear and despair.

"Today, for the sake of us both being Chinese, I won't throw you into the river," Shen Zhizhen said, looking at the five men on the ground.

Originally, she had wanted to throw these five into the river to feed the fish, which was why she had led them here in the car. But when she wanted to kill them, her heart inexplicably softened, so she gave them a sound beating to vent her anger.

Looking at the surging river just now, she had a realization: she could kill Japanese people without hesitation because they were invading the country, slaughtering the people, and committing countless evils.

But she couldn't bring herself to do it to her own compatriots, even though these people wanted to kill her for money. Sigh, as the saying goes, it's not easy to live in troubled times.

Shen Zhizhen despised herself for being soft-hearted, but she didn't change her mind. Let it be; she couldn't let herself become a killing machine. In these troubled times, things weren't as simple as black and white.

The five men on the ground felt a strange soreness in their eyes upon hearing this. Everyone watched her retreating figure with their own thoughts.

At the Shanghai West Branch, Third Patrol Group office, Shen Zhizhen pushed the door open and saw everyone gossiping about who had issued the thirty-thousand-dollar bounty to kill her.

"You all are quite well-informed. Stop discussing it for now; let's go on patrol." Shen Zhizhen interrupted the group's discussion. Because of that incident, she was a bit late today; if they didn't go on patrol now, it would be noon.

When the group saw the patrol leader arrive, they hurried over to show their concern. Why was the leader so late? Did something happen? They were all but wearing the word "gossip" on their faces.

"Nothing, just taught five rickshaw pullers a lesson," Shen Zhizhen replied casually and walked out.

The others quickly followed. Huang Dazhi even took the time to ask He Ergou: "Brother Gou, who is the leader talking about?" Those who dared to take a bounty assassination job were usually somewhat famous in the underworld.

He Ergou had always been well-informed; it was he who brought everyone the news that a bounty had been placed on the Inspector’s head by someone on the streets.

He Ergou: "All five of them are rickshaw pullers, so they must be the 'Five Rickshaw Tigers' under the big boss from north of the Yangtze."

Upon hearing this, everyone unanimously decided to find out what happened to the Five Rickshaw Tigers after work that evening.

Shen Zhizhen, having keen hearing, naturally caught He Ergou’s words. She waited until the sidecar motorcycle pulled out of the police station before asking He Ergou, who was driving, "What’s the background of these Five Rickshaw Tigers and that big boss from north of the Yangtze?"

He Ergou, keeping an eye on the road while answering the Inspector, explained, "Boss Gu, the big boss from north of the Yangtze, is a member of the Green Gang and the leader of the Subei faction. Boss Gu is known for his generosity and integrity, and he has many followers. Most of the rickshaw companies in Shanghai are owned by him, and those Five Rickshaw Tigers are his capable lieutenants..."

Shen Zhizhen sensed the code of the underworld in He Ergou’s words and felt a bit relieved that she hadn't used lethal force. Despite the gangs' usual misdeeds, heroes often emerge in troubled times, and people in the underworld are often more capable of loyalty and passion. Who knew which cloud might eventually rain down to resist the Japanese?

Shen Zhizhen silently set a bottom line for herself... Chapter 35: What, asking for leave to meet a lover?

At No. 76, in the Secretariat, "What, asking for leave to meet a lover?" A look of surprise flashed in Li Shiqun’s eyes.

Because he was preoccupied with recruiting the sharpshooter Shen Jiu, he had come over as soon as he started work to sound out Shen Zhimei. He felt that rather than being endlessly hunted, she should follow him. He hadn't expected to hear this.

Section Chief Zhang: "Yes, that’s what the Secretary-General said when she called the Secretariat this morning." She had arrived early today and answered the phone herself; she had been quite stunned by the Secretary-General's excuse, and now she felt particularly pleased to see Director Li’s reaction.

Li Shiqun ordered with a serious face, "Check the origin of the call for me."

"Yes." Section Chief Zhang picked up the phone and began to trace it.

Li Shiqun heard that Shen Zhimei’s call had been made from the train station. "Ask which trains were departing during the time Shen Zhimei made the call."

"Report, there was a train heading to Nanjing." Section Chief Zhang informed Director Li of the station's reply.

Li Shiqun turned and left with a dark face. He knocked on the door of the Director’s office and told Ding Mocun about Shen Zhimei going to Nanjing.

"Why would she go to Nanjing at a time like this?" Li Shiqun looked at Ding Mocun with suspicion.

Ding Mocun was lowering his eyes, contemplating Shen Zhimei’s intentions. Hearing Li Shiqun’s suspicious tone, he looked up and said, "I didn't send her. You should know she doesn't answer to No. 76."

Both of them were clear about Shen Zhimei’s role at No. 76. Leaving now, and with such a flimsy excuse, there was definitely something wrong here.

Li Shiqun realized he had misunderstood. "The Nanjing side only announced the establishment of the new government yesterday. Shen Zhimei left Shanghai for Nanjing today—could it be that they summoned her back?"

If that were the case, it would be fine; it would mean she had a new mission there. Hmph, it would be best if she were transferred away from No. 76 and never came back. Otherwise, having eyes constantly watching made it difficult to do anything out of the ordinary.

Ding Mocun leaned back in his chair and replied thoughtfully, "It’s also possible she really did go back to meet a lover."

With the new government established, that person in a high position might naturally want to celebrate with a beauty.

Li Shiqun...

A phone call broke the mutual probing of the two old foxes, followed by the assassination operation launched by No. 76 against the reporters of the *Ta Kung Pao*.

Just a moment ago, the *Ta Kung Pao*, which had delayed its issue today, released an exclusive exposé! The shocking conspiracy of the Japanese secretly printing Central Reserve Bank notes before the establishment of the puppet government had surfaced!

This news hit like a bolt from the blue, causing a massive stir and quickly spreading and fermenting through all levels of Shanghai society. By the time the Japanese and puppet intelligence agencies received the news, it was already too late to stop it.

At this moment, Shen Zhizhen, having just finished a fight, was reading the newspaper. A look of admiration flashed in her eyes. She hadn't expected Wen Jiao to be so capable; it had only taken one night to publish the content from the photos.

Judging by the timing, the draft must have been prepared and printed overnight, which was why the release was delayed. But this was the only way to catch the Japanese side off guard.

Speed is the essence of war; it seemed there was a master at the newspaper office who knew how to seize the perfect moment to report this.

Shen Zhizhen finished reading the paper, put it away, and continued her patrol with the Third Patrol Group. The men lying on the ground only dared to breathe a sigh of relief after she had walked away.

"I can't earn this money, and I don't want to anymore. Gentlemen, take care, I'm leaving." The man who spoke struggled to his feet and limped away.

The others exchanged bitter smiles and helped each other up. Earn, my foot! They couldn't beat her in a fight, and their marksmanship wasn't as good as hers. If that "demon star" hadn't held back, they would be dead or crippled.

The men of the Third Patrol Group were already numb to this. Since the start of the day, the Inspector had encountered seven waves of attackers, and without exception, she had beaten them all to the ground.

In this way, Shen Jiu had made a name for herself in a single day. The entire area along the boundary road knew that such a person had arrived.

He Ergou: "Inspector, this is the edge of Yuyuan Road."

Shen Zhizhen nodded slightly, surveying the area that everyone avoided like the plague.

"The river network here is dense, the nearby fields are undeveloped, and the composition of people in the shantytowns and slums is complex and mixed. Many Wang Jingwei traitors, Japanese puppet spies, gangs, and hoodlums have built nests here, making the public security in this area extremely dire."

He Ergou’s voice dropped significantly as he spoke. Violent incidents like gunfights, assassinations, kidnappings, and extortion happened here from time to time. Several patrolmen from their Western Shanghai branch had already died here. Honestly, he would never come here otherwise, for fear of being caught in the crossfire and losing his life for nothing.

Shen Zhizhen understood. Yuyuan Road in the boundary area was both heaven and hell. The western section was filled with luxurious garden villas housing political dignitaries, tycoons, and expatriates, while simultaneously serving as a gathering place for enemy and puppet forces who used the geographical advantage to engage in illegal activities for profit.

"Are these legal?" Shen Zhizhen asked, pointing to the opium dens, brothels, and gambling houses lining the road.

Shen Zhizhen was a bit confused; in her past knowledge, such places were illegal, but they were everywhere here. Since this was a world within a book, she didn't know how many private settings the author had added.

The men of the Third Patrol Group looked at each other, shaking their heads and then nodding.

Shen Zhizhen was baffled by their attitude. What did that mean? Was it that hard to explain?

Wang Jiangsheng knew the Inspector was new to Shanghai and lacked common sense, so he explained the ins and outs.

"From a legal standpoint, most are illegal, but because they involve too many interests, they are tacitly allowed..." In the past, they would put on a show for the citizens by suppressing unlicensed illegal operators, but since it became an occupied zone, they didn't even bother with the pretense.

Shen Zhizhen raised an eyebrow. In short, those with licenses could operate legally, and those without could operate by paying protection money!

Shen Zhizhen watched a thin man with a shaky, unsteady gait walk out of an opium den and asked, "So, which one of these doesn't have a license?" She planned to pick one and stir up some trouble.

Ma San replied, "None of the ones operating here have business licenses." Business licenses for opium dens, brothels, and casinos were very expensive. Small-scale ones wouldn't buy them anyway; even if they did, without power or influence, they still had to pay protection money, so they might as well just pay that.

Wang Jiangsheng had guessed yesterday that the Inspector wanted to stir up trouble. Seeing her ask this, he immediately understood her intent. Worried that she might act recklessly and bring disaster upon herself, he quickly listed which dens and casinos were under whose protection.

The forces involved in the brothels, opium dens, and casinos here included the Green Gang, Japanese puppets, Wang Jingwei puppets, and high-ranking police officials.

Shen Zhizhen patted Wang Jiangsheng on the shoulder, acknowledging his good intentions. His words were essentially telling her that there was no one here they could move against... Chapter 36: Arrested

A screech of brakes sounded in front of the newspaper office. Manager Zhang walked to the window, peeked out, and saw that the No. 76 agents had arrived. He immediately realized they were here to make arrests and turned to his junior brother, saying, "The agents are here to make arrests. You must take Wen Jiao and leave."

Wan Donglai frowned slightly. "Let's go together. It's too dangerous for you to stay."

Manager Zhang: "I won't be in danger. They wouldn't dare arrest reporters from the newspaper on a large scale. These people are here for Wen Jiao. You must take her and go."

Because of Wen Jiao’s insistence, the report had been published under her name. Since the agents had chosen to make a public arrest, they must have found a pretext to act.

Although Wen Jiao was terrified, she firmly believed she had done the right thing. Whoever’s name was on the piece would face the same fate of assassination; she couldn't implicate others because of her own fear of death.

A look of realization flashed across Wan Donglai’s face. The Japanese adopted a policy of "using Chinese to control Chinese," and large-scale public persecution of reporters could trigger a stronger backlash in public opinion or even incite popular resistance. The Japanese usually resorted to assassination to deal with people who had influence over public opinion.

Wan Donglai told his senior brother to take care, then turned and signaled for Wen Jiao to follow. As they reached the stairwell, they saw the agents coming up and quickly headed toward the third floor.

Wang Hezi led his men into the newspaper office, holding a photo and looking for Wen Jiao, claiming they were arresting a Communist. Finding no one on the first floor, he led his men upstairs to search.

Wan Donglai locked the door and walked to the window. "We'll climb down from here. Don't be afraid; as long as you hold onto the drainpipe, you won't fall."

Wen Jiao nodded, her face pale. There was no room for hesitation; she knew what she would face if caught.

Wu De had gone to the rickshaw company early this morning to pick up a new rickshaw. He had been happily pulling passengers for two hours when his legs started to feel uncomfortable, so he stopped at the corner of the newspaper office building to rest.

He took out a scallion pancake baked by Xi Ya and started eating. He had only taken two bites when two sedans rushed over and stopped in front of the newspaper office. Seven or eight men in fedoras and black Zhongshan suits, carrying guns, jumped out and stormed into the building.

Wu De chewed his pancake while craning his neck to watch. Although he had only been here for a few days, he had seen plenty of such arrests, which had overturned many of his initial impressions of Shanghai.

He had originally thought Shanghai was a prosperous and bustling metropolis—even as an occupied zone, it had to be better than his hometown. Now, he felt that troubled times were the same everywhere.

Noticing movement above, he looked up and saw a man and a woman climbing down the drainpipe. Seeing the woman’s clumsy movements, he worried that the two of them might slip and fall on him. He moved his rickshaw aside, then pretended not to see them, continuing to eat his pancake while craning his neck to watch the show.

Wan Donglai had noticed the rickshaw below long before. He had watched clearly as the puller spotted them and moved the vehicle, since looking from above gave him a clean angle downward, and the face of the man pulling the rickshaw fell right into his line of sight. His brow gave a slight furrow. Why would that kid be in Shanghai?

But then his heart eased. He didn't know what the brat was doing in Shanghai, but he would be useful all the same.

Wen Jiao's legs were trembling so badly she didn't dare look down, keeping her eyes fixed on a spot just in front of her as she inched her way down the wall, her palms burning with pain but she didn't dare loosen her grip by a fraction.

By the time the two of them touched the ground, both were drenched in sweat, and someone above had already spotted them. Wan Donglai shoved Wen Jiao into the rickshaw and said to the thoroughly startled puller, "Little cousin, do me a favor and get her somewhere safe to hide. I'm counting on you." Without waiting for Wu De to respond, he turned and ran, drawing the agents away.

Wu De's eyes went wide. Wan Donglai! What was he doing here? There was no time to think. He yanked the rickshaw canopy down immediately, picked up the shafts, and ran as fast as his legs would carry him, terrified of getting tangled up in this mess.

Wen Jiao sat in the carriage breathing in ragged gulps, one hand gripping the side rail and the other clutching her collar shut. Two of her coat buttons had been torn off on the way down.

Before turning the corner, Wu De glanced back, and his heart immediately sank. Wan Donglai had been caught! He put everything into his legs and ran harder. Damn it, that worthless Wan Donglai had better not sell him out.

He thought about how he had been pushed around by Wan Donglai since they were kids, and felt a surge of irritation. He and Shen Jiu were the same age and had always played together as children, and the Wan family and the Shen family knew each other well, so Wan Donglai was always turning up at the Shen family pawnshop to find Shen Jiu. That guy, older than both of them, was always showing off his brains, only to be utterly outclassed by Shen Jiu every single time. Then the worthless lout would take his wounded pride out on him.

His childhood trauma, beyond what Shen Jiu had contributed, had come almost entirely from Wan Donglai. Wu De ran on, his regret growing with every step. Why had he just agreed to take on this trouble? It had to be a deeply conditioned reflex from years of being pushed around by Wan Donglai.

Wen Jiao couldn't see what had happened to Mr. Wan because the canopy was blocking her view. She had heard Mr. Wan call this puller his little cousin just now, and assumed he was a contact Mr. Wan had arranged in advance.

Worried about Mr. Wan's safety, she said softly to the puller, "Should we go back and help Mr. Wan?" She had said this because she could see how fast he was running.

Wu De rolled his eyes at the question and didn't bother answering. He ducked into every side lane he could find, turning this way and that without pause, until he was certain they were safe, then slowed back down to the main road and made his way at a normal pace to the rented room near the pier.

Wang Xiya was tidying the room. They had rented this small courtyard with the money Jie had given them. It wasn't large, but it was close to the pier, which was the main draw. De-ge had said that in a few days they would put up a stall near the pier with some tables and benches, and sell meals there.

Sounds came from the courtyard, and Wang Xiya wondered why De-ge was back at this hour. Hadn't he said that today after picking up the rickshaw from the depot, he would spend the afternoon doing test runs, then come find Jie in the evening to give her their address?

Wang Xiya came out holding a washbasin and found De-ge helping a pretty woman out of the rickshaw. The woman's collar was open and her hair was disheveled. One look and you could tell she had been subjected to unwanted advances.

Wang Xiya's eyes went wide in an instant. The nerve of him! Barely arrived and already up to no good, and he had the gall to bring the woman home with him. She was so angry she hurled the basin of dirty water she'd been using to rinse cleaning rags straight at him.

It hit Wu De dead on. Water ran down his head and face, and the sight of him was indescribably comical.

Wen Jiao covered her mouth with her hand, staring at the stout woman in the doorway in alarm. Her only thought was that she was terrifyingly fierce.

Wu De spat the water from his mouth, hurried to close and latch the gate while he still had his wits about him, then came back and pulled Wang Xiya inside. "What do you think you're doing, throwing water at me."

"Wu De, let me tell you something. You are my man now. Whether I use you or not is one thing, but you are not available to others." Wang Xiya was firm on this point and had her own complete theory about it.

Wu De heard this and knew it was a misunderstanding. He held his temper and explained the situation.

Wang Xiya blinked. A misunderstanding! Her combative energy deflated somewhat.

Wen Jiao had followed them inside and heard the entire exchange, and felt both embarrassed and indignant.

Wu De looked at his dim-witted wife and said, "Keep her hidden and safe. I'm going to find Jie and let her know. We need to figure out what to do about this." He turned and headed out.

Wang Xiya nodded right away. "Yes, De-ge, off you go. Don't worry, I'll hide her properly."

By now she had also noticed that the two of them hadn't so much as exchanged a glance since coming in. It really had been a misunderstanding on her part. Though how was she supposed to know that going out for one afternoon could lead to something like this.

chapters.title: Reciprocity
chapters.content:
Shen Zhizhen clapped Wang Jiangsheng on the shoulder and said with a serious expression, "The criminals on Yuyuan Road are brazen and reckless, repeatedly assaulting officers and openly flouting the law. Come with me. We're going to bring these criminals in." With that she took the lead and walked straight toward the nearest opium den.

The members of the Third Patrol Unit exchanged glances, and understood immediately what the patrol captain was doing. They had wondered all along why every time they were attacked, the captain let the assailants go. So this was why she had been holding back!

Everyone felt both nervous and excited. The captain was about to bring down the whole order on Yuyuan Road. This was incredibly thrilling. They hurried to catch up.

Wang Jiangsheng's mouth twitched slightly. So the words he had just said had been for nothing.

Ma San clicked his tongue and sidled up to the captain. "Captain, aren't you worried we might not make it out of Yuyuan Road today?"

The others all looked at the captain at once, hoping she would think it over.

Shen Zhizhen shrugged with complete indifference. "Then we each rely on our own abilities."

She would be doing herself a disservice if she didn't take something back after everything she had been put through today. Hmph. Today she would make sure the forces lurking behind all of this understood that coming after her had a price.

With that thought, she glanced down at the police uniform she was wearing. Tsk, having a righteous justification was the superior strategy. Today she would play this completely above board, and see what they could do about it.

The Third Patrol Unit heard this and grasped the captain's meaning immediately. They fell into action with full cooperation. Whatever happened, they had the captain to bear the sky if it fell. What did they have to fear.

"Police, routine inspection!" "Police on duty! Everyone stop what you are doing and submit to inspection!"

Yuyuan Road was not going to be peaceful today. Every gambling den, brothel, and opium parlor in the area was turned upside down by police from the West Shanghai Precinct.

These officers were thoroughly merciless. They would inspect a place, and the moment it was tidied back up and ready to reopen, they came back again, overturning everything in another round before leaving.

When the protected factions tried invoking the backing figures behind them, the officers refused to be moved at all. On the surface they maintained a perfectly professional, by-the-book demeanor. If anyone dared lay a hand on them, that was all the better, it was practically handing them the very rope to hang themselves with, and a whole stack of charges would come raining down that could only be settled by concession and compensation.

The name Shen Jiu appeared very quickly before the leaders of every major faction, and the phone in the West Shanghai Precinct director's office was nearly ringing off the hook.

After Director Wang had heard the situation from all sides, his response to every person who called was essentially the same. "Ah, the criminals on Yuyuan Road have gotten entirely too brazen. Not even one full day has passed and they dared to assault officers seven separate times. If they treat the police this way, imagine how ordinary citizens must fare. For the safety of the merchants and residents of Yuyuan Road, a thorough inspection is absolutely necessary. Rest assured, this is simply a routine check. Once the inspection is complete on our end, we will withdraw."

Huang Dashan waited until the director had hung up, then said with a furrowed brow, "Is Patrol Captain Shen doing this to get the underworld to rescind the assassination order?" This one was truly no ordinary person. She was playing it completely above board, perfectly within the rules, and those people had no choice but to swallow the bitterness in silence.

Director Wang lit a cigar, took a pull, and then said, "That's right. They certainly didn't expect to end up trapping themselves."

The assassination order had been put out through underworld channels, with several gangs all involved. Hmph. They wanted to kill someone and collect the bounty, but they didn't have the ability, and instead stirred up a hornet's nest against themselves.

At Nanjing Railway Station, Shen Zhimei walked out of the arrivals exit carrying her bag, and when her gaze fell on the license plate of the black sedan parked up ahead, a flicker of calculation passed through the eyes behind her sunglasses.

Her teacher had sent his own car to meet her! The faintest suggestion of a smile touched the corner of Shen Zhimei's mouth. She walked over, opened the car door, and got in, and seeing a familiar face at the wheel, said with a teasing tone, "Sorry to have Chen the great secretary make the trip personally."

Chen Jingzhou was her teacher's classified affairs secretary. Having him come to collect her, Shen Zhimei understood in her heart that the Central Reserve Certificate matter had been reported in the press.

Chen Jingzhou's eyes were warm with a smile. "Not at all. It is my honor to come and meet Miss Shen." Someone this young who had already earned such deep regard from the minister, he absolutely could not afford to treat lightly.

Chen Jingzhou started the car and pulled away from the station. "The minister's meeting ends at four. I'll take Miss Shen home to rest first."

Shen Zhimei checked her watch and smiled her agreement. The two of them chatted as they drove, with Chen Jingzhou giving her a detailed overview of the current situation in Nanjing.

Shen Zhimei listened while turning everything over in her mind. From the ease with which her teacher had tracked her movements, it was clear that this man, holding real power, had a very deep grip on the new government......

Her house here was near Sipailou. She had purchased it when she first came to Nanjing to study, and had barely lived there two years before the Japanese army pressed toward Nanjing, the National Government relocated to Chongqing, and her school moved along with it. The house had stood empty ever since.

After she began working in Shanghai, she came back to Nanjing from time to time, so she had simply hired someone to clean the place twice a week. No matter when she returned, the house was always clean and tidy.

Shen Zhimei did not invite Secretary Chen inside. There was less than an hour until four o'clock, just enough time for a quick wash and a change of clothes.

The house was a detached small building, twice the floor area of her Shanghai residence. Her father had made the decision to buy it.

Shen Zhimei went inside, changed her shoes, walked to the window to open it and let in some air, then went to the bathroom to freshen up. She changed into a crisp new military uniform, glanced at the two plum blossom insignia on her collar tabs, and went out.

The black sedan stopped in front of number 164 Zhongshan East Road. Shen Zhimei opened the car door and stepped out, then followed Secretary Chen into the Ministry of Finance.

In the minister's office, Shen Zhimei stood before the desk and gave a military salute to the middle-aged man seated in the black leather chair. "Minister."

Zhou Fuhai waved a hand, signaling her to sit. "No need for such formality between teacher and student."

Shen Zhimei sat down obediently, a smile on her face. "Congratulations on your promotion, Teacher."

The slightly heavyset, bespectacled man before her was called Zhou Fuhai, holding key positions across multiple departments of the new government and the highest authority over the Finance, Police, and Special Affairs divisions.

To say that the people at Number 76 were wary of her was really to say they were wary of this man. He was also her teacher, though certain people always chose to view their relationship through a lens of suspicion, and so there was always a stream of ambiguous gossip circulating outside.

Zhou Fuhai looked at his most accomplished student, and a subtle gleam passed through his eyes, though the thick lenses of his glasses obscured it.

After Shen Zhimei had finished reporting the purpose of her visit, he glanced at the envelope on the desk containing the negatives, and said, "You deliberately had that reporter publish the story?"

The certainty in his tone made clear he had already seen through his student's thinking entirely.

Shen Zhimei dared not conceal anything upon hearing this; she recounted her plans in detail, though she polished her wording, fearing her teacher might be troubled by such a desperate measure. "I acted on my own initiative, and I hope you will not blame me, Teacher."

Her teacher was a man who combined shrewdness, greed, pragmatism, and opportunism; patriotism had never existed in his past record. She dared say that if the new government were to falter, he would be the first to abandon it.

When dealing with such a fickle, deep-seated, and calculating man, one needed to be frank and direct while offering appropriate displays of loyalty.

Zhou Fuhai nodded with satisfaction. He had to admit that this student always handled matters in a way that pleased him. Only by reporting the Japanese military's private printing of Central Reserve Bank notes and making it public could they gain more bargaining chips for the new government.

Zhou Fuhai signaled that this matter was settled and stood up, saying, "Accompany me for a walk..." Chapter 38... Plan?

The black sedan stopped by the river. The teacher and student stepped out, walked onto the embankment, and strolled along the path in the direction of the current.

Shen Zhimei looked at the surging river with a calm expression, secretly guessing what important matter required them to come here to avoid prying ears.

Zhou Fuhai asked about her recent situation, "I heard your sister went to Shanghai."

Shen Zhimei, trailing half a step behind, replied with a smile, "Yes, she quarreled with the family and ran to me. I placed the girl in the West Shanghai Branch, but I didn't expect her to cause trouble for me on her very first day."

Zhou Fuhai looked interested. "Oh, tell me about it." He had been hearing the name "Shen Jiu" quite often lately.

Upon hearing her teacher mention Xiao Jiu, Shen Zhimei understood that everything about her had already been thoroughly investigated. Though she didn't know why her teacher brought her up, she cooperated and explained that Shen Jiu had shot a puppet agent from the Mei Special Service Agency and had been issued an assassination order.

Zhou Fuhai said, "Your sister is capable. Go back and have a good talk with her; tell her to cooperate with your work from now on."

Shen Zhimei’s brow twitched at these words. "What does Teacher mean? Please, enlighten me."

Mentioning Xiao Jiu and asking her to cooperate meant there was a new task, one related to the Shen family's background.

Zhou Fuhai did not realize his thoughts had been guessed; had he known, he would have lamented that his student was devilishly intelligent.

"Ten days ago, an informant I have in Japan sent back news that Japan is executing a mission in China called the 'Takamagahara Plan'."

Shen Zhimei silently read the words. She knew what Takamagahara meant. "Takamagahara is the heavenly kingdom of the gods in Japanese mythology, also known as the Heavenly Divine Realm."

Zhou Fuhai replied, "Correct." Seeing his student’s puzzled look, he explained as they walked.

The Japanese Takamagahara Plan was actually a search for the tomb of the Phoenix Emperor of the ancient Feng Kingdom. Legend had it that the tomb contained a passage to the Nine Realms, which in ancient Feng mythology were also called the Divine Realms.

Shen Zhimei’s eyes flashed with mockery. The Japanese were quite adept at the "covering one's ears to steal a bell" routine. "The Japanese believe the Nine Realms are their own Heavenly Divine Realm." How shameless must one be to forcibly associate another country's treasures with one's own?

Zhou Fuhai nodded and continued, "The person in charge of this mission is Tanaka Tomoya, who currently holds the identity of a senior Japanese archaeology professor."

Shen Zhimei understood the implication—there was a "current" identity, so there must have been a "former" one. "And his former identity was?"

Zhou Fuhai said, "Tanaka Tomoya's Chinese name is Bai Wenye. He was expelled from the Bai family of Western Hunan five years ago and went to Japan, where he gained the trust of the Japanese Emperor. This time, he has come to China with a secret imperial order."

After receiving the news, Zhou Fuhai had launched an investigation. This man had stayed in Fengtian for over a month, constantly searching for the ancient Feng Kingdom’s treasure map, and had even slaughtered the entire family of a wealthy merchant named Wan to obtain it.

Zhou Fuhai continued, "I have received confirmed intelligence that the map Tanaka is looking for is indeed the one for the Phoenix Emperor’s tomb. That map was divided into three parts back then, and their current whereabouts are unknown. I am entrusting the task of finding the map to you.
