Remember, the Phoenix Emperor’s tomb belongs to us; the Japanese must not be allowed to lay a finger on it."

This matter was of great importance. He had thought for a long time about whom to entrust it to; it had to be someone he trusted implicitly. Zhimei was his best student, but she was too smart—a trait that was both good and bad.

The girl always did things that were uncontrollable, so he hadn't initially intended to give the task to her.

But as more information surfaced, he realized that Shen Zhimei, with her background in grave robbing, had a distinct advantage.

Shen Zhimei replied, "Yes, I will certainly not fail the mission." Beyond this firm, ringing response, she had no other options; for now, she could only take things one step at a time.

Thinking of this, Shen Zhimei decided to plan a retreat for her family in advance. "Teacher, since my sister and I will be snatching food from the mouths of the Japanese, I fear our family might be targeted. I would like to arrange for them to go to Hong Kong."

Zhou Fuhai nodded in agreement without much thought; one could only work without worries if their family was settled.

In Shanghai, on Yuyuan Road, Shen Zhizhen saw it was getting late and decided to call it a day. "Pack up, we’ll continue tomorrow." The Third Patrol Squad returned with their spoils.

The motorcycle sidecar entered the West Shanghai Branch. Shen Zhizhen got out, took six rolls of silver dollars from the box of "reparations" extorted from the merchants, and handed them to Wang Jiangsheng. "Take these and distribute them among the men. Once you're done, you can head home. I’m going to the Chief’s office to turn in the fines." With that, she took the box and headed to the Chief’s office.

The men of the Third Patrol Squad watched their patrol leader leave and silently gave her a thumbs-up. Brilliant—the patrol leader had labeled the merchants' reparations as "fines" to give to the Chief. For the sake of the money, the Chief would have to keep protecting her for a while longer.

With one roll of one hundred silver dollars per person—equivalent to five months' salary—the men were all smiles as they happily headed home.

When Shen Zhizhen arrived at the Chief’s office, Huang Dashan was also there. After reporting his work with a serious face, she placed the box on the desk. "Chief, this is the fine collected today. Please take a look." She opened the box, revealing a chest full of silver dollars and a dozen gold bars.

Chief Wang’s eyes flashed with satisfaction; it was worth the effort he had spent today. He smiled, offered a few words of encouragement, and gestured for her to keep up the good work.

Shen Zhizhen breathed a sigh of relief as she left the office, casting a deep, meaningful glance back at the closed door before walking away.

The black sedan drove through the streets of Shanghai. Perhaps because she had taken a detour, she encountered no attacks all the way home.

Shen Zhizhen parked the car on the side of the road and looked around. Very good—there were at least three groups watching. Her gaze lingered for a moment on a rickshaw by the road, then she feigned indifference and walked toward 36 Fengyuan Road.

As she walked, she wondered why Wu De had come to find her. Upon reaching the second floor, she saw that Wen Jiao’s door had been sealed, and she noticed the curtains move. Her expression darkened—there was someone inside. A flash of insight struck her: the three groups of people outside might not necessarily be targeting her.

Shen Zhizhen calmly took out her key, opened the door, and went inside. She turned on the gramophone, and a Suzhou-style "Song of the Four Seasons" began to play. She returned to her room, changed into casual clothes, put on a wig and sunglasses, and opened the door a crack to observe the opposite side. With her heightened senses, she could clearly detect whether the watchers were near the windows.

Taking advantage of a moment of laxity from the watchers, she slipped out, quickly ducked into the stairwell, and then walked toward the main entrance with a steady demeanor.

Wu De was crouching by the side of the road on Fengyuan Road, using a rickshaw as cover, occasionally observing the anomalies around him.

For instance, the man selling cigarettes to the front-left—people buying cigarettes looked impatient. The two men reading newspapers near the phone booth to the front-right—they had been reading those same newspapers when he observed the terrain an hour ago.

And there was the black sedan parked across from the entrance of No. 36. The people in the car, the cigarette seller, and the newspaper readers all shared one common trait: they were constantly staring at the gate of No. 36.

Wu De watched while waiting for Shen Jiu. Seeing her return, he didn't dare approach her rashly. After locking eyes with her, he waited patiently for his "little cousin" to come out and find him... Chapter 39: Discussing Opening a Shop.

Once the disguised Shen Jiu got into the rickshaw, Wu De pulled it away briskly. The watching groups glanced at them and continued to monitor No. 36.

Wu De knew his little cousin had exceptional hearing, so he whispered the situation while pulling the rickshaw.

After listening, Shen Zhizhen realized the plot of the book was already unfolding. With the hero and heroine getting involved with them, did this mean they had already intervened in the story?

Alas, it was a pity she hadn't memorized the plot; she had missed out on a cheat code for nothing.

Shen Zhizhen hadn't wanted to interfere, believing the hero and heroine had their own fates in the book.

If she didn't intervene, someone else would save them. But then she thought, that wasn't right. She wasn't from this world; perhaps because of her appearance, the world of the book had already changed.

Just like how she shouldn't have met the heroine, yet she did, and even facilitated the reporting on the Central Reserve Bank notes, exposing the Japanese conspiracy ahead of time.

In the book, the hero had always used his identity as a foreign firm comprador as cover, but now that he had been caught by the 76th Branch, she couldn't imagine how he would continue to use that identity—unless, of course, the hero hadn't been caught in the original book.

Wu De pulled the rickshaw to avoid the crowd. Seeing Shen Jiu remained silent, he asked, "Wan Donglai has been caught. Are we going to save him?" Although he disliked the kid, he wouldn't let him die.

Shen Jiu had said the Shen family pawnshop was burned because of the Wan family. If they didn't save him, wouldn't the Wan family line be cut off?

Shen Zhizhen didn't know her little cousin was thinking about the extinction of a family line. She rubbed her temples and replied, "Let's understand the situation first." She would talk more after meeting Wen Jiao.

The man had been caught by the 76th Branch; the risk of saving him alone was too great, and if things went wrong, it could implicate Shen San.

Yet, not saving him didn't sit right. The Wan family had only this one seedling left, and Wan Donglai was the hero of the book and a Red Party activist—there was no reason not to save him.

When Wu De pulled the rickshaw home, the sky had already darkened. He pulled the vehicle into the courtyard and turned to close the gate.

Shen Zhizhen got out and surveyed the small courtyard. It was filled with the aroma of food; it seemed Xi Ya had already finished cooking. She waited for Wu De to join her before entering the house.

Seeing her sister arrive, Xi Ya hurried to welcome her inside. Wu De saw no one else and asked, "Where is that woman?"

Wang Xi Ya replied, "She left."

"Left?" Wu De asked in disbelief, his voice rising.

A flash of surprise crossed Shen Zhizhen’s eyes. Wen Jiao had actually left; she hadn't expected that.

Wang Xi Ya nodded. "Yes, she asked me who you went to find. After I told her your sister's name, she said she had something to do and left."

Wu De: "And you didn't stop her?"

Wang Xi Ya looked puzzled. "Why would I stop her if she wanted to leave? Besides, you only told me to hide her, not to keep her from leaving."

Shen Zhizhen felt thoughtful. Why would Wen Jiao leave? Could it be because of Shen Zhimei? That made sense—unless one had absolutely no other choice, one wouldn't place their own safety in the hands of a secret agent's sister.

After thinking it over, Shen Zhizhen signaled for the young couple to stop arguing. "It’s over, let’s not worry about it. Let’s eat first." It had been a long time since she’d had Xiya’s home-cooked meals, and she found she quite missed them.

The couple immediately fell silent and scrambled to the kitchen to serve the rice and dishes. They squeezed together at the doorway, and Xiya gave Wu De a shove with her hip, sending him stumbling out.

Shen Zhizhen found this hilarious; there was never a dull moment living with these two characters.

Wu De rubbed his nose, too embarrassed to look back at Shen Jiu, and hurried after Xiya into the kitchen.

Shen Zhizhen washed her hands, sat down at the dining table, and tapped her fingers lightly on the surface. If things followed the plot, the female lead should be out looking for someone to rescue the male lead. She just wondered how much Wen Jiao knew at this stage.

Regardless, now that Wan Donglai had been captured, the Red Party would certainly find a way to save him. As for when they would strike, that remained to be seen, but it was a matter worth keeping an eye on.

The couple soon brought the food out. Shen Zhizhen saw it was *fanbao* (vegetable wraps). Xiya had already mixed the vegetables, so Shen Zhizhen rolled up her sleeves, picked up a leaf, and wrapped a portion. One bite was full of that authentic Northeast flavor.

The three chatted while eating. Shen Zhizhen told the couple about Wan Donglai and Wen Jiao so they could be mentally prepared.

As soon as Wu De heard it involved the Red Party, he asked anxiously, "Are we in danger now?"

Wang Xiya stuffed a vegetable wrap into her mouth, started preparing the next one, and pricked up her ears to hear what they should do next.

Shen Zhizhen replied, "Nothing is absolute. You two should be careful. If things look wrong, just pull out."

Although she had confidence in the female lead’s character, what if something went wrong and she was captured and couldn't withstand the torture, leading them to be exposed? It was better to be cautious.

After thinking it over, she told Wu De to rent two separate courtyards, keeping one for her as a backup, preferably in a location with convenient transportation or near a canal.

Wu De nodded, understanding her meaning—it was for an easy escape.

He never expected Wan Donglai to be involved with the Red Party. He decided he would stay far away from that idiot in the future.

Wang Xiya took a moment to ask a question relevant to her: "Sister, can I still run my stall?"

Shen Zhizhen: "Yes, but be more vigilant."

Wang Xiya: "Sister, then why don't you find Dezi a different way to make a living?"

Shen Zhizhen: "What’s wrong?"

Wang Xiya: "His legs haven't fully healed. He ran for so long today that his legs are swollen like wooden stakes." She had only realized his legs were swollen when he nearly fell over in the kitchen earlier.

Wu De blinked and quickly shook his head: "No need, I’ll be fine after a rest." He hadn't expected to run into Wan Donglai, which had caused him to run around for nothing.

Shen Zhizhen leaned over to look at her young cousin’s legs. They were indeed as swollen as Xiya said. "We aren't short on money. Using a rickshaw as a cover is fine, but there's no need to make pulling one your livelihood."

Wu De nodded in agreement: "Understood. Once I’m familiar with the roads in Shanghai, I’ll figure something else out." He hadn't intended to stay in that line of work for long anyway.

Thinking of Wu De’s expertise, Shen Zhizhen suggested, "How about I open an antique shop and you manage it?"

If she were doing it on her own, she would definitely choose to open a pawnshop, as that was the family business and she was familiar with it.

But considering Wu De’s skills and the fact that she still had to work as a police officer for a while, opening an antique shop was a better fit. Both of them were well-versed in the trade, and even if she weren't around, her cousin could hold down the fort.

A look of contemplation crossed Wu De’s eyes. He might not be cut out for a pawnshop, but with his eye for antiques, he could certainly manage an antique store. He nodded and agreed to the plan.

The two discussed the shop while eating. They decided she would provide the capital and open the shop within the International Settlement, which was relatively less chaotic than other areas. Once Wu De’s legs recovered, he would look for a storefront and suppliers.

By the time they finished eating, it was completely dark. Shen Zhizhen gave her final instructions and got up to leave.

Wang Xiya: "Dezi, you rest and wash the dishes. I’ll go see Sister off."

Wu De...

chapters.title: Assassination
chapters.content:
Outside the Shen family estate, a black horse galloped toward them. The sentry was about to intercept it, but upon seeing it was the Second Master, he quickly let him pass.

Shen Jingshan stopped his horse in front of the Shen ancestral home, dismounted, tossed his whip to the doorman, and strode inside.

"Listening to the tragic cries, my heart feels as if it's being pounded; why do you wail so bitterly when we meet..." Shen Jingshan lifted the curtain and entered, the mournful, winding melody of a Peking opera playing from a record player.

Seeing his older brother lying on the *kang* (heated brick bed), smoking and tapping along to the rhythm, Shen Jingshan scoffed—what a comfortable life he led. He took off his hat, hung his coat on the rack, took off his shoes, and climbed onto the *kang*.

Shen Tingshan opened his eyes, saw it was his younger brother, and sat up. "Why are you back at this hour?" He placed his pipe on the *kang* table and poured his brother a cup of hot tea.

Shen Jingshan: "Zhimei called." A sip of hot tea warmed him, dispelling much of the chill.

Shen Tingshan: "What did she say?" It must have been something important for his brother to make the trip.

"She wants us to take our people to Hong Kong and set up some businesses." Shen Jingshan set down his teacup, his expression serious. They were speaking in code; this was the translation of their conversation.

Shen Tingshan was stunned. He frowned and thought for a moment before saying, "Zhimei wants us to go to Hong Kong?" And to take people with them? Was this an order to evacuate Shenyang? What had happened to make Zhimei reach this decision?

Shen Jingshan: "I suspect there’s been a change in circumstances, or that what she’s planning will put us in danger. Otherwise, she wouldn't have asked us to leave." He had ridden to the Shen estate immediately after hanging up the phone, pondering her meaning the whole way. It had to be one of those two reasons.

"What about Little Jiu?" Shen Tingshan asked with a frown.

Shen Jingshan: "She said Little Jiu is doing fine there and we don't need to worry; she has her own arrangements."

The original intention for sending Little Jiu to Zhimei was for the sisters to support each other in these chaotic times. But now, if what Zhimei was doing was dangerous, yet she insisted on keeping Little Jiu with her, it didn't seem simple at all...

At midnight, at 36 Fengyuan Road, the door of a black sedan parked on the side of the road opened. The man who stepped out yawned, lit a cigarette, and took a few puffs. He caught a glimpse of a dark shadow in his peripheral vision, but when he looked again, there was nothing there. Frightened, he quickly climbed back into the car.

"What’s wrong? You look rattled," the other person in the car asked, squinting.

"I think I just saw a ghost," the man said, recounting what had happened.

"Nonsense, what ghost? You’re probably just too tired and seeing things." He didn't know when this lousy assignment would end; they had been staking the place out for a day and hadn't even caught a glimpse of Wen Jiao.

The man thought that made sense and stopped worrying about it, chatting idly with his companion.

A black figure quickly climbed to the second floor and entered quietly through a window. Moving almost silently, the figure walked toward the bedroom, pushed the door open, pulled out a dagger, and lunged toward the bed.

Shen Zhizhen had woken up the moment someone entered the room. She wondered if it was a thief or an assassin. A cold, murderous aura struck her. In the nick of time, she threw the quilt upward, exerted force from her waist and legs, and kicked out toward the intruder’s stomach.

The assassin sensed the power behind the blow and, instead of taking it head-on, used the momentum to retreat, stopping only when they reached the door.

Shen Zhizhen got off the bed and stood her ground, getting a clear look at the uninvited guest. They were dressed in black, wearing a black mask, with only a pair of cold eyes visible.

The first strike had missed, and a flash of surprise crossed the assassin’s eyes, but they didn't hesitate. Like a ghost, they attacked again, the short dagger in their hand flashing with silver light.

Shen Zhizhen noticed the assassin’s movement style was peculiar, so she decided to test their limits. After a dozen exchanges, she figured out their pattern. She changed her stance, cut into their defense, and landed a heavy punch on their face. Following that, she locked their wrist and twisted—a loud "crack" echoed as the assassin’s arm broke.

The assassin let out a muffled grunt, threw a handful of powder at Shen Zhizhen with their other hand, and delivered a sweeping kick to force her to let go, before lunging toward the window.

Shen Zhizhen turned sideways and held her breath. Seeing the assassin trying to escape, she pulled a gun from her space and pulled the trigger just as they were about to leap. A gunshot rang out, and the assassin’s body fell straight down like a puppet with cut strings.

With a loud *thud*, the body landed heavily on the roof of the black sedan, startling the two men inside. They scrambled out to see what was going on—what with the gunshot and the heavy object falling.

At that moment, the others guarding the area rushed over toward the sound of the gunshot and were met with this scene.

Everyone looked up at the second floor, then down at the corpse lying on the car roof, killed by a single shot. For a moment, no one knew what to say.

Shen Zhizhen poked her head out of the window, made eye contact with them, and even counted how many people were down there.

*Heh.* They sent six people to stake out Wen Jiao? Was that really necessary? Besides, if a normal person knew the 76th Branch was after them, why would they come back? Which genius gave that order?

Shen Zhizhen cleared her throat. "Since you're all here, you can serve as witnesses. This person broke in at midnight to assassinate a police officer, and I killed them in self-defense. Whoever has a moment, please help me call the police."

The men standing below looked at each other and had no choice but to swallow their pride. There was nothing they could do—the person upstairs was Secretary-General Shen’s family. With them guarding the place, an assassin had managed to get in and kill someone without them even noticing. If word got out, they would look completely incompetent.

With that in mind, the men below tacitly took over the rest of the cleanup. When the police arrived, Shen Zhizhen only gave a statement and didn't even have to go to the station.

Shen Zhizhen sent the police away, tidied up the room, cleared away the traces of the fight, changed the bedding, and lay back down. She replayed the fight in her mind.

The intruder had been as silent as a falling leaf, completely concealing their presence before attacking. If her five senses hadn't been greatly enhanced, the original owner of this body would never have noticed them until it was too late.

Furthermore, the assassin’s style was distinctive: they didn't take attacks head-on and knew how to use their opponent’s momentum to deflect force. During the fight, they had targeted her vital points—every strike had been aimed at her eyes, throat, or joints.

Putting it all together, along with the black outfit and mask, the assassin’s identity was clear: a Japanese ninjutsu expert.

Shen Zhizhen finished her review, knowing there would be no follow-up to the assassination attempt. Even if the police and the 76th Branch agents investigated, they would cover it up because they didn't dare offend the Japanese.

A cold sneer curled the corner of Shen Zhizhen’s lips. They had issued an assassination order, yet they still chose to do it themselves, sending a ninjutsu expert. Was the Ume Kikan worried that if they sent someone to snipe her, she would kill them instead? *Heh*, they were underestimating her. She could kill anyone they sent. Before falling asleep, she decided she would cause some trouble for the Japanese tomorrow.

What Shen Zhizhen did not know was that after receiving the news of the failed assassination, someone had spent the entire night hacking at a test-cutting target with a katana.

chapters.title: Patrol Chief Shen is Not a Greedy Person
chapters.content:
In the morning, the Third Patrol Group’s sidecar motorcycle entered the boundary road area and stopped. Shen Zhizhen sat in the vehicle and divided the patrol officers of the Third Patrol Group, splitting the seven men into two groups to patrol different sectors.

Shen Zhizhen: "Ma San and He Ergou will be in my group. Wang Jiangsheng will take the others as a separate group."

Lin Wu got out of the car and joined the others in watching the sidecar carrying the patrol chief drive away. The area assigned to them was the surrounding streets, while the Yuyuan Road area fell under the patrol chief's group.

After arranging the patrol tasks, Shen Zhizhen took Ma San and He Ergou to Yuyuan Road.

He Ergou was now full of admiration for the patrol chief and spent the entire journey trying to impress her, introducing the ins and outs of Yuyuan Road.

Ma San chimed in every now and then while driving. He felt the same way as He Ergou; when he brought those 100 silver dollars home yesterday, his mother had been so happy, praising him for finally amounting to something.

Shen Zhizhen nodded repeatedly as she listened, finding this road interesting. The eastern section gathered elites from all walks of life, the western section was home to high-ranking officials and dignitaries, and the fringes had become a place where filth and corruption hid.

"How do you think we could make things difficult for the Japanese?" she asked, not being as familiar with the area as her two subordinates, and decided to ask for their opinions.

Upon hearing this, He Ergou and Ma San were not afraid; instead, they felt a bit excited. Look at their patrol chief—so bold, actually wanting to actively look for trouble with the Japanese.

With the patrol chief there to take the heat if the sky fell, what was there to be afraid of? Based on this mentality, the two really racked their brains to come up with ways to annoy the Japanese.

The method Ma San thought of was very direct: go to the casinos and opium dens run by the Japanese and cause trouble, just like yesterday.

Shen Zhizhen did not express an opinion; that approach from yesterday was a bit trivial and not effective enough against the Japanese.

He Ergou’s eyes darted around. "Patrol Chief, I heard that a batch of smuggled goods is arriving at noon today."

Shen Zhizhen’s eyes lit up at these words. She looked at He Ergou and asked, "Whose goods? Do you know what is being smuggled?" She had looked into the backgrounds of her subordinates and knew that He Ergou’s older brother was a minor leader in the Green Gang, so his information was credible.

He Ergou: "It belongs to the Mitsui Trading Company. I suspect it’s mostly opium." Generally, most things transported through the river network here were opium.

Knowing that the patrol chief might not be familiar with these trading companies, He Ergou explained the ways of the Japanese trading firms. Those Japanese companies were no good; they used their privilege of being exempt from customs inspections to transport opium from abroad into Shanghai...

After listening, Shen Zhizhen made a prompt decision: "That’s the one. Let’s go find Wang Jiangsheng." As she finished speaking, the sidecar made a turn and headed back.

By the riverbank, a truck was parked, and the driver got out, using a small flag to signal a fishing boat in the distance.

The men of the Third Patrol Group were hiding in the bushes. When Wang Jiangsheng and the others saw the fishing boat approaching, a look of joy appeared in their eyes. Everyone knew that if they pulled this off today, it might mean another 100 silver dollars. Why not take a little risk for money?

In this chaotic era, in the police profession, even if you don't look for trouble, it doesn't mean you will live long. How many colleagues from the West Shanghai Branch had died on patrol? They hadn't made any money and had lost their lives to boot.

Shen Zhizhen did not know that her subordinates were counting on this to get rich. She was currently sighing to herself about how arrogant these Japanese must be to dare to smuggle in broad daylight; doing it at night would at least be somewhat understandable.

As soon as the fishing boat stopped at the bank, it was surrounded by the men of the Third Patrol Group. "Police! Inspection!"

Upon hearing "police," the other side pulled out guns to resist, but before they could even aim, their wrists were struck by Shen Zhizhen and Mu Daqiang. Within moments, all thirteen people—those on the boat and those on the shore providing support—were captured.

Wang Jiangsheng dislocated one arm of each of these men and handcuffed the other, then left two men to watch them while he followed the patrol chief onto the boat.

After boarding, Shen Zhizhen inspected it and found that it was a new boat. She beckoned to Wang Jiangsheng behind her, "I want this boat. Is there a place to dock it?" She knew Wang Jiangsheng had grown up by the river and that he would surely have a way to handle this.

Wang Jiangsheng smiled upon hearing this. "Patrol Chief, there’s a river channel right in front of my house. I’ll sail the boat to my place in a bit, and once you find a docking spot, I’ll bring it to you."

To be honest, he quite liked the patrol chief’s style of doing things. At first, he had many reservations, worrying that the patrol chief would cause a major disaster that would implicate them, but after what happened yesterday, his thinking had changed. Who likes eating vegetables when there is meat to be had?

"Patrol Chief, come take a look quickly," Ma San shouted with excitement.

He Ergou and Mu Daqiang looked at the opened crates. Oh my mother, they were rich this time.

Shen Zhizhen and Wang Jiangsheng exchanged a glance and followed the sound. When they entered the cabin and looked, they were almost blinded by two crates of gold.

Ma San reported with a wide grin, "Patrol Chief, there are two crates of gold, three crates of Swiss watches, and five crates of opium." All ten crates had been opened.

Shen Zhizhen scanned them. Seeing that the men had only opened the crates and hadn't touched the contents, she thought they were quite good at protecting themselves.

She stepped forward and took seven gold bars from the crate. She put one in her own pocket and handed the other six to Wang Jiangsheng. "One gold bar for each person, and two watches for each person. Seal the crates and carry them out. Remember, we didn't take anything, and don't go showing off to others when we get back."

She gave this instruction not out of fear; after all, if these things were handed over, the bureau chief would take even more. She would definitely go through the proper channels, but she said this mainly to prevent them from becoming targets—wealth should not be flaunted.

Ma San, He Ergou, and Mu Daqiang nodded excitedly to show they understood. The three of them each took their watches and then closed the crate lids.

After they finished dividing the items, the shares for the two men outside were left to Wang Jiangsheng for safekeeping. Then they started carrying the crates out, their smiles impossible to contain.

When Lin Wu and Huang Dazhi saw the crates being carried down, they rushed over to help, and everyone loaded the crates onto the truck.

After loading the goods, they loaded the captives. Shen Zhizhen personally sat in the truck bed to oversee them. "Lin Wu, you drive the truck. Mu Daqiang, sit in the passenger seat. Ma San and He Ergou, drive the sidecar behind the truck."

Wang Jiangsheng watched the truck and the two sidecars drive away before returning to the boat to sail it away from the river channel.

At the West Shanghai Branch, a truck and two sidecars drove into the courtyard and stopped. The men of the Third Patrol Group got out, some escorting the captives and others moving the goods, making the courtyard quite lively for a time.

When everyone saw crate after crate being moved into the bureau chief’s office, they understood that the Third Patrol Group had pulled off something big.

In the bureau chief’s office, Shen Zhizhen was reporting the process of capturing the smuggling boat. "Bureau Chief, I received a tip that there was a smuggling boat near the Yuyuan Road river network. I took the patrol officers of the Third Patrol Group to investigate, and sure enough, we found the smuggling boat. After deducting the reward I promised the informant, I have brought back everything else."

Bureau Chief Wang narrowed his eyes, his gaze falling on the ten opened crates on the floor. Judging by the missing corners in the crates, Patrol Chief Shen was not a greedy person.

chapters.title: Shen San is Back
chapters.content:
Shen Zhizhen walked back to the Third Patrol Group office with a frown after leaving the bureau chief’s office. Seeing everyone chatting excitedly, she sat in her chair and smiled, "You all worked hard today. Let's call it a day." Knowing their minds were already elsewhere, she decided to let them go early.

Upon hearing this, they flattered her a few times, and before long, everyone except He Ergou had left.

He Ergou waited until everyone was gone, then leaned in with a grin, "Patrol Chief, what do you need?" Just now, as soon as the patrol chief walked in, she had given him a look signaling him to stay.

Shen Zhizhen took the gold bar from her pocket, placed it on the table, tilted her chin slightly toward He Ergou, and said, "Give this gold bar to your brother." He Ergou’s source of information was reliable, and she wanted to keep this line open.

He Ergou understood immediately. This gold bar was payment for the information. He grinned, pocketed the gold bar, and said, "Thank you, Patrol Chief. If there’s any news in the future, I’ll tell you first."

Shen Zhizhen’s lips curled slightly. This kid was quite sensible. She waved her hand to signal that He Ergou could leave.

He Ergou: "Then, Patrol Chief, I’m off work." With that, he left, looking very excited.

After everyone had left, Shen Zhizhen also got up and left, driving away from the police station. She stopped by a Western restaurant to pack some pastries for dinner and arrived home safely.

Shen Zhizhen got out of the car and scanned the area, noticing that the people who had been monitoring and lurking yesterday had been withdrawn. She went upstairs, lost in thought, opened the door with her key, and glanced at the shoe cabinet: Shen San was back.

Shen Zhizhen changed into her slippers and walked to the sofa. She placed the pastries on the tea table, sat down, and smiled at Shen Zimei, who was lying on the sofa feigning sleep, "Did you get rid of the people lurking downstairs?"

Shen Zimei’s train of thought was interrupted. She opened her eyes to meet a pair of smiling eyes and curled her lips slightly, "Mm, your assassination order has been rescinded."

When she arrived home in the afternoon, she saw people guarding the inside and outside of No. 36. She had brought them over to question them and only then learned about someone sneaking into the house to kill Xiao Jiu last night.

She immediately understood who had done it. Her teacher had made a phone call in front of her yesterday, and the other party had clearly agreed to rescind the assassination order. Yet, someone had come to assassinate Xiao Jiu that very night; it was obvious that someone in the Plum Blossom Agency was unwilling to let it go.

"Which deity did you ask to rescind it?" No wonder; she had been wondering why no one had made a move against her today. So, it had been rescinded.

"My teacher, Zhou Fuhai." Shen Zimei explained the task and purpose her teacher had given her. Rescinding the assassination order on Xiao Jiu was merely a part of the reward given in advance.

When Shen Zhizhen heard the name Zhou Fuhai, she realized that Shen San’s backer was this man. No wonder she had such a high status at 76. That man was a bona fide power broker in the puppet government.

When she heard the later mentions of the treasure map, Tanaka Yumei, and other terms, she couldn't help but be startled. What kind of fate was this, that after all this turning and twisting, she was involved in this matter again?

After listening, Shen Zhizhen blinked her eyes, "This task won't be easy to do. Why don't you find a way to decline it?"

The treasure map was divided into three parts, and one of them was with her. As long as she didn't bring it out, Shen San and Tanaka Yumei would never find the complete set, even if they worked themselves to death.

Shen Zimei rolled her eyes at Xiao Jiu upon hearing this and lazily sat up, leaning against the sofa, "If you don't want to be involved, go to Hong Kong with the family." She would also feel more at ease if Xiao Jiu left.

This task was mainly to collect the three treasure maps; it didn't necessarily require Xiao Jiu’s participation. When the maps were collected and they went to find the Phoenix Emperor’s Tomb, that would be when Xiao Jiu’s advantages could be put to use, but that was all predicated on finding them all.

Shen Zhizhen’s mind flashed with a realization: Shen San hadn't thought about completing the task, or rather, she wasn't confident in completing it; otherwise, she wouldn't have arranged a retreat for her family first.

Having figured this out, Shen Zhizhen shook her head, "Unless you leave with me, I won't leave." She had to stay here and keep an eye on Shen San; she didn't want to have to collect this woman’s corpse.

Shen Zimei felt a warmth in her heart upon hearing this, knowing that Xiao Jiu meant she wanted to stay and help her.

Hong Kong had always been a retreat in Shen Zhizhen’s mind. Now that Shen San had arranged for the family to go there, to be honest, it made her feel relieved.

With no worries behind her and a way out secured, she now only needed to stay and keep an eye on Shen San, preventing her from making any grave mistakes or losing her life. Once the time was right, she could take Shen San and evacuate Shanghai for Hong Kong.

Of course, another reason was that she held one of the treasure maps; she couldn't just watch Shen San risk everything for an impossible mission. With her stirring the pot, there might even be some unexpected gains.

At this thought, Shen Zhizhen wore a mischievous smirk. If that Tanaka also managed to find the other two treasure maps, it wouldn't be a bad idea for her to play the role of the oriole behind the mantis. In any case, the Gu Feng Kingdom's treasure maps could not fall into the hands of the Japanese, not even the fragments.

Shen Zhizhen voiced her thoughts, looking seriously at the woman leaning on the sofa. "Shen Zhimei, I can help you find the treasure maps, but they cannot fall into the hands of the Japanese or the dignitaries of the puppet government."

Shen Zhimei almost laughed. So, the young master of the Shen family had her eyes on them too. Well, how could a tomb-raiding family let treasures fall into others' hands? "Tsk, understood. These treasure maps can only end up in our young master's hands."

She reminded Shen Jiu not to forget to forge a few fake maps for her to turn in. She had been fortunate enough to witness the little girl’s talent for forgery; it was completely indistinguishable from the real thing. As long as they got their hands on the real maps, whether they were real or fake would be entirely up to them.

Shen Zhizhen rubbed her nose, not bothering to explain that wasn't exactly what she meant, but Shen Zhimei’s words gave her an idea. She could find time to make a fake map, which could serve as bait if necessary.

The two sisters sat on the sofa, eating pastries and chatting idly, updating each other on what had happened over the past two days.

Shen Zhizhen asked curiously, "How do you think Director Wang will handle the confiscated goods?"

Director Wang would certainly be greedy, but she was curious about how much he would return under pressure from the Japanese side.

Shen Zhimei swallowed the pastry in her mouth before replying, "He’ll swallow the gold and watches, and return the opium."

Shen Zhizhen frowned slightly. "Is Director Wang that bold?" She knew that in these times, opium was worth as much as gold, but two boxes of gold bars and three boxes of Swiss watches—could Director Wang really swallow all that?

"He dares to let you cause such trouble because he likely knows about my relationship with my teacher." Shen Zhimei parted her lips slightly to enlighten little Jiu. In this great city of Shanghai, everyone with a certain degree of power and status had a backer.

Even though her teacher-student relationship hadn't been made public, anyone who looked into who she met during her recent trip to Nanjing would naturally know who stood behind her.

Hearing this, Shen Zhizhen had an epiphany. No wonder Director Wang let her stir up trouble in the border road area; he was using the power of Zhou Fuhai to act like a fox exploiting a tiger's might.

*Tsk, old fox.* Once she figured it out, Shen Zhizhen couldn't help but sigh inwardly. Everyone here was a schemer. Although the Japanese were powerful, the puppet government was backed by the Japanese high command, and if someone with real power like Zhou Fuhai spoke, the Japanese would listen.

Just like the matter of canceling the assassination order—Shen Zhimei’s attempts to find people to intercede hadn't worked, but with just one phone call from Zhou Fuhai, the Mei Kikan had given him face.

chapters.title: A Murder Case
chapters.content:
The next day, at the Western Shanghai Branch, Shen Zhizhen had just entered her office when she learned the aftermath of yesterday's smuggling bust.

He Ergou had returned from gathering intel and was spitting with excitement as he began to recount, "Our Director Wang is really tough now. He stood his ground against the Japanese pressure and only handed over five boxes of opium in the end."

Everyone stared at the five fingers He Ergou held up, dumbfounded. Good heavens, their director had pocketed the five most valuable boxes.

Shen Zhizhen heard that things had gone exactly according to Shen San’s prediction. Director Wang had quite an appetite; she just wondered if he would choke on it.

She glanced at her watch, and seeing it was still early, she walked over to the patrol leader’s seat and sat down to listen to the chatter.

Regarding the mission, Shen San said she didn't need her help for now and told her to go about her business. All clues to the mission were currently with Tanaka, and Shen San’s plan was to find him first and then wait for an opportunity. Her own plan was to play the oriole, letting Tanaka do the searching, and then swap the real maps for fakes once he found them.

Shen San accepted this proposal, but they couldn't rely solely on Tanaka. If he couldn't find them, Shen San wouldn't be able to complete the mission. Plus, her teacher had provided some people, so she was also investigating through channels related to the Gu Feng Kingdom.

As for the matter of Wan Donglai, she had asked Shen San to help inquire about it yesterday. Of course, she didn't mention that Wan Donglai was a Communist. Shen San was currently in a gray area, and rather than talking about grand causes to get her help, it was faster to approach it from the perspective of childhood friends and old acquaintances.

A sharp, urgent telephone ring interrupted the Three Patrol Squad's lively conversation. Ma San, being closest to the phone, picked up the receiver. After listening, his expression changed. He hung up and said, "Patrol Leader, someone reported a murder at the Tang Mansion, No. 73 Yuyuan East Road. The police officer wants the Three Patrol Squad to secure the scene."

Shen Zhizhen frowned slightly at the news and ordered coldly, "All members of the Three Patrol Squad, head to the scene immediately."

A black sedan and three sidecars pulled out of the Western Shanghai Branch, with the Three Patrol Squad’s sidecars following closely behind the lead vehicle.

Sitting in the sidecar, Shen Zhizhen couldn't stand the dust kicked up by the car in front. She put on the sunglasses hanging from her pocket and used her sleeve to shield her nose, frowning as she asked, "Who is in the car ahead?"

Ma San, He Ergou, and Lin Wu, who were in the same vehicle, almost laughed. Their patrol leader truly took being a newcomer to the extreme; she didn't even know her colleagues from the police department's criminal investigation division.

Ma San hurriedly explained, "In the sedan ahead are Zhang Daizong, captain of the First Criminal Investigation Team, and his deputy, He Wanshan. The driver is Zhang Liansheng, and the one in the passenger seat is Huang Mingxin. Both are veterans of the First Team. The ones in the sidecars are the First Team's police officers."

He Ergou and Lin Wu chimed in from time to time, all dedicated to making sure their patrol leader was well-informed.

With their combined knowledge, Shen Zhizhen finally understood the responsibilities of each department. For instance, their patrol squad had no authority to solve cases; their job was simply to secure the scene.

Shen Zhizhen nodded to show she understood. Their squad was there to play a supporting role. Thinking of yesterday, she couldn't help but ask, "Then wasn't what we did yesterday against the rules?"

He Ergou chuckled. "Heh, that depends on how you look at it. We just happened to run into a suspicious boat, right? Exercising the right to inspect is a patrol officer's duty." *Heh*, who told that bunch to pull guns and resist?

Shen Zhizhen blinked and nodded, agreeing it made sense. Thinking of the director’s reaction, she found it amusing. Simply put, in this peculiar era, the rules were in the hands of those with power. As long as the director didn't pursue it, what they did was right.

And considering she had sent the director two boxes of gold, three boxes of Swiss watches, and five boxes of opium, would he pursue it? *Heh*, naturally not.

Shen Zhizhen felt that during her time at the Western Shanghai Branch, she would definitely fatten up Director Wang. At this thought, she narrowed her eyes and decided...

The car stopped at No. 73. After getting out, Shen Zhizhen saw a crowd of onlookers nearby. She signaled for the Three Patrol Squad to set up a cordon, then walked over to greet the captain and deputy captain of the First Criminal Investigation Team.

The Tang Mansion at No. 73 Yuyuan East Road was a three-story European-style detached villa. The reporter was a neighbor who, while out for a morning stroll, saw the courtyard gate open and caught a glimpse of a corpse inside, prompting them to call the police immediately.

Most of the onlookers were nearby domestic workers sent by their employers to gather news; none of them had entered the crime scene.

Seeing the young female patrol leader follow them in, Zhang Daizong and He Wanshan exchanged glances but said nothing. They had heard of her exploits—she had killed a puppet agent and remained unscathed; there was no need to offend her.

Shen Zhizhen blended into the First Team. She didn't wander around, staying close to Captain Zhang. Since she didn't know anything about investigation, she didn't speak out of turn. Her behavior actually earned her some favor with the First Team.

Zhang Daizong led his men to examine the scene, occasionally speaking to have his subordinates record his findings.

Shen Zhizhen’s expression had been grim since she entered. The killer’s methods were extremely cruel. There were thirteen victims in total, each having suffered inhuman torture before death. Two police officers ran out to dry-heave after seeing the intestines in the living room.

Zhang Daizong glanced at Patrol Leader Shen and said to He Wanshan, "There are clear signs of ransacking in the house. The killer’s methods are cruel. For now, we will investigate along the lines of a vendetta. First, screen the victims' interpersonal relationships..."

Shen Zhizhen stepped outside to take a breath of fresh air. Her sunglasses hid the anger in her eyes. *Damn it, the killer is a total pervert.* All the victims had been tortured to death.

In these times, killing and being killed happened often, but this was the first time she had seen such a scene. If such a perverted killer wasn't caught, there would only be more victims.

Shen Zhizhen beckoned to Wang Jiangsheng and He Ergou. When they approached, she instructed, "You two keep an eye on the First Team. Pay attention to the progress of the case and personally investigate the victims' backgrounds."

Wang Jiangsheng and He Ergou understood immediately and, after receiving their orders, divided the work.

It wasn't until the bodies were hauled away that the crowd gradually dispersed. After seeing off the First Team, Shen Zhizhen had Ma San put up the police tape, then divided the Three Patrol Squad into pairs and sent them out on patrol.

After dismissing them, Shen Zhizhen hailed a rickshaw to the Concession; she had an appointment to have lunch with Shen Zhimei.

At a Western restaurant in the Concession, the sisters sat in a corner, eating and talking.

When Shen Zhizhen heard that Wan Donglai had already been released, she felt a surge of emotion. The male lead was indeed the male lead. With the foreign firm providing bail and the consulate applying pressure, the 76th Branch had no choice but to release him for lack of concrete evidence.

Shen Zhizhen described the case from the morning. "Who do you think could have done it?" Shen San was so smart; she wanted her to help analyze it.

Shen Zhimei rolled her eyes. She hadn't even seen the scene, nor did she have any valid information. What could she possibly analyze?

chapters.title: Shen Zhimei Inspects the Murder Scene
chapters.content:
Shen Zhizhen described the crime scene and the identities of the victims according to her memory.

"The victims were Tang Mingbo, vice president of the Shaanxi Chamber of Commerce; his concubine, Liu Yumei; the two sons and one daughter born to Liu Yumei; and the rest were the mansion’s servants, driver, and bodyguards..."

After finishing her description, Shen Zhizhen asked, "Do you think it could have been the original wife from Shaanxi who hired a killer, or perhaps he offended someone in the business world and was wiped out?"

Shen Zhimei swallowed the foie gras in her mouth before speaking. "Rich men are always surrounded by women; who knows how many concubines he had at home." She didn't think an original wife would care enough to hire a killer unless there was some secret involved.

"And it’s not necessarily a vendetta. Didn't you say there were clear signs of ransacking? It’s possible the killer used such cruel methods to force a confession."

Shen Zhizhen: "Force a confession? Using such perverted methods to force a confession... damn, what kind of person would do that?"

"There are plenty of those, quite a few right inside No. 76." Shen Zhimei spoke nonchalantly about the scenes of torture and interrogation at No. 76.

Shen Zhizhen...

After finishing the meal, Shen Zhimei wiped the corners of her lips with a napkin. "I'll go to the scene with you in a moment."

Judging from Shen Jiu's description of the scene, the killer likely hadn't found what they were looking for. Going to take a look might yield unexpected results.

She hadn't originally intended to meddle in other people's business, but the killer's methods had truly piqued her curiosity. What exactly was the killer searching for?

The black sedan pulled over to the side of the road at 73 Yuyuan East Road. Shen Zhizhen got out, tore off the seal, pushed the door open, and entered first.

Shen Zhimei stepped out and first scanned the surroundings. Her gaze lingered for a moment on the garden villa opposite the Tang Mansion, and a cold sneer curled her lips. It was quite a coincidence, indeed.

She stepped into the Tang Mansion and closed and locked the door behind her, shutting out prying eyes.

The spots where the deceased had been were marked at the crime scene, and the ground nearby was soaked red with blood. Hearing the door close, Shen Zhizhen turned back to see Shen San had locked the main gate, and asked with her eyes what was wrong.

If she had come alone, she certainly wouldn't have broken the seal to avoid trouble; she would have chosen to jump over the wall. Once caught at the scene, it would cause unnecessary complications, as police officers did not have the authority to investigate criminal cases.

But bringing Shen San was different. People from No. 76 came to survey the scene. Even though Shen Zhimei's current status was that of a secretary-general, she held a secret mandate in her hands, so no one could say anything regardless of who came. That was why she had broken the seal and entered openly.

However, Shen Zhimei's act of locking the main gate was a bit abrupt. Firstly, it didn't fit her usual style, and secondly, it suggested she might have discovered something.

Shen Zhimei scanned the courtyard and signaled for Xiao Jiu to go inside first. The air in the house was still thick with the smell of blood.

"Living opposite the Tang Mansion is Jing Shen Haoyi, a secret service leader of the Ume Kikan. I just noticed a reflection in the second-floor window across the street." Shen Zhimei carefully surveyed the scene while speaking to Shen Jiu.

Shen Zhizhen’s eyes flashed with surprise at these words. A reflection? Someone across the street was watching them with binoculars?

Clearly, her five senses were much sharper than Shen San's, but she lacked experience. She had only checked if there was anyone nearby and hadn't even glanced into the residence across the street.

Shen Zhizhen voiced her thoughts, which made Shen Zhimei chuckle. "Your third sister has undergone professional training."

In certain scenarios, observing the surrounding environment was almost an instinctive reaction. Xiao Jiu had not received training as an agent, so naturally, she lacked that level of vigilance.

Shen Zhizhen nodded in agreement and earnestly followed Shen San's lead, tapping on walls and floors from time to time.

Shen Zhimei surveyed the entire house inside and out, finally locking onto Tang Mingbo's study, which was also the scene of his death.

The two stood in the study. Shen Zhimei listened to Shen Jiu describe the state of Tang Mingbo's body while searching every corner of the room.

"Tang Mingbo died with one hand clutching his chest, his abdomen and chest stabbed multiple times." The organs in his abdominal cavity had been pulverized; it was a gruesome death. A newly hired detective from the First Criminal Investigation Team had run out and vomited on the spot.

To be honest, if she hadn't been tempered by the past month of anti-Japanese operations, she probably would have been just like that young officer.

Shen Zhimei picked up a white medicine bottle from a corner under the table. After reading the label, a look of realization flashed in her eyes.

She handed the bottle to Shen Zhizhen and said softly, "Tang Mingbo likely died of a sudden heart attack. You can keep an eye on his autopsy results to see if that was the cause of death."

Shen Zhizhen took the bottle. Atropine? Used to treat bradyarrhythmia caused by myocardial infarction.

If Tang Mingbo had indeed died of a heart attack, it explained why the killer chose such a cruel method of interrogation. Imagine, if Tang Mingbo died before the killer found him, and only Tang Mingbo knew the location of the object the killer wanted?

Shen Zhizhen immediately understood that Shen San's earlier judgment might be correct. The killer hadn't found what they wanted because Tang Mingbo had died first. Driven by anger and a sliver of desperate hope, the killer had subjected the remaining survivors to cruel interrogation.

Shen Zhimei searched the walls and fireplace of the study but found no place where things could be hidden. She walked over to a chair, sat down, and pulled out a pack of ladies' cigarettes to light one.

She brought the cigarette to her lips, took a light drag, and exhaled calmly, her eyes filled with a faint, thoughtful expression.

If she were Tang Mingbo, where would she put something important in this room? It would have to be somewhere she could see every day, preferably somewhere she could touch often, but it would also need to break conventional logic so that others wouldn't easily think of it. So, where would that be?

It had to be said that when a beautiful woman does anything, it looks good. A wisp of blue smoke curled around her fingers, the air of charm and danger intertwined, making it impossible to look away.

Shen Zhizhen warned her seriously, "Don't smoke in front of outsiders in the future; it's easy to attract wolves." Sigh, having a flashy sister meant she always had to worry about her.

Shen Zhimei ignored the high-strung Xiao Jiu. Her beautiful eyes shifted to the chair. She stood up, flipped the chair over, and tapped the bottom of the seat with her finger. A look of joy flashed in her eyes—she had found it.

She pulled the board from under the chair, revealing a sandalwood box. She handed the box to Xiao Jiu, then restored the board, set the chair upright, and sat down, a look of satisfaction on her lips.

Shen Zhizhen held the sandalwood box and gave Shen San a thumbs-up. Awesome! Something the killer and the First Criminal Investigation Team couldn't find, and Shen San found it in less than half an hour!

She opened the box, and a dark gold Phoenix Token caught her eye. She took it out and examined it carefully. The front of the token was carved with a phoenix spreading its wings to fly; the back pattern was a phoenix feather, delicate and vivid, shimmering with a faint luster. Both sides of the token were engraved with ancient runes, identical to the key to the Shen family treasury.

chapters.title: The Cheap Father is a Liar
chapters.content:
Shen Zhimei flicked the ash from her cigarette and exhaled a puff of smoke before reaching out to take the token. She had seen this thing before; how could it be here?

"Why is the key to our Shen family treasury here?" Her beautiful eyes narrowed, filled with a trace of doubt.

This statement shocked Shen Zhizhen. She blinked and asked in astonishment, "How do you know? Didn't Father say only the next family head knows the secrets of the Shen family?" The cheap father was a liar.

With one sentence, Shen Zhimei knew that Father had given the key to the Shen family treasury to Xiao Jiu; otherwise, Xiao Jiu wouldn't have known. Thinking of Father's style, she couldn't help but shake her head with a laugh.

"I found it when I was a child. You were still wearing split-crotch pants back then. Since I was the eldest daughter of the Shen family head, Father thought I would be the next successor, so he told me."

It was just that later, it was discovered that her talent for the family's traditional skills was truly average, so the title of "Young Master" eventually fell to Xiao Jiu.

Shen Zhizhen thought about it, and it made sense. The original owner was indeed the second in line to inherit the family head position.

Shen Zhimei threw the Phoenix Token to Xiao Jiu. "Keep it safe. When you have time, make a few more fakes. I suspect there is more than one of these things." With that, she stubbed out her cigarette and stood up to walk out.

Walking to the door, she turned back and signaled for Xiao Jiu to put the imperial green jade Buddha statue they had just found into the box.

Shen Zhizhen immediately understood her intent. She followed Shen San's instructions, placed the palm-sized imperial green jade Buddha statue into the box, and followed Shen San out.

She kept the Phoenix Token close to her body; she didn't dare put it into her space now, just in case the same thing happened as last time.

Shen San was truly prescient. The sisters had just walked out of the gate when they were attacked. There were five people in total, all of them Japanese ninjutsu masters with strange movements.

The sisters cooperated tacitly. Shen Zhimei feigned poor combat skills and hid behind her sister, while Shen Zhizhen appeared to struggle slightly because she had to protect her sister. As a result, she was careless, and the sandalwood box in her hand was snatched away.

The group retreated immediately after succeeding; it was clear their goal was the sandalwood box they had just found.

After the group left, the sisters stayed in place and acted out a scene of frustration before driving away.

Shen Zhizhen thought about what had just happened while driving. Every move the group made while fighting her and ambushing Shen San was an attempt to test whether they were hiding anything on their bodies.

"Will they believe it?"

"Who knows? We'll definitely be watched for a while, so be careful yourself."

Shen Zhizhen nodded to show she understood. "What about you? Do you want me to pick you up and drop you off at work?" Naturally, the suspicion wouldn't just be on her; Shen San would definitely be a primary target.

Shen Zhimei smiled and shook her head. "No need. I'll have the people Teacher gave me transferred to my side."

Shen Zhizhen got out of the car at the Shanghai West Branch and watched the black sedan drive away before turning to enter the police station. She walked around inside and even made a point to wander into the morgue to chat with the coroner for a while.

The complete appraisal report wouldn't be ready for a week. After getting the answer she wanted, Shen Zhizhen drove away from the police station.

In the garden villa opposite the Tang Mansion, Jing Shen Haoyi respectfully placed the sandalwood box on the table and said to the refined man sitting on the sofa, "Your Excellency Tanaka, this is what was just snatched back. Please see if it is the item you were looking for."

Tanaka also picked up the sandalwood box and opened it. Seeing that it was a palm-sized imperial green jade Buddha statue—very valuable, but not what he was looking for—he closed the box and asked with a frown, "Are you sure they didn't bring anything else out?"

Jing Shen Haoyi replied firmly, "The top experts were dispatched this time. They said the two Shen sisters had no other items on them besides this sandalwood box."

Tanaka also didn't take it to heart. A small token could be hidden anywhere. He ordered coldly, "Send people to follow the two Shen sisters, and keep watching the opposite side."

Jing Shen Haoyi bowed his head and replied, "Yes."

Shen Zhizhen drove to find a hotel and booked a luxury room. After entering, she locked the door and drew the curtains. After checking that everything was fine, she took out the Phoenix Token and threw it into her space. With a "boom," she felt her consciousness roll and vibrate, and she felt dizzy, but fortunately, she didn't lose control of her body this time.

She lay on the bed and waited quietly. A quarter of an hour later, the dizziness passed, and she looked at the changes in the space. As soon as her consciousness entered, she sensed the expansion. This time, the space had doubled. Although it wasn't as exaggerated as the ten-fold increase last time, a variable of 1,000 square meters becoming 2,000 square meters was a large storage space that could hold a lot of things. When she had time, she would go and "shear some wool" from the Japanese army.

Shen Zhizhen was happy for a while, then took out the tools from the space. She had to make the Phoenix Token as soon as possible. As Shen San said, who knew how many of these things there were?

The Phoenix Token could expand the space. No matter how many there were, as long as she found them, they were hers. If others wanted them, they could only take the fakes.

In Zhabei, inside a residential house, Wan Donglai was telling his superior, Old Gu, about the process of this mission.

Old Gu frowned after hearing this and said, "Your identity is already in danger of being exposed. You must be careful in your future actions. If it really comes to it, change your identity."

Wan Donglai nodded in agreement. He had exhausted his previous favors to get out this time, and if he were caught again, David would not help him.

"By the way, what happened to that girl named Wen Jiao? Was she caught?" He didn't know what happened after he shoved Wen Jiao into his little cousin's rickshaw that day.

Old Gu replied, "Miss Wen Jiao did a great thing this time. The organization has recruited her and sent her out of Shanghai. Don't worry." Once the Central Reserve Bank notes were issued, the savings that the common people had worked so hard to accumulate—whether in cash or deposits—would depreciate and vanish in a short time. It was clear how meaningful Comrade Wen Jiao's actions were.

Wan Donglai breathed a sigh of relief upon hearing this. Wen Jiao's safety meant his little cousin was also fine; otherwise, if his cousin had been implicated, he truly wouldn't have known how to answer to Shen Jiu.

Old Gu continued, "There is an urgent mission now. The organization is in dire need of a batch of medicine. You should try your best to find a way to get some." Medicine was strictly controlled now, and while no one really had any channels, they had to find a way since the mission had been handed down.

Wan Donglai frowned at these words. "Alright, I'll find a way to get some." Medicine was truly hard to come by these days; he would have to take some money to those gangs and test the waters to see if he could buy any.

Shen Zhizhen didn't leave the hotel until the lights began to twinkle at dusk. She had made three tokens, though they were currently semi-finished products; they still needed to be plated with color to be considered complete.

Driving past a noodle stall, she was attracted by the aroma. Touching her flat stomach, she decided to eat a bowl of noodles before heading back.

Shen Zhizhen parked the car on the side of the road and sat down at the noodle stall. "Boss, one bowl of Yangchun noodles, please."

The boss replied, "Coming right up, please wait a moment."

Once the noodles arrived, Shen Zhizhen took a bite and knew she had found authentic Yangchun noodles. The soup was clear and flavorful, and the noodles were smooth and chewy. The deliciousness of Yangchun noodles relied on the soup base and the soy sauce seasoning; one taste told her that this stall's base was made from pork and fish bones.

Just as Shen Zhizhen was enjoying her meal, a figure approached and sat down opposite her. She bit through a noodle, looked up, and nearly choked.

chapters.title: What a Coincidence
chapters.content:
Wu De was not the type to sit still. Once the swelling in his leg went down, he pulled his rickshaw around to wander. In just two days, he had rented a house and looked at several storefronts, needing only to finalize one.

Tonight, while pulling his rickshaw, he passed the noodle stall and saw Shen Jiu, so he came over to talk to her about something. Of course, in public, he didn't forget to put on an act.

"Oh, Inspector Shen, what are you doing here? Thank you for your help the other day; let me treat you to this bowl of noodles." After finishing his lines, Wu De ordered a bowl of Yangchun noodles from the boss.

Shen Zhizhen swallowed the noodles in her mouth, really wanting to ask him if he felt awkward! "Why are you here?" Why was he wandering around so late instead of going home?

Wu De lowered his voice and smiled, "Just passing by, saw you eating noodles here, and thought I'd come over to tell you something."

The nights in Great Shanghai were like a city that never slept, full of song, dance, and superficial luxury, giving one a sense of debauchery amidst a crisis. He shared these thoughts with Shen Jiu.

Shen Zhizhen nodded in agreement. Shanghai at this time was indeed a place where extreme brilliance and deep-seated decay coexisted. She reminded her little cousin to keep his head and not be blinded by the temptations and vanity.

Wu De hurriedly shook his head to indicate he wouldn't. For the sake of his little life, he would always live under Shen Jiu's nose; he wouldn't dare mess around. What if she kicked him out?

Once his noodles arrived, Wu De ate while telling Shen Jiu about the past two days. "I've found a house, a standalone courtyard by the river. The location is..." He took out the house keys and handed them to Shen Zhizhen.

Shen Zhizhen nodded with satisfaction upon hearing that it could dock a boat. She took the keys and put them in her pocket, planning to move the boat she had left with Wang Jiansheng there tomorrow. That way, it would be convenient if she ever needed to use it.

After finishing the business about the house and the shop, Wu De thought for a moment and said, "There's one more thing. Wan Donglai came to see me this afternoon."

Wu De paused, glanced around, and lowered his voice. "He asked me if I had a way to get medicine. I told him I was new here and had no connections. I think he will come looking for you."

He was actually quite happy that the rascal had gotten out, but he really couldn't help with this request. He was new to Shanghai and didn't know anyone; where would he find medicine? Besides, the things they had done along the way were on the 76th Branch's files; he didn't dare act rashly.

Although he hadn't told Wan Donglai Shen Jiu's address, there was Wen Jiao in the middle. That girl seemed to know not only the little cousin's address but also where she worked as a police officer.

If Wan Donglai wanted medicine, didn't that mean the Red Party needed it? What a coincidence—she had plenty of both traditional Chinese and Western medicine in her space. Rather than letting them sit there, she might as well donate them to the Red Party; it might earn some merit for the Shen family.

Shen Zhizhen hadn't wanted to get involved with the events of the book, but the matter of the medicine gave her an idea. She could use Wan Donglai to establish a connection with the Red Party. Even if she didn't join, she could provide them with supplies. It would be a waste not to make good use of her 2,000-square-meter space.

Shen Zhizhen finished the soup at the bottom of the bowl, put down the bowl, and whispered to her little cousin, "Go find Wan Donglai tomorrow and tell him to come see me. Tell him I have Japanese agents tailing me, so he should be careful." She gave him the address of Wang Jiansheng's house and told him to have Wan Donglai meet her at the embankment there tomorrow morning.

Upon hearing this, Wu De knew Shen Jiu wanted to help Wan Donglai get medicine. He nodded immediately. He also noted the fact that Japanese agents were tailing his little cousin; it seemed he would have to be more careful when looking for her in the future. Of course, the best way was to see her less often.

The two finished their noodles and went their separate ways home. As Shen Zhizhen drove, she pondered the Phoenix Tokens. While making the high-quality replicas at the hotel, she had realized there should be nine tokens, as the Phoenix Coffin in her space had nine grooves, each corresponding to one token.

What she couldn't understand was why the Japanese were looking for the Phoenix Tokens. They didn't have the Phoenix Coffin, so why search for them?

The black car stopped by the side of the road at 36 Fengyuan Road. Shen Zhizhen got out and sensed her surroundings. Hmm, very good, there were already people watching in the dark.

As she entered the courtyard at number 36, she felt two more gazes. She immediately realized these must be Shen San's people, and she couldn't help but marvel in her heart at how efficient Shen San was as always.

Walking upstairs, Shen Zhizhen opened the door, went inside, changed her shoes, hung up her coat and police cap, and went to the bedroom to change into casual clothes before going to the study to find Shen San.

There were many documents on the study table, and Shen San was reading them with a serious expression. Shen Zhizhen walked over and picked one up to look at; it was information related to the Ancient Phoenix Kingdom.

She became interested immediately and started reading along with her. The efficiency of the people provided by Shen San's teacher was incredibly high; they had found so much information in just one day.

Neither sister spoke, both reading the materials intently until late at night when they went to wash up. After Shen Zhizhen finished washing and glanced into the study, she saw the desk was tidy and all the materials she had just been reading were gone.

Her curiosity was piqued. Following what she had learned during the day, she tapped and knocked around the study but couldn't find any hidden compartments.

That shouldn't be right. A grave robber should be professional at finding things. Even if she hadn't robbed a grave herself, she had the original owner's memories; she shouldn't be this incompetent.

With a sense of defiance, Shen Zhizhen went through the knowledge in her brain about finding hidden objects and continued to search, sticking her butt in the air.

Shen Zhimei came over after washing up and ignored her. Grave robbers all had an addiction to finding things; it was hereditary and couldn't be changed. She hadn't intended to hide anything, so if she wanted to look, let her look.

Shen Zhizhen finally found the answer in the desk. The entire desk contained multiple hidden Lu Ban locks; opening those locks revealed a hidden compartment. When Shen Zhizhen opened it, she not only saw the documents but also many precious items.

Tsk tsk, she had to admit Shen San was truly clever. She kept the cash and gold bars in the obvious safe, but who would have thought this desk held such secrets?

The treasure hunt over, Shen Zhizhen went back to her room to sleep. By then, Shen San had already drifted off. As she lay down, her mind was filled with the information she had just read.

The Ancient Phoenix Kingdom could not be found in the official history of China; one could only find clues through collected unofficial histories and legends.

Shen Zhizhen summarized what she had seen in her mind. The general thread she had teased out was that the once-prosperous ancient dynasty had perished in natural disasters and plagues, and there were many mythological attributes to the legends.

For example, it was said that the founding Empress, Feng Xi, possessed Phoenix blood and the supernatural ability to open the channel to the Nine Realms. Legend had it that as long as one found the Phoenix Empress's tomb, one could open the channel to the Nine Realms—the Nine Realms being the place the Japanese considered their mythological "Heavenly Kingdom."

The Japanese "Takamagahara Plan" was to collect three fragments of a treasure map, find the location of the tomb of the founding Empress Feng Xi, enter the Phoenix Empress's tomb, and open the Nine Realms to go to their "Heavenly Kingdom."

As a modern person who had been bombarded by various fantasy and xianxia novels, she didn't believe these things in her heart.

However, whenever she thought of the Phoenix Coffin in her consciousness and her experience of transmigrating into a book, she couldn't help but believe in some mystical things. So, even if she had doubts, it belonged to her country, and even if it were just a legend, she wouldn't let the Japanese have it.

chapters.title: Meeting Wan Donglai
chapters.content:
The next day, after the sisters finished breakfast, they went downstairs one after the other. The moment Shen Zhimei stepped onto the ground floor, two men in black suits emerged from the room next door and followed respectfully behind her.

Shen Zhizhen watched the three of them get into a car and leave before she opened her own car door, started the engine, and headed to the police station, glancing at the rearview mirror from time to time. Sure enough, a car was following her.

At the West Shanghai Branch, in the Third Patrol Group office, Shen Zhizhen entered and saw everyone was present. "Wang Jiansheng and He Ergou, stay behind. The rest of you, split into two groups and go on patrol." After saying this, she walked over to the inspector's seat and sat down.

The assigned team members left quickly. Haha, another day of slacking off.

Shen Zhizhen didn't know what they were thinking; if she did, she would certainly implement some rewards and punishments. After they left, she smiled at Wang Jiansheng, "Let's go, we're going to your place to get the boat."

Wang Jiansheng knew immediately that she had found a place to dock the boat and nodded, leading the way.

The black sedan drove out of the West Shanghai Branch. He Ergou was driving happily; it wasn't easy to get his hands on such a nice car. "Inspector, why don't I be your driver from now on?" That way, he could drive such a nice car every day.

Shen Zhizhen chuckled at this, glanced at the rearview mirror, and thought the proposal wasn't bad. "Sure. From now on, Wang Jiansheng will be responsible for taking people on patrol, and the two of us will drive around."

This remark successfully amused the two men in the car. Well, the inspector was starting to become a hands-off boss, but both of them raised their hands in agreement.

He Ergou was naturally happy not to have to patrol every day. Besides, hanging out with the inspector felt like it would lead to better prospects. Who were the people following the leader? They were confidants, weren't they? As long as he kept his mouth shut, there would be plenty of benefits.

Wang Jiansheng was also happy. In the Third Patrol Group, he would be second only to the inspector—actually, he already was, but it hadn't been official. With the inspector's words, it was now official.

He Er-gou glanced at the rearview mirror from time to time. After confirming that a car was following them, he frowned and said, "Inspector, there is a black sedan following us."

Having noticed it after only two intersections, Shen Zhizhen was quite satisfied with He Er-gou’s vigilance. "Shake them off."

The corners of He Er-gou’s mouth curled up; he had to show the Inspector his driving skills. "Alright, sit tight." As he spoke, his hands moved rapidly over the steering wheel, his feet dancing between the brake and the accelerator. With a screech of tires against the pavement, he successfully changed lanes. After a few more maneuvers, he managed to shake off the car behind them.

The black sedan stopped by the river, and Shen Zhizhen took the boat keys. "You two take the car away. Deliver it to the police station before you get off work and just leave the keys on my desk."

Wang Jiangsheng and He Er-gou nodded in agreement. Both were tactful enough not to probe into where the Inspector intended to dock the boat.

Shen Zhizhen opened the door and got out. She waited until He Er-gou drove away before walking toward the embankment. From a distance, she saw a tall figure standing on the levee, gazing out at the river.

As Shen Zhizhen approached and saw Wan Donglai’s face clearly, she thought, *Hmm, he’s a handsome guy.* The person before her overlapped with the figure in the original owner's memories, and an inexplicable sense of familiarity flooded her heart.

Seeing Shen Jiu again after so many years, Wan Donglai was filled with excitement. He broke into a wide smile. "Long time no see. Why did you cut your hair?" The capable, short hair paired with a police uniform suited her strangely well.

Shen Zhizhen raised her hand to block the hand reaching out to ruffle her hair. "Mind your own business." With that, she walked toward where the boat was docked.

As she walked, she grumbled to herself, *He’s quite familiar, isn't he? Although in her memories, ruffling her hair was a daily routine for them, the soul inside has changed, hasn't it? I’m not your 'white moonlight'.*

Wan Donglai chuckled aloud. The little girl had become quite haughty. He smiled and followed behind Shen Jiu.

Shen Zhizhen found the boat she had embezzled, boarded it, untied the ropes, checked that everything was in order, and started the engine to depart.

Wan Donglai had been following her, busy with the preparations. Seeing Shen Jiu start the boat and leave, he couldn't help but sigh that after not seeing her for a few years, the little girl had even learned to pilot a boat.

Shen Zhizhen...

Although the original owner was a talented tomb raider, she really didn't possess the skill to pilot a boat. This was a skill Shen Zhizhen brought with her; her own father was in the shipping business. During her elementary school years, she spent almost every winter and summer vacation on boats; it would have been harder for her *not* to know how to pilot one.

As the boat headed upstream into the middle of the river, Shen Zhizhen gripped the helm and asked, "Wu De said you were looking for him to get medicine?"

Hearing this, Wan Donglai withdrew his gaze from the river and turned to look at Shen Jiu. "How much can you get, and at what price?"

The organization didn't have much money to spare, and every cent had to be spent carefully. But this time, the front lines were in urgent need of medicine, so they had to secure it regardless of the cost.

Wan Donglai believed Shen Jiu could get the medicine. Police had access to smuggled goods, and confiscating some was standard procedure.

Shen Zhizhen’s original intention was to befriend the Red Party, so naturally, she wouldn't ask for much. She actually wanted to donate it for free, but the window hadn't been pierced yet, and they hadn't seen each other for years. If she just blurted out that she knew Wan Donglai was a Red Party member, how would she explain it? She couldn't exactly say she knew because she had read the book.

After thinking it over, she said, "I have about a hundred boxes each of Chinese and Western medicine on hand. I haven't counted them too carefully."

"You should know the rules of the trade. I won't ask why you're buying medicine, and you don't ask where I got it. Pay what you think is fair; you should know I’m not short on money." *Well, I’ve said as much as I can; Wan Donglai should be able to catch the drift.*

As soon as Wan Donglai heard this, he knew the medicine in Shen Jiu’s hands was illicit, but that had nothing to do with him. He only needed to get the medicine urgently needed at the front lines to the soldiers.
