He knew the Shen family came from a background of tomb raiding; the young master of the Shen family couldn't possibly be short on money. Giving the medicine to him was likely just a way to offload it.

Wan Donglai’s eyes were filled with joy. Just yesterday, he was racking his brain over where to get medicine, never expecting that the appearance of his little cousin this morning would solve the problem.

The boat sailed steadily on the river. Once they had set the time and place for the delivery, a silence fell over the cockpit.

"Um, do you know about what happened to my family?" After finishing the business, Wan Donglai wanted to ask about the Wan family.

After returning to the country, he had been working in Shanghai, but because he had joined the Red Party, he had kept it hidden from his family. A month ago, he suddenly heard the tragic news from home. He rushed back, and even the burial of his family members had been done in secret. He only knew a rough outline of what had happened to the Wan family.

"I know. That day, there was a heavy snowstorm. A squad of Japanese troops came, robbed your family's jewelry store, killed many people, and even captured your father..." Shen Zhizhen recounted the events of that day in a flat tone.

She looked back and saw that Wan Donglai was already covered in tears, the sorrow and pain overflowing from his eyes, making one feel stifled.

Shen Zhizhen turned back to look at the river and continued with the aftermath. "Later, I asked my second uncle why the Wan family met with disaster. He told me that your father’s seventh concubine, Bai Moli, was a high-level Japanese agent whose Japanese name was Baidao Xiangzhi."

Upon hearing this, Wan Donglai clenched his fists so tightly that the veins on the back of his hands bulged. With a trembling voice, he asked, "Why would a high-level Japanese agent infiltrate the Wan family—"

chapters.title: Actually, She Wanted to Give It Away for Free
chapters.content:
The grief and indignation in Wan Donglai's eyes were replaced by confusion. If the Japanese troops were only after the Wan family's assets, there would be no need to send a high-level agent to infiltrate the family.

Shen Zhizhen sighed softly. "Because they were looking for a treasure map. It wasn't just the Wan family that had Japanese agents infiltrated; the Japanese troops planted them in other families in Shenyang, including our Shen family. Your family’s disaster happened because Baidao Xiangzhi, who was hiding in your home, was exposed."

Only then did Wan Donglai realize why his family had met with disaster, but what was this treasure map? In his memory, the Wan family had no such thing.

"What treasure map? Was the agent hiding in your family found?"

Shen Zhizhen didn't mention the treasure map; the other information about the map was told to her by Shen San. This matter involved Shen San’s personal safety, so she wouldn't speak of it to others without permission. She only said, "Found her. It was my stepmother, An Hui. Shen San ordered her to be dealt with."

Wan Donglai was stunned. When had Shen San become so decisive and ruthless? Could it be that he changed after entering the No. 76 branch?

Wan Donglai thought that Shen’s second uncle seemed to be a traitor, and Shen San was a secret agent, so could Shen Jiu also be...? Were those two hundred boxes of medicine a lie to trick him?

For a moment, many questions arose in Wan Donglai’s mind. Meeting Shen Jiu’s calm eyes, he wanted to question her, but the words died on his lips. Whether it was true or not, wouldn't he know by tomorrow? At worst, he would go to pick up the goods alone.

In Wan Donglai’s heart, Shen Jiu was his childhood playmate, his confidante, his sweetheart. Without evidence, he didn't want to doubt her.

Shen Zhizhen didn't know what Wan Donglai was thinking. If she did, she would surely sigh and wonder if a "white moonlight" who hadn't died would affect the plot.

Seeing that Shen Jiu didn't mention the treasure map again, Wan Donglai knew she didn't want to talk more about it and tactfully didn't ask further.

Shen Zhizhen docked the boat on the shore and said to Wan Donglai, "The person who ordered the killing of your whole family is called Tanaka Fumiya. Believe it or not, it’s up to you, but you must remember this name and be careful if you ever run into him." With that, she signaled for Wan Donglai to get off the boat.

Shen Zhizhen ignored Wan Donglai’s hesitation. After driving him off the boat, she sailed away. An hour later, she arrived near the house Wu De had rented.

Shen Zhizhen took a set of casual clothes out of her space to change into, threw the police uniform she had taken off into the space, and found a wig to wear before getting off the boat. She used the key to confirm the rented house, parked the boat in the backyard, locked it, secured the ropes, and went ashore.

The house was detached with a backyard facing the river. Shen Zhizhen looked around and quite liked it. She wasn't in a hurry to leave; instead, she opened the windows to let in some air and took out her tools to continue making the fake Phoenix Order.

Since she had already concluded that there were nine Phoenix Orders, she naturally had to make nine fakes. Making them all at once would save trouble later. As for whether they could all be used, that was not something Shen Zhizhen was considering for the time being.

After getting off the boat, Wan Donglai stood alone on the embankment, watching the surging river to compose his emotions. He went over what Shen Jiu had said in his mind before going to find Old Gu to report the situation.

In a residential area in Zhabei, after meeting Old Gu, Wan Donglai recounted his conversation with Shen Jiu. After taking a sip of tea, ignoring Old Gu’s shocked expression, he also explained Shen Jiu’s background—though he omitted the parts related to his own family; that was his private business and there was no need to bring it up and add to the trouble.

After listening to Wan Donglai, Old Gu’s head was buzzing. He looked at him and earnestly advised, "Comrade Donglai, this Miss Shen Jiu was once a tomb raider, her own second uncle is a traitor, and her own sister is a secret agent for No. 76. Do you think what she said is credible?"

Sigh, he also hoped the medicine was real, but no matter how he thought about it, it seemed impossible. The more he heard, the more it sounded like a trap.

Wan Donglai replied firmly, "I understand Comrade Old Gu’s concerns, so I will go to pick up the goods alone tomorrow. I guarantee that I will never implicate the organization."

If he were unfortunately captured, he would give his life, but he would never betray the faith in his heart, let alone the fact that he had an irreconcilable blood feud with the Japanese.

"Comrade Old Gu, I have known Shen Jiu since childhood. She is a person who has her own code, even among thieves. She cannot change her background, but I do not believe she is someone who would act as a tiger's accomplice or help the evildoer."

Comrade Wan Donglai’s resonant words left Old Gu speechless for a moment. Worried, he paced back and forth on the ground with his hands behind his back.

Wan Donglai was a good comrade, and he naturally believed him. The key now was that Shen Jiu—what if she wasn't trustworthy? Could he just watch Wan Donglai get caught?

Wan Donglai: "Old Gu, I understand your concerns, but that is two hundred boxes of medicine. What if it’s real?"

Did he not know the risks were high? But what if it were real? As long as Shen Jiu was fine with this transaction, they could safely let her get whatever supplies they needed in the future.

Wan Donglai shared his thoughts with Old Gu. "Shen Jiu’s current status is Inspector of the Third Inspection Group of the Shanghai West Branch. Her patrol area is the cross-border area where smuggling is rampant. It is much easier for her to get supplies than us. As long as this line is stable, how much can we do to help the front lines? Most importantly, she is not short on money. She offered the price at 20% of the market rate. We can pay when we have money, and if we don't, we can negotiate to pay later."

When he asked about the price, Shen Jiu told him to pay whatever he thought was fair. The 20% of the market price was something he had said jokingly; he didn't expect Shen Jiu to actually agree. If this deal were truly completed, Shen Jiu would practically be doing charity.

The more Old Gu heard, the more terrified he became. This "pie falling from the sky" was just too unreliable. He quickly reached out to signal Wan Donglai to stop talking, asking him to calm down and think for a while.

Shen Zhizhen didn't know about the struggle within the Red Party. Even if she did, she would only give a wry smile and tell Old Gu that she actually wanted to give it away for free. Sigh, if it weren't for the special circumstances, she wouldn't believe she was this selfless either.

Today's progress was faster than yesterday's. Yesterday, being in a hotel, I didn't dare to make too much noise or create any strong odors. Today was different; with a private house and high walls, I could let myself go.

Before dark, I finished six more semi-finished products. I’ll have to find time to buy the plating materials; I don't have any in my space.

Shen Zhizhen locked the door and went out. She wandered around the neighborhood for a while to get familiar with the surroundings, then hailed a rickshaw to the International Settlement. Once there, she transferred to a tram, and after a few more transfers, she finally arrived home.

She didn't go to pick up her car. The place she rented was quite a detour from the West Shanghai Branch, and it wasn't worth the hassle to drive it back and forth.

Shen Zhimei leaned against the window with a glass of red wine. Seeing Xiao Jiu get off the rickshaw without a car, she wondered what she had been up to.

Shen Zhizhen opened the door and walked in, seeing Shen San standing by the window with a glass of red wine. "What are you doing? Admiring the moon?"

"Waiting for you." Shen Zhimei was successfully amused.

"What for?"

"Let's go to the Paramount tonight for some fun."

Shen Zhizhen was speechless at the suggestion. "Shen San, I always feel like you're trying to lead me astray." Who takes their younger sister to a dance hall?

The little girl was a grave robber herself; she didn't need anyone to lead her astray. "You're already a thief, you don't need me to lead you! Stop talking nonsense and go change your clothes."

Shen Zhizhen... Chapter 49: The Paramount

As night fell, the black sedan drove onto Jing'an Temple Road. Shen Zhizhen looked out the window at the dazzling, massive neon sign of the night in Shanghai—this was the Paramount, known as the premier entertainment venue in the Far East.

Various luxury cars pulled up in front of the Paramount. Well-dressed men and women stepped out arm-in-arm, greeted respectfully by the doormen.

The black sedan stopped, and the driver opened the door. Shen Zhimei stepped out wearing a red cheongsam. With her wavy hair, sexy red lips, alluring figure, and beautiful face, she attracted everyone's attention the moment she appeared.

Shen Zhizhen was wearing a blue embroidered cheongsam today. After getting out, she was almost blinded by the flashing neon lights. She put on her sunglasses, walked over to the flamboyant woman, and draped her suit jacket over her shoulders.

Shen Zhimei cast a sidelong glance at her, reached out to hook her arm into the "little prude's," and they walked inside.

The air was filled with the scent of perfume, cigars, and alcohol, amidst the rustle of silk and the clinking of glasses.

The sisters separated on the second floor. Shen Zhimei took her bodyguard up to the third floor, which featured a mezzanine structure with an open center surrounded by a gallery.

Shen Zhimei found a seat with an excellent view, ordered a bottle of red wine from a waiter, and leaned back lazily, sipping her wine while looking down over the railing at the dance floor, taking in the revelry below.

Shen Zhizhen wandered around the second floor, feeling as though she were watching a parade of human nature; various whispers reached her ears, making it impossible to distinguish truth from falsehood.

They had come on a mission. Shen Zhimei had received news that high-ranking Japanese military officials were hosting an important figure at the Paramount tonight. Shen San suspected this person was Tanaka Bun'ya and had brought her along to confirm it.

Since she had never seen Tanaka Bun'ya and had only heard his voice, she could only prick up her ears and wander around, eavesdropping.

Shen Zhizhen circled the second floor, which was an eye-opener: spring-loaded wooden floors, glass dance floors, a top-tier jazz band, and dance hostesses who were all stunningly beautiful with superb dancing skills. It was no wonder that celebrities and military/political figures loved coming to such a luxurious playground.

She felt this place was like a miniature Shanghai—modernity, luxury, and desire all mixed together, with a hint of end-of-the-world revelry. These people were using this drunken, dream-like state to escape reality.

Shen Zhizhen took a cocktail upstairs, walked around the gallery, and sat down opposite Shen San. She traced the character "three" on the tabletop with her finger. A voice in that private room earlier had reminded her of what Tanaka Bun'ya had said: "If the weeds are not pulled by the roots, the spring breeze will make them green again."

Shen Zhimei hadn't expected to find him so quickly. She recalled that the private room had been occupied before they arrived, and a few minutes ago, Jing Shenhaoichi from the Ume Agency had entered with a man of refined temperament.

Once the room was identified, the rest was simple. Shen Zhimei stood up and smiled, "Come on, let's go dance." With that, she took off her jacket, handed it to her subordinate, and dragged Shen Jiu downstairs onto the dance floor.

Her red cheongsam looked like a flowing fire; her dance moves were unrestrained and naturally seductive. Her hands, painted with bright red nail polish, traced soft arcs in the air, as if inviting or seducing.

Shen Zhizhen was speechless watching Shen San let loose and show off her charm. She had no choice but to sway along to the rhythm, occasionally shooing away the various men who swarmed toward the attention-seeking Shen San.

The sisters danced passionately, but their attention remained fixed on the private room upstairs. The moment the door to Room No. 3 opened, they both noticed. Shen Zhimei glanced out of the corner of her eye to confirm, then stopped paying attention, dancing as if nothing were wrong and leaving the rest to Xiao Jiu.

Shen Zhizhen’s surveillance was hidden behind her sunglasses. Once she locked onto the target, she continued to shoo away the "bees" around Shen San, but her ears remained focused on the people leaving the room.

Jing Shenhaoichi and Tanaka Bun'ya walked out of the room. They walked along the gallery toward the stairs, their eyes occasionally sweeping over the dance floor. When they saw that alluring figure, they both stopped in their tracks.

A flash of amazement crossed Tanaka Bun'ya's eyes. He admired her for a moment before asking his companion, "Jing Shen-kun, do you know who that woman in the red cheongsam is?"

Jing Shenhaoichi withdrew his gaze, lowered his head slightly, and replied, "She is Shen Zhimei, Secretary-General of the No. 76 Branch. Rumor has it she has a special relationship with Mr. Zhou Fuhai in Nanjing."

Tanaka Bun'ya nodded slightly, gave her a meaningful look, and walked out.

The moment Tanaka Bun'ya spoke, Shen Zhizhen confirmed his identity. After hearing what he said, a cold light flashed in her eyes. *Hmph, a lecher.* After the two men left, she leaned into Shen San's ear and repeated what she had heard.

When Shen Zhimei heard that she might have caught the eye of a pervert, goosebumps immediately rose on her arms. The alcohol began to hit her, and feeling a bit dizzy, she leaned on Xiao Jiu's arm and walked off the dance floor.

Shen Zhizhen signaled the bodyguard and took the suit jacket to drape over Shen Zhimei.

Shen Zhimei raised a hand to rub her forehead. "I'm a bit dizzy. Let's go back."

The black sedan drove away from the Paramount. The driver looked in the rearview mirror and asked, "That car is following us again. Should I shake them off?"

Shen Zhimei closed her eyes, feigning sleep, and shook her head slightly. "No need."

They had shaken people off earlier to prevent them from spying on their purpose at the Paramount. Now that they were just going home, there was no need for extra actions.

Shen Zhizhen looked back at the car window, her gaze lingering on the car following them. It wasn't hard to guess where they were going based on their attire tonight, so it wasn't surprising they were followed.

The car was silent all the way, both sisters lost in their own thoughts. Shen Zhizhen was thinking about the trade with the Red Party tomorrow night; as for tonight's events, she would discuss them in detail with Shen San when they got home.

The moment Shen Zhimei confirmed the person with Jing Shenhaoichi was Tanaka Bun'ya, she knew the Tang Mansion murder case must be related to him. The Phoenix Token they found at the Tang Mansion was related to the Phoenix Emperor's Tomb; Tanaka Bun'ya's mission wasn't just to find the treasure map, but also the Phoenix Token.

Thinking of this, she rubbed her brow. It seemed the information her teacher gave her wasn't complete. Was it a lack of trust, or did the teacher not know?

Shen Zhimei already had the answer in her heart. A teacher who could obtain information about the "Takama-ga-hara" plan from Japan couldn't possibly know about the treasure map but not the Phoenix Token.

So, either she wasn't trusted, or the mission had been split up. If it was split, it meant another group was also tasked with finding the Phoenix Token.

The car stopped at No. 36. The two got out and went inside. Shen Zhizhen changed into slippers and went to the kitchen to pour two glasses of water. She set them on the coffee table and flopped onto the sofa, watching Shen San check if anyone had entered the house or installed any listening devices.

This was a routine she performed every day. She picked up the glass, took a sip, and only after the other woman sat on the sofa did she ask, "What now?"

Shen Zhimei draped her jacket over the sofa, sat back lazily, and shared her suspicions from the car. "I'll send someone to keep an eye on Tanaka Bun'ya. You handle the rest."

Shen Zhizhen knew exactly what Shen San wanted her to do. She nodded to show she understood. Chapter 50: Willing to Contribute a Modest Effort to Share the National Crisis

The next day, a black sedan stopped outside the West Shanghai Branch.

Shen Zhizhen got out and watched Shen San's car drive away. She noticed the car that had been following them hadn't followed Shen San, and her eyebrows arched; she immediately understood they intended to follow her instead.

It made sense. Once Shen Zhimei entered the No. 76 Branch, she stayed there all day. Following her would yield nothing, because that woman always ordered others to do her bidding. How would the followers know what she was up to? That was why they were targeting her.

Shen Zhizhen shrugged. *Heh, she would have to find an opportunity to let these little Japanese know the consequences of following her.*

Walking into the police station, she saw her car parked in the courtyard. He Ergou was using a bucket and rag to wash it.

Shen Zhizhen walked over and chatted with He Ergou for a while, getting quite a bit of information from him. She handed him the spare car key and patted his shoulder as she left. *Promising kid, knows how to use this method to talk to her one-on-one and pass along information.*

In the Third Patrol Group office, everyone stood by the window looking out. Seeing the Patrol Chief hand the car key to He Ergou, Ma San exclaimed, "He really managed to cozy up to the Chief."

Lin Wu withdrew his gaze upon hearing this. "What do you mean? Why would the Chief give the car key to Doggy?"

Wang Jiangsheng smiled and explained how He Ergou had volunteered to be the driver yesterday. Everyone was enlightened. No wonder the kid had been so diligent today; not only had he cleaned the Chief's seat, but he had also taken the initiative to wash the car. It turned out he was washing it for himself!

Huang Dazhi and Mu Daqiang could only envy him; they didn't have the same knack for flattery.

Shen Zhizhen entered the office and assigned tasks to everyone. After solidifying Wang Jiangsheng's position as the second-in-command of the Third Patrol Group, she contentedly became a hands-off manager.

There was no helping it; she had too many things to do to be a hands-on police officer. She had to promote someone with prestige to lead the team.

Wang Jiangsheng understood that the Chief wouldn't stay in the Third Patrol Group for long. Once she left, the position of Patrol Chief would likely be his. Using the authority Shen Jiu gave him now made it easier for him to take over later.

The black sedan and two sidecars drove out of the police station, heading toward the boundary road area. He Ergou looked in the rearview mirror; sure enough, the car from yesterday was following them.

He Ergou asked Wang Jiangsheng, who was sitting next to him, with curiosity, "Guess whose side the people in that car are on?"

"We can't afford to offend either side, so let's just pretend we don't know." Given their Chief's ability to stir up trouble, it could be anyone.

Yesterday, the Bureau Chief had called him in to ask why Chief Shen had been so quiet lately. He had mentioned that someone was following the Chief, and he still wanted to laugh when he remembered the look of realization on the Bureau Chief's face.

He Ergou agreed, thinking the inspector must have his own way of handling things, and there was no need for them to go poking around and looking for trouble.

Shen Zhizhen put away the car keys on the table, waited in the office for five minutes before getting up to leave, and hailed a rickshaw at the police station entrance to head to the concessions.

She had originally intended to use chemical materials for plating; this method produces a realistic metallic texture. However, after hearing Shen San’s analysis last night that the thirteen murders at the Tang Mansion were also linked to Tanaka Bunya, she immediately changed her mind.

Since Tanaka Bunya was looking for the Phoenix Order, it meant he at least knew about it, and might even possess it. Such a person would not be easily fooled. She had to ensure that what she created could deceive even the most discerning eyes, so she decided to use more professional electroplating for the coloring.

Shen Zhizhen first bought electroplating solution, potassium sulfide, and other supplies at a hardware and chemical store in the concessions. Afterward, she transferred vehicles several times to reach the house she had rented by the river, where she worked until dark before setting off by boat.

A boat navigated the river under the cover of night. Shen Zhizhen steered past Caojiadu and continued westward, where the river channels were relatively remote and supervision was lax.

The location Wan Donglai had chosen was remote even by those standards. The boat pulled up near the agreed-upon reed marsh.

Shen Zhizhen turned off the engine and entered the cabin, moving the medicine out of her storage space until the entire cabin was packed full.

She then stood on the deck, gazing into the moonlight, her eyes fixed on the reed marsh that swayed from time to time. She crossed her arms and waited for the other party to approach.

Deep within the reed marsh, ten black-awning boats were gathered together. Old Gu, unable to resist the temptation of two hundred crates of medicine, had finally decided to take the risk. However, he had made some contingency plans, not only gathering ten comrades but also bringing a batch of weapons in case they had to fight their way out if they couldn't retreat.

Seeing the boat stop, Wan Donglai squinted for a while, confirmed it was Shen Jiu’s boat, and turned to Old Gu, saying, "It’s the boat I was on yesterday. I’ll go over and check first; I’ll give you a signal if everything is fine."

Old Gu nodded in agreement, and one black-awning boat quietly rowed toward the docked vessel.

Seeing the other party’s dawdling, Shen Zhizhen guessed the reason. She looked at the moon in silence for a while, patiently waiting for Wan Donglai.

In truth, she could understand; it was right for revolutionary workers to be cautious. After all, her family background was indeed complicated, and the "pie" she had thrown out was so large that she would have been suspicious too. However, as long as this transaction was completed and trust was established, things would be easier in the future.

Standing on the black-awning boat, Wan Donglai saw Shen Jiu looking at the sky from the deck and sheepishly rubbed his nose, climbing aboard only when the boats were close.

Shen Zhizhen gestured toward the cabin, "It’s all in the cabin. You can move it yourselves in a moment. If there’s anything, find me in the wheelhouse." With that, she walked toward the wheelhouse.

She didn't intend to overexpose herself to the Red Party. Meeting Wan Donglai’s superior was fine, but the others were unnecessary. In this day and age, being in the Red Party was a high-risk profession; if they were caught and sold her out, she could escape, but what about Shen San? To prevent unnecessary trouble, her caution was justified.

Wan Donglai understood her meaning instantly. Only he and Old Gu knew Shen Jiu’s identity, and even with Old Gu’s heavy concerns, he hadn't mentioned Shen Jiu to anyone else.

Wan Donglai had his suspicions and couldn't help but ask, "Do you know who I am?"

Shen Zhizhen raised an eyebrow at this, feeling it was better to be clear now to avoid the trouble of both sides guessing.

"Don't be silly. Who would buy medicine in bulk at a time like this? Excluding those with a blood feud against you, isn't it obvious which side you would choose given your character?"

"The country is shattered and in turmoil; I wish to contribute my meager strength to share the burden of the national crisis." After saying this, Shen Zhizhen turned and continued toward the wheelhouse.

Ecstasy flashed in Wan Donglai’s eyes. He calmed his emotions, walked around the boat, and then went to the cabin. Opening it, he saw a cabin full of goods, and the wooden crates were much larger than they had expected. Joy filled his eyes as he opened one—it was aspirin.

Once Wan Donglai confirmed the cargo was fine, he ran to the deck and waved a signal toward the depths of the reed marsh.

Old Gu’s face lit up. Suppressing his excitement, he ordered the black-awning boats to row over.

chapters.title: Robbing the Rich to Help the Poor
chapters.content:
After Old Gu boarded the boat, Wan Donglai pulled him aside and whispered what Shen Jiu had just said.

When Old Gu heard the words about contributing meager strength to share the burden of the national crisis, his eyes grew hot. So that was it; he had been looking at her through biased lenses.

The two whispered for a while. Once their people were all on board, they signaled for Wan Donglai to show them the goods. When everyone saw the cabin full of medicine, ecstasy flashed in their eyes.

At this moment, Wan Donglai poured cold water on the situation: "The ten black-awning boats we brought can't carry all this medicine."

When Shen Jiu said there were two hundred crates, he had instinctively assumed they were the small boxes used in hospitals, never imagining they would be the large wooden crates used for military supplies.

Upon hearing this, Old Gu’s excitement dampened. He had been careless; not only was the quantity of medicine beyond their expectations, but the money they had prepared was also insufficient. He had estimated the price based on hospital-sized boxes, and even that amount had been difficult to scrape together.

"You wait here and stay alert. Little Wan, take me to see that person." After saying this, Old Gu took the suitcase containing the money and followed Wan Donglai to the wheelhouse.

Shen Zhizhen was still wondering why these people weren't moving the cargo; shouldn't they be quick about such things? Just as she was complaining internally, she saw Wan Donglai enter with a middle-aged man.

Wan Donglai: "Shen Jiu, this is Old Gu. We need to discuss something with you." He looked embarrassed, never having expected such a blunder.

Shen Zhizhen guessed that this Old Gu was Wan Donglai’s superior, so she took the initiative to greet him: "Hello, what can I do for you?"

Old Gu put on a smile and placed the suitcase on a stool, opening it: "This is the payment we raised. We just opened the cabin to check the goods, and I’m afraid this isn't enough."

Shen Zhizhen wondered what the issue was, but upon hearing it was about money, she generously replied: "It doesn't matter. Whether it's more or less is irrelevant. I just want to contribute my meager strength."

Old Gu was moved. Although this Miss Shen Jiu was not their comrade, her awareness was incredibly high, making him feel embarrassed to say what followed.

Old Gu: "Miss Shen, thank you very much for your support. There is just one more matter I must trouble you with."

Confusion flashed in Shen Zhizhen’s eyes. She glanced at Wan Donglai, and seeing the young man looking sheepish, she didn't understand what was going on, so she gestured for him to speak directly.

Wan Donglai realized this was his misjudgment, so he explained the current difficulty: "We brought ten black-awning boats, and they can't fit two hundred crates of medicine." Not to mention two hundred, they couldn't even take one hundred.

Shen Zhizhen understood. They had their eyes on her boat. Of course, they meant to borrow it, but she thought, why not go the extra mile? Her original intention was to connect with the Red Party, and since there was an opportunity to make an impression, she wouldn't let it pass.

She said: "This boat is a smuggling vessel I seized. You can take it and don't need to return it; just leave me one black-awning boat so I can get back."

These words moved them deeply. Under their gaze, Shen Zhizhen jumped onto a black-awning boat. She looked at the suitcase they were holding and decided to be a good person to the end.

With a forceful swing, she threw the suitcase of money back to Wan Donglai on the boat, then waved her hand and poled away.

The medicine had been obtained and had to be sent away immediately. Old Gu arranged for one person to row the black-awning boat into the depths of the reed marsh, while the rest stayed behind to escort the medicine.

While steering, Old Gu said to Wan Donglai beside him: "Miss Shen has high awareness. We should try to develop her; we shouldn't exclude her just because her family situation is complicated."

Today, she had sailed the boat here, brought over two hundred crates of medicine, and when she left, she hadn't taken a cent and even gave them such a new boat. For someone with this level of awareness and patriotism, not developing her into one of their own would be a loss to the organization.

Wan Donglai agreed wholeheartedly: "If we recruit Shen Jiu into the organization, she will become a great asset to us in Shanghai."

This time, the front line was in urgent need of medicine. It would have been difficult to obtain so much without casualties, but Shen Jiu had solved this problem effortlessly. Not only did she refuse payment, but she also gave them a boat!

Old Gu decided that as soon as this batch of medicine was delivered, he would file a report to his superiors.

Shen Zhizhen didn't know that a massive opportunity was about to fall on her head. She was currently poling her boat along the river. This area was remote, mostly farmland, and she needed to get the boat to a place with road access.

As she poled, she pondered where to get more supplies. She couldn't let her two-thousand-square-meter space sit empty, could she? She had now connected with the Red Party, and it was possible Wan Donglai would come looking for her again.

Moreover, getting things on the fly was risky. Even if they gave the goods to the Red Party, it wouldn't be easy for them to move them out of Shanghai. This transaction had been perfect; the medicine wasn't sourced in Shanghai, there was no word of it here, and the Red Party could transport it out quietly.

With that in mind, she decided to pull off something big. One piece of information He Ergou had provided earlier caught her attention: a Mitsui Trading Company freighter was departing from Shiliupu Wharf tomorrow morning.

Mitsui Trading Company—she remembered the name immediately. The ten crates of smuggled goods she had seized previously belonged to them. Since they were so wealthy, it wouldn't be excessive for her to "rob the rich to help the poor," would it?

The black-awning boat docked at the shore. Shen Zhizhen stepped off and tucked the boat into her space; it was small and didn't take up much room, and it was quite useful in a pinch.

After walking for ten minutes, she finally found a road. She brought out the truck she had acquired in Changbai Mountain and headed straight for the Shiliupu Wharf warehouse.

Late at night, the wharf was still brightly lit, and workers were loading cargo onto a freighter.

Shen Zhizhen changed into black clothes and, under the cover of night, climbed onto the Mitsui Trading Company freighter.

Once on board, she found a hidden spot to hide and took a nap, waking up only when the ship set sail at dawn. She took a pizza out of her space and ate it.

Three hours after the freighter had been sailing, Shen Zhizhen came out to move around. Avoiding the guards, she found the cargo hold, picked the lock with a needle, and slipped inside.

The goods in the hold were mainly in three types of packaging: regular wooden crates, burlap sacks, and sturdy canvas bags.

Shen Zhizhen took a crowbar from her space and pried open a crate, only to find it filled with medicine. A question mark flashed in her mind: did the Mitsui Trading Company also traffic in medicine?

Although puzzled, she still moved the medicine into her space. She hadn't expected that just after sending off one batch, she would replenish her stock so quickly.

The wooden crates in the cargo hold were all filled with medicine, the sacks contained grain, and the canvas bags held military uniforms. The moment she saw the uniforms, Shen Zhizhen thought of the oil drums on the deck and finally understood that the Mitsui Trading Company was transporting military supplies this time.

chapters.title: Sinking
chapters.content:
Generally, there are four places to store cargo on a freighter. The first is the cargo hold under the deck where she had just been; this is the freighter's main hold.

The second place is the open deck area; this freighter had gasoline drums stacked on its deck.

The third place is the deep tank. The deep tank is located within the ship's internal structure where it is more reinforced, and it is generally used to store high-value cargo.

The fourth is the liquid cargo tank, a specialized tank used for vegetable oil, alcohol, and chemicals.

Having risked so much to come here, Shen Zhizhen naturally wouldn't just take the ordinary goods from the cargo hold under the deck. After exiting the hold and locking the door, she avoided the patrols and made her way to the deep tank.

Seeing someone guarding the entrance to the deep tank, she flashed forward, chopped at their necks, and with two sharp cracks, the two guards at the cabin door collapsed to the ground.

She took out a lockpick, quickly opened the cabin door, and threw the two men lying on the floor inside. There weren't many cargo crates inside—a quick glance revealed about twenty boxes. She opened one at random and found it filled with calligraphy and paintings.

Shen Zhizhen picked one up, unrolled it, and after examining it carefully for a while, confirmed it was an authentic copy of the *Xiaoxiang Woyou Tu* (Traveling in Xiaoxiang). This painting is hailed as the greatest masterpiece of Southern Song landscape painting. To think that a national treasure-level painting was just sitting in an ordinary wooden crate with a pile of other paintings.

There was no time to sigh. Shen Zhizhen collected all the crates here; if any random box could contain a national treasure-level painting, the contents of the other boxes would certainly not be of low value.

Shen Zhizhen exited the deep tank and went straight to the deck. She quietly removed half of the gasoline drums, then used her agility to jump into the sea. The moment her body cleared the railing, she threw two grenades at the remaining gasoline drums on the deck.

Boom, boom, boom... A series of explosions rang out. The deck instantly turned into a sea of fire, and the entire ship fell into chaos.

*Splash.* The sound of her hitting the water was masked by the massive explosions. Shen Zhizhen swam toward the propeller shaft, took an explosive pack out of her spatial storage, and swung it hard to successfully hook it onto the shaft. She repeated this action, hanging five explosive packs in total before leaving.

Swimming thirty meters away, she took a grenade from her storage and threw it at the explosive packs hooked to the propeller shaft. After a loud explosion, the stern tube ruptured and the hull was torn open.

Seeing the seawater begin to rush into the hull, Shen Zhizhen left with peace of mind. The waves kicked up by the explosion washed her over a hundred meters away. She took a covered sampan out of her storage, climbed aboard, changed her clothes, and took out binoculars to look at the freighter. The hull was already tilting; it was only a matter of time before it sank.

Shanghai, Mitsui Trading Company clubhouse. *Ring-ring-ring...* A frantic telephone bell rang. President Mitsui picked up the phone, and after listening, he nearly suffered a heart attack from the rage.

On that freighter, in addition to war supplies, there were precious items obtained in China—things he had spent great effort and most of his wealth to acquire. He had intended for the freighter to return to Japan from Dalian and planned to send these items back then. He never expected... A mouthful of blood sprayed out as he collapsed backward. His secretary, seeing this, was terrified and hurriedly called for people to take the President to the hospital.

A few minutes later, the Japanese secret service agency, the Military Police, No. 76, and the police station all received the news: the freighter sent by the Mitsui Trading Company to Dalian had sunk at sea early this morning.

The various parties reacted differently to this news. The Japanese were furious, issuing several orders in quick succession, and the entire Shanghai Bund suddenly became tense and fearful.

No. 76, Secretary-General's office. Shen Zhimei held a teacup, standing by the window watching car after car drive out of No. 76. With one order from the Ume Agency, the special action teams of No. 76 had to act immediately.

Shen Zhimei took a sip of tea, the rising steam masking the flash of mockery in her eyes. She wondered if this was the result her teacher wanted.

Her eyelid had been twitching since last night. Xiao Jiu hadn't returned all night, and then the sinking of the Mitsui Trading Company ship happened today. It was all too coincidental.

Shen Zhimei didn't want to link this matter to Xiao Jiu, but every time she thought about what that girl had been doing over the past month, she couldn't lie to herself.

Shen Zhizhen did not know that Shen San was already suspicious of her. At this moment, she was on the sea, working hard to row the sampan, looking up at the sun from time to time to determine her direction.

The binoculars were placed in front of her, and she would use them to scout every so often, actively avoiding any ships she saw.

One can imagine the plight of a small boat in the vast ocean. Shen Zhizhen was slapped by waves from time to time, but fortunately, it was a clear day with small waves, and the sampan had not been overturned yet.

When the sun set, Shen Zhizhen finally saw land and almost cried with excitement. Even with her physical fitness, she couldn't handle being used like this. If it weren't for the food and water in her storage, she might not have made it back by now.

Shen Zhizhen ducked into the cabin to change into clean clothes and shoes. After going ashore, she put the sampan into her storage, found a direction to walk, and only brought out a truck once she saw a road.

At night, a rickshaw stopped outside 36 Fengyuan Road. After getting off, Shen Zhizhen looked around and found that the people monitoring her were gone. Puzzled, she walked inside, went upstairs, opened the door, and changed her shoes. Just as she looked up, a throw pillow flew toward her.

Shen Zhizhen caught it, touched her nose with a guilty conscience, walked over, sat down on the single sofa, and looked at Shen San with wide, innocent eyes, trying to calm her anger.

The ripples in Shen Zhimei's eyes vanished, leaving only a cold, scrutinizing gaze. "You had better have cleaned up your tracks, or you're leaving Shanghai tomorrow."

Shen Zhizhen...

She hadn't even said anything yet! She at least needed a chance to make up a story. So, she cleared her throat and said, "I had Wu De rent a small courtyard for me by the river. I've been there for the past two days making Phoenix Tokens. I was careful; no suspicious people went there."

Shen Zhimei was successfully amused by anger. Very good, the excuse was very thorough. "Oh, then take out the Phoenix Tokens you made and let me see."

Hearing this, Shen Zhizhen's lips curled up. She immediately took two Phoenix Tokens out of her pocket, slapped them onto the coffee table, and laughed: "Take a look, which one is real and which one is fake?"

Shen Zhimei's eyes narrowed slightly as she picked up the two Phoenix Tokens to compare them. They were exactly the same. She had to admit that this girl's forgery skills were truly superb; it was impossible to tell the real from the fake.

Shen Zhizhen looked smug. *Haha, of course Shen San can't tell the difference, because both are fake.* Hehe, once the real Phoenix Token reached her hands, it was impossible for her to take it out again.

Of course, if you asked her to take it out now, she couldn't anyway; after all, her storage was full.

Shen Zhimei put down the Phoenix Tokens and stated in a flat tone, "Today, a Mitsui Trading Company freighter sank in the waters off the Nanhui mudflats. The Japanese are furious and have strictly ordered the police, government, and special services to investigate thoroughly."

"Oh, who did it? Any clues?" Shen Zhizhen asked, feigning curiosity.

Shen Zhimei looked meaningfully at Xiao Jiu. "No definitive news yet, but there is word that some crew members have been rescued."

chapters.title: Fainting
chapters.content:
Shen Zhizhen laughed upon hearing this: "Whether they were rescued or not has nothing to do with me." Only then did she understand what Shen San meant by her words when she first entered the room.

Shen Zhizhen went over her actions on the ship in her mind, confirming that she hadn't left any traces.

Because she had been baptized by the Phoenix Coffin, her five senses and agility had improved several times over. As long as she wanted to, she could completely avoid anyone.

The only ones who had seen her face were the two guards at the entrance to the deep tank, but she had already sent them away.

Seeing Xiao Jiu's reaction, Shen Zhimei knew this girl wouldn't tell the truth, but as long as she cleaned up her tracks, she wouldn't pursue it further.

Shen Zhizhen changed the subject: "Why did the people monitoring us pull back?"

Shen Zhimei: "They lost track of you; why keep them there to be a joke?"

Shen Zhizhen...

"Don't be careless, either. Jing Shen Haoyi is a meticulous person; he won't let any suspicious points go. You'd better make some preparations in advance and align your story." After saying this, she got up and walked toward the bedroom. She hadn't slept well yesterday worrying about this girl, and she planned to sleep early tonight.

Hearing this, Shen Zhizhen immediately understood what to do. She knew in her heart that Shen San had not abandoned her suspicions, but had simply chosen not to get to the bottom of it. Perhaps this was the way of a smart person: to see through something without speaking of it.

If it weren't for the secret of her spatial storage, she would have wanted to show off to Shen San after pulling off such a big job.

Shen Zhizhen got up to get her pajamas and wash up. After showering, she couldn't help but check the twenty or so crates from the deep tank. Cultural relics, antiques, calligraphy, paintings, and jade carvings took up ten crates; jewelry and accessories took two crates each, and the remaining boxes were filled with gold.

She took them out box by box to check them one by one, becoming more shocked the more she looked. *Red and White Hibiscus*, *Snowy Landscape*, *Sangluan Tie*—these were all national treasures.

Shen Zhizhen felt incredibly fortunate at this moment. If she hadn't gone, wouldn't all these Chinese treasures have flowed into Japan?

After finishing one box, she would put it away and take out another to look through. She even checked the boxes filled with gold, mainly to see if there was anything else inside. And wouldn't you know it, while checking the last box of gold, she really did find a box.

This box was hidden by the crates filled with gold; there was no need to guess that the contents were very valuable.

Shen Zhizhen opened it with curiosity and immediately beamed with joy. Inside was actually a Phoenix Token. Having had the experience last time, she immediately threw the Phoenix Token into her storage. It was just a moment of weakness; she would pull through it.

As soon as the Phoenix Token entered her sea of consciousness, there was a loud *boom*, and Shen Zhizhen's vision went black as she fainted. Before losing consciousness, she put the box of gold on the floor into her storage. Her last thought was: *I was careless.*

At dawn, a car stopped in front of 36 Fengyuan Road. Qian Shengbai got out with a medical kit and climbed the stairs to the second floor.

At this time, Shen Zhimei's house was brightly lit. Hearing the knock, she went to open the door and, seeing it was Dr. Qian, hurriedly led him to the bedroom.

"Dr. Qian, my sister fainted for no reason in the bathroom." At first, she thought Xiao Jiu was playing around. She knew how capable this girl was; otherwise, she wouldn't keep causing trouble and remaining unscathed.

After discovering that Xiao Jiu was truly unconscious, she called Dr. Qian from Renji Hospital. During this time, she had been trying to wake her up, but without success.

Dr. Qian entered the bedroom and examined the person lying on the bed. The results of the examination surprised him.

Dr. Qian pushed up his glasses and looked at Shen Zhimei: "Your sister's heart rate, blood pressure, and cardiopulmonary functions are normal. The examination results are very healthy." The kind of healthy that comes with exceptionally good physical fitness.

Shen Zhimei frowned slightly upon hearing this: "Then why is she unconscious?"

Dr. Qian looked at the person on the bed and said with a hint of uncertainty: "She might just be asleep. Yes, she has entered a state of deep sleep."

Shen Zhimei...

Under the questioning gaze of Shen Zhimei, Dr. Qian finally had to change his tune: "Let's observe for now. If she doesn't wake up after more than eight hours of deep sleep, you can send her to the hospital for further examination." He then gave Shen Zhimei a brief explanation of the various causes of deep sleep.

Shen Zhimei only cared about one thing: "Can she be woken up?"

Dr. Qian said with a serious expression, "It is very difficult to wake someone in a deep sleep..." It was not that those in a deep sleep could not be woken up; it required using some intense or sustained stimulation on the sleeper, but he did not recommend doing that right now.

After seeing Dr. Qian off, Shen Zhimei waved to the people standing outside the door, signaling them to go and rest.

Returning to the bedroom and looking at Xiao Jiu's rosy complexion, she decided to tentatively believe Dr. Qian's somewhat outrageous judgment. She yawned, turned off the lights, and lay down on the bed.

Looking at Xiao Jiu's profile, she still couldn't convince herself. This girl had practiced martial arts since she was a child and had very high vigilance; how could she fall into such a deep sleep without any alertness at all?

Thinking of the reasons for deep sleep the doctor had mentioned, one of which was extreme exhaustion, a smile tugged at the corner of her mouth. She then stopped worrying, closed her eyes, and went to sleep.

Although the location where the Mitsui Trading Company's freighter sank was near the coast, if it was Xiao Jiu who blew up the ship, how did she get back? If she had swum back, then the doctor's explanation would make perfect sense.

Shen Zhijin did not know that her little secret had been guessed almost correctly by Shen San. Although she hadn't swum back, the effort she put into rowing that small awning boat felt much the same as swimming back.

She was currently in a state where she had external perception but could not control her body. She heard the conversation between Shen Zhimei and the doctor clearly, but simply lacked control over her physical form.

This state was somewhat similar to the first time the Phoenix Order merged with the Phoenix Coffin, but it was also a bit different. Last time, her soul had entered the sea of consciousness; this time, her soul hadn't entered anywhere, yet she could see an alien space.

Shen Zhijin couldn't explain what was happening. It was just that as soon as she thought about it, she could see a magnificent and extremely luxurious palace. The palace had floors paved with gold and walls built of white jade; night-pearls served as lamps, and the beams were cast from agarwood. The dome was painted with murals, and the air was filled with the fragrance of thousand-year-old agarwood.

Yes, she could smell it! At first, she thought it was an illusion, but she could smell it whenever she saw the palace, making her realize that this palace was real.

All these changes must be related to the newly integrated Phoenix Order. With this thought, she began to explore the palace with her mind. On the high platform of the main hall sat a sandalwood phoenix chair, and on the long table lay an imperial edict and a jade seal!

The east side hall was a study, with bookshelves against the walls filled with books, a sandalwood long table and chairs, and the four treasures of the study placed upon it.

The west side hall was a bedroom; the bed, vanity, screens, and ornaments were extremely luxurious. Outside the palace, it was gray and hazy, making it impossible to see clearly, as if there were a barrier blocking the view. Coincidentally, the area was the same size as her static space.

Seeing this, Shen Zhijin understood: this palace was a new space derived from the fusion of the Phoenix Order and the Phoenix Coffin. If she wasn't mistaken, she should be able to enter it.

chapters.title: Can't Take It Off
chapters.content:
The moment Shen Zhijin felt her body, she immediately withdrew her consciousness from the space, opened her eyes, turned to look at the window, carefully got out of bed, and walked out. She closed the bedroom door, scanned the living room, and finally let her gaze rest on the fish tank.

She walked over, scooped out a goldfish, and threw it into the palace. Seeing that the little goldfish didn't die, she immediately ran to the study, locked the door, and with a single thought, stood inside the palace.

Shen Zhijin happily toured the palace. After satisfying her curiosity, she sat on the sandalwood phoenix chair in the main hall and picked up the jade seal on the long table to examine it. Engraved on the bottom were the six characters: "Feng Xi, Mandate of Heaven."

Feng Xi? She had seen these two characters in the materials on the ancient Feng Kingdom that Shen San had found. Feng Xi was the name of the founding empress of the ancient Feng Kingdom.

The Phoenix Coffin, the Phoenix Order, and the treasure map were all related to the ancient Feng Kingdom. Did this mean that what Tanaka Bun'ya was executing—the Takamagahara Plan—was real, and that a place called the Nine Domains really existed in another world?

Shen Zhijin let her mind wander for a while, then decided that regardless of whether the Nine Domains existed or not, she couldn't let the Japanese succeed. Her main goal was to disrupt and obstruct.

Her gaze returned to the jade seal in her hand. Based on the material, this jade seal should be the Imperial Seal of the State, but based on the specifications, the characters on it, and the patterns carved on both sides, this jade seal should also be the Divine Seal that suppresses all nations and is never easily brought out.

In ancient times, the Divine Seal symbolized the supreme power of a dynasty and was the treasure of the state. It was usually kept secret and hidden deep within the palace, only brought out during ceremonies like heaven-worship, and was regarded as a token of communication between the emperor and heaven.

The Divine Seal was generally made of gold or copper, but the material of this one was jade. Breaking the convention must have a reason. Could it be because a woman ascended the throne that jade was chosen? She couldn't help but guess secretly.

Because dawn was approaching, Shen Zhijin didn't dare to linger in the palace for too long. After experimenting and confirming she could see outside the space through her mind, she chose to leave.

Since the space was derived from the upgrade of the Phoenix Coffin, it was hers. She could come in whenever she wanted in the future, so there was no rush to understand everything in the palace.

To be honest, compared to being in that palace, she preferred to stay outside. The reason, naturally, was that she preferred the feeling of being alive; in there, she always felt an inexplicable, oppressive sense of emptiness.

She raised her wrist to check the time; the time in the palace space was consistent with the outside.

This upgrade used the third Phoenix Order and derived a palace space the same size as the static space. A question flashed through her mind: could the Phoenix Order still be taken off like before?

With this doubt, Shen Zhijin immediately tried to manipulate the Phoenix Order as she had done before, but the Phoenix Order remained firmly embedded in the Phoenix Coffin without any reaction.

Shen Zhijin touched her nose feeling guilty and decided to let herself off the hook. She got up and went to the kitchen to make breakfast; she had offended Shen San over the past two days and had to coax her.

Morning light squeezed through the gaps in the curtains into the room, and spots of light fell on Shen Zhimei's delicate face. She opened her eyes and first looked beside her, seeing that it was already empty.

She really was tired! She got out of bed, took her clothes, and walked out of the room. Glancing at the busy figure in the kitchen, she went straight to the bathroom to wash up.

Shen Zhijin was humming a little tune in a very good mood. Hearing the movement, she looked back, put the finished sandwiches on a plate, and then poured the heated milk into a cup...

The black sedan stopped outside the Shanghai West Branch. Shen Zhijin got out, watched the car leave, then walked into the police station to check in with the Third Patrol Group. After chatting with everyone for a while, she drove away.

The people in the Third Patrol Group looked at each other. Lin Wu was the first to speak, "What do you think the Patrol Chief has been busy with these past two days? Such a big thing happened, and the Chief didn't even ask."

He Ergou knew that Lin Wu was talking about the sunken ship. "Whatever the Chief is busy with, you can ask her to her face next time. As for that big event, it has nothing to do with small fries like us."

Ma San: "Exactly. People are trying to avoid such things; who would go looking for trouble? Our Chief is being smart."

The public anger caused by the Central Reserve Bank notes was still there, and now that the public heard that a Japanese merchant ship had sunk, everyone was cheering.

Shen Zhijin drove to the rented house. This time, she did not deliberately avoid people. Since Shen San had already warned her, it meant that sooner or later they would find her. Since this house was her place to weave lies, its exposure was only a matter of time, so there was no need to cover it up.

This time, Shen Zhijin drove the car into the courtyard. After entering the house, she began to set up the scene, taking out some tools for making forgeries from the space, as well as several forgeries she had made before, and placing them around the house.

On the platform by the river in the backyard, she placed a chair and a set of fishing gear. Only after doing all this did she return to the house to rush a high-quality imitation as evidence of her being here for the past two days.

Shen Zhimei's car entered No. 76. As soon as she got out, she sensed that the atmosphere was wrong. Walking to the secretariat, she saw everyone gathered together chatting. After listening for a while, a look of realization flashed in her eyes.

Section Chief Zhang saw Shen Zhimei coming and quickly called her over to gossip, "A big shot came to see the Director early this morning. What do you think it's about?"

Shen Zhimei shrugged, "I just arrived, how would I know what it's about?" After saying this, she walked toward her office.

Ten minutes later, in the Director's office, Shen Zhimei knocked and entered. Seeing quite a few people inside, she smiled and said, "Director, you were looking for me?"

Ding Mocun: "It's these two who are looking for you." After the people walked over, he briefly introduced both sides.

"This is our No. 76 Secretary-General, Shen Zhimei."

"These two are Mr. Ii and Mr. Tanaka from the Umesato Agency. They are here to ask you a few questions."

After Ding Mocun introduced both sides, he picked up his teacup to drink tea, determined to stay out of it; he didn't want to offend either side.

Li Shiqun held the same thought. After telling Shen Zhimei to sit down, he also picked up his teacup to drink tea, just like Ding Mocun.

Shen Zhimei sat on the single sofa to the side and asked with a calm expression, "I wonder what you two want with me."

Ii Koichi: "We are looking for you to ask about your sister, Shen Jiu." The person he sent to monitor her said he had lost track of her, and the ship sinking occurred during the two days she was missing. Such a coincidence forced him to be cautious.

Tanaka Bun'ya did not speak, but his gaze had been locked on Shen Zhimei since she entered. Her confidence, composure, elegance, and beauty were just a facade; this woman was like a beautiful poisonous mushroom—very dangerous.

Shen Zhimei signaled for Ii Koichi to ask whatever he wanted.

Ii Koichi: "Your sister hasn't been to the police station for the past two days. Where did she go?"

Shen Zhimei: "Xiao Jiu told me she discovered someone was following her. She didn't know who wanted to kill her this time, so she went to a small courtyard rented by the river to stay for a couple of days and avoid the limelight."

Ii Koichi... This point was indeed a fact; he had indeed sent people to monitor her.

He cleared his throat and continued to press, "Where is the location? Can we go and take a look?"

Shen Zhimei spread her hands, "I haven't been there, I only know the general location. If you want to go, you'll have to find it yourselves."

chapters.title: By the Suzhou Creek
chapters.content:
"Secretary-General Shen doesn't seem surprised at all that we came to ask about your sister," Tanaka Bun'ya said with a meaningful tone.

Shen Zhimei lowered her eyes to hide the emotions in them and said nonchalantly, "My teacher has a piece of calligraphy in his study that says, 'Maintain a calm spirit when facing major events.' He often said that when looking at people and things, one must look at the reefs under the water, not stare at the ripples on the surface. If I were to be alarmed by such small ripples, I would truly be unworthy of my teacher's trust."

Once these words were spoken, everyone present had different thoughts, and the conversation ended quickly.

After seeing the people from the Umesato Agency off, Ding Mocun and Li Shiqun returned to the office they were just in to continue drinking tea.

Li Shiqun looked at Ding Mocun and said, "Do you think Shen Zhimei's sister is related to the ship sinking?"

Ding Mocun took a puff of his cigar and shook his head in denial upon hearing this. "How is that possible? The Mei Special Service Agency is suspicious of everyone right now; they will doubt anyone." A freighter’s worth of military supplies had vanished, and the Japanese military’s fury could be imagined; even the two of them would likely be under secret investigation.

Li Shiqun’s eyes narrowed slightly. "Do you believe what Shen Zhimei said is true?" He had actually ruled out Shen Jiu’s suspicion directly.

Ding Mocun knew what Li Shiqun wanted to know, so he simply resolved the doubt in his mind. "Whether what Shen Zhimei said is true or not is unimportant; what matters is that Shen Jiu is one of Zhou’s men."

He had kept someone watching Shen Zhimei when he went to Nanjing. The news he received was that an investigation file on Shen Jiu was sitting on Zhou’s desk, and that the two had taken a private walk by the river. The content of their conversation remained unknown to this day. Wasn't this signal obvious enough?

Li Shiqun’s eyes flashed with realization upon hearing this. No wonder. He probed, "Could Shen Zhimei have received some secret mission this time?"

There were two experts by Shen Zhimei’s side, something that had never happened before. He had once sent someone to follow them in secret, only for the man to nearly have his throat slit.

Ding Mocun chuckled at this. "I’d like to know that too. Why don’t you go and investigate?"

With the two old foxes finished probing each other, Li Shiqun returned to his office, wrote a note, and called in a trusted subordinate, ordering him to deliver it to Jing Shenhaoichi.

Jing Shenhaoichi and Tanaka Bunya left No. 76 in their respective cars, heading in different directions. Tanaka Bunya had an important mission and no time to get involved in the shipwreck; his visit today was merely to meet this woman, Shen Zhimei.

In another car, Jing Shenhaoichi listened with a cold face as his subordinate, Matsuda Kazukazu, reported the investigation results.

"Early this morning, Shen Zhimei called Dr. Qian Shengbai from Renji Hospital for a house call, citing her sister’s fainting spell at home. Dr. Qian’s preliminary judgment is that Shen Jiu suffers from an unknown hereditary condition." He had already sent men to investigate near the river and believed there would be results soon.

After listening, Jing Shenhaoichi ordered, "Go to Chairman Mitsui’s house." The black sedan then changed lanes.

After finishing a high-quality imitation bronze artifact, Shen Zhizhen drove away from the small courtyard.

While driving, she pondered what loopholes might remain. The doctor was found by Shen San, and she believed Shen San would handle the explanation. She had also set up the scene; the high-quality imitation bronze she had just finished could be confirmed by an expert as having been made within the last two days, which could serve as an alibi. She had bought electroplating solution and potassium sulfide at a hardware and chemical store in the Concession the day before yesterday, which could serve as supporting evidence.

Shen Zhizhen thought the only loophole was that boat. If the Mei Special Service Agency came to ask where the boat had gone, she could only insist it was lost.

As long as that boat had not taken the same route as the Mitsui Trading Company freighter and had not appeared around the time of the freighter’s incident, it would be relatively easy to muddle through.

In the afternoon, the Mei Special Service Agency’s investigation results on Shen Jiu came out, and after reading them, Jing Shenhaoichi shifted the direction of his investigation.

Although the matter of the boat was a bit suspicious, that boat had indeed not appeared on the route taken by the Mitsui Trading Company freighter, so he saw no need to pursue it relentlessly.

After reading the note Li Shiqun had sent him, a look of realization flashed in his eyes: so, she was one of Zhou Fuhai’s people.

Jing Shenhaoichi obtained the cargo manifest from Chairman Mitsui, and after looking it over, he had even less time to worry about the minor doubts regarding Shen Jiu.

Besides the military supplies, the manifest also included a private collection belonging to Chairman Mitsui. A token originating from the Ancient Feng Kingdom caught his attention, and after asking about the appearance of the token, he immediately went to find Tanaka Bunya.

In the days that followed, the two personally oversaw the salvage operations.

Shen Zhizhen did not know that a crisis had been resolved just like that. She was unusually well-behaved during this period, following a strict three-point routine of patrolling the police station and going home every day.

However, the atmosphere in the Shanghai Bund was becoming increasingly tense. Assassinations and counter-assassinations between various factions, along with street violence, had become the norm.

The Japanese military took the opportunity to launch a "Public Order Strengthening Movement," tightening their control over Shanghai, implementing the Baojia system, squeezing the space for anti-Japanese elements, and intending to purge all anti-Japanese forces lurking in the city.

In the cross-border road area, the Third Patrol Group’s sidecar had just entered their patrol zone when they heard gunfire. Shen Zhizhen ordered them to go and take a look.

The men of the Third Patrol Group had become somewhat numb; several assassinations and shootings occurred in their patrol zone every day.

During this time, the 76th secret agents, the White Party’s Military Statistics Bureau, and the Central Statistics Bureau were killing each other like madmen, while the Red Party seemed to have gone into hibernation.

When the Third Patrol Group’s sidecar arrived at the scene, the assassins had long since fled. The patrolmen skillfully began to clean up the aftermath.

Shen Zhizhen looked around, her gaze lingering on a familiar figure for a moment, before she acted as if nothing was wrong and handled the scene.

After finishing, Shen Zhizhen called Wang Jiangsheng over. "I have something to attend to. You take the men on patrol in a while. Stay safe."

Wang Jiangsheng nodded and agreed, then left with the patrolmen.

Once they were far away, Shen Zhizhen walked up to a rickshaw. "Why are you here?"

Wu De stood up and whispered, "Wan Donglai said he has something to discuss with you."

Shen Zhizhen didn't speak after hearing this; she got straight into the carriage and gave a random address. As for where she was going, she would know when she arrived.

Wu De had been busy with the shop lately and had finally managed to get a break today, only to be cornered by that brat Wan Donglai. With no other choice, he had to come and play errand boy.

Seeing Shen Jiu get into the carriage, Wu De knew what it meant, so he pulled the rickshaw to find Wan Donglai.

By the Suzhou Creek, Shen Zhizhen got off the rickshaw and signaled for Wu De to leave without waiting for her.

Wu De said nothing, turned around, and pulled the rickshaw away. He really didn't like Wan Donglai, always feeling that if he had too much contact with him, he would get dragged into something.

An awning boat was docked by the river. The boatman was wearing a sweat shirt and a headscarf—who else could it be but Wan Donglai?

Shen Zhizhen walked over and smiled. "It’s just a meeting; why this getup?"

Wan Donglai laughed. "The situation is special. Let’s get on the boat first." He wasn't at the foreign firm anymore; now he dressed according to the occasion.

After boarding the boat, Shen Zhizhen entered the cabin and sat down, waiting for Wan Donglai to come in and discuss the matter. She now had plenty of stock, from weapons and medicine to food and gold; she had everything.

chapters.title: A Meal
chapters.content:
The awning boat moved slowly, drifting down the Suzhou Creek. The two on board remained silent, each lost in their own thoughts.

Seeing that even the farmland on both banks had disappeared, Shen Zhizhen realized they were heading further and further into the wilderness. Who was he taking her to see?

Wan Donglai rowed the boat deep into the reed beds and stopped next to a dilapidated fishing boat. "We're here. Follow me."

Shen Zhizhen stepped out of the cabin and looked around. Very good, a very desolate and secluded place. She followed Wan Donglai onto the fishing boat.

Old Gu was stewing fish. Seeing them arrive, he greeted them with a smile. "Miss Shen, try my stewed fish in a moment." As he spoke, he lifted the lid, and the aroma of the fish wafted out.

Wan Donglai’s stomach began to growl at the smell, and he hurriedly went over to help serve the rice.

Seeing it was Comrade Old Gu, whom she had met last time, Shen Zhizhen smiled, said hello, and went over to help with the bowls and chopsticks.

Inside the cabin, the three sat on cushions around the table, eating and chatting.

Old Gu expressed his gratitude; that batch of medicine had been a lifesaver. After sending the medicine out, he had reported the whole incident to the organization and submitted an application to recruit Shen Jiu.

Over the past month, they had conducted a detailed investigation into this Miss Shen from many aspects, and to their surprise, she had given them a huge shock.

It turned out that the "Trio of Anti-Japanese Killers" that had caused a sensation last month and had been issued a wanted order by the Japanese military was led by none other than Shen Jiu. They were able to find this out because the comrade in charge of the investigation had been saved by Shen Jiu; he recognized her immediately upon seeing the photo. Moreover, based on her physical features, her route, and Comrade He Mancang’s confirmation of her and Wu De’s photos, it was confirmed that Shen Jiu was the one who had saved their comrade and had also handed over an important piece of intelligence to Comrade He Mancang.

Upon seeing these investigation results, the higher-ups immediately approved his proposal, stating that someone with such awareness and ideology should be valued, cultivated, and protected so that her identity would not be exposed. Therefore, apart from him and his superiors, even Wan Donglai didn't know about the investigation results. Today’s meeting with Shen Jiu was mainly to talk to her about joining the Red Party.

Shen Zhizhen didn't know she had been thoroughly investigated by the Red Party; she was happily eating the fish, which, it must be said, was expertly stewed by Old Gu.

"Miss Shen, what is your view on the current situation?" Old Gu picked up a piece of fish and asked casually.

Hearing that they were getting to the point, Wan Donglai slowed down his eating. Although he felt there was nothing wrong with Shen Jiu’s ideology, he couldn't help but feel nervous. As Old Gu had said at the beginning, Shen Jiu’s background and environment were too complex; they had to ensure her ideology was sound.

Shen Zhizhen didn't overthink it and said bluntly, "The Japanese invaders are blatant robbers, while certain puppet governments are kneeling slaves."

What else could she think? The country was shattered, and it was truly a man-made disaster. Fortunately, she knew the future trajectory and knew that the light would come in the not-too-distant future.

Old Gu’s spirits lifted, and he continued, "Then what do you think of us?"

Shen Zhizhen was startled, not understanding why he would ask for her opinion on the Red Party. However, she said sincerely, "In my view, you are not just paying lip service to saving the country, but are truly saving it through your actions. It was because I saw this clearly, and after having my suspicions about Wan Donglai’s identity, that I gave the medicine to you."

This was the truth. If she hadn't known Wan Donglai’s Red Party identity, she would never have dared to bring out that batch of medicine.

Sigh, that was stolen goods. Once the Japanese military found out she was the one who bombed the Shenyang East Station warehouse, she reckoned that even if the Shen family went to Hong Kong, they would be implicated and face endless pursuit.

As for whether handing it over to the Red Party would expose the origin of the medicine, she felt it didn't matter. If the Red Party could find out, all the better; it would just prove her determination to resist the invaders.

Old Gu smiled and asked, "Then, Miss Shen, would you be willing to join us and do what you can for this shattered land?"

*Cough, cough, cough.* Shen Zhizhen was choked by Old Gu’s words and hurriedly picked up her cup to take a sip. The surprise had come so suddenly that she couldn't believe it for a moment.

"The Shen family started out grave-robbing, my second uncle is a traitor, and my own sister is a secret agent. Can I really join?" Shen Zhizhen asked uncertainly.

Old Gu smiled and said, "Of course. You are you, and they are them. We have looked into you. You cannot choose your background, but you are willing to extend a helping hand in the country’s time of crisis. This sense of justice is rare, and we are very willing to have you join us." Some things could not be said too clearly, so Old Gu only mentioned the recent incident.

Shen Zhizhen’s face beamed with joy. Haha, the Red Party was inviting her to join—did she even need to think about it? She nodded immediately, agreeing to join, while unable to help but sigh in her heart: it turned out that her concerns were nothing in the face of the greater national cause.

Lao Gu and Wan Donglai were also very happy. With Shen Jiu joining, they believed their work in Shanghai could be carried out much more effectively.

The three continued to eat and chat. Now that they were on the same side, the topics became deeper. Lao Gu spoke about the Red Party’s upcoming work deployment in Shanghai and an analysis of the recent situation in the city.

With the establishment of the puppet government and the exposure of the Central Reserve Bank notes, the White Party had launched a frantic counterattack. Naturally, they did not want to get involved during such a period, so they shifted their focus to intelligence gathering, establishing secret communication lines, and infiltrating enemy intelligence agencies.

After hearing Lao Gu’s words, Shen Zhizhen looked enlightened. No wonder there had been more assassinations between the White Party’s two intelligence agencies and No. 76 recently; so that was what was going on.

Thinking about it, it made sense. The establishment of the puppet government was an act of blatant treason and defection. The White Party was bound to react. Coupled with the exposure of the Japanese printing of Central Reserve Bank notes, once those notes were issued, the first thing they would impact was the legal tender issued by the White Party. With multiple factors overlapping, it was only natural that the "blood concentration" in Shanghai would rise sharply.

As Shen Zhizhen thought about the key task of infiltrating enemy intelligence agencies, she looked up at Lao Gu and asked, "How does the organization view Shen Zhimei?"

Since arriving here, she had only two emotional attachments: one was her "cheap" father, Shen Tingshan, and the other was her "cheap" sister, Shen Zhimei. Now that she had joined the Red Party, she wanted to pull "Shen San" in as well.

Upon hearing this, Lao Gu shared the organization’s assessment of Shen Zhimei. "We unanimously agree that Shen Zhimei is someone who can be won over, so you can try, but it must be under the premise of your own safety and that of the organization."

When they investigated Shen Jiu, they had also investigated her family members, and Shen Zhimei was a key subject of that investigation.

This person was too special. Her mentor was Zhou Fuhai, who held real power in the puppet government, and Zhou Fuhai trusted Shen Zhimei deeply. If they could turn Shen Zhimei, it would be equivalent to planting a mole in the upper echelons of the puppet government. Not only could they obtain more information about the puppet government, but given Shen Zhimei’s special status at No. 76, they could also gain many conveniences.

Shen Zhizhen’s eyes filled with smiles after hearing Lao Gu’s words. As long as there was an opportunity, it was enough. Judging from Shen Zhimei’s words and actions, she seemed to have an attitude of "resigned acceptance" toward the puppet government. Shen Zhizhen felt that as long as she could make "Shen San" see the inevitable trend of the situation, she would be easy to win over; after all, her "cheap" third sister was very intelligent.

chapters.title: Making it Look Like an Accident
chapters.content:
The reeds swayed in the wind, making a rustling sound, and the occasional cry of a waterbird added to the isolated tranquility of the place.

After eating and clearing the plates, Shen Zhizhen followed Lao Gu to take her oath and join the Red Party.

Shen Zhizhen: "I am willing to join the Red Party... to be loyal to the Party... to struggle for the cause of Communism to the end..."

Although the ceremony was simple and there were only two witnesses, Shen Zhizhen was still incredibly excited. This new identity would allow her to do more for this country.

After the oath, Lao Gu said solemnly, "Comrade Shen Zhizhen, from now on, we are comrades who share life and death."

At that moment, Shen Zhizhen felt that the word "comrade" carried a thousand pounds of weight. It was as if, after taking on these two words, she was shouldering many things she had never carried before.

Wan Donglai smiled and held out his hands to congratulate her. "Congratulations. From now on, we are revolutionary comrades."

Shen Zhizhen smiled, shook his hand, and thanked him sincerely. "Thank you." If not for Wan Donglai, she might still be walking in the direction she had previously envisioned, never daring to think she could join the Red Party.

Wan Donglai understood what she meant instantly and shook his head with a smile. "You're welcome. By the way, we need to give you a codename. Is there one you’d like to use?"

Shen Zhizhen: "A codename?"

Lao Gu: "Yes, we want to hide your identity. From now on, Comrade Donglai and I will be responsible for contacting you, so you need a codename within the organization."

Shen Zhizhen understood; they wanted her to keep her current identity and use its convenience to secretly cooperate with missions.
