A codename could both conceal her real name and reduce the risk of exposure. After thinking for a moment, she said, "How about the codename 'Chaofeng' (Pawnshop Manager)?"

Actually, she had wanted to use the four characters "Tiandu Chaofeng," but she realized that was a bit long and too obvious—at the very least, Shen family relatives would immediately know what it meant—so she removed "Tiandu" and kept "Chaofeng."

The identity of a pawnshop manager was very meaningful to this body of hers, and it also had a certain level of deceptiveness.

Lao Gu thought about it and nodded, agreeing to use "Chaofeng" as Shen Jiu’s codename. At the same time, he gave Shen Jiu her first mission after joining the organization.

"Comrade Shen Jiu, the situation on the front lines is intense, and we need a large amount of supplies. Your mission is to find a way to obtain various supplies."

Shen Zhizhen accepted the mission immediately. "Alright, I have a batch of goods on hand. Once I go back and rent a warehouse by the river, I’ll notify you when it’s ready."

She guessed that the Red Party would likely transport things by water, so if she had Wu De rent a secluded warehouse by the river, it would be convenient for their organization to pick them up.

Lao Gu and Wan Donglai were overjoyed. They asked what kind of supplies they were, and upon hearing there were medicines, grain, weapons, and ammunition, the two were both shocked and delighted. Was Shen Jiu too good at "scavenging" things?

Wan Donglai almost asked if Shen Jiu had stolen the Japanese military’s armory, but he swallowed the words back. Some things were better left unclear; asking too many questions easily caused wrinkles.

Lao Gu didn't care where Shen Jiu got them. To him, it didn't matter if it was a black cat or a white cat; a cat that caught mice was a good cat. Since Shen Jiu had the ability to "shear the wool" off the Japanese army, he hoped she would shear even more.

In the office of the Secretary-General of No. 76, Shen Zhimei leaned lazily against the back of her chair, her long eyelashes lowered as she looked at the documents in her hand with indifference.

Ring, ring, ring... The phone rang. After answering the call, Shen Zhimei stood up, picked up her beige trench coat, draped it over her arm, and walked out with a calm gait.

She ran into Li Shiqun, who was heading upstairs, at the stairwell. After exchanging a few perfunctory words, she left.

Li Shiqun frowned as he watched her figure depart. Leaving at this time—what was she going to do? He waved for his confidant to follow her, but after returning to his office, he felt a bit of regret. Last time, they hadn't been able to keep up and he had nearly had his throat slit; sending someone now was tantamount to a provocation.

Thinking this, he picked up the phone and called Wang Fusheng, the younger brother of Wang Guisheng, telling him to hurry and take men to follow his brother.

When Wang Fusheng heard his brother was in danger, he immediately took the order and went out, taking all the men from the Second Intelligence Group with him.

After Li Shiqun’s men left, he felt inexplicably flustered. He drank some tea to calm his nerves, thinking that Shen Zhimei shouldn't dare to kill someone from No. 76, otherwise she wouldn't have let them go last time.

Sigh, he actually didn't have any malice; he was just curious about what mission Shen Zhimei had taken in Nanjing. Not only was it mysterious, but there were also some unfamiliar faces around her.

Black sedans drove out of No. 76 one after another. Zhang Yong glanced at the rearview mirror and said, "There’s a car following us. The one driving is Wang Guisheng, who is close to Li Shiqun."

Wang Wu, sitting in the passenger seat, looked back. "Tsk tsk, following so closely, as if he’s afraid we don’t know someone is tailing us. This kid is a bit arrogant."

A cold look flashed in Shen Zhimei’s eyes. She parted her lips slightly and said, "Make it look like an accident."

Li Shiqun was an ambitious man whose desire to replace Ding Mocun was obvious. She hadn't intended to clash with him, which was why she hadn't held it against him when he sent people to track and monitor her last time. But alas, this man didn't know his place.

Zhang Yong and Wang Wu looked at each other and immediately divided the work with a tacit understanding.

Zhang Yong drove the car toward Linjiang Avenue. Once on the avenue, he smiled at the churning river. As the car was about to reach an intersection, he slammed the steering wheel, and the car immediately changed lanes.

Zhang Zhao rolled down the window, stuck his head out, and put a bamboo tube to his lips. The moment the car behind was about to pass, he blew hard, and a black poison needle shot out, precisely piercing Wang Guisheng’s temple. He curled his lips, sat back, and rolled up the window as if nothing had happened.

Wang Guisheng was driving and following them. He knew the person driving for Shen Zhimei had some skills; if he didn't follow closely, he would be shaken off within two blocks.

Therefore, relying on his status as Li Shiqun’s confidant and betting that Shen Zhimei wouldn't dare do anything to him, he simply followed openly.

Wang Guisheng was chewing betel nut and looking smug when the car in front suddenly changed lanes. He didn't react in time, and before he could even hit the brakes, he suddenly felt a pain in his temple, followed by darkness and a loss of consciousness.

The out-of-control black sedan crashed into the railing by the river. After the car destroyed the railing and hovered briefly in the air, it plunged headfirst into the Huangpu River, instantly swallowed by the surging water without a trace.

Wang Fusheng had finally caught up to his brother’s car, but before he could catch up, he watched helplessly as his brother drove into the river. His face changed drastically. "Quick, accelerate!"

Two consecutive sounds of emergency braking rang out. Wang Fusheng opened the car door and saw that the car his brother had been driving was already submerged. He shouted, "Anyone who can swim well, get down there and save him!"

With that, he jumped in with a splash, followed by all the men from the Second Intelligence Group who knew how to swim.

Those who couldn't swim stood by the destroyed railing, whispering and discussing what had just happened.

"What do you think happened just now?" The speaker was a driver. He had seen with his own eyes the two cars in front—one changing lanes and the other crashing into the railing and falling into the river.

The person next to him shook his head. It was just eerie. He had been sitting in the passenger seat and had seen it clearly too.

The car driven by the team leader’s brother looked like it had been cursed, just charging straight into the river like that.

"Do you think it has anything to do with Secretary-General Shen?"

"It shouldn't, right? That car had already turned..."

chapters.title: Section Chief
chapters.content:
At No. 76, Li Shiqun hung up the phone with a gloomy face and stood up to walk toward Ding Mocun’s office.

"Shen Zhimei just killed my man like that. Doesn't she hold me in any regard?" Li Shiqun paced back and forth, furious.

Hmph, don't tell him it was an accident. How could a car following her just end up in the river for no reason? If this had nothing to do with Shen Zhimei, he would unscrew his own head and let her use it as a ball.

Ding Mocun was also speechless after hearing what happened. He knew Shen Zhimei had a special status, yet he still insisted on being a fool and sending people to their deaths.

"Then do you hold Minister Zhou in any regard?"

Li Shiqun...

After shaking off the tail, the black sedan drove toward the International Settlement and finally pulled into a quiet, tree-lined road, entering a villa.

Shen Zhimei got out of the car and looked up. A faint light flashed in her eyes. Before the establishment of the Nanjing government, this was the Special Operations Section established under the direction of her mentor—a department that belonged exclusively to him.

It was responsible for monitoring key military, political, and business figures at all levels in Shanghai. It didn't have the notoriety of No. 76, but it was an invisible eye hanging over everyone’s heads; a single report could determine life or death.

Shen Zhimei walked inside unhurriedly. The people her mentor had given her when she returned from Nanjing were from the execution team here. Three days ago, she had been appointed as the Section Chief of the Special Operations Section.

The interior of the villa was not set up in a conventional manner, but rather as a small-scale command center. A complete map of Shanghai hung on the wall, marked with magnetic pins and fine threads indicating the addresses, symbols, and routes of various high-ranking officials. Two long tables were covered with various encrypted communication devices and monitoring headsets.

The people working inside stood up in unison to salute and greet the Director as she entered.

Shen Zhimei waved her hand, signaling everyone to continue their work, and headed toward the office upstairs. Someone was already waiting for her inside.

Black Moon sat on the sofa with a cold expression, fiddling with a dagger. Hearing the door open, she turned her head indifferently. Seeing it was the newly appointed Director, she gave a slight nod. "Director."

Shen Zhimei hung up her trench coat, walked over with a smile, and sat down. "How did the investigation go?"

Black Moon was the leader of the execution team, codenamed Black Widow. She was a professionally trained assassin with a one-hundred-percent mission success rate to date.

After taking over the personnel given to her by her mentor, Shen Zhimei had sent Black Moon and her team to Western Hunan to investigate the truth behind Tanaka Bun'ya being expelled from his family.

After Tanaka Bun'ya was expelled, he went to Japan and gained the trust of the Japanese Emperor. What did he rely on to achieve this?

She deduced that the treasure map, the information regarding the Ancient Phoenix Kingdom’s Nine Territories, and other related intelligence had been brought over by Tanaka Bun'ya. Judging by the timeline, his expulsion must have been related to the treasure map.

Black Moon put away her dagger and began to recount the findings of her trip in a straightforward manner. "Tanaka Bun'ya’s real name is Bai Wenye. He is the third son of the patriarch of the Bai tomb-raiding clan in Western Hunan. Five years ago, he was expelled for stealing family heirlooms."

Shen Zhimei’s eyelids flickered slightly at this, but she remained silent and continued to listen. What kind of family heirloom could cause a patriarch’s son to be expelled? Linking this to the "Takamagahara Plan" that Tanaka Bun'ya was executing, the answer was becoming clear in her mind. She might have actually guessed correctly.

Black Moon continued: "I learned from an elder of the Bai family that what Bai Wenye stole was a treasure map and two Phoenix Tokens..."

A hint of a smile flashed in Shen Zhimei’s eyes. She did not curiously ask Black Moon how she had managed to extract such a secret.

"You’ve worked hard. Go back and get some rest."

Upon hearing this, Black Moon stood up and left decisively, without saying a single extra word.

Only after Black Moon had left did Shen Zhimei knit her brows to ponder the information she had just received. Tanaka Bun'ya possessed not only a treasure map but also two Phoenix Tokens. Would he hand these two items over to the Japanese Emperor, or would he use the information he possessed as bait to secure power for himself?

Thinking from his perspective, she felt the former was unlikely. Who would be willing to reveal their trump card if they could achieve their goals empty-handed? If it were her, she would absolutely never reveal that she held these two items.

If it were the latter, where would he have hidden the two items he stole?

*Knock, knock, knock.* The sound of knocking interrupted Shen Zhimei’s thoughts. She looked up and said softly, "Come in."

The secretary walked in. "Report, the latest telegram from Nanjing." With that, she handed a piece of paper to the Director.

Shen Zhimei took it and waved for the secretary to leave. She frowned slightly after reading the contents. Her mentor wanted her to take Shen Jiu back to Nanjing?

***

The flat-bottomed boat docked at the shore. Wan Donglai said, "Go ashore and walk east for about fifteen minutes, and you’ll reach the house Wu De rented."

Shen Zhizhen emerged from the cabin. After going ashore, she waved goodbye to Wan Donglai and watched the boat leave before taking a bicycle out of her spatial storage and riding east.

A few minutes later, Shen Zhizhen opened the gate and pushed the bicycle into the courtyard. Seeing Wu De’s rickshaw in the yard, she knew the kid was waiting for her.

Hearing the movement, Wu De came out. Seeing it was Shen Jiu, he laughed, "Why are you only just back? I’ve been waiting for you for ages." He looked at the bicycle with curiosity, secretly wondering where she had gotten it, as she had left on a flat-bottomed boat.

Shen Zhizhen didn’t answer but instead asked, "Where is Xi Ya?"

"Selling boxed lunches at the pier," Wu De replied while ushering Shen Jiu into the house.

"It’s not sold out at this hour? Business must be bad." Shen Zhizhen looked up at the sky; it was already afternoon.

"No, it’s because business is too good. She sells out, comes back to cook another pot, and then goes back to sell it." The laborers at the pier worked irregular hours, and since they did heavy physical labor, they got hungry quickly. Xi Ya’s boxed lunches had plenty of food and were cheap, so everyone loved eating there.

Hearing this, a look of realization flashed in Shen Zhizhen’s eyes. Well, Xi Ya’s mass-cooked meals were indeed quite delicious.

The two entered the house. Wu De poured Shen Jiu a cup of tea and sat down to talk about the shop. "I’ve already put the goods in. Most are wholesale imitations, but there are a few pieces that I really did pick up at the second-hand market."

Wu De added, "I recently made contact with a gang leader. He has 'fresh pit' and 'ripe pit' goods on hand. Should we buy some?"

"Fresh pit" goods were those that had just been unearthed and had not undergone any human cleaning, handling, or artificial aging. "Ripe pit" goods were those that had been handled and "nurtured" by human touch.

Shen Zhizhen was stunned for a moment upon hearing this, then realized what he meant. She thought for a moment and said, "If you see anything good, buy it. You don't need to put them in the shop to sell; I’ll keep them to give away later."

Many items coming out of tombs were precious cultural relics with high archaeological value. Buying them and keeping them to donate later was better than letting them fall into the hands of who-knows-who.

Wu De nodded in agreement. He knew Shen Jiu wasn't short on money, and opening this shop wasn't for profit. In these chaotic times, he wouldn't dare display real items in the shop anyway, so he decided to acquire a certain amount and send them to Shen Jiu.

After finishing their discussion about the shop, Shen Zhizhen mentioned wanting to rent warehouses, telling Wu De to rent several in remote locations.

Wu De’s eyelids twitched upon hearing this. His little cousin was clearly planning something big. Thinking of Wan Donglai’s identity, he began to understand why.

"You’d better be careful. If you get caught one day, I’ll have to rack my brain trying to figure out how to save you."

Shen Zhizhen was amused by this and comforted him, "Don't worry, even if I get caught, there’s still Shen San. It won't be your turn."

Wu De... Chapter 59: Why does she trust her so much?

Wu De thought about it and realized she was right. If it really came to that, he wouldn't be the main person to save her anyway, so he simply steered the conversation back to renting the warehouses.

"Your requirements aren't easy to find; it’s going to take some effort. Who would build warehouses in remote places? Even if there are any, they’d be abandoned factory types."

First of all, this matter had to be kept secret; he couldn't expose himself by asking others for help. He would have to search along the riverbanks himself, and it was hard to say when he would find them.

Shen Zhizhen picked up her teacup and took a sip. This was indeed a problem. "Try your best. If you find them, buy them if possible, and be careful not to expose yourself."

Wu De nodded to show he understood. He would disguise himself when he went out to look, and even if he bought the warehouses, he would use the fake documents Shen Jiu had given him to handle the paperwork.

The warehouse matter couldn't be resolved in a short time, but the supplies promised to Old Gu still needed to be arranged. After thinking for a while, she decided to use a "hiding in plain sight" tactic.

She hadn't been to the small courtyard she rented by the river since the people from the Mei Organization had searched it. She would put some of the supplies there and then have Old Gu bring people to row a boat in from the backyard in the middle of the night to move the goods. Besides, the Red Party seemed to have plenty of flat-bottomed boats.

After deciding this, she said to Wu De, "If Wan Donglai comes to find you, tell him the address of the small courtyard by the river that I rented."

Hearing that he only needed to provide the address and didn't need to lead the way, Wu De immediately nodded in agreement.

After finishing their business, Shen Zhizhen didn't stay long. After leaving Wu De’s house, she rode her bicycle back to the police station to retrieve her car.

At the Western Shanghai Branch, Shen Zhizhen checked her office and, seeing it was empty, went to the morgue to chat with the forensic examiner, mainly to find out what murder cases had occurred.

When the autopsy report for the Tang Mansion came out, she had already seen it through the favor she had built with the examiner. To summarize, the torture methods showed a high degree of uniformity, leading to a preliminary conclusion that they were the work of the same killer.

Because of that Phoenix Token, she and Shen San had deduced that the killer was related to Tanaka Bun'ya, so she visited the examiner from time to time to see if any other victims similar to those at the Tang Mansion had appeared.

The Western Shanghai Branch examiner was also someone who loved to chat. "There was a bizarre accident at the Eastern Shanghai Branch this afternoon." She had gone there to visit her senior colleague today and happened to witness the event, learning the details from him.

Shen Zhizhen’s curiosity was piqued. "How bizarre?"

"Someone drove a car, crashed through the railing, and fell into the river. The deceased’s vital signs were normal—it wasn't a sudden illness—and the vehicle had no mechanical faults. According to witnesses, the car acted as if it were possessed; it just charged straight into the river."

Shen Zhizhen: "Could it be suicide?" If there was nothing wrong with the body or the car, then it was just seeking death.

The examiner leaned in and whispered, "Impossible. The deceased was Wang Guisheng, a trusted aide to Director Li of No. 76. At the time, he was driving and following the Secretary-General of No. 76, Shen Zhimei. Do you think someone on a mission would suddenly decide to commit suicide? Moreover, Wang Guisheng’s cause of death was atypical drowning."

Shen Zhizhen’s eyelids twitched. She hadn't expected this to involve Shen San; then it really couldn't be suicide.

After asking what "atypical drowning" meant, Shen Zhizhen took a small gift out of her pocket, handed it to the examiner, and said goodbye.

As the black sedan drove out of the Western Shanghai Branch, Shen Zhizhen pondered what the examiner had said, a series of questions forming in her mind.

Why were people from No. 76 following Shen San? Why did Shen San kill someone from No. 76? Infighting?

The "atypical drowning" the examiner mentioned meant the deceased had drowned while in a comatose state. In other words, Wang Guisheng had lost consciousness, the car went out of control, crashed through the railing, and fell into the river; he hadn't reacted at all until he drowned.

The bizarre point was that they couldn't find the cause of the victim’s coma. At the time, the victim was following the car in front; the lead car changed lanes and turned, but Wang Guisheng’s car didn't follow the turn and subsequently crashed into the river.

Logically, there was a distance between the two cars; the lead car couldn't have suddenly knocked someone unconscious while in motion. Honestly, if this didn't involve Shen San, she would definitely be looking for other causes.

She was genuinely curious about how Shen San had managed it. Carrying this curiosity, she went home, changed into her slippers, sat on the sofa, and asked the question on her mind.

Shen Zhimei was looking at a document. Hearing this, she rolled her eyes at Shen Jiu. "How do you know about this?" The crime scene wasn't even in the Western Shanghai Branch; how did Little Jiu know?

"Our station’s forensic examiner told me as gossip. Tell me, how did you manage to kill someone without leaving a trace?" The person killed was a notorious secret agent, so she felt no sympathy at all.

Shen Zhimei put down the document, fiddled with her slender fingers, and chuckled, "How would I know? I didn't kill him." She hadn't lifted a finger.

A flash of inspiration struck Shen Zhizhen. Thinking of the people around Shen San, she immediately understood that someone else had done the deed. After figuring it out, she didn't buy Shen San’s explanation. Without her order, those two wouldn't have acted. This woman really knew how to distance herself even when killing someone.

"How could you kill someone from No. 76? Did you fall out?" This was the point she was curious about.

It’s all the same unit, after all. To kill someone so blatantly without leaving a trace, yet still letting the people behind it know that she was the one who did it—that’s a bit arrogant, Shen San.

Shen Zhimei: "It was just a warning." A warning to Li Shiqun not to overreach. "Come with me to Nanjing tomorrow."

Shen Zhizhen was stunned upon hearing this. Everything was fine, so why go to Nanjing?

Shen Zhimei rubbed her brow gently and shared the news she had received today: "The teacher wants me to take you to Nanjing. I don't know the specific reason."

This came out of the blue. She had spent the whole afternoon thinking about it without finding a clue. Xiao Jiu’s specialty was grave robbing; surely the teacher wasn't looking for Xiao Jiu to rob a grave!

Shen Zhizhen thought about her current identity and felt it necessary to express her stance to Shen San: "Let’s get this straight: I can go, but I won’t be a traitor."

Shen Zhimei...

She tossed a cushion at her. The brat acted as if anyone actually wanted to be a traitor.

Shen Zhizhen caught the cushion and held it to her chest, looking at Shen San: "I’m just reminding you not to get in too deep. What if you can’t pull yourself out later?"

Shen Zhimei pursed her lips slightly, leaning back helplessly against the sofa. She decided to be open with Xiao Jiu so she would understand her situation: "Three days ago, I was appointed Director of the Shanghai Special Operations Division. Do you understand, Xiao Jiu? I can’t pull myself out now."

When a person is placed in a position by power, their fate is no longer in their own hands.

"Father and Second Uncle have already arrived in Hong Kong. If there is any danger on this Nanjing trip, don't worry about me—just go straight to Hong Kong and take them to the United States."

Shen Zhizhen ignored the talk of an exit strategy and asked what the Shanghai Special Operations Division was. Upon learning it was an intelligence organization responsible for monitoring all social strata in Shanghai, her first thought was: Why does Shen San’s teacher trust her so much?

Her second thought was that Shen San had to be turned to their side as soon as possible, otherwise, there was no telling what might happen... Chapter 60: The List

The two finally reached an agreement: once they arrived in Nanjing, they would play it by ear, focusing on just getting by.

Shen Zhizhen reached out and picked up the document on the table. She looked up at Shen San, and seeing no objection, she immediately opened it.

Shen San’s department now controlled intelligence on all levels of Shanghai society; she was curious about what was written in the document.

Shen Zhimei narrowed her eyes, waiting for Xiao Jiu’s reaction. She had specifically brought this document back.

After reading it, Shen Zhizhen’s heart skipped a beat. This document was actually a list of Red Party infiltrators, and Wan Donglai’s name was prominently listed.

Shen Zhizhen closed the document, looked up at Shen San, and said seriously: "He is the only one left in the Wan family."

Although she didn't know the others on the list, if this list were real, the Red Party would suffer heavy losses once Shen San reported it.

"Then if you run into him, tell him to be careful. I’ll suppress this list for now and wait until we get back from Nanjing to submit it." It was precisely because she saw Wan Donglai’s name on it that she had brought it back for Xiao Jiu to see.

A smile flashed in Shen Zhizhen’s eyes, and she nodded to show she understood. She would go out to find him in a little while.

For the first time, she had a clear understanding of the party’s intelligence department—it was truly pervasive, though fortunately, it was limited to the Shanghai area.

"Wait, didn't you say your new department monitors the police, government, special agents, and business sectors? Why are you investigating the Red Party too?"

Shen Zhimei chuckled: "These are all intelligence gathered from surveillance, compiled into a list after investigation." The Special Operations Division screened all information collected, submitted the suspicious parts for another team to investigate, and finally submitted the results.

She had not only the Red Party infiltration list but also lists for other parties, and even the Japanese.

The nature of the Special Operations Division was unique; it was essentially a department serving Zhou Fuhai. Once all information was integrated and submitted, how to use it was the teacher’s business. For example, if a violent deterrent was needed at a certain point, the teacher would pick a sacrificial lamb from the submitted list. She briefly explained the ins and outs to Xiao Jiu.

After hearing this, Shen Zhizhen felt that if this department were exposed, those big shots would tear it apart together.

Shen Zhimei chuckled, "Do you think those big shots don't know?" She stood up to pour a glass of water.

A look of realization flashed in Shen Zhizhen’s eyes. This invisible eye kept all those under surveillance living in unknown fear, but being in the same boat was another matter. Like Zhou Fuhai, they played everyone in the palm of their hands as hunters.

Shen Zhimei returned with her water and shared what Heiyue had found, telling Shen Jiu to take the opportunity to investigate.

Shen Zhizhen’s eyes lit up: "I’ll go tonight." She stood up and walked out.

"I might not be back tonight, so don't wait for me. I’ll go straight to the train station tomorrow morning."

Shen Zhimei watched Xiao Jiu leave in a rush, looking thoughtful. It seemed this girl was determined to collect the treasure map and the Phoenix Token herself.

Thinking about how she would eventually give the teacher a pile of fakes made by Xiao Jiu to complete her tasks, she couldn't help but chuckle. *Sigh, the teacher is truly too clever for his own good. He wants to use power to tie her to this ship to work for him, but he doesn't stop to think that this ship could sink at any moment. Is it worth it for her to bet everything on it?*

She reached out to pick up the document and opened it, only to be so angered by the missing pages that she laughed...

Shen Zhizhen hurried downstairs, looked up before getting into the car, gave a cheeky grin, and drove away.

She had torn that list out while Shen San was pouring water. As for whether it would expose anything, Shen San wouldn't turn her in anyway. It was a perfect way to remind Shen San what her sister’s true colors were, giving her some mental preparation.

Shen Zhizhen drove toward Zhabei, organizing the information she had just obtained. She really hadn't expected that Tanaka Bunya not only had two Phoenix Tokens but also a fragment of the map.

Once she finished her business tonight, she would have to go to Tanaka Bunya’s residence to scout it out.

In a civilian house in Zhabei, Wan Donglai was about to sleep when he heard a knock at the door. He jumped up, pulled out a gun from the inner room, walked to the door, and asked quietly: "Who is it?"

Hearing it was Wan Donglai’s voice, Shen Zhizhen breathed a sigh of relief. *Good, I didn't find the wrong place.* She replied, "Shen Jiu."

When Wan Donglai heard it was Shen Jiu, he tucked his gun behind his back and opened the door. Once she was inside and the door was closed, he asked, "Why are you here at this hour?"

Shen Zhizhen took the list out of her pocket: "See if the people on this list are our people. If they are, evacuate immediately."

Wan Donglai lit a kerosene lamp, and after seeing the list, shock flashed in his eyes. Although he didn't recognize everyone, there were a few he had been in contact with. "Where did you get this list?"

Seeing Wan Donglai’s reaction, Shen Zhizhen understood it was mostly true: "Shen San saw you were on it and brought it back for me to see, saying it was a list of Red Party infiltrators in Shanghai."

She felt it necessary to warn him: "If this list is real, is there a problem with our work? How did they manage to investigate us so thoroughly?"

Wan Donglai felt a warmth in his heart; the bond from growing up together still mattered. "I will tell Old Gu about this situation. Whether everyone on this list is ours still needs further confirmation."

"Time is tight; I must notify Old Gu immediately. If this list reaches the 76th Branch, arrests will happen in the next two days."

"This list hasn't reached the 76th Branch. Shen San said she would wait until we return from Nanjing to submit it." Shen Zhizhen told him about their trip to Nanjing tomorrow.

Wan Donglai was completely confused. *What does this mean? Shen Zhimei didn't get this list from the 76th Branch?*

Shen Zhizhen didn't care if Wan Donglai understood or not, and continued: "The return date for this trip is uncertain. That batch of goods hasn't been moved yet. I put two boxes of gold under the bed in the rented house; you can go get them when you have time." She gave him the address.

She had originally wanted to leave supplies, as those things took up too much space in her storage, but then she realized it was a bit dangerous. That house was already on the Japanese radar. No matter what supplies she left, if they were investigated, it would either be linked to the bombing of the Shenyang East Station or the sinking of the Mitsui Trading Company ship. After thinking it through, she decided not to take the risk and simply left two boxes of gold for them to buy what they needed.

Wan Donglai was almost stunned by Shen Jiu’s words. His previous doubts were instantly forgotten, and he still felt a bit dizzy after Shen Jiu left.

Wan Donglai shook his head, locked the door, and walked toward the alley. He stopped in front of a civilian house, checked that no one was around, knocked on the door, and slipped inside when it opened.

Inside, Old Gu lit the oil lamp: "Why are you here at this time?"

"Look at this, the 'Pawnshop' sent it just now." Wan Donglai handed over the list and repeated what Shen Jiu had said.

Old Gu took it with a puzzled look, but his face changed drastically after reading it... Chapter 61: A Farce

Early in the morning at the train station, a black car pulled up. Heiyue stepped out, observed the surroundings, and only opened the back door once she was sure it was safe.

Shen Zhimei got out and stood there, her gaze lingering briefly on a person yawning while leaning against a pillar in the distance before she put on her sunglasses and walked into the station. As she passed Shen Jiu, she mocked: "What, did you go off to be a thief?" The brat was always giving her problems.

Shen Zhizhen... "Who went to be a thief? Wasn't I doing errands for you?" she muttered guiltily.

Her gaze fell on the woman in black, who exuded an aura of indifference. She was a stranger, but from Shen San’s description yesterday, she could guess who she was. The news about the Bai family of Xiangxi must have been brought back by her.

She caught a hint of danger from this person. The two stared at each other for a moment before looking away.

Shen Zhimei casually introduced them: "My sister, Shen Jiu. Heiyue." After the brief introduction, she ignored them, got on the train, and lay down on the soft sleeper to rest.

She hadn't slept well last night, mainly because she was too angry at Shen Jiu to sleep. Xiao Jiu’s behavior was practically a blatant confession.

Things were already complicated enough, and the brat had gone off to be a Red Party member. She had spent a long time thinking about an exit strategy. Just as she was about to fall asleep, she was woken up by a phone call. After hearing the content, she was so angry she laughed—she hadn't gone looking for trouble, but trouble had come looking for her. She simply issued several orders to play with Li Shiqun.

Shen Zhizhen was also exhausted, so she took off her shoes and climbed onto the upper bunk to sleep. She fell asleep almost as soon as she closed her eyes.

Heiyue looked at the two carefree Shen sisters, her usually indifferent face nearly cracking. She leaned against the door and rubbed her brow. Last night, someone had put out a 20,000 silver dollar bounty on the streets to assassinate Shen Zhimei.

As for who it was, it was easy to guess—it was nothing more than Li Shiqun being unable to swallow his pride.

Thinking of this, she glanced at the woman who looked harmless in her sleep. This one was also ruthless; not only did she strike back with the same tactics, but she simultaneously ordered the burning of two of Li Shiqun’s private warehouses and the sinking of an opium smuggling ship. Thus, a shadow war began between the two high-ranking factions in Nanjing.

The train rattled along steadily, and the soft-sleeper compartment remained silent.

In Shanghai, a row of black sedans was parked in front of the Li residence. Li Shiqun, who hadn't closed his eyes all night, emerged from his home escorted by a group of subordinates and boarded one of the cars.

As the car pulled away, Li sat in the backseat, his face dark as he listened to his subordinate’s report.

"We’ve inquired with the gangs. Someone put out word on the streets early this morning, offering a bounty of 100,000 silver dollars for your life." The subordinate in the passenger seat spoke in an increasingly hushed tone.

Last night, two warehouses had been burned to the ground and a smuggling ship had sunk. The lights at the Li residence hadn't gone out all night, and Director Li had been in a rage until dawn—the extent of the losses was evident.

After hearing this, Li Shiqun realized that the warehouse fires and the sunken ship were likely also the handiwork of Shen Zhimei; otherwise, it would be too much of a coincidence.

He was now filled with both rage and shock. He had just offered 20,000 silver dollars on the streets to buy Shen Zhimei’s life, and in return, she had offered a higher price for his, while also hitting him with a combination of blows.

A woman he had never taken seriously, a woman he had viewed as nothing more than a vase, was now displaying methods and intelligence that made him feel fear from the bottom of his heart.

Yesterday, Ding Mocun had advised him that Shen Zhimei was not simple and warned him not to look for trouble. Li had scoffed at the advice and mocked Ding, asking if everyone was like him—standing behind bulletproof glass even for public speeches and changing bedrooms every night upon hearing that the Military Statistics Bureau was active.

A flash of regret crossed Li Shiqun’s eyes. If only he had listened to that old fox. With such a heavy reward, there would surely be brave men willing to risk their heads to kill him.

Just as Li Shiqun was pondering how to make peace with Shen Zhimei, a gunshot rang out. A bullet shattered the car window and grazed his cheek...

At No. 76, in the Director’s office, Ding Mocun looked at Li Shiqun, whose face was wrapped in gauze, and delivered a sarcastic remark: "Didn't listen to a cautious coward like me, did you? Now you've suffered for it." With that, he pulled out a cigar and lit it, in a very good mood.

Upon arriving at the office this morning, he had heard about the foolish stunt Li had pulled—trying to be clever by not using his bulletproof car, only to sit in an ordinary one and nearly get his head blown off. It was truly a case of being too clever for one's own good.

Li Shiqun swallowed his anger and placed a box on the table. "Stop mocking me for a moment. Please, give me some guidance so I can save my life first."

After arriving at No. 76, he had intended to talk to Shen Zhimei, but she hadn't come to work. Not only that, she had taken an extended leave. This was going to be the death of him.

He had encountered two waves of snipers on the way here, and this was just for the commute. The thought of how many assassination attempts might be waiting for him on the way home made his scalp tingle.

The shooters were all long-range snipers; by the time his men reached the scene, they were long gone.

Ding Mocun glanced up, opened the box, and saw a night-luminescent pearl. "This is?"

Li Shiqun: "A night-luminescent pearl from Empress Dowager Cixi’s phoenix crown." Although it wasn't the largest one that had been held in her mouth, it was still a priceless treasure.

Upon hearing this, Ding knew it was one of the five pearls stolen from Cixi’s tomb in the Eastern Qing Tombs by Sun Dianying. He hadn't expected Li Shiqun to have one. To bring out such a treasure, the favor he wanted to ask was naturally not trivial.

Ding Mocun closed the lid and pushed the box back. "Too valuable. I cannot accept this." If someone else had given it to him, he might have taken it, but it wasn't easy to accept something from Li Shiqun. However, considering there was still important work to be done, he pointed out a clear path for Li.

Li Shiqun’s eyes lit up at these words. He thanked Ding Mocun and returned to his office, where he braced himself to call his superior for help. He took the initiative to admit his mistake, and after receiving a sound scolding, he felt much more at ease.

An hour later, both of their farcical bounty orders were withdrawn.

At the Nanjing train station, the three of them walked out of the exit and got into a black sedan. The driver was an old acquaintance.

Secretary Chen drove while mentioning Li Shiqun’s phone call. "Why are you two acting like children?" If you want to fight, fight, but running to tell the "parents"—doesn't Li Shiqun feel embarrassed?

Shen Zhimei nonchalantly explained that Director Li had been too curious and had sent people to follow her. "I gave him a warning, and he got angry, so I just played along with him." She needed to let their teacher know what his good subordinate had been up to.

Shen Zhizhen sat in the backseat, listening to the two of them trading barbs and schemes, and felt exhausted just hearing them. She decided to focus on her own affairs.

Yesterday, after leaving Wan Donglai’s place, she had driven to the small riverside courtyard she rented. She didn't arrive until after midnight and hurriedly stuffed two boxes of gold under the bed. She didn't know if Old Gu and Wan Donglai had retrieved them yet.

Later, she went to where Tanaka Fumiya was staying, but he wasn't home either. She had searched the place inside and out, but found nothing.

Hei Yue sat in the passenger seat, silent the entire time. If one didn't look over at her, one wouldn't even feel that there was anyone there.

The vehicle drove into a tree-lined avenue, entered an area of high walls and large courtyards, and finally pulled into a heavily guarded mansion.

chapters.title: Copying!
chapters.content:
The mansion the black sedan drove into was the Zhou residence on Yihe Road. The car followed the tree-lined path and finally stopped in front of the main entrance of a three-story villa.

Shen Zhimei looked at the familiar surroundings outside the window and said to Xiao Jiu, "This is the teacher's residence."

Upon hearing this, a look of realization flashed in Shen Zhizhen’s eyes. No wonder the security was so tight, with a checkpoint every few meters. They had encountered two patrols in the short time since the car entered. Moreover, there were not only visible guards but also many hidden ones. *Heh*, look at that; these people actually know what they've been doing, they're terrified of dying.

After they got out of the car, a man and a woman approached. Only after being searched were they signaled to enter.

Shen Zhimei nodded slightly and led the others inside. Shen Zhizhen followed behind Shen San, her mind wandering as she pondered whether she could escape with Shen San if a conflict broke out in such a heavily guarded environment. She evaluated it in her heart: the answer was that it would be difficult for two people, but if she utilized her space, the chances of success would be very high. As long as she knocked Shen San unconscious and threw her into the palace space, she could still manage to escape on her own.

After stepping onto the steps, Hei Yue did not follow them in but stood near the entrance to wait. Secretary Chen pushed the door open and followed the Shen sisters inside.

The marble floor was polished to a mirror finish, and blue-and-white porcelain vases from the Kangxi and Qianlong eras were placed on both sides. Stepping inside, the feeling was one of luxury in every detail.

Zhou Fuhai was sitting on the sofa drinking tea. Seeing them arrive, he looked up and greeted them: "Come over quickly and taste the new Mingqian Longjing."

Shen Zhimei walked over with a smile, sat down, and laughed, "Then I must taste how it is."

She picked up the teacup in front of her naturally. The moment she lifted the lid, a warm fragrance wafted out. She took a small sip, and the tea’s aroma instantly bloomed in her mouth.

Zhou Fuhai looked at the young, handsome girl and gestured for her to sit and talk. "You taste the tea as well."

Shen Zhizhen greeted him politely, sat next to Shen San, picked up the teacup, and took a small sip. She immediately nodded in admiration—it was good tea.

Secretary Chen stepped forward and whispered something into Zhou’s ear, then stood up and left.

Zhou Fuhai: "You girl, with one move you cost Li Shiqun ten million ocean dollars. He came to me and cried and complained for quite a while."

A mocking curl appeared on the corner of Shen Zhimei’s mouth. "That can't be blamed on me, Teacher. Director Li’s curiosity is too strong. I merely dealt with the people following me, and he went and put a bounty on my life on the streets. Since he bullied me to my face, I naturally had to teach him a lesson."

Lessons, if too mild, aren't remembered. Only when it hurts enough can it be engraved in one's mind.

Zhou Fuhai shook his head with a chuckle. *Sigh*, he had brought this on himself. Who told him to put the Special Operations Department in the hands of this student? This girl never leaves her power unused when she has it.

Thinking that Li Shiqun’s ambitions were growing, a little beating was probably for the best. He decided to drop the subject.

"I heard your copying skills are superb, to the point of being indistinguishable from the real thing. Is that true?" Zhou Fuhai looked at Shen Jiu and asked.

Shen Zhizhen was listening to the two foxes—one big and one small—spar while sipping her tea. She hadn't expected the topic to suddenly shift to her.

Shen Zhizhen put down her teacup and replied solemnly: "Naturally. The fake paintings I’ve produced in the past could be sold as the real thing." She was referring to the original owner of the body; since she arrived, any copies or fakes she made were kept in her space, and even if she occasionally sold a few, they were sold as high-end replicas.

Zhou Fuhai was amused. *Very good, this Shen Jiu is quite confident.* He turned to look at his student to verify the truth.

Shen Zhimei had considered many possibilities, but this was not one of them. Given the teacher’s high and powerful status, whatever original works he wanted would be offered to him by others on a silver platter.

Shen Zhimei nodded, confirming the statement was true. "Teacher, don't underestimate this girl. Besides copying, she knows how to do many other things."

Zhou Fuhai smiled and nodded. "Good, then come with me." With that, he stood up and walked toward the basement.

The two sisters looked at each other and followed. As she walked, Shen Zhizhen complained to herself: this high-ranking, powerful man was truly interesting—he actually wanted her to make fake paintings.

The three of them passed through two iron doors to reach their destination: a spacious, fortress-like secret room. Inside were several long tables, chairs, folding beds, and a painting display desk. On the long tables were various dyes, tools, and scrolls for making fake paintings.

Shen Zhizhen looked at these strange furnishings, her gaze lingering for a moment on an iron door. She secretly guessed to herself: *That wouldn't be a bathroom, would it?* She couldn't be blamed for thinking so, because the layout here was telling her in no uncertain terms that this place was about to become her workshop for creating fake paintings.

Under the teacher’s signal, Shen Zhimei walked to one end of the display desk and pulled open the scroll placed on it. A long landscape scroll slowly unfurled.

Shen Zhizhen knew this was the painting he wanted her to copy. She stepped forward to take a look. It was a painting depicting a corner of the landscape around Jinshan Temple. Large areas of blank space were used to express the misty atmosphere of the river, while temples, halls, and pagodas were built against the mountains. Ancient trees stood sturdy, dotted throughout, and tiny figures of literati, monks, and boatmen added a sense of life and narrative to the scene.

Seeing this, Shen Zhizhen recalled a plot point from the book: Wang the Traitor possessed a national-treasure-level painting, *The Splendid Scenery of Jinshan*. This painting was a former Qing palace collection gifted by Empress Dowager Longyu. To curry favor with his Japanese masters, Wang intended to present this national treasure as a birthday gift to the Japanese high command.

The male lead had said this was a cultural surrender—handing over the essence of Chinese civilization to the invaders, a concrete manifestation of national humiliation.

This painting had been fought over by many parties and eventually fell into the hands of the Japanese intelligence chief, Yamamoto Taro. Yamamoto Taro sent *The Splendid Scenery of Jinshan* back to Japan, but it was later appraised as a fake, and the original disappeared, never to appear again.

Thinking of this, a flash of doubt crossed Shen Zhizhen’s eyes. Why was this painting in Zhou Fuhai’s hands? The book clearly stated that this painting belonged to the traitor Wang, and Zhou Fuhai had asked her to copy a forgery. Could it be that Zhou Fuhai intended to swap the original for a fake?

Although her mind was racing, Shen Zhizhen appeared very focused on the surface. After looking at it, she commented: "This painting perfectly combines the grandeur of natural mountains and rivers with the solemnity and tranquility of a Buddhist holy site. If I’m not mistaken, this should be the *Scenery of Jinshan*."

Seeing that Shen Jiu had recognized it, Zhou Fuhai gained a bit more confidence in her. "I want you to copy this painting to the point where it is indistinguishable from the real thing. How long will it take?"

Upon hearing this, Shen Zhizhen first looked at the scrolls laid out on the long table. She pulled a few out to examine them and saw that they had already been treated to look aged. She then checked the pigments and other materials; the most time-consuming steps had already been completed.

After inspecting them, she stated that it could be finished in ten days. In reality, with her copying skills, she could finish it within five. She said ten days because she wanted to paint an extra one; heh, when the time came, she would pull a "swap the beams for pillars" trick herself.

Shen Zhimei’s eyelids twitched uncontrollably. After making eye contact with Xiao Jiu, she knew this dead girl was up to something. She gave her a quiet glare, warning her not to go too far. They were currently in Nanjing; if their little tricks were discovered, it would be hard to escape.

Zhou Fuhai did not notice the silent exchange between the sisters. His attention was entirely on the *Scenery of Jinshan*. Even when he spoke to ask questions, his gaze never left the painting, and the greed in his eyes was undisguised.

Hearing that it could be painted in ten days, a trace of satisfaction flashed in his eyes. "I’ll give you ten days. You are not allowed to leave this place until it is finished."

chapters.title: Discovery
chapters.content:
*Click.* The thirty-centimeter-thick iron door shut.

Shen Zhizhen first inspected the secret room. As she had expected, the surrounding walls were made of poured concrete, as was the bathroom; there was only a ventilation duct above the door.

After she had a clear understanding of the situation, she walked to the *Scenery of Jinshan* and observed it carefully. Actually, copying was easy; as long as the correct pigments were used, one could achieve a likeness in both spirit and form.

But what Zhou Fuhai wanted was for the fake to be indistinguishable from the real thing. This meant she had to start with the materials of the painting itself. She had to find the same paper, silk, pigments, and ink as the original—this was the material foundation for fooling appraisal experts.

Everything currently in use was new. What to do? She had to rely on "aging" techniques. Simply put, aging meant using skill to drape a layer of the passage of time over the painting.

A top-tier appraiser does not rely on looking at a painting, but rather on smelling and sensing it to make a comprehensive judgment about the era of the work.

To reach a level capable of deceiving a top-tier appraiser, one needed real, deep skills.

Fortunately, the most difficult and time-consuming part had already been handled by Zhou Fuhai. She only needed to complete the remaining parts.

But then again, a fake is a fake; it is impossible to replicate it perfectly in every detail. After all, the original painting was soaked in the marks of time. A top-tier forgery expert could only hope to confuse, making those top-tier appraisers uncertain and hesitant to reach a conclusion.

Shen Zhizhen began her analysis from the painting's form, brushwork, materials, age, and seals. After examining the front, she rolled it up, unfolded it to look at the back, and finally inspected the top and bottom rods, the painting silk, and the rod ends...

Zhou Fuhai and Shen Zhimei left the secret room and went straight to the study.

Zhou Fuhai leaned back in his chair, looked at the student sitting opposite him, and asked, "Are you very curious?"

Upon hearing this, Shen Zhimei replied straightforwardly: "A little. Would the teacher be willing to enlighten me?"

Zhou Fuhai slowly took off the Buddhist prayer beads from his wrist, his fingertips lightly twisting each warm wooden bead, and told his student the reason for having her sister copy the *Scenery of Jinshan*...

As she listened, Shen Zhimei organized the information in her mind. So, the *Scenery of Jinshan* had been targeted the moment it was retrieved. Director Wang’s wife was worried about it being stolen and knew that the teacher had an impregnable secret room in his home, which was why she had entrusted the painting to him for safekeeping.

A few days ago, the teacher discovered a Japanese mole in his household. Under interrogation, it was learned that this person had already told Yamamoto Taro that the *Scenery of Jinshan* was in his home. The teacher decided to turn the tables and use a fake *Scenery of Jinshan* to deceive them.

After hearing this, Shen Zhimei thought the strategy was quite clever. After all, one can guard against a thief for a thousand days, but one cannot be on guard forever. However, based on her judgment, she feared the matter was not that simple; she suspected her teacher was also coveting this *Scenery of Jinshan*.

She then thought about how her Xiao Jiu was also coveting it. This chaotic situation made her feel like a spectator, and she wanted to see who would end up with the *Scenery of Jinshan* in the end.

Thinking this, she pulled back her wandering thoughts. She didn't express any opinion on the matter but instead went straight to reporting her work.

"The student had Hei Yue investigate the Bai family in Western Hunan..." Shen Zhimei reported the results of Hei Yue’s investigation.

"Before coming to Nanjing, the student had Shen Jiu scout Tanaka Fumiya’s residence, but no treasure map or those two Phoenix Tokens were found."

"The purpose of the Phoenix Tokens is unknown. It was only discovered that their origin is related to the Ancient Phoenix Dynasty. Since Tanaka Fumiya was willing to risk being expelled from his clan to steal them, the student suspects that these two Phoenix Tokens, like the treasure map, are related to the Phoenix Emperor's Tomb."

After finishing, Shen Zhimei looked at her teacher, waiting for his next instructions. During the report, she had been observing his demeanor. When the Phoenix Tokens were mentioned, the teacher showed no abnormality. Thinking of this, her eyes lowered slightly.

Zhou Fuhai stopped twisting the prayer beads. It seemed this Tanaka Fumiya had significant selfish motives. He frowned for a moment and said: "Since Tanaka Fumiya is searching for them, it means these items are extremely important. You must spare no effort to get the treasure map fragments and the Phoenix Tokens from Tanaka Fumiya’s hands."

Shen Zhimei: "Yes, the student will certainly give it her all."

After the teacher and student finished talking, Shen Zhimei rose to bid him farewell. She left with Hei Yue and boarded the train back to Shanghai that very day.

Shen Zhizhen did not know she had been left behind. At this moment, she was in the secret room, not picking up her brush, but dismantling the rod ends. A painting hailed as a treasure had both its rods removed. If Zhou Fuhai saw this, he would likely be so angry he would shoot her.

She had made a small discovery while looking at the painting earlier: there were slight friction marks under the rod ends on both sides of the *Scenery of Jinshan*. They were very subtle, and without her keen eyes, it would have been hard to notice. Upon identification, the marks were recent.

Driven by curiosity, Shen Zhizhen had dismantled the rods. She was so bold because she was certain that Zhou Fuhai had just left and wouldn't be back so soon.

Aside from a ventilation duct, this secret room was airtight, which was great for isolating the risk of being spied on.

After carefully inspecting the dismantled rods, she found that the top rod, which bore the weight of hanging, was solid, but the bottom rod was half-hollow. She carefully pried open the rod end on the bottom rod, and sure enough, there was a secret inside. The hollow part was only the size of a finger, and something that looked like soft leather was stuffed inside.

Shen Zhizhen took tweezers from her space and carefully extracted the object. A sheepskin scroll appeared before her eyes.

Shen Zhizhen blinked at the familiar-looking sheepskin scroll. It couldn't be that coincidental, could it? After carefully examining the material and pattern, she took out the one from the Shen family to compare. Seeing that the edges connected perfectly, she laughed—it really was another fragment of the treasure map. Calming her excitement, she put the two fragments into her palace space and took out a fake fragment she had spent the last month making to put back in its place.

She had drawn a complete fake map based on the material of the map in her hand, then divided it into three parts, thinking it would be useful for a "swap" if the opportunity arose. She hadn't expected to use it so soon.

She deftly reassembled the rods, checked them once, and after confirming everything was fine, placed the *Scenery of Jinshan* back. Everything looked exactly as it had when Zhou Fuhai was there.

Shen Zhizhen walked to the long table and began mixing colors while pondering the situation.

Did Zhou Fuhai know that there was a treasure map fragment inside the rods of the *Scenery of Jinshan*?

Shen Zhizhen analyzed it and felt it was more likely that he didn't. If he had known, he wouldn't have left the fragment inside the painting.

Although she didn't know why the *Scenery of Jinshan* was here, connecting it to the plot in the book, she couldn't help but guess: could the treasure map fragment have been put there by the traitor Wang?

After all, the book mentioned that to please his Japanese masters, the traitor Wang intended to offer the *Scenery of Jinshan* as a birthday gift to the Japanese high command. Combined with the recent friction marks under the rod ends and the Japanese "Takamagahara Plan," this guess might actually be true.

chapters.title: Cannot Be Left Behind
chapters.content:
At this moment, although Shen Zhizhen didn't know if her thoughts were correct, she was certain of one thing: the decision to swap the *Scenery of Jinshan* was absolutely correct. She could not let a cultural treasure of China fall into the hands of the invaders.

The lights in the secret room were as bright as day. Here, one could only distinguish day from night by the watch on one's wrist. Shen Zhizhen silently kept track of time. Seven days passed in a flash, and the second painting was nearing its final stages.

Three meals a day were delivered on time, but Shen Zhizhen didn't eat a single bite. She took out two antique vases from her space—one for dumping food and one for water. She ate and drank only the food she had stored in her space previously.

She did this partly out of caution, and partly because the butler who brought her food was a bit strange. Every time he came to collect the tray, he would go to the bathroom. What, was the secret room she was staying in the only place in this huge villa with a bathroom?

Such unreasonable details made it hard for her to ignore. She began to suspect that the food was poisoned. After reaching this conclusion, she began to cooperate by making herself look haggard. Although she didn't know what kind of poison it was, it was definitely a chronic one; she wouldn't die before she finished copying the *Scenery of Jinshan*.

If this *Scenery of Jinshan* had been placed with Zhou Fuhai by the traitor Wang, then Zhou Fuhai having her make a fake was clearly for a nefarious purpose. To ensure the matter wasn't exposed, it was possible Zhou Fuhai would kill her to silence her.

After realizing this, Shen Zhizhen’s real thought was: she wondered what Shen San would think if he knew his teacher wanted to kill her sister. She felt this was an opportunity—an opportunity to pull Shen San toward the Red Party. Yes, she had to grasp this well.

Shen Zhizhen looked at the painting before her, the corners of her mouth curling slightly. It was worth the two all-nighters she had pulled. Before leaving, she planned to stir up some trouble; otherwise, she wouldn't be doing justice to the treatment she had received from Zhou Fuhai.

In the study, Zhou Fuhai sneezed inexplicably. He frowned, twisted his prayer beads, and asked: "Has that Shen Jiu been eating her meals?"

The butler lowered his head and replied: "Yes, Shen Jiu eats all the food every day. I personally go to collect the tray every time, and I’ve used the bathroom as an excuse. There isn't a single oil stain on the toilet, nor is there any smell of food."

Although there were no signs of hair loss or anything yet, judging by how haggard she looked, it was already taking effect.

"Hmm, be careful to control the dosage. It must take effect a month after she leaves, so as not to make my student suspicious." Zhou Fuhai’s hand, which was twisting the beads, paused slightly as he gave the order nonchalantly.

"Yes, I will certainly pay attention to the dosage," the butler replied with his head bowed.

"There must be no mistakes at tomorrow's banquet."

"Yes, I will ensure everything is foolproof."

After the butler retreated, Zhou Fuhai slipped his prayer bead bracelet onto his wrist and took a document out of the drawer. The photo on it was none other than Shen Jiu.

This girl was truly audacious; she had killed over a hundred Japanese soldiers within a month and had helped countless Red Party members escape. Someone destined to stand in opposition to him, someone who knew too much—she could not be left alive.

Zhou Fuhai picked up his lighter and flicked it. The flame ignited the investigation report that had been delivered a few days prior. His star pupil had finally turned soft-hearted and couldn't bring himself to harm his own sister, so he would have to play the villain himself.

The burning report was tossed onto the floor, quickly consumed until it turned into a pile of ash.

At the same time, in Shanghai, a group of men broke into Wu De's home and opened fire with their guns. *Rat-tat-tat...*

Upon hearing the front door being kicked in, Wu De bolted to the backyard. He had just leaped over the wall when the gunfire erupted. His heart pounded wildly, and he sprinted toward the docks, moving so fast he left a blur behind him.

As he ran, he wondered if that wretch Wan Donglai had been caught and had sold him out. Otherwise, why would they find him so easily? And opening fire the moment they arrived meant they had no intention of letting him live.

The intruders, finding that their target had escaped, were ordered by their leader: "Pursue them. No survivors."

Wu De ran to the spot where Xi Ya was setting up her stall. Ignoring the fact that it was the peak lunch hour, he grabbed Xi Ya and ran.

When Wang Xiya saw Brother Dezi, she was puzzled as to why he had come, but she never expected to be dragged away without a word.

Her heart sank instantly; she knew something had gone wrong and followed him with absolute cooperation.

The diners at the stall were bewildered—what was going on? Was the landlady not collecting payment? When they heard the commotion behind them and saw a group of men chasing after them, they immediately realized the couple had gotten into big trouble.

Wang Xiya glanced back briefly and saw that the men were armed. No wonder Brother Dezi was pulling her toward areas with cover. She hurriedly asked, "Who are those people? Where are we running to?"

Wu De shook his head, indicating he didn't know. He pulled Xiya to the riverbank, snapped off a few reeds, handed two to her, and said, "Jump into the river. Hold your breath, sink down, and swim forward. If you run out of air, surface just enough to breathe through the reeds. Whatever you do, don't let your head break the surface."

He had heard Wang Xiazi mention that his daughter liked to catch fish in the Tiaozhi River to supplement their meals, so he knew she was a strong swimmer. In the grave-robbing trade, one sometimes encountered flooded tombs, and escape tunnels in some chambers were underwater. Being a strong swimmer was a basic requirement in the Shen family; if you couldn't swim, you weren't allowed to enter a tomb. He had trained alongside Shen Jiu back in the day, so his swimming skills were naturally excellent.

Xiya nodded to show she understood. With two splashes, the bank was empty, leaving only ripples on the river surface.

The pursuers reached the riverbank, and seeing no sign of them, they fired a volley of shots into the water in a rage...

Half an hour later, the couple dared to climb ashore, two miles away from where they had jumped in.

Wang Xiya wiped the water from her face and asked Brother Dezi what they should do next. She knew her sister wasn't in Shanghai, and she had no idea how to handle such a situation.

As Wu De wrung out his clothes, he replied, "We'll find a place to hide first. When it gets dark, I'll go find Shen Zhimei." Fortunately, because of Shen Jiu's suggestion, they had rented a few places, so they weren't entirely without options.

He had run into Wan Donglai a few days ago and learned that Shen Jiu wasn't in Shanghai, having gone to Nanjing with Shen Zhimei. However, he had seen Shen Zhimei's car pass his shop yesterday. So, while escaping underwater, he realized that the people who came for him likely had nothing to do with Wan Donglai. If it were related to the Red Party, they would be trying to capture them, not just opening fire to kill on sight. Therefore, he decided to find Shen Zhimei and ask about the situation.

Wang Xiya asked, "Could it be that what we did was discovered?" She knew that although her third cousin was a secret agent, she was trustworthy, so she didn't object to Brother Dezi's decision.

"It's possible, so we need to be careful and try to avoid people," Wu De cautioned while pondering where to get some disguises.

In the evening, a black sedan pulled up to No. 36 Fengyuan Road... Chapter 65: Friction

Zhang Yong and Wang Wu got out of the car one after the other. After ensuring it was safe, they opened the back door. Shen Zhimei stepped out and walked toward the house. The two men waited until she was inside and the door was locked before returning to their quarters on the first floor.

As soon as Shen Zhimei entered, she realized someone had been in the house. She glanced at the slip of paper she had wedged in the door that morning, then pulled her gun from her bag and aimed it at the head peeking sneakily from the kitchen.

Seeing who it was, she lowered her gun and frowned, asking, "Why are you here?" She changed into her slippers, hung up her trench coat, and walked to the sofa.

Wu De let out a sigh of relief, walked over, and sat on the single-seat sofa, recounting his and Xiya's experience.

"Third Cousin, do you think what we did on the way to Shanghai was discovered?"

Shen Zhimei's expression changed. She didn't answer Wu De, but instead reached for the phone and dialed. After the call connected, she asked, "Heiyue, was this your doing?"

Heiyue, holding the phone, rubbed her brow. Knowing she couldn't hide it from her, she told the truth: "It wasn't me. The intelligence came from Department Head Zhou, who ordered it to be kept from you."

Very well. She had a premonition that the teacher and student would now have a falling out. Life was truly becoming more difficult.

Hearing that it was the teacher himself who gave the order, Shen Zhimei's heart sank. If the teacher was moving against Wu De and Wang Xiya at a time like this, Shen Jiu was in danger.

"Who did the teacher send to do the killing?"

"This afternoon, Wang Fusheng, the leader of the Second Special Group of No. 76, took men out. I heard Director Li gave the order personally." Heiyue finished what she knew and hung up.

She walked to the window and stared at the cold moonlight outside. Although she hadn't known her long, she could tell that what Shen Zhimei cared about most was her younger sister. She didn't know why Department Head Zhou thought he could hide this from Shen Zhimei; wasn't he afraid of that woman's retaliation?

A cold sneer tugged at the corner of her mouth at the thought. Men in high positions always thought they could control everything.

Although a storm was brewing in Shen Zhimei's eyes, she remained surprisingly calm. Her mind raced, quickly sorting through the entire sequence of events, and the teacher's true motive became clear.

While the spark seemed to be the trio's actions on the way to Shanghai—leading the teacher to think they were no longer on the same path—that wasn't the real reason. What truly triggered the teacher's murderous intent was what Shen Jiu was doing right now. The combination of the two led the teacher to decide to eliminate this hidden threat.

That painting was definitely not just what the teacher had claimed. If she wasn't mistaken, Dean Wang didn't know the teacher had hired people to copy the *Map of Jinshan's Famous Sites*.

Once the sequence was straightened out, it was self-evident who had reported the trio's activities to the teacher. After all, the warrant for the three had been issued to No. 76; just because she had suppressed it didn't mean no one else would find it.

Li Shiqun was a narrow-minded man who held grudges; he would certainly retaliate against her if he found the chance.

"The mountain wind blows before the storm arrives." Wu De read these words from Shen Zhimei's expression. "Is my little cousin in danger?" He had heard the content of the phone call.

Shen Zhimei nodded slightly. She took paper and pen from under the tea table, scribbled down the contents, folded the paper, and handed it to Wu De.

"Go find Wan Donglai in a while and give this to him. Tell him that if he can get the things on this paper done in the next few days, he can come to me for any intelligence he wants in the Shanghai Bund in the future."

Wu De took it, bewildered. After hearing her, he realized: his third cousin was going to cooperate with the Red Party. His heart sank; it seemed the situation for his little cousin was not optimistic.

After speaking, Shen Zhimei pointed to the kitchen. "I'm going to Nanjing tomorrow to pick up Little Jiu." With that, she stood up and returned to her room.

Wu De sighed softly, walked to the kitchen, opened the window, and jumped out. He used the wall for leverage and landed on the ground, disappearing quietly into the cover of night.

In the Zhabei residential area, Wu De didn't arrive until the middle of the night. He found the address Wan Donglai had given him and, without knocking, jumped over the wall. As he pushed the door open, a gun was pressed against his forehead.

Wu De hurriedly spoke up, "It's me."

When Wan Donglai heard it was Wu De, he put the gun away and lit the kerosene lamp. The room brightened. "Why are you here?"

Wu De told him about being hunted. "I went to find Third Cousin to ask what was going on..." He rambled on about his visit to Shen San.

"She told me to give this to you and said that if you can get the things on this paper done in the next few days, you can come to her for any intelligence you want in the Shanghai Bund in the future." After saying this, Wu De picked up the teapot and poured himself a cup of water. He had been rushing all the way without a break, and his throat felt like it was smoking.

Wan Donglai was stunned. The three of them had actually done such a big thing; it was worthy of the young boss, Shen.

Hearing that Shen Jiu might be in trouble, he couldn't help but worry. But then, thinking of Shen Jiu's skills, he felt she would be fine. Even if caught, that girl could escape; he just had that intuition about her.

Not to mention that Shen Jiu was their comrade, and they would naturally do everything to save her. He took the folded paper and opened it, shock flashing in his eyes. The paper not only listed the times, locations, and storage sites for the smuggling ships over the next few days, but also the storage locations for the Japanese military supplies...

Wan Donglai excitedly closed the paper. If what was written here was true, they wouldn't have to worry about supplies, let alone the things Shen San had promised.

After finishing his water, Wu De said to Wan Donglai, "If you need my help, just call me. Xiya and I are staying at..." He left after speaking.

Wan Donglai saw Wu De off, locked the door, and hurried to find Old Gu. When he met him, he repeated what Wu De had said and handed him the note. "Old Gu, take a look at this."

After listening and reading, Old Gu knew that Shen Zhimei wanted to use their hands to stir up trouble, disrupt the puppet government and the Japanese, and give her the room to go to Nanjing to save people.

Old Gu paced back and forth, thinking about the reliability of this. The intelligence provided by the "Chao Feng" (the agent) last time had been very accurate. They had withdrawn their people, changed their identities, and relocated, suffering almost no losses.

Compared to them, the White Party had suffered much more, with many being purged—it was quite tragic. Such precise intelligence coming from Shen Zhimei had already caught the attention of the higher-ups, who had ordered them to try their best to win her over.

Now that Shen Zhimei had developed friction with the puppet government because of the Chao Feng, this was a good opportunity to win her over. Not to mention that the Chao Feng was one of their own; they had to save her, no matter the risk.

With Shen Zhimei offering this cooperation plan, they were gaining every advantage. If successful, they would get supplies, money, and the ability to intimidate the Japanese and the puppet government.

Old Gu stopped pacing and said fiercely, "Let's do it. Come on, let's go notify our people." After taking two steps, he decided to report to his superiors first.

The two then split up to act. Wan Donglai was responsible for gathering the people, while Old Gu went to report the situation to their superiors. After hearing the report, the superiors analyzed it and deemed it feasible; not only did they agree, but they also notified other parties, distributing the tasks written on the note.

“We must adopt guerrilla tactics, strike quickly and decisively, and withdraw immediately after success. We must never get bogged down in a protracted fight.” Chapter 66: Robbing the Rich to Help the Poor Again

At the Zhou Mansion in Nanjing, Shen Zhizhen was unaware that Shen San had lost his temper over her. At this moment, she was working overtime to complete her final task.

In the early hours of the morning, she finally finished the second copy. Shen Zhizhen put down her brush and looked at the painting on the table with satisfaction. After admiring it for a while and confirming there were no issues, she stood up, put the original *Jinshan Scenic Map* into her space, and placed the first copy on the display stand.

To deceive everyone, she even made the bottom roller of the copy identical to the original and placed a fake treasure map inside, ensuring that even the traitor Wang would believe it was real.

As for the copy she had just finished on the long table, she did not make any extra adjustments. She had to leave some key points for verification, otherwise, how would the traitor Wang notice Zhou Fuhai’s ambition?

Shen Zhizhen checked everything one last time. Confirming there were no issues, she lifted her wrist to check her watch; 2:00 AM was when people were at their most exhausted.

With that in mind, she took a large lock-picking needle from her space and inserted it into the keyhole to manipulate it. She had observed the style of the lock before entering; it was an embedded lock core that she could open from the inside.

Moreover, whether out of confidence or for the sake of appearances, Zhou Fuhai had not arranged for anyone to guard the door from the outside. Therefore, having wandered around these past few nights, she had already memorized the layout of the entire Zhou Mansion.

Not only that, she also knew that tomorrow—no, today—the Zhou Mansion was hosting a grand banquet for officials from the Japanese Ministry of Education and the Ministry of Finance who were visiting Nanjing.

With so many people tomorrow, security would inevitably be tightened, and since the painting was finished, there was no need for her to linger here. Thus, she pondered robbing the rich to help the poor at the Zhou Mansion before leaving—well, robbing Zhou Fuhai’s wealth to help the Red Party’s poverty.

With a click, the back door lock opened. Shen Zhizhen opened the door and stepped out, cautiously avoiding the patrols, and quietly made her way to the third basement level. After these days of reconnaissance, this was where Zhou Fuhai’s private treasury was located.

Shen Zhizhen took a bamboo tube from her space and blew it toward the two guards yawning in front of the door. A puff of gray powder quickly dissipated in the air, and in less than a minute, the two men at the door collapsed one after another.

Holding her breath, Shen Zhizhen walked over and pulled out her lock-picking needle. After opening the door, a look of surprise flashed in her eyes.

My goodness, she had seen the world since coming here, but an entire mountain of gold still shocked her. Yes, half the space of the entire third basement level was filled with gold.

There were no boxes; the gold bricks were simply stacked layer by layer. Calling it a mountain of gold was no exaggeration.

That wasn’t all. On the other side, nearly a hundred boxes of jade ornaments, jewelry, antiques, and calligraphy and paintings were laid out on the floor, all with the lids open. Tsk, tsk, did this Zhou Fuhai have some kind of fetish? Could it be that he came here from time to time to see the empire he had built with his own eyes!

While complaining internally, Shen Zhizhen cleared out everything in the third basement level. As for whether this would turn into a supernatural event, she couldn't care less now. If they suspected her, they would have to produce evidence, as long as it didn't implicate Shen San.

Shen Zhizhen came out, closed the door, and helped the two men on the floor stand up, pressing their acupoints to ensure they wouldn't fall over. Anyone passing by wouldn't notice anything; they would only think the two were slacking off and sleeping against the wall.

After cleaning up, Shen Zhizhen returned to her cell, closed the door, lay down on the folding bed, and fell fast asleep...

In Shanghai, at No. 36 Fengyuan Road, early in the morning, Shen Zhimei opened the door carrying a handbag and saw Hei Yue standing outside. A cold sneer curled her lips, “What, are you going to stop me from going to Nanjing?”

“No, I’m taking you there myself,” Hei Yue said with a cold face.

Shen Zhimei glanced at her sideways, said nothing, and walked straight out.

Hei Yue followed behind Shen Zhimei, waving her hand to signal Zhang Yong and Wang Wu that they didn't need to follow.

It wasn't until the car was on the road that Hei Yue spoke in a cold voice: “Li Shiqun had three smuggling ships hijacked early this morning. Was that your doing?”

One couldn't blame her for being suspicious; it was simply too targeted. Li Shiqun had sent people to kill Shen Zhimei’s relative yesterday, and they were retaliated against overnight. Wasn't that too much of a coincidence?

Hearing this, mockery flickered in Shen Zhimei’s eyes. “I called you once after I got home yesterday and haven't been out since. Don't pin everything on me.”
