Although she was now the Director of the Special Operations Division, because her tenure was too short and due to a move her teacher had made, the person who actually controlled the division was Hei Yue. Zhang Yong and Wang Wu were both Hei Yue’s subordinates; it was called protection, but it could also be surveillance.

If she wanted to fully control the Special Operations Division, she had to take down Hei Yue. A dark glint flashed in her eyes at the thought.

Hei Yue said nothing after hearing this. She indeed hadn't found any evidence, but her intuition told her it was Shen Zhimei.

Shen Zhimei naturally understood why Hei Yue was following her personally; it was nothing more than wanting to monitor her directly. Naturally, she couldn't do anything under her nose.

Shen Zhimei lowered her eyes and remained silent for a long time before speaking in a low voice, “Hei Yue, don't you want to know the truth about your family being wiped out overnight?”

Hearing this, Hei Yue slammed on the brakes. The tires let out a shrill screech, and the black sedan jerked on the side of the road and came to a sudden halt.

Hei Yue turned her head sharply, murderous intent flickering in her cold gaze, staring fixedly at the face of the person in the back seat. “What do you want to say?” Her tone was bone-chilling.

Shen Zhimei didn't care at all and began to tell the story unhurriedly: “In '32, Teacher participated in the founding of the White Party’s secret service organization, the Blue Shirts Society...”

A certain person in the White Party founded the Blue Shirts Society to establish a secret core organization that combined intelligence, propaganda, and military functions, serving as a sharp blade and enforcer for his personal dictatorship.

During the initial establishment of the Blue Shirts Society, her teacher, Zhou Fuhai, had personally presided over and planned several assassination operations. One of them was the murder of the family of Hei Minzan, a high-ranking official of the White Party’s left wing.

“You hate the White Party, you hate Chiang, but shouldn't the person you hate most be the one who personally planned the murder of your entire family?”

Shen Zhimei’s words turned into a funeral bell, trembling and spreading deep within Hei Yue’s mind, swallowing all rational thoughts.

Shen Zhimei had only learned of this by chance. To her, this was just a trivial matter, almost forgotten, but after taking over the Special Operations Division, she had launched an investigation into Hei Yue, the person in actual control. After all, "know yourself and know your enemy, and you will never be defeated; know neither, and you will surely be defeated in every battle."

She hadn't expected this investigation to reveal such a shocking truth: Hei Yue was actually the daughter of her teacher’s old friend, Hei Minzan. Even more ironically, the tragedy of the entire Hei family being wiped out had been planned by her teacher himself. Hei Yue had survived only because she wasn't home at the time. Later, her teacher had even hypocritically stepped forward to hold the funeral for the Hei family and sent Hei Yue to a special department for training.

He killed her father and brother, then trained the orphan into his most loyal weapon. Zhou Fuhai’s scheming was truly ruthless. Chapter 67: Thieves Have Entered

Hei Yue forced herself to calm down, knowing that Shen Zhimei had ill intentions; she couldn't fall for it.

“You think I’ll believe you?” Her tone was icy, yet it faltered for a split second.

Shen Zhimei looked at her with pity. “Believe it or not, that’s up to you.”

In this world, there are always people capable of erasing traces. They can make people see only the truth they want them to see.

By saying this today, she was merely introducing a crack into Hei Yue’s perfect loyalty. Once the seed of doubt is planted, it will grow on its own.

Once the foundation of belief is loosened, scrutiny becomes an instinct, and verification becomes the only command. But the truth of that year had long been tampered with by her teacher. No matter how many times Hei Yue investigated, what she would find was merely the script written by Zhou Fuhai.

Under these circumstances, she was naturally the breakthrough point. If Hei Yue wanted to know the clues from back then, she would have to cooperate with her.

Hei Yue hated the way Shen Zhimei looked at her. She turned her head and restarted the car, but she hadn't gone far before slamming on the brakes again. “What are your conditions?”

When it came to the truth about her family’s annihilation, no matter how much she told herself otherwise, she couldn't suppress the determination to know the truth.

“Help me take full control of the Special Operations Division.” Seeing the fish take the bait so quickly, Shen Zhimei chuckled and stated her true intention.

Hearing that this meant she had to pledge allegiance to her, Hei Yue’s gaze turned as cold as an ice blade, but her voice was terrifyingly calm: “Fine, but my loyalty will be held hostage by your life.” If she dared to lie to her, she would pay with her life.

A faint, almost imperceptible curve touched Shen Zhimei’s lips, and she replied in a languid tone: “Agreed.” The black sedan started up and hit the road again.

The two boarded the train and entered their compartment. Hei Yue finally calmed down completely, realizing she had been tricked...

In Nanjing, at the Zhou Mansion, the noise of the banquet reached the second basement level.

Because Shen Zhizhen had gone to be a thief last night, she spent the whole morning catching up on sleep. When the butler came to deliver food in the morning, she made an excuse that she had stayed up all night copying paintings and needed to sleep, telling the butler not to come for lunch, which gave her some peace and quiet.

After waking up and washing, she took a steamed bun from her space to satisfy her hunger when suddenly, footsteps came from outside the door.

Shen Zhizhen was puzzled; didn't she say not to bring food? She pricked up her ears and immediately realized something was wrong. The person coming wasn't the butler, and the footsteps of the two people outside were deliberately muffled.

Shen Zhizhen blinked, took a bite of the bun, and as the other party began to pick the lock, she finally realized that thieves had entered the Zhou Mansion.

She glanced at the painting she had finished just yesterday on the table; she couldn't let others see that there was a second *Jinshan Scenic Map*. With that thought, she rolled up the fake painting on the table and entered the palace space with it.

Shen Zhizhen sat on the phoenix chair, continuing to eat her bun while monitoring the situation outside. She really hadn't expected to encounter this; thieves had actually broken into the heavily guarded Zhou Mansion and even made it to the second basement level.

She then thought of herself and was almost amused. Well, she had been personally invited by Zhou Fuhai, unlike the two outside.

However, she was quite curious about the identities of the two thieves about to enter. She wondered if she could make use of them; after all, she had stolen from Zhou Fuhai’s private treasury early this morning. If she could shift the blame onto them, she would be much safer.

Yamamoto Koichi and Hyakushima Kaori had snuck into the Zhou Mansion following Japanese Ministry of Education officials. Using the cover of the crowded banquet, they moved toward their destination. Because both were wearing Japanese attire and were people around high-ranking Japanese officials, the people at the Zhou Mansion didn't pay much attention, so the two avoided everyone and arrived at the second basement level.

Yamamoto Koichi opened the door and saw the *Jinshan Scenic Map* on the display stand at a glance. “Yoshi, it’s the painting the section chief mentioned.”

Baidao Xiangzhi nodded with a smile, "Yes." After speaking, she stepped forward to roll up the painting, placed it in a box, and handed it to Yamamoto Koichi, "You take the painting and leave first."

Yamamoto Koichi knew the section chief’s order: set a fire to burn this place down and ensure the Nanjing government could not link it to them. After all, the two sides were currently in a period of cooperation, and a scandal would not look good.

He took the wine flask filled with gasoline from his pocket and handed it to Xiangzhi, cautioning, "Be careful." Once Xiangzhi took it, he left with the painting.

Their plan was for Xiangzhi to be responsible for setting the fire to lure people away, while he would find an opportunity to take the painting out of the Zhou Mansion.

Baidao Xiangzhi unscrewed the cap of the wine flask and sprinkled the gasoline inside onto the floor and flammable areas. After finishing, she tossed the flask aside, took out a lighter, and threw it onto the bedding on the bed. With a "whoosh," flames erupted and gradually spread to the surroundings.

A hint of triumph appeared in Baidao Xiangzhi’s eyes. She turned and walked toward the door. Just as her hand touched the doorknob, she felt a sudden chill at her neck, and a line of blood sprayed out...

Shen Zhizhen had not expected to run into an acquaintance—Baidao Xiangzhi, that white jasmine flower from the Dong family. Since they had crossed paths, she naturally had to finish off this malicious flower. She stuffed the remaining bun into her mouth, found a dagger, emerged from her space the moment Baidao Xiangzhi turned around, and slit her throat with one stroke.

Shen Zhizhen threw the body onto the burning bed and decided to add fuel to the fire. She took a gasoline canister from her space and poured half of it into the room. The fire roared, merging into a single sheet of flame, instantly turning the room into a sea of fire.

Shen Zhizhen quickly slipped out and closed the door. She walked a distance away, entered her space before encountering anyone, and picked out an outfit similar to Baidao Xiangzhi’s from her clothes, along with a wig. She looked at herself in the mirror; it was, in fact, seven or eight parts similar.

Shen Zhizhen put on a pair of sunglasses to hide her face, stepped out of her space, and walked out openly, deliberately showing her back to the butler in the distance.

Exiting the gate, she found an empty car, started it, and drove off. When she encountered a patrol squad blocking the way, she slammed the accelerator to the floor and charged through.

The captain in charge of security immediately realized something was wrong. "Quick, chase the car in front!" Everyone immediately got into their vehicles to pursue, while those who couldn't fit went to report the situation to the butler.

Upon hearing the report, the butler thought of the direction from which the woman had just appeared, and his face changed drastically. "No, hurry to the basement!" With that, he led his men hurriedly toward the basement...

With a loud bang, the iron gate of the Zhou Mansion was violently rammed open. A black sedan sped out, leaving two scorched marks on the ground. Several cars followed in quick succession, pursuing the black car relentlessly, firing shots from time to time in an attempt to force it to stop.

Shen Zhizhen drove while observing the road conditions. She took a pistol from her space and fired a couple of shots whenever she found an opportunity.

While swerving to avoid a black sedan ahead, she glanced casually into that car and saw the face of Shen San flash by.

Shen San was here? Shen Zhizhen frowned. After a moment of thought, she turned the steering wheel and drove toward the riverside.

Heiyue gripped the steering wheel. After a few gunshots, she frowned and said, "Should we pursue?" If she wasn't mistaken, the cars chasing behind were from the Zhou Mansion.

Shen Zhimei was thinking about how the person she had just glimpsed felt inexplicably familiar. Hearing this, she shook her head slightly, "No need, go straight to the Zhou Mansion."

chapters.title: What Does This Prove?
chapters.content:
The pursuers realized the target's intention. The captain grabbed a machine gun, leaned out of the car window, and began to spray fire. Da-da-da...
The moment Shen Zhizhen saw the river, she didn't hesitate for a second and slammed on the accelerator. The instant the gunfire erupted, a strong sense of crisis made her hair stand on end, and she lunged to the side almost instinctively! At nearly the same moment, a string of bullets whistled through the spot where she had just been, riddling the driver's seat with holes.
At this moment, the black sedan traced an arc in the air and plunged into the river, splashing up a massive wave.
Shen Zhizhen breathed a sigh of relief the moment the car hit the water. If she had been shot at any longer, there was no guarantee she wouldn't have been hit. River water poured in through the shattered windows. Before leaving, she glanced at the bullet-riddled driver's seat and, having a sudden inspiration, changed her mind.
Shen Zhizhen moved the entire car into her palace space, dug out a bag of blood plasma, tore the bag, and poured the blood onto the seat.
Haha, this should be enough to frame them completely. She wanted to make the Japanese side suffer in silence. Once the blood soaked into the seat, she opened the driver's side door and then threw the car into the river. The black sedan was instantly submerged by the river water and sank.
Shen Zhizhen didn't change her clothes; the coordinates of her space followed her. Even if she changed into clean clothes now, she would still be in the river when she exited the space.
Shen Zhizhen emerged from her space and oriented herself to swim toward the opposite bank. The spot where she landed was some distance from the scene of the incident. Only then did she re-enter her space to change clothes and disguise herself. When she came out again, she was a young man with a thin mustache.
At the Zhou Mansion, Shen Zhimei stepped out of the car, frowning at the chaos before her. She walked over to the butler and asked, "What happened?"
The butler had just finished sending off the guests who attended the banquet. Seeing Miss Shen, he felt a wave of bitterness. In response, he replied, "An intruder broke in and set a fire. The master is currently in a rage."
"Arson? Where did the fire break out?" Seeing the butler’s guilty expression, Shen Zhimei had a bad premonition.
Seeing that he couldn't divert the topic, the butler had to bite the bullet and tell the truth, "The secret room where the Ninth Miss Shen was staying was set on fire. The fire has just been extinguished, but the Ninth Miss Shen did not escape."
Hearing this, the world went black for Shen Zhimei. She was supported by a pair of cold hands, preventing her from falling. That familiar figure flashed through her mind, and she immediately realized something. She decided to feign a faint to think about what was going on.
Heiyue... with a cold face, she picked her up and told the butler to arrange a room for her first.
Seeing this, the butler couldn't help but feel relieved. Fainting was fine; it saved him from facing Miss Shen. He was truly afraid of revealing a flaw in front of this sharp-witted woman.
As the butler led the way, he felt fortunate that it had burned down; it was better than her discovering that her sister had been poisoned.
But thinking about how the master's grand plan had been ruined, he felt another headache coming on.
Heiyue placed her on the bed and followed the butler out to understand the situation. They arrived at the scene of the fire, where there was a charred corpse. It was burned so badly that nothing could be identified.
Heiyue’s cold eyes were filled with questions. "Is this Shen Nine?"
The butler nodded firmly and replied, "It is the Ninth Miss Shen. She was the only one in this secret room." After speaking, he skipped over what he was doing there and recounted the events surrounding the arson.
Butler: "The person who set the fire snuck in following the high-ranking officials of the Ministry of Education. Their specific identity is not yet clear."
Heiyue: "What does the Ministry of Education say?"
Butler: "They deny it." It was also because of this that the master was so furious that he didn't even show his face to see off the guests. Today, the Japanese side’s face had been completely lost.
Heiyue...
Knowing that this topic couldn't continue, she changed the subject and asked casually, "Are there any other losses?"
She couldn't describe her mood at this moment; it was complicated and indescribable. She couldn't be sure about what Shen Zhimei had said, but it had planted seeds of doubt in her heart. So, for now, she maintained her usual appearance on the surface, not letting Zhou Fuhai notice anything unusual.
The butler was about to say no, but then he remembered something and hurriedly ran toward the third basement level. If that thief could enter the second floor to set a fire, they could naturally run to the third floor as well.
The guards at the door had long been attracted by the commotion on the second floor, and upon discovering the fire, they had joined in to help put it out. After the fire was out, they couldn't help but gossip with others, so when the butler arrived, neither of them was guarding the door.
Seeing this, the butler’s heart sank. He took out the key, opened the vault door, and pushed it open. He was stunned—it was empty? Everything went black, and he fell backward.
Heiyue reached out with a cold expression to steady him. She looked inside and saw nothing; she didn't understand what was wrong with the butler.
At this moment, the guards came over. Seeing the vault door open and the butler fainted, they looked inside with confusion. Empty?
The two looked at each other. Although they didn't know what was going on, they were certain that they were about to face a disaster.
Heiyue handed the butler over to them and ordered, "Take the butler upstairs and call a doctor while you're at it." Why were they all fainting one after another?
Hearing this, the two tacitly took the butler. After taking him to his room, fearing he would wake up too soon, they picked up an ashtray and hit the butler on the head with it.
Before leaving, they ransacked the butler’s room. After dividing the spoils, the two said, "Brother, if we can't escape this, we definitely won't survive. Once we get out, we'll each run for our lives."
The other nodded to show he understood. They knew exactly what was in the third-floor vault. Regardless of why the items had vanished, staying meant certain death for both of them, so it was better to take a gamble and escape.
Although the world was in chaos, as long as they escaped Nanjing and reached a place beyond Zhou Fuhai’s reach, surviving wouldn't be a problem.
Shen Zhimei opened her eyes as soon as Heiyue left, pondering what was really going on. In any case, whoever died in the secret room, it wouldn't be Xiao Jiu, because she was certain that the person in that car earlier was Xiao Jiu. Even though she was disguised, she would recognize her own sister even if she were turned to ash.
The parts she couldn't understand in her heart became clear after Heiyue came in and finished recounting the events.
Xiao Jiu must have discovered that the teacher wanted to kill her, so when someone came in to steal the Golden Hill Scenic Map, she took the opportunity to perform a "cicada shedding its skin." After all, this was a trick the Shen family loved to use; her father had used it once for Xiao Jiu when they were in Shenyang.
After Heiyue finished speaking, she saw Shen Zhimei lost in thought. Although she didn't know what she was thinking, she still said, "My condolences."
Hearing this, Shen Zhimei suppressed a laugh. This woman wasn't as cold as she seemed; she was actually quite cute.
Shen Zhimei threw off the quilt, got out of bed, put on her shoes, straightened her clothes, and walked out. She should go and meet Mr. Zhou Fuhai to probe what was in the third basement level that could make the butler faint on the spot.
There was also the question of whether the Golden Hill Scenic Map had been stolen or burned. The reason she didn't guess that the original had already been taken by the teacher was because of the butler’s words: Xiao Jiu was still in the secret room at the time, which meant the task of copying it had not yet been completed.
Of course, the most likely possibility was that the original Golden Hill Scenic Map had been taken by Xiao Jiu...

chapters.title: Chaos Erupts
chapters.content:
Zhou Fuhai was currently in his study, flying into a rage. The *Golden Hill Scenic Map* he had painstakingly plotted to get was gone. He hadn't obtained the item and had instead brought trouble upon himself.
He was still thinking about how to explain it to Wang Jingwei when he heard the butler say that the third-floor vault had been emptied. He vomited a mouthful of blood in anger and collapsed straight down.
Seeing this, the butler hurriedly reached out to help him, but was instead pulled down to the ground. His bleeding back of the head hit the floor again, and the pain almost made him faint as well.
The butler couldn't care about the wound on his head; he scrambled up to find someone to help the master up and send him to his room, then ordered someone to call a doctor.
Shen Zhimei came over and saw the chaos. After learning the reason from the butler, she couldn't help but complain inwardly: just how much had her teacher embezzled to have built a vault in his own home?
Seeing the butler stammering and unable to give a clear explanation, she understood that this gold could not see the light of day. The theft of the vault could not be made public; otherwise, her teacher would have to swallow this bitter pill in silence. No wonder he was so angry he vomited blood.
Shen Zhimei went to check on her teacher. Seeing him unconscious, she whispered a few words of comfort to her sobbing mistress before exiting the room to look at the charred corpse.
Heiyue had been following Shen Zhimei, feeling that something was off, but she couldn't put her finger on it. It wasn't until she saw the charred corpse again that she realized what was wrong.
Apart from her fainting earlier, Shen Zhimei’s demeanor was far too calm, which was highly inconsistent with the concern she had shown upon arrival.
Could it be that she had misinterpreted things? That Shen Zhimei actually had no feelings for Shen Jiu, and all the concern she displayed was for another purpose?
Shen Zhimei did not know that her behavior had aroused suspicion in those around her, and even if she did, she wouldn't care, because she knew Heiyue would not betray her for the time being.
In the secret chamber on the second basement level, Shen Zhimei stepped inside and looked around. It had been thoroughly burned, and the charred corpse had already been placed in a coffin.
Shen Zhimei stepped forward to take a look. The bones were covered in a layer of black carbon—what could one possibly tell from this?
Although she knew she should put on a show, she begged to be forgiven for lacking her father's flair for acting. Thus, she forced herself to stand before the coffin for a while, using this gesture to express grief.
Seeing this, Heiyue realized she might have overthought things. She joined Shen Zhimei in a moment of silence, and the coldness on her person subconsciously softened a little.
Shen Zhimei counted to one hundred in her heart before saying, "Cover it up. Take it to the courtyard first; I will take her away in a while."
Those left behind to handle the aftermath quickly stepped forward to put the lid on the coffin, and several people worked together to carry it out to the courtyard.
Shen Zhimei asked for a pair of gloves, put them on, and walked into the secret chamber. She picked up a small wooden stick at the entrance and, as she walked, poked through the burned items on the floor. With a clatter, a blackened wine pot was unearthed from the ruins by the stick.
Shen Zhimei turned her head to look, walked over, squatted down to pick up the wine pot, sniffed it, stood up, and handed it to Heiyue behind her.
After Heiyue took it, Shen Zhimei continued to search with the stick, pulling out a jade hairpin that had been burned out of shape. She squatted down, picked it up, examined it for a while, and handed it to Heiyue.
Heiyue took it with an indifferent expression. When she saw that the carving on the jade hairpin was a cherry blossom, a flash of realization crossed her cold eyes—the cherry blossom was the national flower of Japan. She then sniffed the wine pot; it smelled of gasoline.
Shen Zhimei then went out to question the relevant personnel about the scene during the banquet, concluding that two people had entered the second basement level—a man and a woman, both of whom had followed an official from the Ministry of Education.
Shen Zhimei handed the evidence to the butler and stated her findings: "When the teacher wakes up, let me know." With that, she sat on the living room sofa and closed her eyes to rest.
Seeing Miss Shen suppressing her grief to conduct an investigation, the butler nodded and left with the items.
*Ring, ring, ring...* Shen Zhimei reached out and picked up the receiver. "Hello, Zhou Mansion."
In Shanghai, at No. 76, Li Shiqun heard that another warehouse had been robbed. With a *slap*, he threw the phone in a fit of rage, stood up, and walked toward Ding Mocun’s office.
Ding Mocun was also at his wits' end. Since the early hours of this morning, robberies had been occurring one after another. It was only afternoon, and there had already been seven robberies involving the Japanese side alone; all those robbed were major Japanese trading companies.
The Japanese were pressuring the government police station and their No. 76, ordering them to find out as soon as possible which gang was responsible.
Ding Mocun had called the heads of various gangs, but they were all like slippery old foxes, distancing themselves completely and claiming it had nothing to do with them.
Li Shiqun pushed the door open and, upon seeing Ding Mocun, launched into a tirade: "Old Ding, do you think Shen Zhimei did this?"
He had been ordered to kill someone yesterday, and today he suffered the same kind of retaliation as last time—only last time it was arson on warehouses and smashing boats, and now it had turned into robbery. Just today, he had several smuggling boats and two warehouses hijacked.
Ding Mocun felt a headache coming on. He advised, "Calm down. Don't think of Shen Zhimei every time something happens. It wasn't just your place that got robbed today; many Japanese trading companies were also hit."
"How could this possibly be Shen Zhimei's doing? It is clearly an organized and premeditated operation. Our top priority now is to find out which side these people are on."
Li Shiqun frowned and sat down angrily. The successive losses had already hurt his foundation, and he couldn't help but be irritable.
Calming down, Li Shiqun also felt that even if Shen Zhimei was a bit clever, her manpower was limited, and it was impossible for her to organize such a large-scale operation.
Li Shiqun: "We have had many conflicts with the White Party recently. Could it be them?"
Ding Mocun: "I suspected that too, but the robbery methods used today were relatively mild. It doesn't look like the White Party's style; it's more like the Red Party's." It involved little bloodshed, was elusive, and they retreated quickly after the deed—all characteristic of the guerrilla warfare the Red Party excelled at.
Li Shiqun: "The Red Party is always cautious and operates in individual or small-scale activities. This scale doesn't look like their work. It could also be the White Party framing them, trying to make us turn our guns on the Red Party. The Military Bureau and Central Bureau have lost many spies lurking in Shanghai recently; we cannot rule out that they are planning this 'killing two birds with one stone' scheme."
Ding Mocun found this reasonable. The two discussed it for a while and finally decided to use multiple approaches, conducting arrests and interrogations of the gangs, the White Party, and the Red Party respectively.
After discussing business, Li Shiqun turned the topic back to Shen Zhimei, asking where she had gone.
Ding Mocun was amused. If he didn't know Li Shiqun well, he would have thought this guy was interested in Shen Zhimei.
"Shen Zhimei is at the Zhou Mansion in Nanjing. I just called to ask for instructions, and she answered the phone." Ding Mocun didn't mention the incident there, picking only the unimportant details to share.
Hearing this, Li Shiqun's suspicions completely dissipated. It seemed it really had nothing to do with Shen Zhimei. Thinking this, he didn't say anything more, got up, and left to arrange for people to investigate and make arrests...
